body.translated_text: The <s>Sūtra</s> Foundation
The <s>Anuvyākhyāna</s>

children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose single body is complete with all qualities, faultless, the most attainable, [knowable] also through all auspicious words, /

children.text: asyodbhavādidamaśeṣaviśeṣato 'pi vandyaṃ sadā priyatamaṃ mama sannamāmi // MAnuv_1,1.1 //
children.translated_text: from whom this [universe] has arisen, who surpasses all in every respect — I bow down to him who is always to be worshipped, my most beloved. // MAnuv_1,1.1 //
Having bowed to him who is the source of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), the teacher of the teachers of the world, readily /

children.text: viśeṣato me paramākhyavidyāvyākhyāṃ karomyanvapi cāhameva // MAnuv_1,1.2 //
children.translated_text: and especially, I myself now compose a commentary on the supreme knowledge called <s>paramā vidyā</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.2 //
<s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), having manifested as <s>Vyāsa</s>, entreated by <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and others, /
composed the unsurpassed <s>śāstra</s> called the supreme knowledge (<s>paravidyā</s>). // MAnuv_1,1.3 //
<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> is the teacher of teachers, the source of the <s>śāstras</s>. /
Therefore, the authority [of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>] uttered by him is [established] from [the example of] <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others, by virtue of its meaning. // MAnuv_1,1.4 //
The attainment of the interests of the speaker and the listener, their suitability, /
its being the statement of an authoritative person, its rootedness in <s>śruti</s> (scripture), /
and its rootedness in reasoning — the great threefold validity /
of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> is seen in one place, whereas elsewhere [it is seen] in all [these respects] separately. // MAnuv_1,1.6 //
Therefore, nothing is regarded as more authoritative than this. /

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtāpi tadvayākhyā kriyate spaṣṭatārthataḥ // MAnuv_1,1.7 //
children.translated_text: Even though a commentary on it was composed by himself [<s>Vyāsa</s>], a commentary is [again] composed for the sake of greater clarity of meaning. // MAnuv_1,1.7 //
Therein, the <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) is accepted as the root of all scripture in the most eminent sense, /
and since it pervades everything, it is uttered separately by all. // MAnuv_1,1.8 //
For the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> signifies pervasion; that [<s>Oṃ</s>] declares his pervasion through qualities. /
He who is the meaning of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is [also] indicated by the word '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.' // MAnuv_1,1.9 //

children.text: sa eva bhargaśabdārtho vyāhṛtīnāṃ ca bhūmataḥ /
children.translated_text: He is the meaning of the word '<s>Bharga</s>' and of the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, by virtue of abundance; /

children.text: bhāvanāccaiva sutvācca so 'yaṃ puruṣa ityapi // MAnuv_1,1.10 //
children.translated_text: and by virtue of sustaining and of being good, he is also [expressed by] 'this is the <s>Puruṣa</s>.' // MAnuv_1,1.10 //
He alone is the meaning of all the <s>Vedas</s> — inquiry into him is hereby enjoined. /

children.text: jñānī priyatamo 'to me taṃ vidvāneva cāmṛtaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.11 //
children.translated_text: 'The knower [of <s>Brahman</s>] is most dear to me; knowing him, one becomes immortal.' // MAnuv_1,1.11 //

children.text: vṛṇute yaṃ tena labhya ityādyuktibalena hi /
children.translated_text: 'He whom [<s>Brahman</s>] chooses, by that one he is attainable' — and so forth, by the force of reasoning; /
the knowledge arising from inquiry leads to liberation through his grace alone. // MAnuv_1,1.12 //

children.text: dravyaṃ karma ca kālaśca svabhāvo jīva eva ca /
children.translated_text: Substance, action, time, intrinsic nature, and the individual soul — /

children.text: yadanugrahataḥ santi na santi yadupekṣayā // MAnuv_1,1.13 //
children.translated_text: by whose grace they exist, and by whose disregard they do not exist — // MAnuv_1,1.13 //

children.text: narte tvat kriyate kiñcidityāderna hariṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: 'Nothing is done without you' — and so forth; without <s>Hari</s>, /

children.text: jñānasvabhāvato 'pi syānmuktiḥ kasyāpi hi kvacit // MAnuv_1,1.14 //
children.translated_text: liberation would not come about for anyone anywhere, even by the very nature of knowledge. // MAnuv_1,1.14 //
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the giver of knowledge to the ignorant, and the giver of liberation to the knowledgeable; /

children.text: ānandadaśca muktānāṃ sa evaiko janārdanaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.15 //
children.translated_text: he is the giver of bliss to the liberated — he alone is <s>Janārdana</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.15 //
From this statement, the falsity of bondage does not require liberation at all; /
and the falsity of bondage is not [established], because of the contradiction with direct perception. // MAnuv_1,1.16 //
If suffering and the like were false, that would follow from that very statement; /

children.text: mithyāyāḥ sādhakatvaṃ ca na siddhaṃ prativādinaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.17 //
children.translated_text: but the capacity to prove [falsity] is not established for the opponent. // MAnuv_1,1.17 //

children.text: tacca mithyāpramāṇena satā vā sādhyate tvayā /
children.translated_text: And is that [falsity] proved by you through a false means of knowledge or through a real one? /

children.text: satā ced dvaitasiddhiḥ syānna siddhaṃ cānyasādhanam // MAnuv_1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: If through a real one, duality would be established; and proof through something other [than real] is not established. // MAnuv_1,1.18 //
The probative capacity of what is real is accepted by one who desires proof through the witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣin</s>); /

children.text: svīkṛtaṃ hyaviśeṣasya sādhyā sādhakatā punaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.19 //
children.translated_text: for that which is without distinction — its probative capacity is yet to be proved. // MAnuv_1,1.19 //
And that is to be proved through a means of knowledge without distinction — hence there is an infinite regress. /
Those who do not accept the reality of the universe [cannot be considered] debaters. // MAnuv_1,1.20 //
Therefore, all conventional practice is established as real alone. /
For this reason, the conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) has indeed come [to be known] as real. // MAnuv_1,1.21 //
And the probative capacity of even the conventionally real is as before. /

children.text: sattraividhyaṃ ca mānena siddhayet keneti pṛcchyate // MAnuv_1,1.22 //
children.translated_text: The threefold [classification of] reality — by what means of knowledge would one establish it? — this is asked. // MAnuv_1,1.22 //
For that too, by the manner stated above, there is simply no proof whatsoever. /
By this, the difference between the existent and the non-existent is also negated. // MAnuv_1,1.23 //
The distinctiveness of the real and also of the non-real — the proponent of difference in reality himself [must accept it]; /

children.text: asataścāpi viśvasya tenāniṣyaṃ kathaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.24 //
children.translated_text: since [he accepts] the non-reality of the universe — how then can that be undesired [by him]? // MAnuv_1,1.24 //
If it be said 'from everything' — then the establishment of difference in reality [follows]; /

children.text: sanmātratvaṃ brahmaṇo 'pi tasmāt tadapi no bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.25 //
children.translated_text: the mere realness of <s>Brahman</s> too would therefore not hold. // MAnuv_1,1.25 //
The sublatability by knowledge too is not established for the opponent; /

children.text: vijñātasyānyathā samyag vijñānaṃ hyeva tanmatam // MAnuv_1,1.26 //
children.translated_text: for what is correctly known otherwise than as known — that indeed is their view. // MAnuv_1,1.26 //
For in order to cognize what is different from the non-existent, the non-existent itself must be known. /
Therefore, how is the cognition of the non-existent negated by him? // MAnuv_1,1.27 //
Therefore, otherness, being non-existent, is cognized only in error. /

children.text: sattvasyāsata evaṃ hi svīkāryaiva pratītatā // MAnuv_1,1.28 //
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, the cognition of the existence of the non-existent must be accepted. // MAnuv_1,1.28 //
If its indescribability [is maintained], there would indeed be an infinite regress. /

children.text: nirviśeṣe svayaṃ bhāte kimajñānāvṛtaṃ bhavetaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.29 //
children.translated_text: In that which is without distinction and self-luminous, what would be covered by ignorance? // MAnuv_1,1.29 //
Even a false distinction requires the establishment of ignorance; /
and ignorance as a covering is not accepted [by the opponent] when [<s>Brahman</s>] is not real. // MAnuv_1,1.30 //
Because of having a nature devoid of luminosity, ignorance is not attributed to the inert. /
If ignorance does not exist, all scripture will become purposeless. // MAnuv_1,1.31 //
And if the falsity of ignorance is [derived] from ignorance — in such a supposition, /
there would be an infinite regress, or alternatively, mutual dependence. // MAnuv_1,1.32 //
Because the doctrine of intrinsic ignorance is faultless, that [objection] would not apply. /

children.text: avidyādurghaṭatvaṃ cet syādātmāpi hi tādṛśaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.33 //
children.translated_text: If [it is said that] <s>avidyā</s> is difficult to establish — even the self (<s>ātman</s>) would be of such a kind. // MAnuv_1,1.33 //
Therefore, being devoid of [proper] subject, object, and fruit, /

children.text: anantadoṣaduṣṭaṃ ca heyaṃ māyāmataṃ śubhaiḥ // MAnuv_1,1.34 //
children.translated_text: and being afflicted with infinite faults — the <s>Māyā</s> doctrine should be rejected by the virtuous. // MAnuv_1,1.34 //
Therefore, because of the reality of suffering and the like, because of the contradiction with direct perception, /

children.text: na brahmatāṃ vaded vedo jīvasya hi kathañcana // MAnuv_1,1.35 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Veda</s> would never in any way declare the identity of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) with <s>Brahman</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.35 //
Just as the statement that the sacrificer is the sacrificial grass (<s>prastara</s>) would not be the intended meaning of <s>śruti</s>, /
so too the identity of the <s>jīva</s> with <s>Brahman</s>, because there is no distinction from what is directly perceived. // MAnuv_1,1.36 //
<s>Śruti</s> reveals the Lord as possessing qualities such as omniscience, and as different from the <s>jīva</s>. /
The [scripture] that speaks of identity depends upon and operates in reference to that very [scripture declaring difference]. // MAnuv_1,1.37 //
Because of contradiction with what it depends upon, the identity [interpretation] of that [scripture] does not hold. /
And in independence and in superiority, there is scope for both identity and [difference]. // MAnuv_1,1.38 //
In the case of similarity, the statement of identity is properly accommodated as desired; /
the <s>śruti</s> of difference, being undeprived of scope, how can it be not powerful? // MAnuv_1,1.39 //
Because of the very impossibility of ignorance, false difference has been refuted. /
Therefore, since real bondage does not cease without the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, // MAnuv_1,1.40 //
inquiry is hereby enjoined for that purpose. /

children.text: yathā dṛṣṭayā prasannaḥ san rājā bandhāpanodakṛt // MAnuv_1,1.41 //
children.translated_text: Just as a king, being pleased by what he has seen, removes bondage, // MAnuv_1,1.41 //

children.text: evaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ sa bhagavān kuryād bandhavibhedanam /
children.translated_text: even so, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, when seen, would effect the breaking of bondage. /

children.text: kāryatā ca na kācit syādiṣṭasādhanatāṃ vinā // MAnuv_1,1.42 //
children.translated_text: And there would be no obligation [to act] whatsoever without the desire to accomplish what is desired. // MAnuv_1,1.42 //

children.text: kāryaṃ na hi kriyāvyāpyaṃ niṣiddhasya samatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: For obligation is not [something] pervaded by action, because of its equality with what is prohibited. /

children.text: na bhaviṣyatkriyā kāryaṃ srakṣyatīśa iti hyapi // MAnuv_1,1.43 //
children.translated_text: It is not the case that action will produce obligation — 'the Lord will create' — this too [does not hold]. // MAnuv_1,1.43 //
There would be no obligation at all; and an obligation that cannot be accomplished is not accepted. /

children.text: sāmyādeva niṣiddhasya tadiṣṭaṃ sādhanaṃ tathā // MAnuv_1,1.44 //
children.translated_text: Because of the very equality with what is prohibited, that which is desired is [the true] means of accomplishment. // MAnuv_1,1.44 //
The obligation is the means to accomplishing what is desired; the <s>Bhagavān</s> is the desired deity. /

children.text: mukhyeṣyaṃ vā sumanasāṃ preyastaditi ca śrutiḥ // MAnuv_1,1.45 //
children.translated_text: The primarily desired, or [the object] of the virtuous, is the dearest — thus says <s>śruti</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.45 //
'<s>Prāṇa</s>, intellect, mind, self, body, offspring, wealth, and so forth — /

children.text: yatsamparkāt priyā āsaṃstataḥ ko nvaparaḥ priyaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.46 //
children.translated_text: by whose contact they became dear — what other [entity] is dearer than that?' // MAnuv_1,1.46 //
From such statements, expectation, proximity, and fitness, /
since all [these conditions are fulfilled] in this very [<s>Brahman</s>] — the derivation 'desiring [to know]' is accepted. // MAnuv_1,1.47 //
In [sentences like] 'Your brother eats cakes' — and so forth, from obtaining [the meaning] /
and from removing [doubt], from being in the present tense, and by the force of expectation and so forth, // MAnuv_1,1.48 //
even a child arrives at the derivation [of meaning] — from sentences like 'don't bring [him].' /
When derivation is possible by the mere perception of what is being brought, // MAnuv_1,1.49 //
why would one wait for the bringing, the leading away? /

children.text: vyutpanno vartamāne tu kriyāśabde bhaviṣyati // MAnuv_1,1.50 //
children.translated_text: One who has derived [the meaning] in the present-tense verbal form will [then understand the] future. // MAnuv_1,1.50 //
Again, by mere perception, having heard the word, one will subsequently derive the meaning — /

children.text: vartamānamatītaṃ ca bhaviṣyaditi ca kramāt // MAnuv_1,1.51 //
children.translated_text: present, past, and future, in sequence. // MAnuv_1,1.51 //
Since [it is] endowed with expectation and so forth — whence is the derivation of meaning from an injunction? /
For one whose word-meanings are known through perception, there will be expectation of further words. // MAnuv_1,1.52 //

children.text: vyutpattiḥ prathamā tasmād vatarmāne gate tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the first derivation is in the present [tense]; then, for the past, /
everyone desires what is desired — one does not await [mere] activity. // MAnuv_1,1.53 //
Knowledge — whether direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) or indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>) — is the means to what is desired. /

children.text: kvāpi ceṣyā tadarthā syādattirhi rasavittaye // MAnuv_1,1.54 //
children.translated_text: Somewhere, even desire for that [knowledge] may arise — for eating is indeed for the experience of flavor. // MAnuv_1,1.54 //
Through mere knowledge of the meaning of a statement, what is desired may sometimes come about. /
And the purport of <s>śruti</s> would not be [limited to] the ladle, the smaller ladle, the fire, and so forth. // MAnuv_1,1.55 //
Even [in the case of] performing any action whatsoever, it would be of the nature of sacrifice [in any case]. /

children.text: tasmādupāsanārthaṃ ca svārthe tātparyavad bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.56 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [<s>śruti</s>] should have its purport in meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) and in its own subject matter. // MAnuv_1,1.56 //
When [the word] '<s>iti</s>' has led [the meaning] to the fire, the <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) would follow. /
But there are indeed statements without the word '<s>iti</s>' — that suffices. // MAnuv_1,1.57 //
'The self alone' — and such [statements], in the context of meditation (<s>yoga</s>), apply equally to the fire. /
And in the context of single-sentence unity, even of the entire <s>Veda</s>, // MAnuv_1,1.58 //

children.text: vākyabhedo na yuktaḥ syād yogaśca syānmahāphale /
children.translated_text: the splitting of sentences would not be proper; and unity would be [maintained] in the great fruit. /

children.text: iti brūyāditi vaco gatamagnau samīpagam // MAnuv_1,1.59 //
children.translated_text: Thus one would say — this statement pertains to the fire, being proximate [to it]. // MAnuv_1,1.59 //
If there were the defect of excessive assumption when separate purports are possible, /

children.text: kalpanāgauravādeva padārthā na syureva hi // MAnuv_1,1.60 //
children.translated_text: then by the very defect of excessive assumption, word-meanings themselves would not exist. // MAnuv_1,1.60 //
If [you say that word-meanings] are established through means of knowledge — purports [too] are exactly like that. /

children.text: tasmāt padārthe vākyārthe tātparyamubhayatra ca // MAnuv_1,1.61 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, purport exists in both the word-meaning and the sentence-meaning. // MAnuv_1,1.61 //
And the separate sentence-hood [of subsidiary statements] follows from their separate syntactic connection. /

children.text: avāntaratvād vākyānāṃ vākyabhedo na dūṣaṇam // MAnuv_1,1.62 //
children.translated_text: Since the sentences are subordinate, the splitting of sentences is not a fault. // MAnuv_1,1.62 //
Because even by them, the word-meanings are accepted separately; /
the fault of splitting sentences arises from the syntactic connection with a different action-word. // MAnuv_1,1.63 //
Therefore, when there is contradiction with direct perception and so forth, since even a figurative meaning is possible, /
non-purport in a word-meaning should not be supposed when there is no contradiction. // MAnuv_1,1.64 //
Therefore, actions are for the fruit of knowledge; knowledge indeed /
is the primary [means for] the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and inquiry [into <s>Brahman</s>] would be for that [purpose]. // MAnuv_1,1.65 //
Therefore, inquiry should be undertaken, by virtue of the authority of <s>śruti</s>. /

children.text: pratyakṣavacca prāmāṇyaṃ svata evāgamasya hi // MAnuv_1,1.66 //
children.translated_text: And the authority of scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is self-established, just like [the authority of] direct perception. // MAnuv_1,1.66 //
Otherwise there would be an infinite regress; and invalidity [would come] from another [source]. /
Because of false designation, deception, and so forth — therefore, what contradicts the <s>Veda</s> // MAnuv_1,1.67 //
is not authoritative; and the eternality of the <s>Vedas</s> must be accepted. /

children.text: na hi dharmādisiddhiḥ syānnityavākyaṃ vinā kvacit // MAnuv_1,1.68 //
children.translated_text: For the establishment of <s>dharma</s> and so forth would not be possible anywhere without an eternal statement. // MAnuv_1,1.68 //
Non-deceptiveness, knowledge of that [truth], being composed by him — and so forth — /

children.text: kalpyā gauravadoṣeṇa puṃvākyaṃ jñāpakaṃ na tat // MAnuv_1,1.69 //
children.translated_text: are to be attributed [to the <s>Vedas</s>], but the defect of [excessive] complexity [follows]; the statement of a person is not [self-validating] in that [manner]. // MAnuv_1,1.69 //
If it be objected that <s>dharma</s> is directly perceptible to someone, because of being a real entity — /

children.text: na buddho dharmadarśī syāt puṃstvādityanumāhatiḥ // MAnuv_1,1.70 //
children.translated_text: even the <s>Buddha</s> would not be a seer of <s>dharma</s>, because of [merely] being a person — this [follows from] a strike by inference. // MAnuv_1,1.70 //
The statement of one who teaches <s>adharma</s> (non-righteousness) is simply purposeless. /

children.text: dharmābhāvo 'pi no tena pratyakṣāvagato bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.71 //
children.translated_text: Nor would the non-existence of <s>dharma</s> be established for us through direct perception. // MAnuv_1,1.71 //
Therefore, when doubt and fitness [are present], a statement [of scripture] is a valid means of knowledge, like direct perception. /
And the capacity of words in their own connected meaning is indeed experienced. // MAnuv_1,1.72 //
Therefore, the doctrine of connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>) [is correct]; complexity follows from the alternative supposition. /
And there is no impossibility of expression; and activity is twofold, [not] otherwise. // MAnuv_1,1.73 //

children.text: etat sarvaṃ tarkaśāstre brahmatarke hi vistarāt /
children.translated_text: All this has been stated at length in the logical treatise, in the <s>Brahmatarka</s>. /
But because it is a separate discipline, it is indicated here only in brief. // MAnuv_1,1.74 //
The proper training in <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) and reasoning is done through the logical treatise. /
But inquiry into the objects of knowledge, established through those very <s>pramāṇas</s> and reasoning — that is <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> (investigation). // MAnuv_1,1.75 //

children.text: brahmatarkaṃ ca bhagavān sa eva kṛtavān prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>) Himself, the Supreme, composed the <s>Brahmatarka</s>, /
from the [original work] composed in the body of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, extending to fifty <s>koṭis</s> (five hundred million [verses]). // MAnuv_1,1.76 //
<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> extracted five thousand [<s>sūtras</s>]. /
Therefore, by 'ataḥ' (hence), he indicated: 'for this purpose, in brief.' // MAnuv_1,1.77 //
Since for one who directly experiences, everything is already established — therefore, /
being occupied with topics difficult [to understand] even for the <s>devas</s>, he did not make [the sūtras] excessively lengthy. // MAnuv_1,1.78 //
He composed these arguments that refute the opposing positions, [which] should not be disregarded. /
One incapable of direct perception — which position would he even look at here? // MAnuv_1,1.79 //
Therefore, because of being incapable of [directly perceiving] the thesis, it was disregarded in the treatise on liberation. /
By the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself, '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — this was stated first. // MAnuv_1,1.80 //

children.text: sa viṣṇurāha hīyante devaśāstrasya tena hi /
children.translated_text: That <s>Viṣṇu</s> said: 'They diminish [the authority] of the divine scripture.' Indeed, /

children.text: ādyantaṃ devaśāstrasya svayaṃ bhagavatā kṛtam // MAnuv_1,1.81 //
children.translated_text: the beginning and end of the divine scripture was composed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself. // MAnuv_1,1.81 //
The middle portion was composed straightforwardly by <s>Paila</s> and <s>Śeṣa</s>, by His command. /
Therefore, because the proof of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s [supreme status] is found right there, He indicated 'Brahman.' // MAnuv_1,1.82 //
Since the words 'fault,' 'deficiency,' and 'hole' are synonymous, therefore /

children.text: guṇā nārā iti jñeyastadvān nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.83 //
children.translated_text: qualities are to be known as '<s>nāras</s>'; the one who possesses them is known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.83 //
The word '<s>Brahman</s>' too declares precisely the fullness of qualities. /
Therefore, it is the inquiry into <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone that is enjoined here. // MAnuv_1,1.84 //
Since the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is established as referring to <s>Viṣṇu</s> clearly in the <s>Śruti</s>, /
'The boundless one in the waters' — thus spoken, conveyed by the word <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.85 //

children.text: āpo nārā iti hyāha sa evāpsvantarīritaḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is said: 'The waters are <s>nāras</s>' — and He is spoken of as dwelling within the waters. /
By His own will, through <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) Herself, who bestows the positions of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others, // MAnuv_1,1.86 //
as the womb — it is stated that [all] abide in <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the Self. /

children.text: yasmin devā adhītyuktavā samudraṃ sthānameva ca // MAnuv_1,1.87 //
children.translated_text: 'In whom the <s>devas</s> [dwell]' — thus said; and the ocean, which is His abode, // MAnuv_1,1.87 //

children.text: nāma cākṣaramityeva ṛca ityuditaṃ tu yat /
children.translated_text: and the name 'the Imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>)' — thus what is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s> (Ṛgveda), /

children.text: yataḥ prasūtetyuktavā ca tadeva brahma cābravīt // MAnuv_1,1.88 //
children.translated_text: 'from whom [all beings] are born' — thus stated; and He indeed declared [this to be] <s>Brahman</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.88 //
That which is within the ocean, the cause of the creation of the universe — /
as stated in the <s>sūkta</s>, <s>Upaniṣad</s>, and so forth — is indicated by 'that from which birth and the rest [proceed].' // MAnuv_1,1.89 //
Creation, sustenance, dissolution, regulation, knowledge, concealment, /

children.text: bandhamokṣāvapi hyāsu śrutiṣūktā hareḥ sadā // MAnuv_1,1.90 //
children.translated_text: and bondage and liberation too — in these <s>Śrutis</s>, they are always said to be of <s>Hari</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.90 //

children.text: yaṃ nāmāni viśantyaddhā yo devānāmiti hyapi /
children.translated_text: 'Into whom all names enter' and also 'who [is the Lord] of the <s>devas</s>' — /
from the <s>Śruti</s>, all names belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; therefore, // MAnuv_1,1.91 //

children.text: ato na mukhyato nāma tadanyasya hi kasyacit /
children.translated_text: no other entity has a name in the primary sense. /

children.text: guṇāḥ śrutā iti hyasmānna doṣo 'rthaḥ śruterbhavet // MAnuv_1,1.92 //
children.translated_text: Since qualities are heard [in <s>Śruti</s> as His], therefore no defect — that is the meaning of <s>Śruti</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.92 //
Because of the predominance of devotion (<s>prīti</s>) and liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), the purport is not in fault-finding. /
For the great purport of all statements is indeed here. // MAnuv_1,1.93 //

children.text: tadvirodhe na mānatvaṃ phalaṃ muktirhi vākyataḥ /
children.translated_text: What contradicts that has no validity; for the fruit [declared] by scripture is liberation. /
The <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like would not be valid in a meaning that contradicts <s>Śruti</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.94 //
Because of being the basis of other philosophical systems, and for the purpose of delusion, by the command of <s>Hari</s> — /

children.text: na sarvanāmatānyeṣāṃ śrutāvuktā hi kutracit // MAnuv_1,1.95 //
children.translated_text: the [attribute of having] all names is nowhere stated of others in <s>Śruti</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.95 //
And because of the statement of faultlessness, [all names belong] invariably to <s>Hari</s> alone in <s>Śruti</s>. /

children.text: ajñānaṃ pāratantryaṃ ca praḷaye 'bhāva eva ca // MAnuv_1,1.96 //
children.translated_text: Ignorance, dependence, and non-existence at the time of dissolution, // MAnuv_1,1.96 //
and incapacity — are stated of all others in <s>Śruti</s>. /
Therefore, 'that from which birth and the rest [proceed]' — this is the defining characteristic of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. // MAnuv_1,1.97 //
Being the direct cause of the creation and the rest of this [universe] is His own defining characteristic. /
Under the pretext of meditation on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, He Himself declared [this] in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.98 //
Therefore, the Teacher of the World also refuted the identity [of <s>Brahman</s>] with the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>). /

children.text: na hi janmādihetutvaṃ jīvasya jagato bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.99 //
children.translated_text: For the individual soul cannot be the cause of birth and the rest of the universe. // MAnuv_1,1.99 //
And the fault of failure to create and so forth — the Lord Himself will state it. /

children.text: nirguṇatvaṃ ca tenaiva niṣiddhaṃ prabhuṇā svayam // MAnuv_1,1.100 //
children.translated_text: And attributelessness (<s>nirguṇatva</s>) was refuted by that very Lord Himself. // MAnuv_1,1.100 //
When the primary meaning is possible through difference alone, how can there be secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>)? /
How could there be identity for this one who eternally possesses qualities, through the absence of qualities? // MAnuv_1,1.101 //
Since He always possesses qualities, what is different [from Him] would always be without qualities. /

children.text: na ca mithyāguṇatvaṃ syādanirvācyasya dūṣaṇāt // MAnuv_1,1.102 //
children.translated_text: Nor could there be illusory quality, because of the refutation of the indescribable (<s>anirvācya</s>). // MAnuv_1,1.102 //
Attributelessness would then amount to being a demon (<s>āsura</s>) — and not otherwise. /
Whether the <s>lakṣya</s> (referent) and <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (definition) are different, non-different, or both — // MAnuv_1,1.103 //

children.text: iti pṛṣṭe tadaikyasya gatireva na vidyate /
children.translated_text: when this is asked, there is simply no recourse for [the position of] identity. /

children.text: aikyābhede na śāstreṇa jñeyaṃ tat svaprakāśataḥ // MAnuv_1,1.104 //
children.translated_text: If identity [means] non-difference, then it need not be known through scripture — by its self-luminosity. // MAnuv_1,1.104 //
If [they are] different, then, because of the falsity [of difference], the truth of difference would follow perforce. /

children.text: bhedābhedau yadi tadā syādeva hyanavasthitiḥ // MAnuv_1,1.105 //
children.translated_text: If both difference and non-difference, then there would indeed be an infinite regress. // MAnuv_1,1.105 //
If [you say] 'self-sufficiency' — then even 'the external is the carrier' would be a synonym. /

children.text: paryāyo bhedavān vā syādanavasthobhayatra ca // MAnuv_1,1.106 //
children.translated_text: Or it would be a [term] possessing difference — and in both cases an infinite regress. // MAnuv_1,1.106 //
Even in [terms like] 'truth,' 'knowledge,' and the like — there is no purpose in exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>). /
If what is excluded is without distinction, then the indivisible is divided. /
Attributelessness by this [reasoning] would be like [the statement] 'I am mute.' // MAnuv_1,1.107 //
Even in what is non-different, this distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>) indeed inevitably applies. Therefore, /
self-sufficiency obtains for both <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) and its possessor. // MAnuv_1,1.108 //
Where there is no [real] difference, the determiner of non-synonymous alternative words /

children.text: viśeṣo nāma kathitaḥ so 'sti vastuṣvaśeṣataḥ // MAnuv_1,1.109 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>viśeṣa</s> (intrinsic distinction) — it exists in all entities without exception. // MAnuv_1,1.109 //
And those <s>viśeṣas</s> are infinite, mutually distinguishing each other, /
possessed of self-sufficiency — they exist in all entities without exception. // MAnuv_1,1.110 //
Therefore, <s>Brahman</s> is declared to possess infinite qualities and yet to be without [real internal] division. /
Thus, by the <s>Śruti</s> 'thus [possessing] all attributes,' His non-difference [from His qualities] is also declared. // MAnuv_1,1.111 //
But through the observed fruit obtained through the <s>Śaiva</s> and other <s>Āgamas</s>, /
another [scripture's] validity is inferred by analogy with those statements. // MAnuv_1,1.112 //
If [one says:] 'because they are the words of the Lord' — [we reply:] since that [inference] is deviated from by [contradictory evidence], /

children.text: aprāmāṇyānumā ca syānna pṛthak cānumeśvare // MAnuv_1,1.113 //
children.translated_text: there would be an inference of invalidity; and there is no separate inference regarding the Lord. // MAnuv_1,1.113 //
By the force of the cause of personhood alone, through the very path stated before, /
the [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the source of scripture follows by the force of [being the] cause. // MAnuv_1,1.114 //
From statements like 'Not through non-<s>Vedic</s> [knowledge], not through reasoning, can this understanding [be gained]' — /

children.text: tarko jñāpayituṃ śakto neśitāraṃ kathañcana // MAnuv_1,1.115 //
children.translated_text: reasoning is unable to make known the Supreme Lord in any way. // MAnuv_1,1.115 //
Of the Lord, who is [merely] a thesis in the form of 'maker of the forest' and so forth, /

children.text: kiñcijjñānaṃ hi puṃstvena śakyaṃ sādhayituṃ sukham // MAnuv_1,1.116 //
children.translated_text: some limited knowledge can be easily established through personhood. // MAnuv_1,1.116 //
The maker of a tree does not know the entire tree, [yet] through personhood — like [the case of] <s>Caitra</s>. /
Through such an inference, rivaling [this], an inference about the Supreme Lord /
is not capable of making [Him] known; and by such an inference there would be overextension. // MAnuv_1,1.117 //

children.text: vastutvāt turagaḥ śṛṅgī puṣpavat khaṃ sutairyutā /
children.translated_text: 'Because it is an entity, a horse has horns'; 'the sky has flowers'; '[a barren woman] is endowed with sons'; /

children.text: citriṇī ca rasaḥ ṣaṣṭho rasatvāt sottaro bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'a variegated [river]'; 'a sixth taste exists, because of being a taste' — and so one could go further. /
From indicators such as the opening, and so forth, no other inference [about <s>Brahman</s>] is possible. // MAnuv_1,1.118 //
Those [indicators] themselves are called <s>anvaya</s> (concordance); when properly investigated through them, /

children.text: mukhyārtho bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sarvaśāstrasya nāparaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.119 //
children.translated_text: the primary referent of all scripture is the <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s> — not another. // MAnuv_1,1.119 //
Because of being the one to be inquired into (<s>īkṣaṇīya</s>), <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the [direct] referent — not otherwise. /

children.text: lakṣyatvaṃ kvāpi dṛṣṭaṃ hi kiṃ tadityanavasthitiḥ // MAnuv_1,1.120 //
children.translated_text: Being merely the indicated [secondary referent] is seen [only] in certain cases — and [asking] 'what is that?' leads to infinite regress. // MAnuv_1,1.120 //
Special qualities such as sweetness and the like are always expressed by those very words. /
The meaning of a sentence too is expressed by the very word for the sentence-meaning. // MAnuv_1,1.121 //

children.text: nāvācyaṃ tena kiñcit syād yata ityādikairvadan /
children.translated_text: Therefore, nothing would be inexpressible. One who says 'from which...' and the like, /
how could a wise person say 'it is inexpressible' — like [the statement] 'I am mute'? // MAnuv_1,1.122 //
The one who said 'that which is indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>)' — he spoke by means of the word '<s>lakṣya</s>.' /

children.text: ekasyāpi hi śabdasya gauṇārthasvīkṛtau satām // MAnuv_1,1.123 //
children.translated_text: When even a single word's secondary meaning is accepted by the wise, // MAnuv_1,1.123 //

children.text: mahatī jāyate lajjā yatra tatrākhilā ravāḥ /
children.translated_text: great shame arises. And one who says, in every case, that all utterances /
have non-primary meanings — /

children.text: kathaṃ na jāyate lajjā vaktuṃ śābdatvamātmanaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.124 //
children.translated_text: how does shame not arise for the followers of that path, in claiming their own linguistic competence? // MAnuv_1,1.124 //
Words such as '<s>ātman</s>' (self), '<s>Brahman</s>,' and the like directly denote the Full One. /

children.text: janmādikāraṇaṃ brahma lakṣitaṃ ca yadā tadā // MAnuv_1,1.125 //
children.translated_text: And when <s>Brahman</s>, as the cause of birth and the rest, is indicated — then, // MAnuv_1,1.125 //
having imagined without evidence that the referent is tinged with <s>māyā</s> (illusion), like the son of a barren woman, /

children.text: kalpayitvā vinā mānaṃ lakṣyaṃ śuddhaṃ vadan padaiḥ // MAnuv_1,1.126 //
children.translated_text: and speaking of the indicated [<s>Brahman</s>] as 'pure' through [other] words — // MAnuv_1,1.126 //
the knowledge of the very one denoted by the word '<s>ātman</s>' is the means [to] the state of the liberated. /
[The Advaitin] states — [but this amounts to] abandoning <s>Śruti</s> and imagining what is not in <s>Śruti</s>. // MAnuv_1,1.127 //

children.text: syāt sarvatra ca yatraikamapi loko jugupsate /
children.translated_text: This would apply everywhere; and where even one [position] is abhorred by the world, /
both [positions] would necessarily apply — for one whose view [is contradicted] by both one's own and the other's doctrines. // MAnuv_1,1.128 //
This one is always adorned with ornaments that are impossible fabrications. /

children.text: andhantamo nityuduḥkhaṃ tasya syād vasanadvayam // MAnuv_1,1.129 //
children.translated_text: Blinding darkness and perpetual suffering would be his two garments. // MAnuv_1,1.129 //

children.text: anandā nāma te lokā andhena tamasā'vṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Joyless indeed are those worlds, enveloped in blinding darkness; /
to them, after death, go those unwise, deluded people.' // MAnuv_1,1.130 //

children.text: asuryā nāma te lokā andhena tamasā'vṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Demoniac indeed are those worlds, enveloped in blinding darkness; /

children.text: tāṃste pretyābhigacchanti ye kecātmahano janāḥ // MAnuv_1,1.131 //
children.translated_text: to them, after death, go those people who are slayers of the self.' // MAnuv_1,1.131 //
These and hundreds of other <s>Śrutis</s> are the evidence, throughout. /

children.text: heyatvāvacanāccaiva nātmā gauṇaḥ śrutau śrutaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.132 //
children.translated_text: And because there is no statement that it is to be abandoned, the self (<s>ātman</s>) heard in <s>Śruti</s> is not secondary. // MAnuv_1,1.132 //

children.text: tamevaikaṃ jānathānyā vāco muñcatha ceti ha /
children.translated_text: 'Know that One alone — abandon other words' — thus indeed /

children.text: ukta ātmā kathaṃ gauṇo heyapakṣe hyasau śrutaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.133 //
children.translated_text: the self is spoken of. How can it be secondary, when it is heard on the side of what is not to be rejected? // MAnuv_1,1.133 //
Even those that are to be grasped as attendants are to be rejected from the standpoint of what is principal. /
'From the Full (<s>Pūrṇa</s>), the Full is taken; the Full alone remains.' // MAnuv_1,1.134 //
Thus, even with the departure of the Full from His own Full [Self], [the Full] is cited. /

children.text: kathaṃ māyāvyavacchinnaḥ pūrṇo mukhyatayā bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.135 //
children.translated_text: How could one delimited by <s>māyā</s> be Full in the primary sense? // MAnuv_1,1.135 //

children.text: padaṃ ca nirguṇa iti kathaṃ gauṇaṃ vadiṣyati /
children.translated_text: And the word '<s>nirguṇa</s>' (without qualities) — how will it be secondary? /

children.text: guṇābhāvopalakṣyaṃ cet padaṃ tadapi vācakam // MAnuv_1,1.136 //
children.translated_text: If the word indicates the absence of qualities — even so, that word is [still] expressive. // MAnuv_1,1.136 //
Therefore, how could this doctrine — the great repository of all defects headed by infinite regress — /
be regarded by wise and discerning persons? // MAnuv_1,1.137 //
And the <s>Bhagavān</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) did not compose these <s>sūtras</s> for the purpose of refuting the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> [alone]. /
For He does not accept that the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is not denoted by words. // MAnuv_1,1.138 //
When <s>samanvaya</s> (concordance) has been proposed, it is the very being-within-the-scope-of-words /
that should be demonstrated first. In its absence, how could there be concordance? // MAnuv_1,1.139 //
And how could one who advocates secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) speak of the concordance of <s>Brahman</s>? /

children.text: yo 'sau śabdasya mukhyārthastatraiva syāt samanvayaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.140 //
children.translated_text: The concordance should be precisely in the primary meaning of the word. // MAnuv_1,1.140 //
Regarding the direct cause of birth and the rest, the Lord declared concordance. /

children.text: uktaṃ tadeva jijñāsyaṃ kvāvakāśo 'tra nirguṇe // MAnuv_1,1.141 //
children.translated_text: What has been said is the very thing to be inquired into — where is there room here for an attributeless [<s>Brahman</s>]? // MAnuv_1,1.141 //
And how could there be impossibility when the primary meaning has not been refuted? /
By what means of knowledge should the inexpressible, unknowable, attributeless [<s>Brahman</s>] be known? // MAnuv_1,1.142 //

children.text: ameyaṃ cenna śāstrasya tatra vṛttiḥ kathañcana /
children.translated_text: If it is immeasurable, then scripture has no application to it whatsoever. /
Therefore, what is to be inquired into through scripture is our [<s>Brahman</s>] — the ocean of qualities, // MAnuv_1,1.143 //
known as <s>Vāsudeva</s>, beyond duality, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the highest of all. /
by the priority of being knowable, expressible, and indicable, and by all [other] distinctions // 1.1.144 //

children.text: nirgataṃ manaso vāco yadi tat syādagocaram /
children.translated_text: If that which has gone beyond mind and speech were beyond the range [of words], /

children.text: astu tanmā vaded vādī nacāsmacchāstragaṃ tu tat // MAnuv_1,1.145 //
children.translated_text: let it be so — let no speaker speak of it; but that is not what is found in our scripture // 1.1.145 //
Why does one who says 'the inexpressible is expressible' speak falsely like a madman? /
He who contradicts his own statements strives for the theft of our scripture // 1.1.146 //
That which is the cause of creation and so forth, directly named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, /

children.text: vadantu śrutayo brahma śāstraṃ caitat tadarthataḥ // MAnuv_1,1.147 //
children.translated_text: let the <s>Śrutis</s> declare it as <s>Brahman</s>, and this scripture [does so] for that very purpose // 1.1.147 //
Moreover, for those by whom even the self-luminosity of knowledge has been denied, /

children.text: kathaṃ sarvajñatā tasya svajñānādhigamaṃ vinā // MAnuv_1,1.148//
children.translated_text: how can His omniscience be [established] without the attainment of self-knowledge? // 1.1.148 //
Let the inexpressible be accepted by you — but you should never say anything about it; /
that which is inexpressible by all words — having spoken of it, [you have made it] the object [of words] again // 1.1.149 //
We, having bound you by <s>Śruti</s> and reasoning, [examine] our scripture directly; /
we investigate with <s>Śrutis</s> and with reasoning, respectfully // 1.1.150 //
It is inexpressible because of its wonderfulness, and inconceivable and unknowable indeed, /
because of its fullness of infinite qualities — thus the <s>Śruti</s> of the <s>Paiṅgins</s> proclaims. /
'Inexpressible' is used even in common parlance for what is most wondrous on earth // 1.1.151 //
Thus, regarding its cognizability through scripture, the unborn [<s>Brahmā</s>] teaches the harmonization (<s>samanvaya</s>) in detail /
through the chapter beginning with '<s>ānandamaya</s>' and so forth // 1.1.152 //
Therein, the harmonization of words that are well-known elsewhere as referring to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, /
words denoting the possessor of qualities [and] general [attributes], in the first <s>pāda</s> // 1.1.153 //
The Lord first teaches the harmonization of words denoting qualities; /
the <s>Śruti</s> [declares Him] as reclining on the ocean, the source of all creation // 1.1.154 //
'That alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — thus the <s>Śruti</s> sang with firm determination, /
because of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' being fixed in that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] alone // 1.1.155 //
'He who [knows] food as <s>Brahman</s>' and such forms — from repetition in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>, /
and in other branches too, in such forms, thousands of times // 1.1.156 //
<s>Hari</s> Himself is to be denoted by the words '<s>ānandamaya</s>' and the rest; /
the words beginning with '<s>ānandamaya</s>' have the character of being indicatory // 1.1.157 //
Because of the brevity of syllables in the <s>sūtra</s>, for the determination of all branches, /
and again because of a [further] reason that leads [to the conclusion], there is a separate topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) there // 1.1.158 //

children.text: sarve vedā āmananti yat padaṃ tviti hi śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All the <s>Vedas</s> declare that state' — thus indeed is the <s>Śruti</s>; /
but regarding the <s>ānandamaya</s> form of <s>Brahman</s>, because of the mention of 'tail' (<s>puccha</s>) // 1.1.159 //
since by all means the non-<s>Brahman</s>-hood is not obtained, the name <s>ānandamaya</s> indeed [refers to <s>Brahman</s>]; /
and because of the repetition of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' clearly in the five forms and so forth // 1.1.160 //
<s>Brahman</s>-hood may belong to the part as well as to the whole by its own nature, /
just as the complete <s>Brahman</s>-hood of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who has dark hair // 1.1.161 //

children.text: darśitā caiva pārthāya niḥsīmāḥ śaktayo 'sya hi /
children.translated_text: was shown to <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), for His powers are limitless; /

children.text: ṛtaṃ satyaṃ paraṃ brahma puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇapiṅgalam // MAnuv_1,1.162 //
children.translated_text: 'Truth, reality, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, dark-tawny' // 1.1.162 //
has been declared elsewhere by the name <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and as '<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>' (of upward seed) with regard to that; /
the inferior one, by the name <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, is declared as [secondary] <s>Brahman</s>, established in His vow // 1.1.163 //
If there is co-referentiality, the subsequent 'blue-red' (<s>nīlalohita</s>) /
would become a repetition of the 'dark-tawny' (<s>kṛṣṇapiṅgala</s>) form // 1.1.164 //
'<s>Brahmādhipati</s>' — here in the <s>Tāpanīya Śruti</s>, previously, /
ending with the word '<s>Brahman</s>' with <s>svarita</s> accent, it will have the [analysis of a] <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound // 1.1.165 //
'<s>Svāhendraśatru</s>, grow!' — in the great grammar [of <s>Pāṇini</s>] the <s>sūtra</s> /
that determines the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> status [is relevant] in the determination of accent // 1.1.166 //
When the <s>svarita</s> accent is on the prior member, the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> status for masculine [is established]; /
in the great grammar, the <s>sūtra</s> — thus in the determination of accent // 1.1.167 //
'Truth, reality, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — and so forth; the second case-ending is that of the referent; /
'<s>Ūrdhvaretas</s>' and so forth in the nominative case pertains to <s>Rudra</s> // 1.1.168 //

children.text: tasmād viṣṇuṃ paraṃ brahma prati rudro vrate sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Rudra</s> is established in the vow toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; /

children.text: ūrdhvaretā iti hyeva śrutyartho 'vasito bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.169 //
children.translated_text: the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> should be understood as '<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>' indeed // 1.1.169 //

children.text: ṛtaṃ satyaṃ paraṃ brahma prati viṣṇuṃ sadāśivaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — truth, reality — <s>Sadāśiva</s>, /

children.text: ūrdhvaretā dhyāyati ha śaṅkaro nīlalohitaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.170 //
children.translated_text: of upward seed, meditates indeed — <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the blue-red one' // 1.1.170 //
The supreme <s>Nīlagrīva Śruti</s>, belonging to the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, states precisely this meaning; /

children.text: ārtharvaṇī paraṃ brahma tasmādeko hariḥ śrutau // MAnuv_1,1.171 //
children.translated_text: therefore <s>Hari</s> alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> in the <s>Śruti</s> // 1.1.171 //
'That indeed is the truth (<s>ṛta</s>)' — how could the <s>Śruti</s> say otherwise, /
ascertaining directly the truth-hood and so forth of that [<s>Hari</s>] alone? // 1.1.172 //

children.text: eko nārāyaṇa āsīnna brahmā na ca śaṅkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone existed in the beginning — neither <s>Brahmā</s> nor <s>Śaṅkara</s>; /

children.text: vāsudevo 'gra evāsīnna brahmā na ca śaṅkaraḥ // MAnuv_1,1.173 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsudeva</s> alone existed in the beginning — neither <s>Brahmā</s> nor <s>Śaṅkara</s>' // 1.1.173 //

children.text: nendrasūryau na ca guho na somo na vināyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Neither <s>Indra</s> nor <s>Sūrya</s>, neither <s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>), /
neither <s>Soma</s> nor <s>Vināyaka</s>' — from such statements, the origination of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is through descent (<s>avatāra</s>) // 1.1.174 //
<s>Hari</s> is therefore the primary <s>Brahman</s>; and because of the introduction as 'supreme,' /

children.text: mukhyabrahmagrahe yukte nāmukhyaṃ yujyate kvacit // MAnuv_1,1.175 //
children.translated_text: when the primary meaning of <s>Brahman</s> is appropriate, a non-primary meaning is never suitable // 1.1.175 //
Only when the primary meaning is impossible would the acceptance of a secondary meaning be appropriate; /
and all the meanings of abundance of the suffix <s>-mayaṭ</s> are demonstrated here // 1.1.176 //
The sense of being enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>) and primacy here belong to <s>Hari</s> by virtue of being the sustainer; /
the meaning in the '<s>annamaya</s>' [passage] should be: 'the great enjoyer, the great object of enjoyment' // 1.1.177 //
He is the great vital breath, the great awakener, and possessed of great consciousness; /
through the relation of specific and general, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is also [called] <s>manas</s> (mind) // 1.1.178 //
The statement regarding <s>Hari</s>, who is of the nature of knowledge alone, is made through division; /
even though there is no [real] difference, <s>Hari</s> is spoken of as 'other' by way of distinction // 1.1.179 //
Words denoting difference express distinction in <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and others because of [actual] separateness; /
they would express the difference of <s>Hari</s> from <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) and <s>jaḍa</s> (insentient matter) too, primarily // 1.1.180 //
The statement of <s>Brahmatarka</s> is also thus: 'therefore He is one, [yet described] fivefold'; /
the statement '<s>annamaya</s>' and so forth will be told of <s>Bhṛgu</s> // 1.1.181 //
The suffix <s>-mayaṭ</s> is used in the sense of attainability — nor is anything else stated there; /
therefore, since He is indeed abundant in food and so forth, He is called '<s>anna</s>' and '<s>annamaya</s>' as well // 1.1.182 //
This is stated without distinction — nothing else is stated here; /

children.text: mahānandatva evāsya hetuḥ ko 'nyāditi sphuṭam // MAnuv_1,1.183 //
children.translated_text: the reason for His being of supreme bliss is clearly stated: 'what else [could there be]?' // 1.1.183 //

children.text: uktaḥ śrutyantare yasmāt sukhaṃ labdhvā karotyayam /
children.translated_text: 'Since He, having obtained bliss, creates' — this is stated in another <s>Śruti</s>; /

children.text: karoti nāsukhī bhūmā sukhaṃ nālpe sukhaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_1,1.184 //
children.translated_text: 'One who is not happy does not act; bliss is the <s>Bhūmā</s> (the great); there is no bliss in the small' // 1.1.184 //
What is stated [is that] activity such as dancing, singing, and so forth is from bliss, /

children.text: duḥkhād rodādikā caiva sarvakartṛtvato 'sya ca // MAnuv_1,1.185 //
children.translated_text: while weeping and the like are from sorrow; and because of His being the creator of all // 1.1.185 //
for one of all powers, there can be no sorrow; therefore, by mere sport alone /

children.text: pravartako na cedeṣa prāṇyādanyācca kaḥ pumān // MAnuv_1,1.186 //
children.translated_text: He is the instigator; and if not He, then what person other than the living being [could it be]? // 1.1.186 //
'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the supreme' — what was first indicated, /
that very thing is defined by the <s>mantra</s> words as 'truth, knowledge, infinite' // 1.1.187 //
Therein, truth-hood is indicated, and through creation, of food and vital breath too; /

children.text: uktaṃ jñānaṃ tu manasā vijñānenāpyudīritam // MAnuv_1,1.188 //
children.translated_text: knowledge is stated through <s>manas</s> (mind) and through <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as well // 1.1.188 //
Infinitude likewise is expressed by the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>'; /

children.text: sadbhāvaṃ yāpayed yasmāt satyaṃ tat tena kathyate // MAnuv_1,1.189 //
children.translated_text: 'since it causes beings to sustain existence, it is called <s>satya</s> (truth)' // 1.1.189 //
Thus creation is stated here as what causes the sustenance of the world; /

children.text: brahmeti sthāpanāyaiva sattvaṃ jīvanameva ca // MAnuv_1,1.190 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s>' is for the purpose of establishing existence and life itself // 1.1.190 //

children.text: viśīrṇatā ca sattvaṃ syāt sannamityāhureva yat /
children.translated_text: Being (<s>sattva</s>) may mean dissolution; what they say as '<s>sannam</s>' [means bowing down]; /
therefore, food-hood through nourishing and sustaining is indeed the meaning of the word '<s>satya</s>' // 1.1.191 //

children.text: prāṇaṃ devā anuprāṇanti manuṣyāḥ paśavaśca ye /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>devas</s> breathe after <s>prāṇa</s>, and so do human beings and animals; /

children.text: āyuḥ prāṇo hi bhūtānāmiti yad gatijīvane // MAnuv_1,1.192 //
children.translated_text: <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed the life of beings' — thus regarding movement and life // 1.1.192 //
the root meaning of '<s>sat</s>' is stated as 'movement'; and therefore truth-hood, /
and <s>prāṇa</s>-hood; the root '<s>man</s>' is declared to have the meaning of understanding // 1.1.193 //
'There is no bliss in the small' — by this very statement of '<s>ānandamaya</s>,' /

children.text: anantatvaṃ sunirṇītaṃ pūrṇānando hi nālpake // MAnuv_1,1.194 //
children.translated_text: infinitude is well-determined, for complete bliss does not belong to what is small // 1.1.194 //
Therefore, the elaboration stated in the <s>mantra</s> words is done in its entirety /

children.text: kriyate parayā yasmāditaro 'tra na kathyate // MAnuv_1,1.195 //
children.translated_text: by the supreme [<s>Śruti</s>], since no other [subject] is spoken of here // 1.1.195 //

children.text: puruṣaṃ vetti yo mucyennānyaḥ panthā hi vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'One who knows the <s>Puruṣa</s> is liberated — there is no other path indeed'; /

children.text: iti śruteranyavedī kathaṃ muktiṃ prayāsyati // MAnuv_1,1.196 //
children.translated_text: according to this <s>Śruti</s>, how will one who knows something else attain liberation? // 1.1.196 //

children.text: puruṣaḥ para ātmājo brahma nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Puruṣa</s>, the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, the self-born, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Lord, /

children.text: mahānānanda ud viṣṇurbharga oma itīryate // MAnuv_1,1.197 //
children.translated_text: the great bliss, the exalted, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Bharga</s>, <s>Om</s>' — thus it is proclaimed // 1.1.197 //
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the Lord Himself — these [attributes] belong to no one else; /
therefore, having uttered <s>Om</s>, they perform sacrifice, charity, and so forth // 1.1.198 //
'With the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> the knowers of the Self worship Him' — /
thus the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s> [declares]; therefore one is not liberated through knowledge of another // 1.1.199 //
In that which is denoted by the word '<s>Brahman</s>', employing also the word '<s>Ātman</s>', /
He taught creation from that, beginning with space, in a fourfold manner // 1.1.200 //
The element, the presiding deity of the element, its body, and the inner controller — /
<s>Hari</s> is denoted by the word 'space'; and primarily it is <s>Hari</s> alone // 1.1.201 //

children.text: ā samantāt kāśate yadākāśo mukhyato hariḥ /
children.translated_text: Because He shines (<s>kāśate</s>) everywhere (<s>ā samantāt</s>), '<s>ākāśa</s>' primarily means <s>Hari</s>; /
because of having the nature of power and knowledge, <s>vāyu</s> (wind) and <s>agni</s> (fire) carry [things] forward // 1.1.202 //
<s>Āpas</s> (waters) — because of pervading (<s>āpālanāt</s>); and <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth) — because it is spread out; /
because of being the substratum of plants, He Himself has the name '<s>oṣadhi</s>' // 1.1.203 //
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, stationed in the plants, is resorted to by the hungry; /

children.text: puri śete yataḥ so 'tha puruṣaśceti gīyate // MAnuv_1,1.204 //
children.translated_text: because He sleeps in the city [of the body], He is therefore sung as '<s>puruṣa</s>' // 1.1.204 //
The birth of <s>Hari</s> is His manifestation (<s>prādurbhāva</s>) through being the instigator of action; /
in space and so forth, there is no other presiding deity besides the presiding deity [<s>Hari</s>] // 1.1.205 //
The arising of the body of the presiding deity and of the direct element [is from <s>Hari</s>]; /
thus, having arrived at the body and so forth, it is <s>Hari</s> alone // 1.1.206 //
The <s>Śruti</s> 'That very one, this one' (<s>sa vā eṣa</s>) touches upon [<s>Hari</s>] for the purpose of knowing His fivefold form, /

children.text: tyaktavā bhūtādikaṃ sarvaṃ sa vā eṣa iti śrutiḥ // MAnuv_1,1.207 //
children.translated_text: having set aside everything beginning with the elements // 1.1.207 //
'<s>Sa</s>' (he) refers to the one denoted by the word '<s>Ātman</s>'; '<s>eṣa</s>' (this) refers to the one who has entered the body of the <s>jīva</s>; /

children.text: sārānnamaya evāyaṃ na lokānnamayaḥ prabhuḥ // MAnuv_1,1.208 //
children.translated_text: this one who is the essence is the <s>annamaya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>]; the Lord is not the worldly <s>annamaya</s> // 1.1.208 //
Thus He distinguishes the one who has entered the body by the word '<s>rasa</s>' (essence); /
the demonstrative 'this' (<s>idam</s>) [is used] for the all-pervading Lord as if covered by a garment // 1.1.209 //
The head and so forth would be of the <s>jīva</s>, since the <s>jīva</s>'s head and so forth are established [in that context]; /

children.text: taṃ viditvāsya muktiḥ syānnānyajñānāt kathañcana // MAnuv_1,1.210 //
children.translated_text: by knowing Him, liberation is attained — never through knowledge of anything else // 1.1.210 //
'In the sun and in the person, this one' — from this teaching of difference, /
there is no identity of His with the <s>jīva</s>; nor is inference one that operates at will // 1.1.211 //
'The various bodies are the abodes of my enjoyment' — /
the [<s>Śruti</s> beginning with] 'bodies' and so forth is required in the knowledge of reality // 1.1.212 //
Because of contradiction with perception and so forth, inference devoid of scriptural and sensory support, /

children.text: anumā kāmavṛttā hi kutra nāvasaraṃ vrajet // MAnuv_1,1.213 //
children.translated_text: being of arbitrary operation, where would it not find scope? // 1.1.213 //
'The insentient one is the self' — because of being a real thing, and because of being an object of valid knowledge, the insentient is consciousness; /

children.text: ghana ākāśa ityādyā vāryante kena hetunā // MAnuv_1,1.214 //
children.translated_text: 'solid is space' — by what reasoning are such [absurd statements] prevented? // 1.1.214 //
There should be no suspicion of redundancy in the <s>sūtras</s> [teaching] difference from the <s>jīva</s>; /
because of illuminating other statements, separately — herein lies completeness. /
That which, through [the teaching of] '<s>annamaya</s>' and so forth, praises the fruit as belonging to Him — /
to say that these are sheaths (<s>kośas</s>) even in both positions is sheer audacity // 1.1.215 //
And as for the approach (<s>upasaṅkramaṇa</s>) toward what is taught in the second [section], /
the prefix '<s>upa</s>-' would prevent one who speaks of transgression (<s>atikrama</s>) // 1.1.216 //
How could one grant a place to an unheard, excessive word?
For those devoid of shame who imagine the abandonment of both what is heard and unheard — // MAnuv_1,1.217 //
The abandonment of the food-sheath (<s>annamaya</s>) was made only in the context of the deceased.
Those who [say] 'food is <s>Brahman</s>' and the like — through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of meditations — // MAnuv_1,1.218 //
having declared the five forms [of <s>Brahman</s>], the Vedic speech that again teaches their attainment,
situated in two places — for those who deny that — // MAnuv_1,1.219 //
how could it tolerate their being established in a place other than darkness?
'Teach me, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, <s>Brahman</s>' — thus addressed, beginning with food and <s>Prāṇa</s>, // MAnuv_1,1.220 //

children.text: āha brahma kathaṃ tanna dvāraṃ taditi vādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: he taught <s>Brahman</s>. How is that not a doorway to it? — say those [opponents].

children.text: upasattiṃ kathaṃ vidyurupasannāya hi triśaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.221 //
children.translated_text: How [would one know] the approach, since for one who has approached, thrice // MAnuv_1,1.221 //
<s>Brahman</s> must be declared by the teacher, four times or even

children.text: sakṛd vetyāgamā brūyuḥ sampradāyavido 'pi ca // MAnuv_1,1.222 //
children.translated_text: once — so the scriptures (<s>āgamas</s>) would say, and also those who know the tradition (<s>sampradāya</s>). // MAnuv_1,1.222 //
How could the Lord of Directions speak to one who has approached that it is something trifling?

children.text: na vaded brahma ca kathaṃ māyāvī na hi vārirāṭ // MAnuv_1,1.223 //
children.translated_text: And how could he not declare <s>Brahman</s>? For the Lord of Waters is not a deceiver. // MAnuv_1,1.223 //
'It sees' — hence it is called the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>); because of hearing, it is called the ear.
Because of speech, it is <s>Vāk</s> (Speech) — <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of creation, sustenance, and the rest. // MAnuv_1,1.224 //
And that [<s>Brahman</s>] is declared as eightfold in the <s>Vāghūla</s> branch (<s>śākhā</s>),
together with consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) and bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), distinguished by characteristics of creation and the like. // MAnuv_1,1.225 //

children.text: āvāpodvāpataṣa śākhā yata āhuḥ paraṃ padam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Āvāpodvāpa</s> branch — whence they declare the supreme abode,

children.text: yato bhūtāni jāyanta ityādyairlakṣaṇaiḥ svayam // MAnuv_1,1.226 //
children.translated_text: 'That from which beings are born' — and so forth, by such characteristics themselves — // MAnuv_1,1.226 //
it was indicated by the teacher; afterwards, through <s>tapas</s> (austerity) alone, directly perceived.
Seeing each form individually is a demonstration following the total statement. // MAnuv_1,1.227 //
By one desiring [to know], having received the teacher's command, it was directly perceived through <s>tapas</s> alone.
For those who say 'it is not <s>Brahman</s>' — [they incur] the loss of what is heard and the grasping of what is not heard. // MAnuv_1,1.228 //
When [food etc.] have attained the status of being direct indicators — shame [should be felt] at those utterances.
Since proximity of enjoyment together [with <s>Brahman</s>] is repeatedly stated as liberation, // MAnuv_1,1.229 //
'The difference between the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord) is false' — this [view] would itself be false.
By this, the <s>mayaṭ</s> [suffix] too, because of the imagining of meaning through duality —

children.text: tadanyeṣāṃ matamapi satsaṃsatsu na bhāsate // MAnuv_1,1.230 //
children.translated_text: the view of others too does not shine forth among the truly learned. // MAnuv_1,1.230 //
Therefore, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Lord, through words denoting all qualities without exception,
and also through general words for the possessor of qualities, is primarily spoken of. // MAnuv_1,1.231 //
And by words relating to the inner self (<s>adhyātma</s>) such as <s>Prāṇa</s> and the like, and likewise by those relating to the external elements (<s>adhibhūta</s>),
by words such as 'food' (<s>anna</s>) and the rest, the <s>Bhagavān</s> alone is primarily spoken of. // MAnuv_1,1.232 //
By the <s>sūtra</s> 'That from which the birth [etc.] of this [world]' — for establishing the full complement of qualities

children.text: brahmaṇo lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ śāstramūlaṃ yatastataḥ // MAnuv_1,1.233 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Brahman</s>, the defining characteristic was stated; since scripture is the basis, therefore — // MAnuv_1,1.233 //
the connection (<s>anvaya</s>) of all words leads to the knowledge of the full complement of qualities,
because of the primary connection in Him of the grounds for the application of words. // MAnuv_1,1.234 //
Because of the paucity [of qualities] in other referents, and because of His being the cause of that,
the denotative capacity of words [belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>] — through the abundance and excessive usage — // MAnuv_1,1.235 //

children.text: rūḍhamityeva sādhyaṃ syād rūḍhirhi dvividhā matā /
children.translated_text: it should be established as <s>rūḍhi</s> (conventional usage). For <s>rūḍhi</s> is considered to be twofold:

children.text: avidvadvidvadāptyaiva mukhyā hi viduṣāṃ tu sā // MAnuv_1,1.236 //
children.translated_text: that [attained] by the learned and the unlearned — and the primary one is that of the learned. // MAnuv_1,1.236 //
The <s>rūḍhi</s> of the learned would be Vedic; that is obtained through <s>yoga</s> alone.

children.text: tasmānmukhyārthatā viṣṇoriti kṛtvā hṛdi prabhuḥ // MAnuv_1,1.237 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having established the primary denotation in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord [in the sūtras] // MAnuv_1,1.237 //
establishes the connection (<s>samanvaya</s>); [then], suspecting the capacity of [other] <s>devas</s> there,

children.text: āśaṅkaya tatra rūḍhiṃ ca tacchabdānāmapi svayam // MAnuv_1,1.238 //
children.translated_text: and also the conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) of those words in them, He Himself — // MAnuv_1,1.238 //
through attributes such as 'being situated at the end of the ocean' and the like, having established that <s>Viṣṇu</s> has conventional designation (<s>rūḍhatā</s>)
through those [attributes], He then again set aside [the other designations]. // MAnuv_1,1.239 //

children.text: ceṣṭā hi cetanānāṃ yā sā bhavet tatprasādataḥ /
children.translated_text: For the activity that belongs to conscious beings — that would be through His grace.
But how could the aperture (<s>vivara</s>) and so forth, which are of an insentient nature, [come] from that? // MAnuv_1,1.240 //
For the purpose of removing such doubt, the name '<s>Ākāśa</s>' (space) too
— [the entity] superior even to others — is of <s>Hari</s>, because of the prior indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // MAnuv_1,1.241 //
For the purpose of removing such doubt, the name '<s>Ākāśa</s>' (space) too
— [the entity] superior even to others — is of <s>Hari</s>, because of the prior indicatory mark. // MAnuv_1,1.242 //
Since the causal relation to <s>Prāṇa</s> and the like is perceived, such an extension (<s>atideśa</s>) [is warranted].

children.text: liṅgaṃ balavadeva syāt prerako 'syāpi yaddhariḥ // MAnuv_1,1.243 //
children.translated_text: The indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) would be powerful indeed, since <s>Hari</s> is the impeller even of this. // MAnuv_1,1.243 //
Because of the very eternality of speech, how can that [speech] be of the nature of <s>Hari</s>?
How can the well-known, abundantly used words be non-denotative [of their ordinary referents]? // MAnuv_1,1.244 //
If so, [the reply is:] that is of <s>Hari</s> alone, because of the abundance in both <s>śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s>,
and because of the nature of that power [of denotation]; in the abundance of both <s>śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s> — // MAnuv_1,1.245 //
'The primary denotation belongs to another' — this [view] is not [tenable] for one who belongs to that [Vedic tradition].

children.text: viṣṇoreva tu liṅgāni prāṇasthāni tu sarvaśaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.246 //
children.translated_text: For the indicatory marks pointing to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone are present in <s>Prāṇa</s> everywhere. // MAnuv_1,1.246 //
Preceded by the concord with <s>Prāṇa</s>, primarily [the words] refer to the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) too;
'worship for a hundred years' and 'being of the lineage of <s>Prāṇa</s>' — this too [is indicated]. // MAnuv_1,1.247 //
Therefore, by words going to other [referents], through the principles stated, in every way,

children.text: eko nārāyaṇo devo bhaṇyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // MAnuv_1,1.248 //
children.translated_text: the one Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is spoken of — there is no doubt in this. // MAnuv_1,1.248 //
In the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the rest, He has four forms in every way;

children.text: athavā pañcamūrtiḥ sa prokto 'dhikaraṇaṃ prati // MAnuv_1,1.249 //
children.translated_text: or He is declared as having five forms, with respect to each <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic). // MAnuv_1,1.249 //
For each <s>sūtra</s>, for each word, or even for each syllable,
the suitability [is established] through the particular methods of reasoning and scriptural inference. // MAnuv_1,1.250 //
By the authority of the great scripture (<s>Bṛhattantra</s>), even though containing many meanings, because of the concise summary,
this is stated for the purpose of enabling even ordinary human intellects to grasp something. // MAnuv_1,1.251 //
This work too is of manifold meaning, and the commentary is of excessively vast import.
Only the greatly learned know the meaning of the qualifications of these two.
Therefore <s>Viṣṇu</s> is of supreme qualities, because of the repetition in the scriptures (<s>nāmnāya</s>). // MAnuv_1,1.252 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: The function of words that are of the nature of indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) [is directed] toward the Supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: cintyate sarvagatvaṃ tu prathamaṃ pravicāryate // MAnuv_1,2.1 //
children.translated_text: Omnipresence (<s>sarvagatva</s>) is considered first; it is investigated foremost. // MAnuv_1,2.1 //
Situated in each and every [place], <s>Viṣṇu</s> awakens the powers particular to each.

children.text: dūrato 'pyatiriktaḥ sa līlayā kevalaṃ prabhuḥ // MAnuv_1,2.2 //
children.translated_text: He, even from afar, is transcendent — the Lord, merely through [His] play (<s>līlā</s>). // MAnuv_1,2.2 //
To make this known: as a general rule, there is difference between <s>karma</s> (object) and <s>kartṛ</s> (agent);

children.text: abhedo 'pi viśeṣe syād balī so 'pyanapoditaḥ // MAnuv_1,2.3 //
children.translated_text: even non-difference may exist in particular cases — and that [non-difference] too is strong and unrefuted. // MAnuv_1,2.3 //

children.text: etad bhāvābhidhaṃ liṅgaṃ kriyāliṅge tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: This is an indicatory mark denoting being (<s>bhāva</s>); next, beyond that, the action-indicatory mark —
'The Inner Controller' (<s>Antaryāmin</s>), 'the Inner' — is called the indicatory mark of action-being. // MAnuv_1,2.4 //
The indicatory mark denoting [non-]being — such as invisibility and the like — <s>śruti</s> is superior to <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: anityatvāt kriyāṇāṃ tu kathameva svarūpatā // MAnuv_1,2.5 //
children.translated_text: Because of the impermanence of actions, how indeed [could they constitute] the essential nature? // MAnuv_1,2.5 //

children.text: iti cet sa viśeṣo 'pi kriyāśaktayātmanā sthiraḥ /
children.translated_text: If so, [the reply is:] that distinction too is stable through the nature of the power of action;

children.text: śaktitā vyaktatā ceti viśeṣo 'pi viśeṣavān // MAnuv_1,2.6 //
children.translated_text: the nature of power and manifestation — even the distinction is itself distinguished. // MAnuv_1,2.6 //

children.text: abhinno 'pi kriyādiśca svabhāva iti hi śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though non-different, action and the like are 'own-nature' (<s>svabhāva</s>) — thus indeed [says] <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: jñānaṃ nityaṃ kriyā nityā balaṃ śaktiḥ parātmanaḥ // MAnuv_1,2.7 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge is eternal, action is eternal, power and strength belong to the Supreme Self. // MAnuv_1,2.7 //
Thus the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s> also says: only the existence of power
is to be known as the eternality of action and the rest; elsewhere [there is] impermanence. // MAnuv_1,2.8 //
Thus the statement of the true reality — and duality of one [entity] is proper,
'He who is the bridge' — by the statement of unity, [it is] a qualification. // MAnuv_1,2.9 //
Standing within, He who delights — He is called 'the Inner' (<s>antara</s>).
And 'delight' (<s>ramaṇa</s>) should be taken as [denoted by] the word '<s>ātman</s>' (self) — and He is said to measure (<s>mā</s>). // MAnuv_1,2.10 //
Because of possessing distinguished bliss, <s>Brahmanhood</s> is also distinction.
Mutual regulation and the regulation of the Lord — it would not be otherwise. // MAnuv_1,2.11 //
The distinction that belongs to conscious beings — even [their] own-nature is given by the Lord.
Therefore, in the mutual regulation, infinite regress and impossibility [do not arise]. // MAnuv_1,2.12 //
If the Lord is also the regulator, He Himself has come first.
Why is [this] objected to? Why the vain imagining of an [infinite] series?

children.text: doṣavatyeva tasmāt sā naiva kāryā kathañcana // MAnuv_1,2.13 //
children.translated_text: That [objection] is therefore faulty indeed — it should not be made in any way. // MAnuv_1,2.13 //
'Delight belongs to one who has not exerted' — [it arises] merely from distraction.

children.text: iti cet sarvaniyamo yasya kasmānna śakyate // MAnuv_1,2.14 //
children.translated_text: If so, why can He whose regulation is of everything not [be the cause]? // MAnuv_1,2.14 //
An entity not regulated by the self would be opposed to the self.
How can that which has its existence, power, and the rest dependent on Him be opposed to the self? // MAnuv_1,2.15 //
If qualities, actions, and the like were non-different [from <s>Brahman</s>],
how would the non-difference of [things having] the property of non-existence with <s>Brahman</s> be proper? // MAnuv_1,2.16 //

children.text: nābhāvo bhāva iti ca viśeṣaḥ prāyaśo bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'Non-existence is not existence' — this distinction mostly obtains.

children.text: atadbhāvo 'nyatā ceti na viśeṣo 'sti kaścana // MAnuv_1,2.17 //
children.translated_text: 'Not being that' and 'being other' — there is no distinction [between these]. // MAnuv_1,2.17 //
The absence of faults is a quality — this is well-known even among worldly [people].
Therefore, qualities such as invisibility and the like, the Lord Himself declares. // MAnuv_1,2.18 //
The opposition between existence and non-existence, however, does not exist everywhere.

children.text: tadabhāvo hi tadbhāvavirodhī na tato 'paraḥ // MAnuv_1,2.19 //
children.translated_text: For the absence of that [particular thing] is opposed to the existence of that [particular thing], not to anything else. // MAnuv_1,2.19 //
If they imagine three kinds of difference — separateness, absence-of-that-form, and otherness —
the faults of excessive conceptual elaboration and the like are opposed to that [view]. // MAnuv_1,2.20 //
But the differences of separateness and otherness are constantly
used synonymously by worldly people and also by Vedic [scholars] in every way. // MAnuv_1,2.21 //
'The loss of what is seen [through] the imagining of what is unseen' — this is the very defect.

children.text: yadā tadadhiko doṣo vidyate ko nu vādinām // MAnuv_1,2.22 //
children.translated_text: When such a greater defect exists, what [hope] for the proponents? // MAnuv_1,2.22 //
The distinctions (<s>viśeṣas</s>) — which are of the nature of existence and non-existence — belong to the entity itself.
They should be accepted as non-different, for the sake of establishing [correct] usage. // MAnuv_1,2.23 //
Just as one [relation of] inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) and both difference and non-difference in an entity
must be accepted with distinction by those who engage in transactions, in [their respective] domains — // MAnuv_1,2.24 //
even for the proponent of the partless (<s>akhaṇḍavādin</s>), the distinction would exist even unwished for.

children.text: vyāvṛtte nirviśeṣe tu kiṃ vyāvartyabahutvataḥ // MAnuv_1,2.25 //
children.translated_text: But when the distinction-less is excluded, what, because of the multiplicity of what is to be excluded? // MAnuv_1,2.25 //
Through many well-known conventional names, equipped with many indicatory marks,
[and] well-known through going to other [referents] — <s>Janārdana</s> is to be directly spoken of. // MAnuv_1,2.26 //
Words such as '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' and the rest also denote Him; therefore,

children.text: tāni liṅgāni te śabdā api tadgā hi sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: those indicatory marks and those words too go to Him in every way.
Even the abundant conventional usage of the ignorant does not obstruct the conventional usage of the wise. // MAnuv_1,2.27 //

body.text: || iti śrīmadānandatīrthabhagavatpādaviracite śrīmadbrahmasūtrānuvyākhyāne prathamādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: For the indicatory marks and names established there and elsewhere, <s>Hari</s> again
[declares] the particularly primary function in Himself alone — here, the sacrificer is [He who] speaks. // MAnuv_1,3.1 //
Because the word '<s>ātman</s>' (self) has conventional fixation (<s>rūḍhatva</s>) in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, <s>śruti</s> does not speak of <s>Śiva</s> and the rest;
because of being the Lord of all, <s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite) is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the one surpassing in bliss. // MAnuv_1,3.2 //
Therefore, even what appears contradictory, having explained it in its true sense,
the statement endowed with contradictory characteristics should be construed as [referring to] <s>Hari</s>. // MAnuv_1,3.3 //
<s>Brahman</s> alone [possesses] those indicatory marks; though they do not exist in others,
without contradiction, in <s>Govinda</s> there exist 'not gross' (<s>asthūla</s>) and the like. // MAnuv_1,3.4 //
The negation of grossness and the like, which are the nature of other entities,
[is made] by <s>śruti</s> with respect to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — but not [declaring] that He lacks own-nature. // MAnuv_1,3.5 //
'All <s>dharmas</s>, all names, all <s>karmas</s>' — qualities are declared;

children.text: doṣāḥ śrutāśca netyādyā pramāṇaṃ śrutiratra ca // MAnuv_1,3.6 //
children.translated_text: faults are declared [to be absent by] 'not' and the like — <s>śruti</s> is the authority here. // MAnuv_1,3.6 //
The general indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), the words, the place, the indicatory mark, grace,

children.text: punaḥ śabdā liṅgaśabdau vicāryā dvisthitā iha // MAnuv_1,3.7 //
children.translated_text: again the words, the indicatory mark and words — [these are] to be examined, established in two [ways], here. // MAnuv_1,3.7 //
Multiplicity, [mere] words of indication, non-statement, and contradiction; /
non-vision, absence of connection, and the error of contradictory <s>śruti</s>; // MAnuv_1,3.8 //
the error of absence of scope for indication — such a pair, likewise; /
contradiction with the multiplicity of such [statements] with what you have stated — from this, such is the conclusion. /
All of this — herein these are the reasonings in the prima facie positions. // MAnuv_1,3.9 //
Those very [reasonings], however, when powerful and devoid of alternative conclusions, /

children.text: siddhāntayuktayo jñeyā dṛśyante tāśca sarvaśaḥ // MAnuv_1,3.10 //
children.translated_text: should be known as the reasonings of the established doctrine — and they are seen everywhere. // MAnuv_1,3.10 //
