The approachability of the liberated to <s>Prāṇa</s> (the Supreme), the superiority [of <s>Brahman</s>] in all respects, /
the distinctness of its own-nature, and action preceded by deliberation, likewise; // MAnuv_1,3.11 //
the lordship of the syllable 'a' and the syllable 'ṇa,' the imitation of <s>Sūrya</s> and others, likewise; /
the name <s>Vāmana</s>, the trembling of all [beings], the non-establishment of those words in anything else; // MAnuv_1,3.12 //
the namelessness of the distinction, the authoritativeness of what is relied upon — /
all lordship and so forth — these have been demonstrated by the lord of the <s>Vedas</s>. // MAnuv_1,3.13 //
Eligibility and its diminishment have been considered through implication alone; /

children.text: tatphalāya vidhiḥ siddhe copāsāyā nirākṛtaḥ // MAnuv_1,3.14 //
children.translated_text: the injunction is for the fruit of that; when [the main purpose] is established, <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation) has been refuted. // MAnuv_1,3.14 //
Because <s>Jaimini</s> [spoke of] a different purpose when the [primary] purpose is unestablished, an injunction [is needed]; /
the view of the Lord of Knowledge [<s>Vyāsa</s>] — there is no contradiction between the two, therefore. // MAnuv_1,3.15 //

children.text: mokṣe phalaviśeṣo 'sti na ca sarvaṃ prakāśate /
children.translated_text: In liberation, there is a distinction of fruit; and not everything is manifest. /

children.text: sarvadā tena devānāmapi yuktā hyupāsanā // MAnuv_1,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, worship is appropriate even for the <s>devas</s>. // MAnuv_1,3.16 //

children.text: nityaṃ vṛddhikṣayāpetaṃ viṣṇoḥ pūrṇaṃ tu vedanam /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is eternal, free from increase and decrease, full, /
clear and exceedingly clear, lucid, extending to all objects without remainder — [this is] <s>Brahman</s>'s [knowledge]. // MAnuv_1,3.17 //
The knowledge of others is gradual, always limited to a measured number of objects. /
These and other distinctions are eternally in the heart of the Lord of Knowledge. // MAnuv_1,3.18 //
<s>Jaimini</s> and others, being knowers of the general [only], spoke thus [about it]. /
Therefore, the view of the Lord of Knowledge is never contradicted by the wise. // MAnuv_1,3.19 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> (section) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha</s> [<s>Madhva</s>]. ||

children.translated_text: Words [denoting] the suffering, the bound, the inferior, and so forth apply to <s>Brahman</s> because of [beings'] dependence on it. /

children.text: śabdā brahmaṇi vartante rājñi yadvat parājayaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.1 //
children.translated_text: Words apply to <s>Brahman</s> just as 'defeat' [applies] to a king. // MAnuv_1,4.1 //
Independence and the words' pertaining to it — these are indeed the reason for the operation of words. /

children.text: svātantryaṃ tatra mukhyaṃ syāt kuto rājñi jayo 'nyathā // MAnuv_1,4.2 //
children.translated_text: Independence would be the primary [reason] therein — otherwise how would 'victory' [apply] to a king? // MAnuv_1,4.2 //
For the word 'victorious' is not at all applied to a servant /
so long as, even when [victory] pertains to another, [the king retains] the king's [status] — merely from the appearance of independence. // MAnuv_1,4.3 //
The bondage of the servant and so forth [being attributed] to the king, because of the king's fitness for bondage and so forth — /

children.text: kāraṇaṃ saṃśayasya syāditi naiva prayujyate // MAnuv_1,4.4 //
children.translated_text: would be a cause for doubt — thus it is simply not applied [in that way]. // MAnuv_1,4.4 //
Because of the inauspiciousness of the words, because of the king's connection with the inauspicious, /
because of the unpleasantness of the word — there would be the cessation of application. // MAnuv_1,4.5 //
But where such qualities exist that all [words] are applied even [without reservation], /
especially in the case of those worthy of worship — independence is the primary reason. // MAnuv_1,4.6 //
Therefore, because of extreme remoteness from defect, and because of the impossibility even of doubt /
regarding defects' pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, from the standpoint of the wise person's understanding — // MAnuv_1,4.7 //
intending the meaning of [his] independence, words of defect [are applied] to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. /
And the <s>Vāsudeva</s> <s>śruti</s> declares: there is no inauspiciousness in <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.8 //
Elsewhere there is [both] auspiciousness and inauspiciousness; therefore [one] should not say 'inauspicious' [of him]. /
From the standpoint of independence, a defect in <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not the utterance of inauspiciousness. // MAnuv_1,4.9 //

children.text: bahubhuktavaṃ yathā doṣo nṛṣu naiva harau kvacit /
children.translated_text: Just as 'having eaten much' is a defect in humans, never so in <s>Hari</s>. /
Thus words like 'suffering' and so forth are stated from the standpoint of independence. // MAnuv_1,4.10 //
Defects are never in <s>Hari</s>; those who understand them as pertaining to him are called defect-makers. /

children.text: tasmāt te doṣaśabdāśca tatraiva guṇavācakāḥ // MAnuv_1,4.11 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, those very words of defect are, in him, words denoting qualities. // MAnuv_1,4.11 //
Since light was born and woven in <s>Hari</s>, in the form of <s>Prāṇa</s> — [he is called] '<s>jyotiḥ</s>'; /
from 'he is to be worshipped' [comes] '<s>āyaja</s>'; and '<s>vasanti</s>' — from 'dwelling.' // MAnuv_1,4.12 //
Because of being devoid of covering — 'go' (<s>gaccha</s>); the destroyer of decaying beings; /

children.text: bhuṅkṣetyukto harir huṃ ca hutamasmin jagad yataḥ // MAnuv_1,4.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> is called 'eat' (<s>bhuṅkṣe</s>); and '<s>huṃ</s>' — because the world is offered (<s>huta</s>) in him. // MAnuv_1,4.13 //
Because of openness, he is called '<s>phaṭ</s>'; from 'one who protects what is desired' — /
because armor exists [in him]; because of always having the six qualities — /
'<s>vaṣaṭ</s>'; from [all things] going to him — '<s>vauṣaṭ</s>' is indeed declared. // MAnuv_1,4.14 //
Because he makes his own his own — <s>Janārdana</s> is called '<s>svāhā</s>.' /

children.text: namantyasmin guṇā yasyānnama ityeva kathyate // MAnuv_1,4.15 //
children.translated_text: Because qualities bow down in him — '<s>namaḥ</s>' is thus declared. // MAnuv_1,4.15 //
Thus, by words, names, and terms of all actions, <s>Janārdana</s> alone /
is primarily denoted — by syllables, letters, vowels, and so forth. // MAnuv_1,4.16 //
Therefore, his possession of infinite qualities [is established] from the purport of <s>śruti</s>. /
Since all words are for the purpose of knowledge [of him], there is no defect. // MAnuv_1,4.17 //
Even when accepted, there is no defect in the syntactic connection of sentences, /
because of the possibility of <s>karma</s> and so forth having that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] as their purpose — for one of limited understanding. // MAnuv_1,4.18 //
'Who [is] the union of the <s>chandas</s> (meters)?' — from this <s>śruti</s>, the knower of the reality of the meaning of union [knows that] /

children.text: brahmaiko naiva cānyo 'sti ka ityasyarobhayārthataḥ // MAnuv_1,4.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is one alone, and there is no other — '<s>ka</s>' (<s>ka</s> = who) — from the double meaning of this [word]. // MAnuv_1,4.19 //
From the certainty that even of that [<s>Brahman</s>] which is previously established, [the means] is knowledge alone, /
the eternal connection (<s>yoga</s>) of words with their meanings is also not prohibited. /
And feminine-gender words, all having the sense of negation, are also denotative of <s>Brahman</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.20 //
Contradiction, multiplicity of all, causality, femininity, negation — /
the topics for separate syntactic connection — these are everywhere. // MAnuv_1,4.21 //
Contradiction with all means of knowledge, and the impossibility of even etymological derivation, /
mutual contradiction, and the contradiction between an effect and what possesses it, /
femininity of gender, and negation — these are the reasons in the prima facie positions. // MAnuv_1,4.22 //
The rule of non-contact with defects, the multiplicity of word-meanings, likewise /
the many-formedness of the Lord, the specification of manifest and unmanifest [forms], // MAnuv_1,4.23 //
creation from his own body, and likewise the hiddenness [of the Lord] from the wicked — /

children.text: itayādyā yuktayaḥ sākṣāt siddhāntasthāpakā iha // MAnuv_1,4.24 //
children.translated_text: these and other reasonings directly establish the doctrine herein. // MAnuv_1,4.24 //
The connection of all words cannot be easily known — /
this aversion of the people is what the view of <s>Jaimini</s> and others states. // MAnuv_1,4.25 //
The Lord of Knowledge, the self-sovereign <s>Bhagavān</s>, set forth /
his own doctrine in partial [form] for the establishment [of understanding] among his own disciples. // MAnuv_1,4.26 //
What was understood by them, he stated here, speaking of the gradation among men, /

children.text: teṣu teṣu padārtheṣu rūḍhiraṅgīkṛtā yataḥ // MAnuv_1,4.27 //
children.translated_text: since conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) has been accepted regarding those various objects. // MAnuv_1,4.27 //
Because of the multiplicity of purposes, because of the non-contradiction of each one, /
from the capacity of instruction and so forth — the power is grasped in <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.28 //
Nevertheless, when there is contradiction with this, the denotation of that [other meaning] is removed. /

children.text: avirodhe tu bahvarthā etanmūlatayā matāḥ // MAnuv_1,4.29 //
children.translated_text: When there is no contradiction, the multiple meanings are considered to be rooted in this [<s>Viṣṇu</s>-reference]. // MAnuv_1,4.29 //
For from this [source] the conventional usage of others has its dependence — herein indeed. /

children.text: tatsiddhistadapekṣā ca sāpekṣā ca harīcchayā // MAnuv_1,4.30 //
children.translated_text: The establishment of that [conventional usage] depends on that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], and that dependence is by <s>Hari</s>'s will. // MAnuv_1,4.30 //
Therefore, the supremely primary [denotation] is in <s>Viṣṇu</s>; in other [referents], there is [merely] primary [denotation]. /

children.text: upalakṣaṇā ca gauṇī ca tisraḥ śabdasya vṛttayaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Upalakṣaṇā</s> (indication) and <s>gauṇī</s> (secondary/figurative) — [these with primary] are the three functions of a word. // MAnuv_1,4.31 //
The multiplicity of the cause of application — that should be known as supreme primary [denotation]. /

children.text: tatra prayogabāhulyaṃ yadi tatparatā kimu // MAnuv_1,4.32 //
children.translated_text: Therein, if there is multiplicity of usage, what more [need be said] about [its] primacy? // MAnuv_1,4.32 //
Both are seen in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of all words everywhere. /
Mere multiplicity of usage is called conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.33 //
Similarity with applied usage, or even a connection — from non-primary [denotation] — /
should be known as the cause of [secondary] function; in the absence of the former, the latter is grasped. // MAnuv_1,4.34 //
Him, being thus, by names such as '<s>Śatarcī</s>' and so forth, /
they declared — for herein, 'being' is the determination [of his existence]. // MAnuv_1,4.35 //

children.text: yogasya rūḍheḥ prābalyaṃ vidvadrūḍhiṃ ca tatragām /
children.translated_text: The superiority of <s>yoga</s> (etymological derivation) over <s>rūḍhi</s> (conventional usage), and the conventional usage of the learned going to that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] — /
he shows directly in many ways, with etymology, through the purport [of scripture]. // MAnuv_1,4.36 //

children.text: a iti brahma kathitaṃ tadvayākhyānānmatā tathā /
children.translated_text: The syllable '<s>a</s>' is declared to be <s>Brahman</s>; from the commentary on that, the view is likewise established. /
And of all words as well — one who knows the names has accomplished what is to be done. // MAnuv_1,4.37 //
The nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s name as meaning and form — then he stated [regarding] <s>saṃhitā</s> and so forth, /

children.text: ṇakāraṃ ca ṣakāraṃ ca balaceṣṭātmakaṃ vadan // MAnuv_1,4.38 //
children.translated_text: declaring the syllable '<s>ṇa</s>' and the syllable '<s>ṣa</s>' as having the nature of strength and activity. // MAnuv_1,4.38 //
Because of being preceded by the knowledge of that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], the recitation of <s>saṃhitā</s> is likewise [for that purpose]. /
From having the nature of a prefix, or from the meaning of habitual disposition — '<s>una</s>' likewise. // MAnuv_1,4.39 //
The syllable '<s>ṇa</s>' and the syllable '<s>ṣa</s>' are considered to have the nature of name and form. /
Therefore, the syntactic connection of vowels, consonants, and words is in <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.40 //
How much more so of the <s>Veda</s> — and further, the connection in the form of sentences; /

children.text: ghoṣāḥ sarve 'pi vedāśca sarve vedāśca yat padam // MAnuv_1,4.41 //
children.translated_text: all sounds and all <s>Vedas</s> — and [he is] that <s>pada</s> (supreme abode); // MAnuv_1,4.41 //

children.text: indraṃ mitraṃ yamindraṃ ca prathamaḥ saṅkṛtistathā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Indra</s>' — and the first creation (<s>saṅkṛti</s>), likewise; /
'the name-giver of all <s>devas</s> is one' — and such <s>śruti</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.42 //
This is the authority regarding the matter already stated — that very thing is stated from the beginning. /
Thus, by the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, declaring the complete connection [of all words with <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. // MAnuv_1,4.43 //
It is not the denotability by words of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) that is prohibited here — /
because of the inclusion [of references to it] in all the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Itihāsas</s>, and <s>Purāṇas</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.44 //
<s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) are born of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). /
They bind, O mighty-armed one, the imperishable embodied one in the body. // MAnuv_1,4.45 //
— and in such statements, where no other meaning is desired; /
or even if the material cause is held to be of the nature of fire, water, and food — // MAnuv_1,4.46 //
since it is beginningless, what offense is there when <s>pradhāna</s> is asserted? /
When the <s>śruti</s> states 'the one unborn female' (<s>ajāmekām</s>) — when that is the case, /

children.text: ko doṣaḥ sarvathaivāsti pariṇāmi jaḍaṃ yadi // MAnuv_1,4.47 //
children.translated_text: what fault is there? In every way, if the insentient undergoes transformation, [the objection holds]. // MAnuv_1,4.47 //
For us, the supremely primary meaning is the <s>Bhagavān</s> alone. /
By mere primary [denotation], everything that is conventional is accepted. // MAnuv_1,4.48 //
Of all words, the secondary meaning and so forth — because of non-fitness for that [supreme referent]; /
<s>Hari</s> spoke [each word] intending a twofold meaning, when [the word] operates [in context]. // MAnuv_1,4.49 //
The cause of effects first, the supreme object of words, /

children.text: yogānāṃ paramāṃ siddhiṃ paramaṃ te padaṃ viduḥ // MAnuv_1,4.50 //
children.translated_text: the highest attainment of <s>yogas</s> — the wise know that as the supreme abode. // MAnuv_1,4.50 //
Thus, from the ascent [of meaning] in the intellect, of both <s>yoga</s> (etymological) and <s>rūḍhi</s> (conventional), /
and because of the absence of a reason for rejection — a twofold meaning is accepted. // MAnuv_1,4.51 //
In the absence of a contrary cognition, the prior ascent [of meaning] is the reason. /

children.text: sā bhaved yatra sa vyarthaḥ pūrvāroho bhramo yathā /
children.translated_text: Where that [contrary cognition] would exist, the prior ascent is pointless, like an error. /

children.text: ato jagadupādānaṃ pradhānaṃ vakti sā śrutiḥ // MAnuv_1,4.52 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, that <s>śruti</s> speaks of <s>pradhāna</s> as the material cause of the world. // MAnuv_1,4.52 //
That which is the unmanifest, possessing the three <s>guṇas</s>, eternal, of the nature of being and non-being — /
they call it <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s> — undifferentiated yet possessing differentiations. // MAnuv_1,4.53 //
By five, by five, <s>Brahman</s> [is known]; by four, by ten, likewise. /
This group of twenty-four — they know as pertaining to <s>Pradhāna</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.54 //

children.text: iti bhāgavate prāha vidyādhīśaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Bhāgavata</s> [Purāṇa], the Lord of Knowledge, the self-sovereign Lord, declared. /
And by the word '<s>Prakṛti</s>,' <s>Brahman</s> is not said to be the material cause. // MAnuv_1,4.55 //

children.text: avikāraḥ sadā śuddho nitya ātmā sadā hariḥ /
children.translated_text: Without modification, eternally pure, eternal — the Self is always <s>Hari</s>. /
Always of one form, of the nature of consciousness and strength, of the form of bliss. // MAnuv_1,4.56 //
Without modification, imperishable, pure, free from affliction, unaging, undying. /

children.text: aviśvo viśvakartājo yaḥ paraḥ so 'bhidhīyate // MAnuv_1,4.57 //
children.translated_text: Not-all [yet] the maker of all, unborn — he who is supreme, he is declared [to be <s>Brahman</s>]. // MAnuv_1,4.57 //
Without modification, incomparable, always of one flavor, imperishable — /

children.text: brahmeti paramātmeti yaṃ vidurvaidikā janāḥ // MAnuv_1,4.58 //
children.translated_text: those who know the <s>Vedas</s> know him as <s>Brahman</s>, as <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self). // MAnuv_1,4.58 //
Thus, according to <s>śruti</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> is not subject to modification. /
the attainment of distinction dependent on another, and the irreversible state of being otherwise. // MAnuv_1,4.59 //

children.text: kṣīrādivad vikāraḥ syānnaiva sa syāddhareḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: There would be transformation like milk and such — but that can never occur in <s>Hari</s> at all. /
If the material cause nature (<s>upādānatā</s>) of Him is accepted, it is only as efficient cause (<s>apādāna</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.60 //
That is accepted — like a father, but not that He becomes the universe in His own form. /
Nor is there transformation in the case of the spider (<s>ūrṇanābhi</s>), the generator, or mothers. // MAnuv_1,4.61 //
Because of being conscious, that food indeed would exist in the form of an effect; /
as efficient cause (<s>apādāna</s>), the creatorship of the universe is preceded by intelligence. // MAnuv_1,4.62 //
This has been stated in the <s>Bhāllaviśākhā</s> and in the <s>Brahmatarka</s>, with reverence: /
the creation of the Lord is by mere will alone, He being always without transformation. // MAnuv_1,4.63 //
This is the nature of the Infinite One — the <s>rajas</s> by which the world came into being. /
<s>Janārdana</s>, by His own will regarding His body and so forth, having previously enjoyed the universe, // MAnuv_1,4.64 //
created it, like a father and mother, or indeed like a spider (<s>ūrṇanābhi</s>). /

children.text: pradhānaṃ pariṇāmyeśo nirvikāraḥ svayaṃ sadā // MAnuv_1,4.65 //
children.translated_text: The Lord transforms <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter), while He Himself always remains without transformation. // MAnuv_1,4.65 //

children.text: na cetanavikāraḥ syād yatra kvāpi hyacetanam /
children.translated_text: A transformation of the conscious cannot anywhere become unconscious, /
nor can a transformation of the unconscious ever become conscious. // MAnuv_1,4.66 //
And the nature of one thing becoming another is not seen even in transformation. /

children.text: na kṣīrādanyatā dadhnaḥ kenacid dṛśyate kvacit // MAnuv_1,4.67 //
children.translated_text: The otherness of curd from milk is not seen by anyone anywhere. // MAnuv_1,4.67 //
But the otherness of the world from the omniscient <s>Brahman</s> is indeed experienced. /
Non-difference merely by virtue of existence would apply even to a dwarf and gold. // MAnuv_1,4.68 //
If transformation is of a part, then there is indeed difference between the parts. /

children.text: yo bhāgo na vikārī syāt sa evāsmākamīśvaraḥ // MAnuv_1,4.69 //
children.translated_text: That part which does not undergo transformation — that itself is our <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord). // MAnuv_1,4.69 //

children.text: bhinnānāṃ samudāyasya nāma brahmeti ced bhavet /
children.translated_text: If it be said that the aggregate of different things is named '<s>Brahman</s>' — /

children.text: brahmopādānatā na syāt tadā viśvasya hi kvacit // MAnuv_1,4.70 //
children.translated_text: then the material causality of <s>Brahman</s> with respect to the universe would never hold. // MAnuv_1,4.70 //
From horns [come] hares, from reverse-growing [hair come creatures], from <s>dūrvā</s> grass [comes] cow dung, and likewise /
the scorpion — in such cases, the efficient cause relation (<s>apādānatva</s>) is accepted. // MAnuv_1,4.71 //
Although in these cases a partial material cause relation is observed, /
even here the efficient cause relation alone serves as the example for <s>Brahman</s>. // MAnuv_1,4.72 //
For here the material cause relation alone does not hold, due to the predominance of external components. /

children.text: na cācetanatas tatra cetanasya samudbhavaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.73 //
children.translated_text: And there is no origination of the conscious from the unconscious in those cases. // MAnuv_1,4.73 //
How then by material causality? For the unconscious is the efficient cause, /
and the conscious dwelling in the body of the effect is [separately] observed. // MAnuv_1,4.74 //
'It became <s>sat</s> (being) and <s>tyat</s> (that)' — by this, its becoming the universe is not stated. /

children.text: tat sṛṣṭveti giraivāsya pūrvaṃ viśvasya siddhitaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.75 //
children.translated_text: By the very statement '<s>tat sṛṣṭvā</s>' (having created that), the prior existence of the universe [as separate] is established. // MAnuv_1,4.75 //
Because of being <s>sat</s> (existent), because of the suffix '<s>ta</s>', because of being Vedic, because it cannot be properly expressed [otherwise], /
because of being the substratum, because of being self-dependent, because of being knowledge, because of being difficult to know, // MAnuv_1,4.76 //
because of the extension of '<s>sat</s>' and the suffix, because of not being attained by the wicked, /
because of being always pervaded by qualities that are eternally good, because of being the controller — /

children.text: jagadgatena rūpeṇa brahmaiva hi tathocyate // MAnuv_1,4.77 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> alone is thus spoken of through the form that pervades the world. // MAnuv_1,4.77 //
For the manifestation of the aforementioned qualities with reference to persons, among humans, /
the usage 'it became' and such expressions is appropriate here. // MAnuv_1,4.78 //
Therefore, the sole creator of everything, without transformation, <s>Ramāpati</s> (the Lord of <s>Ramā</s>), /
is denoted by words such as '<s>Prakṛti</s>' and others, which are of feminine gender. // MAnuv_1,4.79 //
'May I become many' — this is fitting only through His own stated method. /
For through the form residing in each thing, He created the world for that purpose. // MAnuv_1,4.80 //
And if this very <s>Brahman</s>, being actually unchanged, is falsely /

children.text: dṛśyate mandadṛṣṭayaiva sa sarga iti kathyate // MAnuv_1,4.81 //
children.translated_text: seen as the universe — by defective vision alone — that is called creation: // MAnuv_1,4.81 //
[We ask:] is that defective vision belonging to <s>Brahman</s> itself, or does it reside in another? /

children.text: brahmaṇaścet kva sārvajñyamanyagā cet svato 'nyatā // MAnuv_1,4.82 //
children.translated_text: If it belongs to <s>Brahman</s>, where is His omniscience? If it resides in another, then [there is] otherness from Him. // MAnuv_1,4.82 //
There is no vision for one without a body — and so its cause is from itself. /

children.text: dehinaḥ kāraṇayutā dehāśca yadi na bhramāt // MAnuv_1,4.83 //
children.translated_text: If the embodied ones have a cause [for their vision], and their bodies are not from error — // MAnuv_1,4.83 //

children.text: kiṃ bhrāntikalpitaṃ tatra bhedo 'pi bhramajo yadi /
children.translated_text: what is imagined by error there? And if the difference too is born of error, /
since error has ignorance as its root, and that [ignorance] depends on difference — // MAnuv_1,4.84 //
nothing is produced by ignorance, for there would be mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). /
And if [error itself] is an error, then this statement too [falls within it], for it falls within that [error]. // MAnuv_1,4.85 //
And the conventional reality (<s>vyāvahārikatā</s>) of this would amount to being unsublatable indeed. /

children.text: bādhyaṃ nārthakriyākāri na ca svapno 'pi no mṛṣā // MAnuv_1,4.86 //
children.translated_text: What is sublatable does not produce practical effects (<s>arthakriyā</s>), and even a dream is not false [in this sense]. // MAnuv_1,4.86 //
Because [dreams] are produced by impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), and because even those [impressions] are accepted [as real], /

children.text: sa hi karteti vākyācca jāgrattvamiti hi bhramaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.87 //
children.translated_text: and because of the statement 'he is the doer' — [the claim that] it is [mere] waking is indeed an error. // MAnuv_1,4.87 //
For even in the case of the rope-snake error, knowledge of that kind indeed exists. /
That very [knowledge] produces practical effects — that indeed is effective in producing results. // MAnuv_1,4.88 //

children.text: brahma tvarthakriyākāri parataḥ svata eva vā /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, however, produces practical effects — whether through another or through itself. /

children.text: aṅgīkṛtaṃ hi tenaiva paratastve na ca pramā // MAnuv_1,4.89 //
children.translated_text: For that is accepted even by him [the Advaitin] — and if through another, then there is no valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.89 //
When what is not primarily real is always the means of proof for both of us, /

children.text: na hi sampratipattiḥ syādatastiṣṭhatu sā pramā // MAnuv_1,4.90 //
children.translated_text: there can be no agreement — let that [supposed] valid cognition stand aside. // MAnuv_1,4.90 //

children.text: na hi vipratipannena śakyaṃ sādhayituṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: For nothing can be established by one who is in disagreement [about fundamentals]. /
But the capacity of the witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣin</s>) to establish reality, for both of us — /

children.text: samyak sampratipannaṃ tanna vivatarmamataṃ bhavet // MAnuv_1,4.91 //
children.translated_text: that is well agreed upon, and therefore the <s>vivarta</s> (illusory transformation) doctrine cannot stand. // MAnuv_1,4.91 //
If nothing at all is accepted, then even the non-acceptance itself /
is not accepted — one would have to be mute. Therefore this is not our [Dvaita] position in debate. // MAnuv_1,4.92 //
'The universe is real' — whatever one knows, in accordance with its true nature — /
all such <s>śrutis</s> (scriptures) declare the reality of the universe. // MAnuv_1,4.93 //
The reality of space and so forth is established by witness-perception (<s>sākṣipratyakṣa</s>). /

children.text: sākṣisiddhasya na kvāpi bādhyatvaṃ tadadoṣataḥ // MAnuv_1,4.94 //
children.translated_text: What is established by the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) is never sublatable anywhere, because it is free from defect. // MAnuv_1,4.94 //
The unsublatability at all times is cognized by the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) alone. /

children.text: kālo hi sākṣipratyakṣaḥ suṣuptau ca pratītitaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.95 //
children.translated_text: For time is directly perceived by the witness, as is evident even in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.95 //
Past and future times too are not beyond the range of the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>). /
Since they cannot be made the subject of a thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), inference does not apply there. // MAnuv_1,4.96 //

children.text: tadetaditi sarvaṃ ca dṛśyaṃ vā smṛtigocaram /
children.translated_text: 'That is this' — and all that is visible or within the range of memory — /

children.text: sākṣisiddhena kālena khacitaṃ hyeva vartate // MAnuv_1,4.97 //
children.translated_text: all exists as embedded in time, which is established by the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.97 //

children.text: tasmānna taṃ vinā kiñcit smartuṃ draṣṭumathāpi vā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, without that [witness-consciousness], nothing can be remembered or perceived. /
Since it is eternally established, there can be no occasion for inference. // MAnuv_1,4.98 //
Hence, the reality of what is cognized without defect is established by the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>). /

children.text: parīkṣādeśca satyatvaṃ tena hyeva mataṃ bhavet // MAnuv_1,4.99 //
children.translated_text: And the reality [established] through examination is likewise established by that [witness] alone. // MAnuv_1,4.99 //
Otherwise, along with <s>śruti</s> (scripture), reasoning, and other means of valid knowledge, /

children.text: akasmād vinivṛttiśca kiṃ viśvasya na śaṅkayate // MAnuv_1,4.100 //
children.translated_text: would one not suspect the causeless cessation of the universe? // MAnuv_1,4.100 //

children.text: itaḥ pūrvaṃ tathābhāvād yadi no saṃsṛtergatiḥ /
children.translated_text: If, because of its non-existence before this, the course of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is denied — /

children.text: vākyānumāditaścet syāt tatprāmāṇyaṃ ca sākṣitaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.101 //
children.translated_text: if it be from verbal testimony, inference, and so forth, then their validity too [depends] on the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.101 //
Just as the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) establishes their validity, so indeed — /
by its steadfastness at all times, and by removing deviation — // MAnuv_1,4.102 //
thus, the reality of the universe, established as free from defect in sense-perception — /
why would this [witness] not establish it, given its power of faultless cognition? // MAnuv_1,4.103 //
'The universe is produced by a single cognition' — what is falsely maintained — /
'the universe is produced by many cognitions' would be the reply to that. // MAnuv_1,4.104 //
One who, while knowing the reality of another, is a thief of his own self, /

children.text: paro nāstīti vadati kimityunmattavad vadet // MAnuv_1,4.105 //
children.translated_text: and says 'the other does not exist' — why would he speak like a madman? // MAnuv_1,4.105 //

children.text: parābhāve hi vāg vyarthā yadi naivocyate tadā /
children.translated_text: For in the absence of the other, speech would be purposeless; if indeed nothing is stated then, /
the whip and cane and such would be the answer to that thief. // MAnuv_1,4.106 //

children.text: prapañco yadi vidyeta nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If the manifold world (<s>prapañca</s>) were to exist, it would cease — there is no doubt. /
This duality is mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion); non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) is the ultimate reality' — // MAnuv_1,4.107 //
'The conceptual distinction would cease if it were imagined by someone. /

children.text: upadeśādayaṃ vādo 'jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyate // MAnuv_1,4.108 //
children.translated_text: This teaching [shows that] duality does not exist for the ignorant' — // MAnuv_1,4.108 //

children.text: ityatra yadiśabdau ca nivarteteti ca dvayam /
children.translated_text: In this [passage], the two words 'if' (<s>yadi</s>) and 'would cease' (<s>nivarteta</s>) — both of these /
declare the reality of the universe; and '<s>vidyeta</s>' [declares] its origination. // MAnuv_1,4.109 //
For the root '<s>vid</s>' indeed [means] origination — from this root, origination alone [is the meaning]. /
The manifold world (<s>prapañca</s>), generally conjoined with cessation and pervasion, is the fivefold difference (<s>bhedapañcaka</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.110 //
The difference between <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Īśvara</s> (God), and likewise the difference between <s>jaḍa</s> (insentient matter) and <s>Īśvara</s>, /
the mutual difference among <s>jīvas</s>, and likewise the difference between <s>jaḍa</s> and <s>jīva</s>, /

children.text: mithaśca jaḍabhedo yaḥ prapañco bhedapañcakaḥ // MAnuv_1,4.111 //
children.translated_text: and the mutual difference among <s>jaḍa</s> entities — [this is] the manifold world as the fivefold difference (<s>bhedapañcaka</s>). // MAnuv_1,4.111 //
This [fivefold difference] is real and beginningless — for if it had a beginning, it would meet with destruction. /

children.text: dvaitaṃ na vidyata iti tasmādajñānināṃ matam // MAnuv_1,4.112 //
children.translated_text: 'Duality does not exist' — this is therefore the view of the ignorant. // MAnuv_1,4.112 //
Thus the meaning of <s>śruti</s> is measured and protected by the knowledge of <s>Hari</s> called <s>māyā</s>. /
The supreme meaning is <s>Hari</s> alone — all else is intermediate and inferior. // MAnuv_1,4.113 //

children.text: vācārabdhaṃ tu sāṅketyaṃ nāma syād vikṛtaṃ bahu /
children.translated_text: That which begins with speech, being conventional, would be a name that is manifold and modified. /

children.text: nityaṃ tu nāmadheyaṃ yanmṛttiketyādi vaidikam // MAnuv_1,4.114 //
children.translated_text: But the eternal name is that which is Vedic, such as '<s>mṛttikā</s>' (clay) and so forth. // MAnuv_1,4.114 //
Because of the primacy [of the essential nature], through the knowledge of that, even a person ignorant of derived [forms] /
is called 'learned' by the wise — thus one who eternally knows the Supreme Self. // MAnuv_1,4.115 //
The eternal truth (<s>sadātana satya</s>) is spoken of as 'eternal' by the wise. /
And the usage occurs further: 'if old age were to reach him — // MAnuv_1,4.116 //
or if this body were to perish — what then would remain of him?' /

children.text: hanyate na vadhenāyaṃ jarayā ca na jīryati // MAnuv_1,4.117 //
children.translated_text: 'He is not slain by killing, nor does he decay by old age.' // MAnuv_1,4.117 //

children.text: etat satyaṃ brahmapuramiti nityatva eva hi /
children.translated_text: 'This is the true city of <s>Brahman</s>' — this is indeed in the sense of eternity. /
When '<s>vācārambhaṇa</s>' (originating in speech) is stated, imagining it to mean 'false' is an unfounded conjecture from the unheard. // MAnuv_1,4.118 //
'Name' (<s>nāmadheya</s>) — the repetition of this [word in the śruti] would render it meaningless [if it meant falsity]. /

children.text: ekaḥ piṇḍo maṇiśceti padavaiyathyarmeva ca // MAnuv_1,4.119 //
children.translated_text: 'One lump,' 'one jewel' — this too would be a distortion of the words. // MAnuv_1,4.119 //
If the intention were to speak of modification (<s>vikāratva</s>), then the cutting of a single nail /

children.text: sarvakārṣṇāyasaṃ ca syādataḥ sādṛśya eva ca // MAnuv_1,4.120 //
children.translated_text: would make everything iron — therefore, it is only in the sense of similarity. // MAnuv_1,4.120 //
The intention here, however, is in the sense of eternity and primacy, through the path already stated. /
The elaboration of creation and so forth is for the purpose of understanding the primacy [of <s>Brahman</s>]. // MAnuv_1,4.121 //

children.text: tasmāt kenāpi mārgeṇa na vivartamataṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by no means whatsoever can the <s>vivarta</s> (illusory transformation) doctrine stand. /
Because of its innumerable defects, it is to be rejected by those who seek the good. // MAnuv_1,4.122 //
Because the defects are innumerable, and also from fear of excessive length of the treatise, /
we desist from [further refutation]. <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by His mere will, effortlessly, /
creates the universe like a father, possessing the fullness of all <s>śeṣa</s>-qualities (auspicious attributes). // MAnuv_1,4.123 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Śrīmad Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s>, composed by the revered <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya</s>. ||

children.translated_text: The <s>samanvaya</s> (complete harmony) has been stated; now non-contradiction (<s>avirodha</s>) is established here. /

children.text: caturvidhasya tasyādau yauktastatrāpi ca smṛteḥ // MAnuv_2,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Of that [non-contradiction], which is fourfold — first, that which relates to reasoning, and within that too, [the objection from] <s>Smṛti</s> — // MAnuv_2,1.1 //
And because that [<s>Smṛti</s> objection] is of four types, each [type] is fourfold. /

children.text: pādāḥ sarve tadaṃśāśca mūrtīnāṃ varṇamā'gamāt // MAnuv_2,1.2 //
children.translated_text: All the <s>pādas</s> (quarters) and their sub-sections — from the <s>Āgama</s> (scripture), the description of the forms. // MAnuv_2,1.2 //
Trustworthiness, equanimity, consistency with <s>śruti</s> — these arise from the strength of equality. /
Conformity with all [other texts], conciseness, non-perception of distinguishing features — [these are] the results. // MAnuv_2,1.3 //
The achievement of the desired [conclusion], and regularity — these are the arguments against the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view). /

children.text: etā eva tvatibalā siddhāntasya niyāmakāḥ // MAnuv_2,1.4 //
children.translated_text: These very [arguments], being exceedingly strong, establish the <s>siddhānta</s> (final conclusion). // MAnuv_2,1.4 //

children.text: āptaiḥ pratyakṣato dṛṣṭvā proktamarthaṃ kathaṃ śratiḥ /
children.translated_text: How can <s>śruti</s> (scripture) [be contradicted by] a meaning declared by the trustworthy ones who have seen it directly through perception? /

children.text: pipīlikālipinibhā vārayeta sarvagā hi te // MAnuv_2,1.5 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Smṛti</s>] resembling a line of ants — how can it obstruct [<s>śruti</s>]? For they [the sages] are all-pervading. // MAnuv_2,1.5 //
If it be said so — if <s>Rudra</s> and the other [deities], headed by <s>Hari</s>, are knowers of everything, /

children.text: kiṃ nāśeṣavido mānaṃ hy ubhayatra samaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_2,1.6 //
children.translated_text: why would they not be all-knowing? For the means of valid knowledge should be equal in both cases. // MAnuv_2,1.6 //
And the certainty of trustworthiness cannot be [established] there, due to the possibility of deviation. /

children.text: nacāsyā vyabhicāre 'pi hīyate mānatā kvacit // MAnuv_2,1.7 //
children.translated_text: And even when it [the Veda] deviates [in some cases], its validity is not lost anywhere. // MAnuv_2,1.7 //
Because of the constant difficulty of determining the qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) stated in the <s>Veda</s>, /

children.text: niyamo vyabhicāro vā naiva jñātuṃ hi śakyate // MAnuv_2,1.8 //
children.translated_text: restriction or deviation can never be ascertained. // MAnuv_2,1.8 //
For qualification is easily stated in other scriptures (<s>āgamas</s>) — that is sufficient. /

children.text: vedokto hy adhikārastu durlabhaḥ sarvamānuṣaiḥ // MAnuv_2,1.9 //
children.translated_text: But the qualification stated in the <s>Veda</s> is difficult to obtain for all humans. // MAnuv_2,1.9 //
In other <s>āgamas</s>, even the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood of those born as <s>caṇḍālas</s> /
is taught gradually through entry into the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle). // MAnuv_2,1.10 //
Having stated a qualification that is difficult to attain, and again [stating] an exceedingly easy one, /
and having stated a means that is impossible, and [then] an easy one for the attainment of that fruit — /

children.text: ucyate 'tastaduktaṃ hi vyabhicāri phale 'pi tu // MAnuv_2,1.11 //
children.translated_text: what is stated [in such scriptures] is therefore said to deviate even regarding the fruit. // MAnuv_2,1.11 //
How would [such a scripture] attain validity? — being eternal, [yet contradicted] by what arises from persons. /

children.text: ujkhitaṃ sarvadoṣaiśca kathaṃ no mānatāṃ vrajet // MAnuv_2,1.12 //
children.translated_text: Abandoned by all defects — how would it not attain validity? // MAnuv_2,1.12 //
'O <s>Virūpa</s>, through the eternal speech, the eternal and the non-eternal, always' — /
and so forth: from these <s>Śrutis</s>, the <s>Veda</s> is understood to be eternal. // MAnuv_2,1.13 //
Even the writing of ants is a valid means [of knowledge], by virtue of non-contradiction. /
Just as [the message] made by the owl for <s>Drauṇi</s> (<s>Aśvatthāman</s>) was informative [despite its source]. // MAnuv_2,1.14 //
What is non-contradictory [is valid]; what is contradictory is invalidated by the very contradiction. /
Since no contradiction is seen, therefore the validity of the <s>Veda</s> is accepted. // MAnuv_2,1.15 //

children.text: tanmūlatvāt smṛtīnāṃ ca virodho yatra na kvacit /
children.translated_text: And because the <s>Smṛtis</s> are rooted in it [the <s>Veda</s>], where there is no contradiction [they are valid]. /

children.text: virodho 'pi sa evoktaḥ pratyakṣeṇāgamena vā // MAnuv_2,1.16 //
children.translated_text: Even a contradiction is stated [to be resolvable] through direct perception or through scripture. // MAnuv_2,1.16 //
When there is a conflict of one scripture with another, reasoning is accepted [as arbiter]. /
But when there is a conflict with what is primary (<s>upajīvya</s>), then another interpretation of the <s>Veda</s> [should be sought]. // MAnuv_2,1.17 //
Direct perception would be primary, and sometimes reasoning too, in some cases. /
In matters where scripture alone is the means of knowledge, scripture itself is primary. // MAnuv_2,1.18 //
If both a reasonable and an unreasonable meaning of scripture are apprehended, /

children.text: syāt tatra yukta evārtho yuktiśca trividhā matā // MAnuv_2,1.19 //
children.translated_text: there the reasonable meaning should be [accepted]; and reasoning is considered threefold. // MAnuv_2,1.19 //
The <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion/invariable concomitance) of which is based on perception, reasoning, or scripture — /
that reasoning which is rooted in perception and scripture is the strongest. // MAnuv_2,1.20 //
Correspondence to reality is validity — that is the primary [meaning] of knowledge and words. /

children.text: arthatvamaryataiva syānna kriyārtheṣu sā matā // MAnuv_2,1.21 //
children.translated_text: 'Being an object' would mean just 'worth knowing' — it is not considered [applicable] in matters of ritual action. // MAnuv_2,1.21 //
In the domain of knowledge, 'being knowable' is primary; in the domain of words, [verbal expression] comes next. /
Reasonings that produce true knowledge are considered true. // MAnuv_2,1.22 //
Perception, reasoning, and testimony are subsidiary <s>pramāṇas</s>; therefore, /
even the validity of a <s>Smṛti</s> that is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) is not diminished. // MAnuv_2,1.23 //
If [one says that] 'correspondence to reality' is the intended meaning of the word 'validity,' /

children.text: aṅgīkṛtaṃ cet prāmāṇyaṃ smṛtyādeḥ kā virodhatā // MAnuv_2,1.24 //
children.translated_text: then if the validity of <s>Smṛti</s> and the like is accepted, what is the contradiction? // MAnuv_2,1.24 //
And one should not say that all <s>Smṛtis</s> that are restatements are fruitless. /

children.text: phalavattvaṃ nacāsmābhiḥ prāmāṇyaṃ hi vivakṣitam // MAnuv_2,1.25 //
children.translated_text: Nor is 'bearing fruit' what we intend by 'validity.' // MAnuv_2,1.25 //
What fruitfulness is spoken of in the perception of grass and the like? /

children.text: sukhaduḥkhādikaṃ kiñcit smṛtāvapi hi dṛśyate // MAnuv_2,1.26 //
children.translated_text: Some happiness, suffering, and so forth is indeed seen in <s>Smṛti</s> as well. // MAnuv_2,1.26 //
And a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) is not merely the effect of delimitation — rather, [the term] '<s>pramā</s>' [means valid cognition]. /
For here, 'direct perception' (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is declared as arising from a flawless sense-faculty (<s>akṣa</s>). // MAnuv_2,1.27 //
The sense-faculty (<s>akṣa</s>) is considered twofold: material (<s>prākṛta</s>) and pure consciousness (<s>śuddhacaitanya</s>). /
The pure [sense-faculty] is [found in] the Lord and the liberated; in others, [it is] combined with the material. // MAnuv_2,1.28 //
The flawless consciousness is accepted as both [types] in others [i.e. bound souls]. /
That which has happiness, suffering, and so forth as its objects is the pure [consciousness] — even in those enmeshed in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // MAnuv_2,1.29 //
Because of its flawlessness and absolute unfailingness, it is considered the most powerful. /
The material [sense-faculty] is remembered as sixfold, due to the distinction of the five senses and the mind. // MAnuv_2,1.30 //

children.text: anumā yuktirevoktā vyāptireva tu sā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: Inference (<s>anumā</s>) is called reasoning; that is remembered as <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance). /
When <s>vyāpti</s> alone is stated for the purpose of establishing the thesis, // MAnuv_2,1.31 //
what else remains [to be stated] here? For one who knows, the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is [implicitly] there. /

children.text: yadi liṅgamasiddhaṃ syāt kuta evāsya mānatā // MAnuv_2,1.32 //
children.translated_text: If the inferential mark is not established, how could it have validity at all? // MAnuv_2,1.32 //
If it were merely a reminder, there would be no purpose for the rememberer here. /
And in the statement of five members [of the syllogism], the dispute would not be resolved. // MAnuv_2,1.33 //

children.text: dṛṣṭāntādiṣu caivaṃ syāt sādhanaṃ punareva hi /
children.translated_text: And in the case of examples (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) and the like, the same [problem] would arise — the proof [would be needed] again. /
And even in the statement of the inferential mark, the conclusion of inference is certain. // MAnuv_2,1.34 //
Contradiction and irrelevance (<s>asaṅgati</s>) are the direct defects of reasoning. /
Non-relation to the thesis is called 'irrelevance' of reasoning. // MAnuv_2,1.35 //
Contradiction too is of three kinds: contrariness to the thesis-meaning, /
absence of the inferential mark, and non-pervasion — while excess and deficiency are verbal [faults]. // MAnuv_2,1.36 //
Non-pervasion is the inverse of what pervades what is to be proved; and non-pervasion of the means of proof. /
Even in a contradiction by a weak [argument], the <s>pramāṇa</s> is not invalidating. // MAnuv_2,1.37 //
Even in a contradiction with one's own statement, [the argument] would not attain the status of proof. /

children.text: saṃvādānuktisaṃyuktā eta eva ca nigrahāḥ // MAnuv_2,1.38 //
children.translated_text: These very [defects], combined with failure to state agreement, are also the points of defeat (<s>nigraha</s>). // MAnuv_2,1.38 //
<s>Vāda</s> (honest debate), <s>jalpa</s> (sophistic debate), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive debate) — these are the three types of discourse known to the wise. /
For one's own purpose or for another's purpose, it is the discourse that leads to the ascertainment of truth — // MAnuv_2,1.39 //
discourse that is merely that is <s>vāda</s>; <s>jalpa</s> is with reference to gain and the like. /

children.text: satāmeva kathā jñeyā vitaṇḍā tvasatāṃ satām // MAnuv_2,1.40 //
children.translated_text: The discourse of the good alone is to be known [as <s>vāda</s>]; <s>vitaṇḍā</s> is of the bad [against] the good. // MAnuv_2,1.40 //
Without revealing one's own established doctrine, the bad person's refutation of the [good person's] position — /

children.text: ukte taiḥ prathamaṃ māne vaktavyaṃ tasya dūṣaṇam // MAnuv_2,1.41 //
children.translated_text: when [evidence] is first presented by them, the refutation of that should be stated. // MAnuv_2,1.41 //
The examination of knowledge (<s>vidyāparīkṣā</s>) must precede <s>vitaṇḍā</s> and <s>jalpa</s> as well; /
because the determination of superiority and inferiority [leads to] victory and defeat. // MAnuv_2,1.42 //

children.text: vinaiva tattvanirṇītiṃ na hi jalpādinā kvacit /
children.translated_text: Without the determination of truth, through <s>jalpa</s> and so forth, /
the knowledge of superiority and inferiority is never [achieved] — hence the examination of knowledge [is primary]. // MAnuv_2,1.43 //
And through <s>vāda</s>, the knowledge of superiority and inferiority becomes clear. /

children.text: iti vādasya pūrvatvaṃ tatsiddhau vyarthatānyayoḥ // MAnuv_2,1.44 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>vāda</s> has priority; when it is successful, the other two are pointless. // MAnuv_2,1.44 //
Even for establishing one's extensive knowledge, <s>vāda</s> is not [merely] a cause. /
Preceded by [the evaluation of] the assembly, the president, and the questioners — even for rivals, // MAnuv_2,1.45 //
<s>vāda</s> alone serves both purposes — producing ascertainment and victory. /
Non-revelation of the truth is the sole fruit of <s>vitaṇḍā</s> and <s>jalpa</s>. // MAnuv_2,1.46 //

children.text: vinā vādena vidyāyā yadi śakyaṃ parīkṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: If the examination of knowledge is possible without <s>vāda</s>, /

children.text: syājjalpādirapi kvāpi vāda evānyathā bhavet // MAnuv_2,1.47 //
children.translated_text: then even <s>jalpa</s> and so forth would sometimes be [equivalent to] <s>vāda</s>; otherwise it would [just] become [honest] debate. // MAnuv_2,1.47 //

children.text: jalpa ityapi nāma syād vādasyaitādṛśasya tu /
children.translated_text: Even [what is called] '<s>jalpa</s>' might [in fact] be a name for <s>vāda</s> of this kind. /
Even the establishment of a mere thesis could [constitute <s>vāda</s>] — as in the case of <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. // MAnuv_2,1.48 //
The assembly, the president of the assembly, and the questioners should be <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>; /
the members of the assembly should be free from passion and aversion, and should be knowers of all. // MAnuv_2,1.49 //
When these [proper assembly members] are lacking in knowledge, the questioners and members /
who are far [removed from bias] should be the authorities for decision, free from partiality. // MAnuv_2,1.50 //
Both proof and refutation [are employed] in <s>vāda</s> and <s>jalpa</s> by both sides. /
The good should employ scripture alone — [that which] establishes what is desired. // MAnuv_2,1.51 //
The bad [debaters] employ reasoning in accordance with their own established doctrine. /
But relying on the discordance with perception and scripture, the alternative interpretation [should be given]. // MAnuv_2,1.52 //
In scripture, the defect to be shown here is the non-conformity of the inferential mark. /
The conformity of the inferential mark to one's own position is the support of <s>Śruti</s> and the like. // MAnuv_2,1.53 //
One who would state an inference with only three or five members, /

children.text: niyamād yo 'numāṃ brūyād taṃ brūyād yadi tādṛśī /
children.translated_text: or with an even number of members — if one should state such [a fixed form], /
[and if he says] 'it is not an inference' — then by what [authority] is the construction of the 'what-is-to-be-proved' member [made]? // MAnuv_2,1.54 //

children.text: ***[NOTE: jump in verse numbering, no lacuna in text!]***
children.translated_text: ***[NOTE: jump in verse numbering, no lacuna in text!]***
When the fixed members are not established, proof should be done /

children.text: kartavyameva tena syāt tasmāt saivānumā matā // MAnuv_2,1.57 //
children.translated_text: through <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) alone; therefore that alone is considered inference. // MAnuv_2,1.57 //
If experience (<s>anubhūti</s>) is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, by what is memory (<s>smṛti</s>) negated? /

children.text: pūrvānubhūte kiṃ mānamityukte syāt kimuttaram // MAnuv_2,1.58 //
children.translated_text: If one asks 'What is the <s>pramāṇa</s> for what was previously experienced?' — what would be the answer? // MAnuv_2,1.58 //
That cognition is mental, and it has the witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣin</s>) as its <s>pramāṇa</s>. /
Just as what is past and future is seen directly by <s>yogins</s>, /
so too what was previously experienced is cognized by the mind itself. // MAnuv_2,1.59 //
'I knew this before by the mind' and 'this was done by me' — /
established from direct experience — how indeed is it negated? // MAnuv_2,1.60 //
Thus, regarding the three <s>pramāṇas</s> defined by their characteristics, for objects such as <s>Brahman</s> and the like, /

children.text: pramāṇaṃ veda evaikas tatprāmāṇyaṃ ca sādhitam // MAnuv_2,1.61 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Veda</s> alone is the <s>pramāṇa</s>; and its validity has been established. // MAnuv_2,1.61 //
Nevertheless, [words like] 'earth,' 'water,' and so forth, which denote cognition, speech, and the like — /

children.text: dṛṣṭavyāptiviruddhatvāt tatra mānaṃ kathaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_2,1.62 //
children.translated_text: since their <s>vyāpti</s> contradicts what is observed — how could they be a <s>pramāṇa</s> there? // MAnuv_2,1.62 //
Therefore, some other person bearing that name exists — /
by non-contradiction with reasoning and scripture, what is obtained is stated here. // MAnuv_2,1.63 //
Even without the conventional meaning [known by] the common people, by relying on the learned convention (<s>vidvadrūḍhi</s>), /
these [words] bearing those names are the presiding deities (<s>abhimānins</s>) of those respective entities. // MAnuv_2,1.64 //
They are said to have a special power beyond others. /
And the <s>vyāpti</s> is in accordance with what has been stated, and they are seen by those who are qualified. // MAnuv_2,1.65 //
And the etymological derivation of the entity stated in scripture is from the indicators in scripture. /

children.text: vyutpattiḥ sā balavatī mūrkhavyutpattitā hi yat // MAnuv_2,1.66 //
children.translated_text: That derivation is powerful, since [the contrary] is the derivation of the ignorant. // MAnuv_2,1.66 //
When there is a conflict with strong reasoning, the principle everywhere is this: /
a reasoning supported by few statements and [yet] having many contradicting [reasonings] — // MAnuv_2,1.67 //
wherever this is so — how could the determination of the truth of the thing be? When stated, /
the settled principle is: [truth is determined] by the abundance of contradicting reasonings. // MAnuv_2,1.68 //
Would not the abundance of reasonings against reasonings, and of scriptures against scripture, /

children.text: kathaṃ na nirṇayaṃ kuryādityasat kāraṇaṃ na hi // MAnuv_2,1.69 //
children.translated_text: produce determination? This is not an invalid cause. // MAnuv_2,1.69 //
The meaning of <s>Śruti</s> is [established] somewhere through reasonings that are predominantly scriptural. /

children.text: avirodhaścaturthe tu pāte samyak samarthyate // MAnuv_2,1.70 //
children.translated_text: And non-contradiction [with other <s>pramāṇas</s>] is properly demonstrated in the fourth <s>pāda</s> (section). // MAnuv_2,1.70 //

children.text: asat kāryaṃ yathā dṛṣṭaṃ vastutvāt kāraṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: 'A non-existent effect [is produced] — as observed; [and] because of being a thing, so is the cause' — /

children.text: iti cenna niṣedhaikasvarūpasya na kartṛtā // MAnuv_2,1.71 //
children.translated_text: if [one says] this — [we reply:] for that whose sole nature is negation, there is no agency (<s>kartṛtā</s>). // MAnuv_2,1.71 //
For purposeful activity (<s>buddhipūrvapravṛtti</s>) is what is determined here as agency. /
But the 'negation-nature' [of destruction] — through the property of non-existence belonging to an entity, /
and through the identity of property and property-bearer — but it does not become mere that. // MAnuv_2,1.72 //

children.text: abhāvasya ca bhāvo 'pi dharmo 'thāpi hi dharmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the existence of non-existence is also a property; or rather, [it is a property] of the property-bearer. /
Mere 'such-ness' is stated; cognition is precisely the absence of that. // MAnuv_2,1.73 //
Being a qualificand (<s>viśeṣya</s>) is property-bearer-hood in the first cognitions. /
Being of the nature of injunction or prohibition is entity-hood or non-entity-hood here. // MAnuv_2,1.74 //

children.text: sarvanāśeṣvapi sadā śiṣṭatvād yasya kasya nuḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in all destructions, because something always remains, /
this destruction too, even if disputed, has a remainder of an agent — because of being destruction. // MAnuv_2,1.75 //
And the total destruction of all persons is not observed, nor is it ever seen. /
Because of being the substratum of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, the person must be accepted even at dissolution (<s>laya</s>). // MAnuv_2,1.76 //

children.text: anāditvaṃ vinādṛṣṭaṃ kathaṃ syāt kāraṇaṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: Without being beginningless, how could it be a cause, when never observed? /

children.text: pūrvādṛṣṭāt parādṛṣṭaṃ yadi naivottaraṃ kutaḥ // MAnuv_2,1.77 //
children.translated_text: If the unseen [merit/demerit] that comes later [is explained] from the prior unseen — then whence the subsequent? // MAnuv_2,1.77 //

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇaṃ no cellaye mānaṃ ca kiṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If unseen [merit] is not [accepted as] a cause, what would be the evidence at dissolution? /

children.text: utpattināśakārī hi buddhimān dṛśyate kvacit // MAnuv_2,1.78 //
children.translated_text: For an intelligent creator is seen somewhere as the cause of production and destruction. // MAnuv_2,1.78 //
By that example, why is a creator not inferred everywhere? /
An inference supported by scripture — this inference is indeed a <s>pramāṇa</s>. // MAnuv_2,1.79 //
In the absence of scriptural support, reasoning would not be well-established. /
It is only when rooted in perception and scripture that this [inference] has firm establishment. /

children.text: anyathāsyāpratiṣṭhā ca svavācā vyāhataiva hi // MAnuv_2,1.80 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be groundlessness of this [position], and it would indeed be contradicted by one's own words // 2.1.80 //
And the [argument of] non-apprehension by disciples — [applies to] the proponent of a Lord from the position of non-Lord; /
therefore, the agency of the remaining <s>jīva</s> and others is here refuted // 2.1.81 //
'That mind did not create' — by this, the origination of mind from non-existence /

children.text: nivāritā tu pūrvatra hyakasmāditi tadvinā // MAnuv_2,1.82 //
children.translated_text: is refuted; but earlier, [it was stated] 'without cause' — that is, without it [i.e., mind] // 2.1.82 //
Here, the apprehension that the universe originates from non-existence is refuted; /

children.text: prāpakaṃ vākyamātraṃ tu parihāro viśeṣitaḥ // MAnuv_2,1.83 //
children.translated_text: but the solution is specified as merely a statement that leads [to the correct understanding] // 2.1.83 //
Seeing that somewhere the creation was made by a <s>jīva</s>, and that it was made by a conscious being alone, /
an inference of the same kind elsewhere is made, because of the reality of the <s>Śruti</s> // 2.1.84 //
Nowhere has anything been seen to have become something other [than itself] in any way whatsoever; /

children.text: ato jīvasya na brahmabhāvaḥ syāddhi kadācana // MAnuv_2,1.85 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the <s>jīva</s> can never have the state of <s>Brahman</s> // 2.1.85 //
What has been seen somewhere as different — how [can it be seen] as non-different? /

children.text: dṛśyenno dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hi tādṛśaṃ na ca dṛśyate // MAnuv_2,1.86 //
children.translated_text: Something like that, which has never been seen before, is not seen [now either] // 2.1.86 //

children.text: bhoktṛtvāpattita iti yanmataṃ tat kuto hariḥ /
children.translated_text: As for the view that there would be the consequence of [<s>Brahman</s>] being an experiencer — from where [does this follow]? <s>Hari</s> /

children.text: bhoktrāpatteriti prāha kathaṃ ca tadananyatā // MAnuv_2,1.87 //
children.translated_text: says [refuting this very consequence] of the experiencer — and how [can there be] non-difference from that? // 2.1.87 //
When the non-transformation of the world has been established by the reasoning stated, /
the otherness of an independent cause is thereby refuted here // 2.1.88 //

children.text: dravyaṃ karma ca kālaśca svabhāvaścetanā dhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Substance, action, time, own-nature, consciousness, and steadfastness — /
by whose grace these exist, and by whose disregard they do not exist' — /

children.text: iti śrutestadvaśasya bhāvo na para ityataḥ // MAnuv_2,1.89 //
children.translated_text: from this <s>Śruti</s>, the state of being under His control means not being supreme; hence // 2.1.89 //
Though capable of creating otherwise, <s>Hari</s>, by the regulation of His own will, /
always creates this world through fixed causes alone // 2.1.90 //
There is eternal difference from the efficient cause; but with respect to the material cause, there is a twofold [relation]: /

children.text: asad yat kāryarūpeṇa kāraṇātmatayāsti hi // MAnuv_2,1.91 //
children.translated_text: that which is non-existent in the form of the effect exists in the form of the cause // 2.1.91 //
Otherwise, there would be infinite regress with respect to origination and destruction everywhere; /
though the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> is capable of not creating, or of creating otherwise // 2.1.92 //
the unborn [Lord] creates the universe as different from Himself, [yet] both different and non-different from the cause — /
from this <s>Śruti</s>, the stated meaning is fully ascertained // 2.1.93 //
He who truly confers a certain capacity even upon the partless <s>jīva</s> /

children.text: kāryeṣu yaḥ karotyaddhā namastasmai svayambhuve // MAnuv_2,1.94 //
children.translated_text: in [its] actions — obeisance to that self-born One // 2.1.94 //

children.text: yadi bhāgena kāryeṣu jīvaśaktiṃ na yojayet /
children.translated_text: If <s>Hari</s> did not confer the power of the <s>jīva</s> partially in actions, /

children.text: haristadā hi sarvatra kṛtsnayatnoṃ'śitāpi vā // MAnuv_2,1.95 //
children.translated_text: then in everything He would be either of complete effort, or even an enjoyer of parts // 2.1.95 //

children.text: aṃśino hi paṭādyā ye bhinnaireva parasparam /
children.translated_text: For those that have parts, such as cloth and the rest, are called possessors of parts /

children.text: aṃśairaṃśina ucyante naivameva hi cetanāḥ // MAnuv_2,1.96 //
children.translated_text: through parts that are mutually different — but conscious beings are not like this at all // 2.1.96 //
Therefore, the <s>Śruti</s> applies to these [<s>jīvas</s>] as 'partless' indeed, /
even though they have many forms — solely by distinction // 2.1.97 //
But the having-of-parts called 'multiplicity of forms' does exist in them; /
because of the invariable concomitance with multiplicity, difference necessarily obtains // 2.1.98 //
If it were not so, the Lord <s>Puruṣottama</s> is the regulator; /

children.text: tasya tvaśeṣaśaktitvād yujyate savarmeva ca // MAnuv_2,1.99 //
children.translated_text: because of His having all powers, it is appropriate even with equality // 2.1.99 //
The contradiction with respect to all distinctions, which is refuted in the second [<s>pāda</s>], /
pertains to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; others go to various [topics] in that chapter // 2.1.100 //
The non-contradiction among the statements of creation and dissolution /
that describe the forms of the <s>jīva</s> is also the subject of the second chapter // 2.1.101 //
By the distinction of the means of knowledge and the object of knowledge, there is no redundancy; /
the Lord's activity is always from His own nature alone // 2.1.102 //
Just as some bodily movements of a person are purposeless, /
the <s>Śruti</s> directly states: 'this is the nature of the Lord' // 2.1.103 //
Making play the purpose of creation would be contradictory to <s>Śruti</s>; /

children.text: iti kevalalīlaiva nirṇītā prabhuṇā svayam // MAnuv_2,1.104 //
children.translated_text: thus, mere sport alone was determined by the Lord Himself // 2.1.104 //
The <s>Śruti</s> prevented the desire for self-purpose; /
'not because of having purpose' — thus says the world-teacher // 2.1.105 //
That creation is merely the will of the Lord — those who are resolved regarding creation [hold this]; /
thus, by praise, by <s>Śrutis</s> regarding desire, and by reasoning, /
and by the purport of the great [<s>Śrutis</s>] — mere will is not refuted // 2.1.106 //

children.text: mokṣārthāḥ śrutayo yasmāt sa ca tasya prasādataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the <s>Śrutis</s> are for the purpose of liberation, and that [liberation] comes from His grace; /
and from the statement of the desire to raise up, and in accordance with worldly observation // 2.1.107 //
since [creation is] caused by will, in its absence how would the <s>Śruti</s>, /
which would be devoid of the great purport, attain the status of a valid means of knowledge? // 2.1.108 //
Truthfulness alone is the status of a valid means of knowledge; and even a statement that is instrumental /
attains the status of validity — therein, that which has a complete purpose // 2.1.109 //
Partiality and cruelty [would constitute] a reason for the invalidity of the <s>Vedas</s>; /
therefore, this should not be accepted; but the other [charge] is not properly called 'partiality' and the like // 2.1.110 //

children.text: yadadhīnā guṇāścaiva doṣā api hi sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: He upon whom all qualities as well as all faults depend in every way — /

children.text: guṇāstasya kathaṃ na syuḥ syurdeṣāśca kathaṃ punaḥ // MAnuv_2,1.111 //
children.translated_text: how can qualities not belong to Him? And how again could faults [belong to Him]? // 2.1.111 //
Because all <s>dharmas</s> are attributed [to Him], by such statements too, /
the Lord <s>Hari</s> is determined as faultless and possessing all qualities // 2.1.112 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: The reasonings of <s>smṛti</s>, reasoning, <s>śruti</s>, and qualities — the many reasonings — /

children.text: evaṃ caturvidhā naiva viruddhayante 'nvayaṃ prati // MAnuv_2,2.1 //
children.translated_text: thus, the fourfold [valid means] are never contradicted with respect to the harmonization // 2.2.1 //
Even though this was determined in the first <s>pāda</s>, because of the attack /
from the activity of [rival] philosophical systems, the dull-witted one doubts again // 2.2.2 //
The doctrines that have been current since beginningless time, in a stream [of tradition] — /
and since there is no cutting off of any doctrine whatsoever — therefore the all-pervading [Lord] // 2.2.3 //
demonstrates separately and clearly that these are rooted in error, /
through the firmest reasonings and through the statements of those who follow scripture // 2.2.4 //
Because of the rarity of those with pure understanding, because of the multitude of those with little knowledge, /
because of the <s>tāmasic</s> nature of the world, because of the attachment to false knowledge, /

children.text: vidveṣāt parame tattve tattvavediṣu cāniśam // MAnuv_2,2.5 //
children.translated_text: because of hatred toward the supreme reality and toward the knowers of reality, constantly // 2.2.5 //
because of the connection with beginningless impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), because of the multitude of <s>asuras</s> (demons), /
because of being grasped through obstinate adherence — doctrines always persist // 2.2.6 //
Nevertheless, for those of pure understanding, who are connected with the grace of the Lord, /
the reasonings that follow scripture always destroy the darkness // 2.2.7 //
Thus the Lord of knowledge properly made the refutation of [rival] doctrines /
for the attainment of the sharpening of the intellect of His own devotees // 2.2.8 //
The non-theists declare that reality is just two: conscious and non-conscious. /
They say that the non-conscious is divided into twenty-five categories; /

children.text: cetanaṃ tadasaṅkhayātaṃ bhinnamanyad layaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.9 //
children.translated_text: the conscious is innumerable, different, and the other undergoes dissolution // 2.2.9 //
The agency of the non-conscious is asserted as independent; /
and the mutual difference of effects would persist up to dissolution // 2.2.10 //
Some say that the conscious is the experiencer; others say not even that — /
that experience is due to the power of essential consciousness and self-luminosity // 2.2.11 //
And the non-grasping of the distinction between <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and one's own nature — /
the proponents of non-experience call experience [the result of] grasping the difference between those two // 2.2.12 //
For the proponents of experience, liberation is proclaimed [as the goal]; the same for the proponents of non-experience; /
because the Lord is not included [in their system], neither of these two is proper in reasoning // 2.2.13 //
When the origination of cloth is seen to follow the will of a conscious being, /
by what [reasoning] is the same nature of another [effect] — which is a real thing — prevented? // 2.2.14 //

children.text: na ca kācit pramoktārthe śrutireva pramā hi naḥ /
children.translated_text: And there is no <s>Śruti</s> whatsoever for the purpose of the liberator; <s>Śruti</s> alone is our valid authority; /
the trustworthiness of the speaker cannot be established by the stated method // 2.2.15 //
Because of accepting the intrinsic invalidity [of cognition], like a <s>māyāvādin</s>, /

children.text: svoktākhilaniṣedhī syānna ca kiñcit prasiddhayati // MAnuv_2,2.16 //
children.translated_text: he would negate everything stated by himself — and nothing is established // 2.2.16 //
'This is not under the control of the non-conscious, because it is a real thing, like what is already established' — /

children.text: ityeva pratiṣiddhasya kena mūlānumā bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.17 //
children.translated_text: of this very thing that has been refuted, what would be the basic inference? // 2.2.17 //
Arrangement (<s>racanā</s>) is an independently operating activity, and how can that belong to the non-conscious? /
'Non-consciousness' and 'independence' — this is self-contradicted // 2.2.18 //
The knowers know independence as merely the following of one's own will; /

children.text: kuta icchācetanasya secchaṃ cet kimacetanam // MAnuv_2,2.19 //
children.translated_text: how can there be will in the non-conscious? If it has will, then how is it non-conscious? // 2.2.19 //
'I desire' — precisely this is one's own experience; because of obstruction by [that experience], /
will is absent from the non-conscious; and if there is non-grasping of difference here [between conscious and non-conscious] // 2.2.20 //

children.text: kathaṃ na sa ghaṭasya syānmano ma iti bhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: how would that not apply to a pot? [One would have to say] 'the mind is not I' — from difference; /
since even the mind is grasped [as conscious], both-natured-ness [would follow] // 2.2.21 //
But desire is of the mind; desire, from the distinction of pleasant and unpleasant, /

children.text: dvaividhyaṃ dṛśyate cāsya tasmād bhedāgrahaḥ kutaḥ // MAnuv_2,2.22 //
children.translated_text: is seen to be twofold — therefore, whence is the non-grasping of difference? // 2.2.22 //
Because of the impossibility of arrangement, the inference of an omniscient [being] is not reached; /

children.text: acetanaṃ jagatkartṛ payo 'mbvādi ca nopamā // MAnuv_2,2.23 //
children.translated_text: the non-conscious is not the creator of the world — milk, water, and the like are not [valid] analogies // 2.2.23 //
From the statement that this [Lord] governs [both] the conscious and the non-conscious — /
even when there is a twofold [nature] of desire and so forth, whence the self's ownership? // 2.2.24 //
What is directly established in experience can be displaced in some way; /
the ownership of desire is itself stated — not that [it is] the state of having desire // 2.2.25 //
Even when partially under its control, ownership would exist as in the world; /
of desire and the like, which are entirely dependent on the self — how much more so of the supreme Lord // 2.2.26 //
And the ownership of desire that is established in experience — even Vedic speech /
is unable to displace; therefore, it [<s>Śruti</s>] speaks of something else // 2.2.27 //
If the desirer of liberation were different from the one who will be liberated, /

children.text: mokṣakāmasya kiṃ tena svanāśārthaṃ ca ko yatet // MAnuv_2,2.28 //
children.translated_text: what use is that to the desirer of liberation? And who would strive for one's own destruction? // 2.2.28 //
Agency is perceived in the very same [entity] as experiencer-ship; /

children.text: vibhāge ca tayormānaṃ naiva kiñcit kvacid bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.29 //
children.translated_text: and there is never any valid authority whatsoever anywhere for the separation of those two // 2.2.29 //
This one who has undertaken the vow of opposing every valid authority — /
he would be compared to a <s>māyāvādin</s>; and by the word 'ca,' he is refuted // 2.2.30 //
But the theistic <s>Sāṅkhya</s> says: endowed with the power of the field and of grace, /
the Lord exists, self-luminous, free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s>, and the rest // 2.2.31 //
That very <s>Prakṛti</s> has the power of the field; the <s>jīva</s> has the power of the seed; /
the Lord is remembered as having divine power, like a rain-cloud // 2.2.32 //
<s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is like the earth; the <s>jīva</s>, merely by proximity, /
is like one who sows seeds — thus the Lord Himself declares here // 2.2.33 //

children.text: anyatra kāpi śaktirna svātantryeṇeśa eva hi /
children.translated_text: No power elsewhere exists independently — the Lord alone /
directly impels those powers, and they are always dependent on Him // 2.2.34 //
The cognitions and activities of <s>sattā</s> (existence), <s>pradhāna</s>, and <s>puruṣa</s>, /

children.text: pravṛttayaśca tāḥ sarvā nityaṃ nityātmanā yataḥ // MAnuv_2,2.35 //
children.translated_text: and their powers — all of these always [exist] through the eternal Self // 2.2.35 //
Just as the Lord eternally, through His eternal power, by His own nature, /

children.text: niyāmayati nityaṃ ca na ṛte tvaditi śruteḥ // MAnuv_2,2.36 //
children.translated_text: eternally regulates — 'not without You' — thus the <s>Śruti</s> [declares] // 2.2.36 //
'Own-nature, <s>jīva</s>, <s>karmas</s>, substance, time, <s>Śruti</s>, actions — /

children.text: yatprasādādime santi na santi yadupekṣayā // MAnuv_2,2.37 //
children.translated_text: by whose grace these exist, and by whose disregard they do not exist' // 2.2.37 //

children.text: iti śruterna sattādyā api nārāyaṇaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: — from this <s>Śruti</s>, neither <s>sattā</s> (existence) and the rest [can function] without <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; /
therefore the doctrine of <s>Patañjali</s>, <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>, and others does not lead to the goal of man // 2.2.38 //
The <s>Cārvākas</s> say: the only valid means of knowledge is perception — no other, anywhere; /

children.text: deha ātmā pumarthaśca kāmārthābhyāṃ vinā na hi // MAnuv_2,2.39 //
children.translated_text: the body is the self, and there is no human goal apart from pleasure and desire // 2.2.39 //
If so, what is the purpose of his philosophical system, which is within the range of perception? /

children.text: labdhastenaiva hi naraiḥ śāstrāt kiṃ mohanaṃ vinā // MAnuv_2,2.40 //
children.translated_text: it has been obtained by people through that [Lord] alone — what [use is] a scripture, apart from delusion? // MAnuv_2,2.40 //
Being devoid of benefit to oneself and others, [the materialist system] is fruitless even by its own doctrine.
Why does the scripture babble in vain, like a madman, on its own? // MAnuv_2,2.41 //
The self, different from the body, shines as the experiencer of embodied beings.

children.text: mama deha iti vyaktaṃ mamārtha itivat sadā // MAnuv_2,2.42 //
children.translated_text: 'My body' — clearly, like [saying] 'my property,' always [indicates the self]. // MAnuv_2,2.42 //
By what is it ascertained that perception alone is a means of valid knowledge?

children.text: yadi tatsādhakaṃ vedaprāmāṇye na kathaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.43 //
children.translated_text: If there is [a means] that establishes it, why would the validity of the <s>Veda</s> not obtain? // MAnuv_2,2.43 //
And the non-validity of other [means of knowledge] is nowhere ascertained by a [valid] means of knowledge.
A thesis that is devoid of purpose by its own doctrine is to be disregarded — such is this [materialism]. // MAnuv_2,2.44 //
If the insentient operates because of the proximity of the sentient,
even so, because it is not preceded by intelligence, the stated fault remains the same. // MAnuv_2,2.45 //
The status of being the principal (<s>aṅgin</s>) belongs to the <s>puruṣa</s> (person/self) alone — this is experienced by all.
And by the statement that it is [merely] a limb of that — one would be a denier of everything.
What more, since from the denial of this Lord of all, [the denial of] everything [follows]. // MAnuv_2,2.46 //
If the principal status belongs to that [<s>puruṣa</s>] alone, and if there is independence — but [there is] not complete [independence],
because of inability even to impel it, another independent [entity] is required. // MAnuv_2,2.47 //
And the independence of this [<s>puruṣa</s>] is not [tenable], because of contradiction with perception and the like,
and because of the faults of not acting for [one's own] benefit and so forth. A good [doctrine] does not regard [anything] as Lord-less. // MAnuv_2,2.48 //
One who is different from the transmigrating [soul], the Lord of all, of all powers, incomparable —
that the existence and the like of this [universe], both sentient and insentient, is dependent on Him —

children.text: nāṅgīkurvanti ye teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca samā ime // MAnuv_2,2.49 //
children.translated_text: those who do not accept this — all these [faults] are equal for them. // MAnuv_2,2.49 //
Therefore, by the authority of <s>śruti</s> and by reasoning, <s>Hari</s> is supreme.
He is the most worthy of acceptance, eternal — this is firmly established by all. // MAnuv_2,2.50 //
Eternal knowledge, effort, and desire — others who declare the Lord endowed with [these] five [qualities],
[say that] impelled by His will and by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit),
the atoms (<s>paramāṇus</s>), of four classes, all combine in pairs. // MAnuv_2,2.51 //
From two atoms alone, a dyad (<s>dvayaṇuka</s>) is born.
From three dyads, a triad (<s>tṛyaṇuka</s>); from four of those, [an entity] of that nature [is formed]. // MAnuv_2,2.52 //
Then, without fixed rule, the production of entities having parts and sections [occurs].
Then, again without fixed rule, the production of all composite things [occurs]. // MAnuv_2,2.53 //
The material cause, called 'inherent' (<s>samavāyi</s>), is the atom and the like.
The will of the Lord, <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), and time are considered the efficient cause (<s>nimitta kāraṇa</s>). // MAnuv_2,2.54 //
Universals (<s>sāmānya</s>), ultimate particularities (<s>antyaviśeṣa</s>), and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) — these three

children.text: nityaṃ kriyā anityāstu guṇadravye dvirūpake // MAnuv_2,2.55 //
