children.translated_text: are permanent. Actions (<s>kriyā</s>) are impermanent, while qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and substances (<s>dravya</s>) are of two kinds [permanent and impermanent]. // MAnuv_2,2.55 //
For qualities and actions in the effect, the material cause is different from the inherent cause.
Qualities and the like residing in the cause — conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is the [efficient] cause for substances. // MAnuv_2,2.56 //
Even when the [<s>Vaiśeṣika</s>] system is thus established, a particular [problem] is conceived therein:

children.text: dvayaṇuke paramāṇau ca hrasvatvaṃ parimaṇḍalam // MAnuv_2,2.57 //
children.translated_text: in the dyad and in the atom — smallness (<s>hrasvatva</s>) and spherical magnitude (<s>parimaṇḍala</s>). // MAnuv_2,2.57 //

children.text: na kāraṇaṃ kāryaguṇe vairūpyaṃ tatra kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: [These are] not the cause of the quality in the effect; dissimilarity [of cause and effect quality] is the cause —
thus they say. But then the Lord of Knowledge (<s>Vidyādhīśa</s>), the Lord Himself, spoke: // MAnuv_2,2.58 //
Greatness (<s>mahattva</s>) and length (<s>dīrghatva</s>) are conceived in triads and the like.
And from that, a similar effect arises in the products of that. // MAnuv_2,2.59 //
Just as from smallness and from spherical magnitude too,

children.text: jāyeta sadṛśaṃ kārye parimāṇaṃ samatvataḥ // MAnuv_2,2.60 //
children.translated_text: a similar magnitude would arise in the effect, because of the equality [of reasoning]. // MAnuv_2,2.60 //
If not, then from greatness too and from length too, there would not be

children.text: sadṛśasya hi kāryasya naiva yogaḥ kathañcana // MAnuv_2,2.61 //
children.translated_text: a similar effect — there is simply no possibility at all. // MAnuv_2,2.61 //
Imperceptibility would thus follow for effects, because of the atomic size [of their causes].
If [you say] no — then how is there greatness in the atom, even in the minute one?
How is atomicity not predicated even of triads and their antecedents? // MAnuv_2,2.62 //
Perceptibility and its absence, with respect to all [entities], depend on the person.

children.text: aṇutvaṃ ca mahattvaṃ ca yato vastuvyapekṣayā // MAnuv_2,2.63 //
children.translated_text: For atomicity and greatness are relative to the entity [being measured]. // MAnuv_2,2.63 //

children.text: tāratamyasthitā yasmāt padārthāḥ sarva eva ca /
children.translated_text: Since all entities are established in a scale of gradation,
just as there is a resting-place for greatness, so also is there one for atomicity — this is desired. // MAnuv_2,2.64 //
If [you say] no, because of being [mere] magnitude — then even for greatness there is a resting-place.
It is seen as 'infinite' — and likewise there is infinity even in the atom. // MAnuv_2,2.65 //
The Lord is not delimited by the quality of greatness — 'He is only this much';
likewise, of the atom too, there is never the [delimitation of] 'this much in extent.' // MAnuv_2,2.66 //
If it is understood that some resting-place of infinite parts exists,
[it] cannot be ascertained — solely because of contradiction. // MAnuv_2,2.67 //
Only by the measure of the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>), time and space too are not finite.
And the non-termination of the atom too is seen by the witness in both [time and space]. // MAnuv_2,2.68 //

children.text: yadi no sākṣigamyaṃ tanmahattvaṃ kena gamyate /
children.translated_text: If it [is said that] greatness is not cognized by the witness, by what is it cognized?
The resting-place is seen through gradation, by means of inference. // MAnuv_2,2.69 //
If from scripture (<s>āgama</s>) that infinite greatness is understood,
why is it not ascertained that atomicity too is infinite? // MAnuv_2,2.70 //
For greatness and atomicity, no resting-place is apprehended.
Infinity is something different [from both] — equal for both greatness and atomicity. // MAnuv_2,2.71 //
Just as in numerability, for plurality and paucity,
infinity of parts is found — [only] that-much-ness is counted. // MAnuv_2,2.72 //
'Smaller than the small and greater than the great' — the <s>Bhagavān</s> is declared by scripture.
The word denoting infinity attains authority even in the twofold infinity. // MAnuv_2,2.73 //

children.text: yāti naiva guṇālpatvaṃ kālātpatvaṃ ca mānagam /
children.translated_text: It does not [lead to] paucity of qualities, and temporally limited smallness is not [validly] measured.
One who pervades all time would have existence even in a small time. // MAnuv_2,2.74 //

children.text: mahāguṇasya cālpo 'pi guṇaḥ syāditi ced bhavet /
children.translated_text: If [one says] a small quality too would belong to one of great qualities — let it be so.

children.text: tāvattvameva naiva syād deśe 'pyetanna no matam // MAnuv_2,2.75 //
children.translated_text: That-much-ness alone would simply not exist — in space too, this is not our view. // MAnuv_2,2.75 //
For even smallness of the great — like space — the knower of the <s>Veda</s> declares.

children.text: yadyalpadeśasaṃsthānaṃ na sarvatrāpi no bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.76 //
children.translated_text: If it is situated in a small space, it would not fail to be in all [spaces] too. // MAnuv_2,2.76 //
For one who is situated in small spaces, omnipresence would certainly follow.
For one not established even in one [place], whence could there be presence everywhere? // MAnuv_2,2.77 //

children.text: śūnyatvameva tasya syād yasyaikatrāpi na sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: There would be mere voidness for that which has no existence even in one [place].

children.text: ato nāṇutvaviśrāntirna mahattvasya ca kvacit // MAnuv_2,2.78 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no resting-place for atomicity, nor for greatness, anywhere. // MAnuv_2,2.78 //
Endowed with infinity in both, therefore, if there is a primarily great [entity],

children.text: tacca brahma paraṃ sākṣāt sarvānantyayutaṃ sadā // MAnuv_2,2.79 //
children.translated_text: that is Supreme <s>Brahman</s> directly — always endowed with all infinities. // MAnuv_2,2.79 //

children.text: yadi sākṣī svayambhāto na mānaṃ kena gamyate /
children.translated_text: If the witness is self-luminous, by what means of knowledge is it cognized?
And that perception and the like are means of knowledge — [this would lead to] infinite regress. // MAnuv_2,2.80 //
Therefore, all entities always have parts.
Because of connection in all directions, indivisibility is the ultimate atomic nature. // MAnuv_2,2.81 //
From the unrestricted conjunction of those [parts], the production of entities would occur.

children.text: dvayoreva tu saṃyoga iti kenāvasīyate // MAnuv_2,2.82 //
children.translated_text: By what is it ascertained that the conjunction is of only two [atoms]? // MAnuv_2,2.82 //
The qualities of the cause would then be present in the effect too.
Through gradation, all [things] are both great and atomic. // MAnuv_2,2.83 //

children.text: na ca tatproktasṛṣṭau tu mānaṃ kevalakalpanā /
children.translated_text: And for the creation declared by them, the [means of] proof — [it is] mere fabrication.

children.text: kathaṃ sākṣimitasyāsya śaknuyād vāraṇe kvacit // MAnuv_2,2.84 //
children.translated_text: How could it succeed in obstructing what is witnessed by the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>)? // MAnuv_2,2.84 //
If this is witnessed by the witness, then inference does not operate there.
Since it cannot be made a thesis, how indeed could inference arise? // MAnuv_2,2.85 //
Where there is no stepping-ground, who could reach that domain?
And the word 'another place' (<s>deśāntara</s>) is like the word 'hare's horn.' // MAnuv_2,2.86 //

children.text: sadṛśaṃ ca sajātīyaṃ nāsmatpakṣe kim eva hi /
children.translated_text: 'Similar' and 'of the same class' — in our system, what [need] is there indeed?
By the very mode through which an utterly unproven [entity] is inferred,
by that very [mode], the existence of a hare's horn and the like can be imagined. // MAnuv_2,2.87 //
Wherever perception or scripture may be a determining [factor],
that alone is the valid pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) — not another, arising from a doubtful foundation. // MAnuv_2,2.88 //
Pervasion is not ascertained by mere co-observation.
Only when the non-deviation is either perception-born or from scripture,

children.text: tannirdhāritayuktirvā vyāptiḥ saivāparā na hi // MAnuv_2,2.89 //
children.translated_text: or a reasoning established by that — that alone is the [valid] pervasion, not otherwise. // MAnuv_2,2.89 //
Otherwise, even the birth of a seventh taste would be entailed by inference.

children.text: aniṣṭāni ca sarvāṇi hyanumā kāmacāriṇī // MAnuv_2,2.90 //
children.translated_text: And all undesirable [conclusions] — inference would roam freely. // MAnuv_2,2.90 //
The relation of cause and effect, and of qualities and the rest — the fivefold [category]:

children.text: bhinnasyaiva tu sambandhaḥ samavāyo 'nya īryate // MAnuv_2,2.91 //
children.translated_text: it is the connection of what is distinct — inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) is said to be [yet] another. // MAnuv_2,2.91 //
Because of the sameness of distinctness, its conjunction with both [relata] would certainly follow.

children.text: sa svanirvāhakaścet syād dravyameva tathā na kim // MAnuv_2,2.92 //
children.translated_text: If it is self-sustaining, why not substance (<s>dravya</s>) too [be self-sustaining] in the same way? // MAnuv_2,2.92 //
If distinction, belonging-to-that, and the like are ascertained in what is non-different,
by what reason is the negation of the form of quality, action, and the like [justified]? // MAnuv_2,2.93 //
Substance alone, therefore, through being of the nature of infinite distinctions (<s>viśeṣas</s>), always
is the cause of diverse usage; infinity is through distinction. // MAnuv_2,2.94 //
And the distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>) and the distinguished one are identical [as entities] — like inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) [being self-relating].
Because of the fault of conceptual excess, [distinction] is not a separate category. // MAnuv_2,2.95 //
Having imagined six categories including non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>),

children.text: ekasmin sa viśeṣaścet kiṃ pūrvaṃ tasya vismṛtiḥ // MAnuv_2,2.96 //
children.translated_text: if distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>) is in one [entity] — what, was it formerly forgotten by them? // MAnuv_2,2.96 //
That [distinction] by which, being perception-established, all usage takes place,

children.text: bhāvābhāvavibhāgena yaṃ vinā na kathañcana // MAnuv_2,2.97 //
children.translated_text: through the division of existence and non-existence — without which, [usage] does not [occur] in any way — // MAnuv_2,2.97 //
and the cognition of non-difference too, with regard to cause and effect and so forth —
in this entity ending in non-existence, [it] is ascertained as possessing distinction. // MAnuv_2,2.98 //
In categories such as universals (<s>sāmānya</s>) and the like, all [properties] such as 'residing in that' and the like —

children.text: kathaṃ dharmā nivāryante vastvaikye 'pi hi vādibhiḥ // MAnuv_2,2.99 //
children.translated_text: how are [these] properties precluded by disputants, even when the entity is one? // MAnuv_2,2.99 //
The residing-in-that of the effect, the pervasion and the like of qualities —

children.text: kathaṃ viśeṣo naivāsti sa ca dharmo 'paro yadi // MAnuv_2,2.100 //
children.translated_text: how is there no distinction [there]? And if that is a different property, // MAnuv_2,2.100 //
there would be an excess over the six categories; and even without a fixed [number of] categories,
from the property of a property being a further property, it would lead to infinite regress. // MAnuv_2,2.101 //
A universal of a universal too, and a quality of a quality too — therefore,

children.text: nāṅgīkṛtaḥ sa ca yadi nānavasthā kvacid bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.102 //
children.translated_text: if that is not accepted, then there is no infinite regress anywhere. // MAnuv_2,2.102 //
In our system, qualities and the like, and their possessors, through distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>),

children.text: ananyatvānnānavasthā bhedo nāśe bhavet tathā // MAnuv_2,2.103 //
children.translated_text: because of non-otherness, there is no infinite regress; difference would [apply only] in destruction. // MAnuv_2,2.103 //
Since distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>), relying on distinction itself, is powerful,
and since from the authority of vision [i.e. perception] — how is there contradiction in perception? // MAnuv_2,2.104 //
For both contradiction and non-contradiction are measured by perception and [scripture].

children.text: tato dṛṣṭe virodhastu sadbhirāpādyate katham // MAnuv_2,2.105 //
children.translated_text: Then how could contradiction in what is perceived be posited by the wise? // MAnuv_2,2.105 //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> is non-different from Himself [in essence], yet different from what is other than Him.
His properties are eternal — all of them never differ from Him. // MAnuv_2,2.106 //
In other [entities], the properties are of both forms — collectively cut off [in destruction].

children.text: bhāve ta eva cocchedāt tadanye ca samastaśaḥ // MAnuv_2,2.107 //
children.translated_text: In [their] existence, they are those very same [properties]; and because of [their] destruction, they are other, in their entirety. // MAnuv_2,2.107 //
Through the non-difference of part and whole, the conjunction of parts [occurs]
in the whole — hence no infinite regress; even though in parts there is no resting-place, // MAnuv_2,2.108 //

children.text: ekasmin jāta evānyaḥ saṃyogo jāyate yadi /
children.translated_text: if when one [conjunction] is born, another conjunction arises,

children.text: anavasthā tadaiva syāt saṃyogaikye bhavet kva sā // MAnuv_2,2.109 //
children.translated_text: infinite regress would follow then; but when conjunction is one, where would it [arise]? // MAnuv_2,2.109 //
Since conjunction is seen in the part, when it is seen, what infinite regress [is there]?

children.text: yadyaṃśago na saṃyogaḥ kāryeṣu prathimā katham // MAnuv_2,2.110 //
children.translated_text: If conjunction does not go to the part, how [is there] extension in effects? // MAnuv_2,2.110 //
The atom has no atomicity, no greatness — this is an astonishing statement!
Without reference to the extension of atoms, even in the triad, that [extension exists]. /

children.text: paramāṇormahattvaṃ ca vinetyetad vacaḥ katham // MAnuv_2,2.111 //
children.translated_text: and the greatness of the atom — without removing [this objection], how [can] this statement [stand]? // MAnuv_2,2.111 //
This non-difference of the possessor-of-parts from its parts — yet difference through the part, [which itself has] difference — /
is the object of universal perception; how indeed can it be refuted? // MAnuv_2,2.112 //
Conjunction and disjunction and difference, each separately, /
are seen to have mutual counter-correlation in both [cases]. // MAnuv_2,2.113 //

children.text: bhinnā iti tu bhedānāṃ samudāyo hi dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: 'They are different' — but what is seen is the collection of differences. /
Just as there is difference among entities, even so between these two [conjunction and disjunction]. // MAnuv_2,2.114 //
The difference of this from that, and of that from this — [difference] is seen as having two properties. /

children.text: tatraikavacanaṃ yattad viprāṇāṃ bhojanaṃ yathā // MAnuv_2,2.115 //
children.translated_text: Therein, the use of the singular is like 'the feeding of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.' // MAnuv_2,2.115 //
Humanness and the like also — they are considered as the properties of each respective [individual]. /

children.text: na sarvadharma eko 'sti samudāyastu bhinnagaḥ // MAnuv_2,2.116 //
children.translated_text: There is no single property of all; the collection, however, belongs to the different [individuals]. // MAnuv_2,2.116 //

children.text: etādṛśaṃ ca sādṛśyaṃ padārtheṣu pṛthak pṛthak /
children.translated_text: And such similarity among entities, individually, /

children.text: ekasmin sa vinaṣṭe 'pi yato 'nyatraiva dṛśyate // MAnuv_2,2.117 //
children.translated_text: since even when one is destroyed, it is seen elsewhere. // MAnuv_2,2.117 //
Whence would humanness again be desired for one who has attained the state of ashes? /

children.text: ekatve nāsti mānaṃ ca śrutirapyāha sādaram // MAnuv_2,2.118 //
children.translated_text: And there is no means of proof for unity; even <s>śruti</s> declares respectfully — // MAnuv_2,2.118 //
all entities are different, and have different properties; /
yet they are non-different from their own respective properties and from their own natures in every way. // MAnuv_2,2.119 //
And the properties, whose destruction has not occurred, have a twofold nature. /
Therefore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is not non-different from anything except his own qualities. // MAnuv_2,2.120 //
Thus, even etymological derivation is understood through similarity alone. /
The word operates simultaneously upon all similar [things]. // MAnuv_2,2.121 //
Nevertheless, from obtainment and from the use of the singular, specifically, /
the understanding of what is desired would be [achieved]; for the capacity resides in the similarity. // MAnuv_2,2.122 //

children.text: tādṛśo 'yaṃ ca tacchabda iti jñāpayati sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: 'This one is of that kind' — and that word clearly indicates [thus]. /

children.text: jātitaścet kathaṃ tāsu tatra cedanavasthitiḥ // MAnuv_2,2.123 //
children.translated_text: If [it is] from universals (<s>jāti</s>) — how [to avoid] the regress in those? If [universals exist] there — [then there is] no stable ground. // MAnuv_2,2.123 //
Likewise, the knowledge of the particular is vitiated by the absence of particularity. /
If that [particularity] exists, of that too, [there is] no stable ground in [further] particularities. // MAnuv_2,2.124 //
How can the essential nature also be known, if it pervades [all instances]? /
The [procedure] ending in a single derivation is vitiated by the regress and so forth. /
Because of the cumbersomeness of postulation, therefore, the postulation of a pervading [universal] is not appropriate. // MAnuv_2,2.125 //
Even [a property] that is adventitiously qualified — is that entity [something other]? What of it? /

children.text: anyat tadeva cedagnimattvaṃ kiṃ tatra bhaṇyate // MAnuv_2,2.126 //
children.translated_text: If it is that very thing — what is to be said about 'possessing fire' therein? // MAnuv_2,2.126 //
If it is merely the conjunction with fire — that would be proving what is already established. /

children.text: bhūdharasyāgnisaṃyogo yadi ṣaṣṭhayartha eva kaḥ // MAnuv_2,2.127 //
children.translated_text: If a mountain's conjunction with fire — what is the meaning of the genitive [case]? // MAnuv_2,2.127 //

children.text: samavāyo yadi hy asya caikatvāt siddhasādhanam /
children.translated_text: If it is <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) of this [fire in the mountain] — then, because of [their supposed] unity, it is proving what is already established. /
If the difference [between them] is adventitious — whence is unity desired? // MAnuv_2,2.128 //
For the inexplicable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) is not accepted by them; therefore, since the adventitious [properties] of both /

children.text: satyatvāt ko viśeṣaḥ syānmāyāvādyanyathā bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.129 //
children.translated_text: are real — what distinction would there be? Otherwise [one] would become a <s>Māyāvādin</s> (illusionist). // MAnuv_2,2.129 //
Produced by a condition and knowable through it — thus it would be adventitious. /
In both cases, there would be infinite <s>samavāyas</s> (inherences), here and there. /

children.text: bhinnatvaṃ caiva teṣvasti ko viśeṣa upādhige // MAnuv_2,2.130 //
children.translated_text: And there is indeed difference among those — what distinction [from other categories] in the adventitious? // MAnuv_2,2.130 //
A <s>samavāya</s> that is indeed non-existent as something other is cognized. /

children.text: upādhinā tadgamakamanumānaṃ na mā bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.131 //
children.translated_text: The condition is the indicator of that; let inference not be [rejected]. // MAnuv_2,2.131 //
Thus the origination of the existent from the non-existent — <s>samavāya</s> is [merely] supposed. /
Even therein, there is nothing whatsoever that prevents the faults already stated. // MAnuv_2,2.132 //
In our position, since <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) is accepted everywhere, /

children.text: nāsti doṣaḥ kvacid bhāvo hyabhāvaśca sa eva hi // MAnuv_2,2.133 //
children.translated_text: there is no defect anywhere; for both existence and non-existence are indeed that very thing. // MAnuv_2,2.133 //

children.text: abhāvasya ca dharmāḥ syurbhāvāsteṣāṃ ca te 'khilāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the properties of non-existence would be existences; and all those [properties belong] to them. /
From the authority of direct perception — all this is not capable of being refuted. /

children.text: sarve bhāvā abhāvāśca padārthāstena sarvadā // MAnuv_2,2.134 //
children.translated_text: All existences and non-existences are therefore always real entities. // MAnuv_2,2.134 //
Nevertheless, that which is first the object of the intellect of negation — /

children.text: so 'bhāvo vidhibuddhestu gocaraḥ prathamaṃ paraḥ // MAnuv_2,2.135 //
children.translated_text: that is non-existence; but the other [— existence —] is first the object of the intellect of affirmation. // MAnuv_2,2.135 //
Therefore, 'destroyed' and 'difference' and so forth are understood as simply 'existing.' /

children.text: astyabhāvo 'sti ca dhvaṃso dehābhāvaśca bhasmatā // MAnuv_2,2.136 //
children.translated_text: 'Non-existence exists'; 'destruction exists'; 'the non-existence of the body is the state of being ashes' — // MAnuv_2,2.136 //
and so forth — all of this is proper, from the authority of direct perception and other means of knowledge. /

children.text: anyonyābhāvabhedau ca pṛthaktavaṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak // MAnuv_2,2.137 //
children.translated_text: Mutual non-existence, difference, and separateness — each separately — // MAnuv_2,2.137 //
what they postulate as [identical with each other] — that has been dismissed because of cumbersomeness of postulation. /

children.text: paryāyatvena te śabdā jñāyante sarva eva hi // MAnuv_2,2.138 //
children.translated_text: Those words are understood as synonymous, each and every one. // MAnuv_2,2.138 //

children.text: bhedasya tu svarūpatve ye vadanti ca śūnyatām /
children.translated_text: But those who assert that difference is of the nature of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness/voidness) — /
how remarkable they are! — since the counter-correlate-hood of another is accepted [by them]. // MAnuv_2,2.139 //

children.text: pratiyogino hi bhedo 'yaṃ natu svasmāt kathañcana /
children.translated_text: For this difference is [in relation to] the counter-correlate, and not in any way from oneself. /

children.text: vibhāgenālpataiva syāt kuta eva ca śūnyatā // MAnuv_2,2.140 //
children.translated_text: Through division, there would be mere diminishment — whence, then, voidness? // MAnuv_2,2.140 //

children.text: na śūnyānāṃ hi saṃyogād bhāvo vastuna iṣyate /
children.translated_text: For the existence of a real entity is not accepted from the conjunction of voids. /
And the verbal root is in the sense of 'tearing apart' — it denotes the quality of division. // MAnuv_2,2.141 //

children.text: avidāraṇe 'pi hyāsyasya bhinnāvoṣṭhau tu tasya ca /
children.translated_text: For even without tearing apart his mouth, his two lips are distinct. /
Therefore, <s>Māyāvāda</s> (the doctrine of illusion) is rejected as being the statement of a madman. // MAnuv_2,2.142 //
The Lord is not devoid of bliss, is an ocean of ever-flowing, infinite qualities; /
the Lord is not to be measured merely by eight qualities, because of being immeasurable. // MAnuv_2,2.143 //
'In me, of infinite qualities, infinite, of infinite form by virtue of qualities, /
an ocean of the power, knowledge, and greatness of infinite qualities' — // MAnuv_2,2.144 //
'<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, supreme, the supreme abode, beyond all conscious beings' — /
by these and infinite other Vedic and related statements, it is ascertained. // MAnuv_2,2.145 //
How indeed can the infinite-qualitied nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s> be refuted? /
And if infinite <s>viśeṣas</s> (distinctions) are prevented, [then] the knowledge of those [would also be prevented]. // MAnuv_2,2.146 //
How is the having-that-and-that-as-object posited for the purpose of omniscience? /
And adventitious distinction has already been refuted previously. // MAnuv_2,2.147 //
And by those who have denied even the self-luminosity of knowledge — /

children.text: kathaṃ sarvajñatā tasya svajñānādhigamaṃ vinā // MAnuv_2,2.148 //
children.translated_text: how can his omniscience [exist] without the cognition of his own knowledge? // MAnuv_2,2.148 //
Knowledge comprehending the universe is one; knowledge of that knowledge is another, supreme. /
Thus, by just these two knowledges, the Supreme Lord is omniscient. // MAnuv_2,2.149 //
If [one says] this is precisely the meaning — if that is ascertained through the knowledge of that [primary knowledge], /
then it would be self-luminosity itself; for this knowledge is a qualifier [of the self]. // MAnuv_2,2.150 //
If [it is known] by yet another knowledge — then there would be a regress. /
Therefore, self-luminosity is irrefutable — [this] follows [inescapably]. // MAnuv_2,2.151 //

children.text: sukhavān duḥkhavāṃśca syāditi vyāptiśca no bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'One who has pleasure would also have pain' — this concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) does not hold. /
Freedom from suffering and supreme bliss are declared by <s>śruti</s> itself for the Lord. // MAnuv_2,2.152 //
'He who transcends hunger and thirst and grief and so forth' — /

children.text: ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān vipāpmetyādikā ca sā // MAnuv_2,2.153 //
children.translated_text: 'knowing the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, free from evil' — and that [<s>śruti</s> states] thus. // MAnuv_2,2.153 //
If it is said that the Lord's desired nature and suffering are [merely] adventitious — /
when this is stated, what reply would one who is intent on disregarding <s>śruti</s> give? // MAnuv_2,2.154 //
And there cannot be a desire for one's own suffering; therefore this is refuted. /
By the mere simultaneous observation [of bliss and suffering in the Lord], one becomes a denier of the <s>śrutis</s>. // MAnuv_2,2.155 //

children.text: yajñāder api pāpasya hetutvaṃ hiṃsayā yuteḥ /
children.translated_text: That even sacrifice and the like would be a cause of sin, because of being conjoined with violence — /
he does not infer [this]; how then [can] prohibition be merely adventitious therein? // MAnuv_2,2.156 //
How would the non-statement of freedom from suffering not become [merely] adventitious? /

children.text: aduḥkhamitarat sarvaṃ jīvā eva tu duḥkhinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Everything else is free from suffering; <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) alone are suffering ones. /
For the removal of their suffering, this <s>śruti</s> operates. // MAnuv_2,2.157 //

children.text: iti śrutirhi paramā śrutyuktir yadi kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: This <s>śruti</s> is indeed supreme — if the statement of <s>śruti</s> is the reason, /
what is to be accomplished by inference, which is like a dewlap on a goat's neck? // MAnuv_2,2.158 //
If through inference, a meaning seen in <s>śruti</s> is refuted — /

children.text: pūrvoktena prakāreṇa neśvaro dharma eva ca /
children.translated_text: by the method stated earlier, [then] neither the Lord nor <s>dharma</s> /

children.text: syāt tatphalaṃ ca tenātra śrutireva pramā bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.159 //
children.translated_text: would exist, nor its fruit — therefore, <s>śruti</s> alone should be the valid means of knowledge herein. // MAnuv_2,2.159 //
Since the Lord is established through inference, <s>śruti</s> would be the valid means of knowledge for <s>dharma</s>. /

children.text: tayā sarvaguṇaiḥ pūrṇa ukta īśo yatastataḥ // MAnuv_2,2.160 //
children.translated_text: Since by it, the Lord is declared to be full of all qualities — therefore // MAnuv_2,2.160 //
the inference of non-bliss [in him] — because of contradiction with [the inference that] apprehends the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) — /
would not be a valid means of knowledge; therefore, inference is not useful here. // MAnuv_2,2.161 //
Because of the eternal desiring of the Supreme Lord, because of atoms being eternal, /

children.text: adṛṣṭakālayoścaiva bhāvāt kāryaṃ sadā bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.162 //
children.translated_text: and because <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) and time also exist — effects should always come about. // MAnuv_2,2.162 //
For there is no distinction of time in that [atomist] position; in our view, [it is] of <s>Hari</s>. /
At the specific time alone is this — the desire for creation and so forth is eternal. // MAnuv_2,2.163 //
And the specific [moments] of time are always under the control of <s>Hari</s>'s will. /

children.text: sarve nimeṣā iti hi śrutirevāha sādaram // MAnuv_2,2.164 //
children.translated_text: 'All moments' — thus indeed <s>śruti</s> itself declares respectfully. // MAnuv_2,2.164 //
'He activates the power called time' — thus his word also [states]. /

children.text: kālasya kālagatvena na virodho 'pi kaścana // MAnuv_2,2.165 //
children.translated_text: Because time [derives] from the nature of time [i.e., is dependent on God], there is no contradiction whatsoever. // MAnuv_2,2.165 //
Because of the innumerable distinctions of will also, always, /

children.text: īśo deśaś ca kālaś ca svagatā eva sarvadā // MAnuv_2,2.166 //
children.translated_text: the Lord, space, and time are always internal to [the Lord] himself. // MAnuv_2,2.166 //

children.text: īśādhīnau ca tau nityaṃ tadādhārau ca tadgatau /
children.translated_text: And those two [space and time] are eternally dependent on the Lord, are his supports, and abide in him. /

children.text: iti śrutirapi prāha kāle svoddiṣṭa eva tu // MAnuv_2,2.167 //
children.translated_text: Thus <s>śruti</s> also declares — at the very time designated by him. // MAnuv_2,2.167 //
Therefore, the Lord always desires the creation of that [specific] time alone. /

children.text: syāt kālaḥ sa tadaiveti kālasya svagatatvataḥ // MAnuv_2,2.168 //
children.translated_text: Time would be that very [moment designated] — because of time's being internal to him. // MAnuv_2,2.168 //
'This desire is indeed from the very nature of the Lord' — so says <s>śruti</s>. /
Even the [inherent] nature is under the control of the Supreme Lord's will — so was stated earlier. // MAnuv_2,2.169 //
'Eternal and non-eternal' — and 'dependent on him' — thus the <s>śruti</s>. /
The non-eternality of atoms is inferable from the causes [such as] form, touch, and so forth. // MAnuv_2,2.170 //
Because of contradiction with the <s>śrutis</s>, that [Vaiśeṣika] view is not [accepted]. /
Therefore, this non-contradictory harmonization is to be adopted. // MAnuv_2,2.171 //
The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> and the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> [hold that] the world is momentary by its own nature, /
and [that it is] a collection of atoms, [arising] from the cause of time and <s>karma</s>; // MAnuv_2,2.172 //
at the time of arising, of those that are conjoined — the self too, and momentary persistence, /
an eternal continuum of these, existing in the form of the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). // MAnuv_2,2.173 //
Persistence in the form of formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), form (<s>rūpa</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and suffering; /
the absence of suffering they call pleasure — a continuum of formless knowledge. // MAnuv_2,2.174 //

children.text: mokṣaṃ sa samudāyo hi naikasmādeva yujyate /
children.translated_text: Liberation [they call] that very collection; for it is not appropriate from a single [element alone]. /
And the dual nature of both is not [established] — in dependence on the collection. // MAnuv_2,2.175 //
Therefore, because of mutual dependence, the collection is not appropriate. /
The awareness of a person's being-a-collection, through mutual dependence — // MAnuv_2,2.176 //
would exist even if it were eternal; and that [awareness] is caused by proximity. /
If so — the cause is effective only in producing [its] effect; // MAnuv_2,2.177 //
but the cause would not be operative in specific effects. /
Therefore, even the nature of a knower — [as defined by] conjunction of the self with object and sense — /
because of the absence of the conjunction-form, there would not be even that knowledge. // MAnuv_2,2.178 //
If the cause is held to produce specific effects, /
whence the uniformity of effects in all respects? // MAnuv_2,2.179 //
Therefore, because of non-determination, anything would be the cause of anything. /
And of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) too — whence would it produce specificity in that very [cause]? // MAnuv_2,2.180 //
Anything whatsoever would produce any specificity whatsoever in anything whatsoever. /

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ caiva yatkiñcid yasya kasyacit // MAnuv_2,2.181 //
children.translated_text: Both the effect and the cause would be anything whatsoever of anything whatsoever — // MAnuv_2,2.181 //
because of the absence of a determiner [for the relation that] 'this is the cause of that.' /

children.text: iti nityavināśitve kena mānena gamyate // MAnuv_2,2.182 //
children.translated_text: By what means of knowledge are perpetual existence and perpetual destruction ascertained? // MAnuv_2,2.182 //

children.text: ***[NOTE: jump in verse numbering, no lacuna in text!]***
yadyākāśasya sattvaṃ na kuta eva narādiṣu /
tau vinā na hy abhāvaś ca kvaciddṛṣṭaḥ kadācana /
na saṃskārārpakatvaṃ ca yujyate kasyacit kvacit // MAnuv_2,2.189 //
ato jñātaṃ mayetyādi na jñeyamanumā kutaḥ /
kuta ātmādikeṣu syād balyevānubhavo yataḥ // MAnuv_2,2.190 //
asambaddhaḥ kathaṃ pūrva uttare vāsanākaraḥ // MAnuv_2,2.192 //
vināśe cenna tatkāryaṃ kāryotpattau ca kā pramā // MAnuv_2,2.195 //
viśeṣadarśanaṃ mānaṃ yadi na sthairyadṛk kutaḥ /
diksukhe ca khadṛṣṭāntād bhāvau saccet kvacid bhaved // MAnuv_2,2.197 //
kathaṃ nu tasya buddhitvaṃ viśvamanyacca kimpramam // MAnuv_2,2.199 //
so 'haṃ tadidamevāhaṃ sukhī sad gaganaṃ diśaḥ /
durmataṃ ko nu gṛhṇīyād vināsuratatiṃ kvacit // MAnuv_2,2.202 //
sadivābhāti satyatvaṃ sāṃvṛtaṃ tasya ceṣyate // MAnuv_2,2.205 //
iti brūte tamuddiśya jagāda jagatāṃ guruḥ // MAnuv_2,2.207 //
nāsato jagato bhāvo na hi dṛṣṭāsato janiḥ /
sataḥ kvacit pramāṇaṃ ca dṛṣṭirevākhilād varam // MAnuv_2,2.208 //
kiṃ nānumīyate tadvad vastutvāt puruṣād bhavaḥ /
sarvasyāpi nacābhāvo viśvaṃ saditi gamyate // MAnuv_2,2.212 //
yadi sattvena kiñcātra bhramo naiva nivartate /
dṛṣṭasya bhrāntitā cet syādadṛṣṭe na bhramaḥ kutaḥ /
dṛśyatvād vimaṃta mithyā svapnavaccediyaṃ ca mā /
mithyā cet sādhyasiddhirna vyabhicāro na ced bhavet // MAnuv_2,2.217 //
tasya cetyanavasthā syāt sattvaṃ cāsyānubhūtitaḥ // MAnuv_2,2.218 //
tenāpyaṅgīkṛtaḥ samyak sa naḥ satyatvameva hi // MAnuv_2,2.220 //
naiva dṛṣṭā pramā sā ca na bhavet svavirodhataḥ // MAnuv_2,2.221 //
svarūpaṃ vastuno bhedo yanna tasya grahe grahaḥ /
anyathāsyāmunā bheda iti vaktuṃ na yujyate // MAnuv_2,2.223 //
syāt pratītivirodhācca na hi kaścit tathā vadet // MAnuv_2,2.224 //
viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaṃ ca tadbhāvaścaiva gṛhyate // MAnuv_2,2.225 //
ko virodhaḥ svarūpeṇa gṛhīto bheda eva tu /
kiñca bhedaḥ kathaṃ grāhya iti yaḥ paripṛcchati /
anyatvaṃ yadi siddhaṃ syāt kathamanyonyasaṃśrayaḥ // MAnuv_2,2.228 //
tatra santatibhedaśca svabhedo bheda eva ca /
ityetadapi no yuktaṃ na hi jñānatayā jagat /
tadrūpameva taditi niyamaḥ kena vāryate // MAnuv_2,2.237 //
aśeṣamāviruddhaṃ ca nirmānaṃ vyāhataṃ sadā // MAnuv_2,2.239 //
svavyāhatatvamityādyā doṣāḥ sarve bhavanti hi // MAnuv_2,2.240 //
lakṣaṇasya nivṛttau tu syānna taccetane kvacit // MAnuv_2,2.243 //
bhautikaṃ tveva rūpādi vyāptaṃ nāśena no mate /
alokākāśamāptasya kathaṃ na vikṛtiśca sā // MAnuv_2,2.247 //
saṃsthānāpagamaścet sa na hi bhūsāgarādiṣu // MAnuv_2,2.248 //
dehavyāptyai viśeṣaḥ kastasyāḥ sthāsnutanau ca nuḥ // MAnuv_2,2.250 //
gītāt puṣpaphalāvāptiḥ sparśāt kārśyaṃ rasāt sthitiḥ /
api vṛkṣasya dṛśyanta iti nānātmatā bhavet /

children.translated_text: And thus, the incompleteness of the self — from that very [reasoning] says the knower of the <s>Vedas</s> // 2.2.251 //
The <s>Pāśupatas</s> say that <s>Sadāśiva</s>, endowed with all qualities such as omniscience and the rest, /
is the creator of the variegated arrangement of the world, free from faults // 2.2.252 //
But this is not acceptable because of contradiction with numerous <s>Śrutis</s>; /

children.text: nopādeyaṃ mataṃ hyasya devasya stuhi gartagam // MAnuv_2,2.253 //
children.translated_text: the view of this <s>deva</s> [<s>Rudra</s>] — 'praise [the one who is] fallen into a pit' [is said of him] // 2.2.253 //
'He crushed his head'; 'You praise the abode of the Lord of beings'; /

children.text: yad viṣṇorupamaṃ hantuṃ rudramākṛṣṭate mayā // MAnuv_2,2.254 //
children.translated_text: 'that which is <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s equal — to destroy [it], <s>Rudra</s> is drawn out by me' // 2.2.254 //

children.text: dhanuryaṃ kāmaye taṃ tamugraṃ mā śiśnadevatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'the bow which I desire' — 'the fierce one'; 'let not the <s>śiśnadevas</s> (phallus-worshippers)' — /
'slaying the <s>śiśnadevas</s>, He alone existed — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the supreme' // 2.2.255 //
'From Him, <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Samprasāda</s> came into being'; the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> sacrifice — /
'by sacrifice they worshipped the sacrifice; they bound the <s>Puruṣa</s> as the [sacrificial] animal' // 2.2.256 //
'He who is the lord of beings, <s>Rudra</s>, the bull who goes along the threads' — /
by the force of such <s>Śrutis</s>, dependence, birth, death // 2.2.257 //
attainment of the supreme dependent on another, ignorance, non-existence at dissolution — /
are cognized; because of having faults, <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) is therefore not the Lord // 2.2.258 //
Because of his being without a body, his connection with the world somewhere /

children.text: kartṛtvena na yujyeta dehino jñānadṛṣṭitaḥ // MAnuv_2,2.259 //
children.translated_text: as creator would not be proper — [this is seen] from the perspective of knowledge regarding embodied beings // 2.2.259 //

children.text: na ca dehādivad viśvamasya syād bhogasambhavāt /
children.translated_text: And the world cannot be like a body and so forth for him, because of the possibility of experience; /

children.text: adhiṣṭhāne sthitaḥ kartā kāryaṃ kurvan pratīyate /
children.translated_text: an agent who is situated in a substratum is perceived as performing action; /
he has no connection with a substratum for beings at the time of dissolution // 2.2.260 //
If bodiless, he would always be non-omniscient, like a stone or a piece of wood; /
if embodied, he would be finite, by the analogy of <s>Yajñadatta</s> // 2.2.261 //
And all this does not [apply] to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because of the weight of Vedic authority; /

children.text: manobuddhayaṅgitāṃ viṣṇorlakṣayāmo ya eva saḥ // MAnuv_2,2.262 //
children.translated_text: we perceive the gestural expression of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s mind and intellect — He who is that very one // 2.2.262 //
He Himself is the body, consciousness, sovereignty, and robust power; /

children.text: deho viṣṇorna te viṣṇo vāsudevo 'grato 'bhavat // MAnuv_2,2.263 //
children.translated_text: 'The body belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>'; '<s>Vāsudeva</s> existed first' // 2.2.263 //

children.text: eko nārāyaṇastvāsīnna brahmā na ca śaṅkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone existed — neither <s>Brahmā</s> nor <s>Śaṅkara</s>'; /
'upon the navel of the unborn one, the supreme one was placed, by a portion' // 2.2.264 //
'Having a true body, having the fragrance of bliss, radiant with knowledge, of true valor, /

children.text: jñānajñānaḥ sukhasukhaḥ sa viṣṇuḥ paramākṣaraḥ // MAnuv_2,2.265 //
children.translated_text: knowledge of knowledge, bliss of bliss — He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme imperishable' // 2.2.265 //
'Bliss alone existed in the beginning — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Lord; /

children.text: priyaṃ tasya śire modapramodau ca bhujau hareḥ // MAnuv_2,2.266 //
children.translated_text: <s>Priya</s> (the beloved) is His head, <s>Moda</s> (delight) and <s>Pramoda</s> (great delight) are the arms of <s>Hari</s>' // 2.2.266 //

children.text: ānando madhyato brahma pucchaṃ nānyadabhūt kvacit /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ānanda</s> (bliss) is the middle, <s>Brahman</s> is the tail — nothing else existed anywhere; /
from His mind <s>Brahmā</s> came into being, and from His forehead <s>Śaṅkara</s>' // 2.2.267 //
'from His wings <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s> [from His coils], from His mouth arose <s>Sarasvatī</s>'; /
'The <s>Puruṣa</s> with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet' // 2.2.268 //
— by the force of such collections of <s>Śrutis</s>, it is established that from the body /
of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is of eternal qualities by nature, the entire world manifested // 2.2.269 //
Because of being established by valid authority, what contradiction is there? A name is accepted somewhere [differently]; /

children.text: avirodho virodhaśca mānenaiva hi gamyate // MAnuv_2,2.270 //
children.translated_text: non-contradiction and contradiction are ascertained by valid authority alone // 2.2.270 //

children.text: ata uktaṃ samastaṃ ca vāsudevasya yujyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, all that has been stated is appropriate for <s>Vāsudeva</s>; /
the <s>Śrutis</s> that [seem to speak of] <s>Śiva</s> and others are [actually] denoting <s>Viṣṇu</s> // 2.2.271 //

children.text: nāmāni sarvāṇi ca yameko yo devanāmadhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All names belong to Him alone — the one who is the giver of names to the <s>devas</s>; /

children.text: viṣṇunāmāni nānyasya sarvanāmā hariḥ svayam // MAnuv_2,2.272 //
children.translated_text: they are names of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not of another — <s>Hari</s> Himself possesses all names' // 2.2.272 //
'The names of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> do not [belong] to others, [and] other [names belong] to <s>Hari</s>' — /
such <s>Śrutis</s> are the authority there, and the harmonization (<s>samanvaya</s>) has been stated // 2.2.273 //
<s>Purāṇas</s> [that contradict] are not valid authority because of contradiction with [other] <s>Purāṇas</s> and so forth; /
there is no authority in what contradicts them, because of contradiction between earlier and later [statements] // 2.2.274 //
And because of contradiction with the equal-level <s>Brāhma</s> [<s>Purāṇas</s>], and by rule, even among <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [<s>Purāṇas</s>], /
[some passages are] stated for the purpose of delusion and for liberation — <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the ocean of qualities // 2.2.275 //
The doctrines of <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and others are thereby /
refuted in their entirety by reasoning, because of no distinction from the established conclusion // 2.2.276 //
Because of the existence of a particular [feature] in the refutation, the <s>Śākta</s> (power-doctrine) is separately /
criticized: 'the great goddess, the <s>hrīṅkārī</s>, the cause of all — /
<s>Tripurā</s>, <s>Bhairavī</s>' and so forth — by such names she is designated // 2.2.277 //
'From her, <s>Sadāśiva</s> and others — <s>devas</s> and humans — are born; /
even this elemental and material [world]' — this is not tenable // 2.2.278 //

children.text: dṛṣṭā pumbhyaḥ sadā sṛṣṭiḥ strīpumbhyo vā viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Creation is always seen from males, or specifically from males and females together; /

children.text: kevalābhyo na hi strībhyastata utpattyasambhavāt // MAnuv_2,2.279 //
children.translated_text: but never from females alone — therefore, origination [from the goddess alone] is impossible // 2.2.279 //
The great <s>Vāma</s> (left-handed) doctrine is not to be honored; by the left-handed ones, another [doctrine] is proclaimed: /
'<s>Śakti</s>, with <s>Śiva</s> as subordinate, created this [world] in all directions' // 2.2.280 //
That too is not tenable, because of <s>Śiva</s>'s being a non-creator; /
and because of bodilessness too, others might say the omniscient one is the Lord // 2.2.281 //
The <s>Aṇu</s> and <s>Vāma</s> [schools] — that is not proper, because of entering into the theistic position; /
the twofold [position] endowed with qualities such as omniscience and the rest, through excessive conceptual construction // 2.2.282 //

children.text: na yujyate hyatastvīśa eka eva prayojakaḥ /
children.translated_text: is not proper; therefore the Lord alone is the sole impeller; /

children.text: uktadoṣaśca tatpakṣa iti naivātra dūṣyate // MAnuv_2,2.283 //
children.translated_text: and the stated fault applies to that position — thus nothing is criticized here // 2.2.283 //
Because of contradiction with the totality of <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and <s>Itihāsa</s>, /

children.text: satāṃ jugupsitatvācca nāṅgīkāryaṃ hi tanmatam // MAnuv_2,2.284 //
children.translated_text: and because of being abhorred by the virtuous — that doctrine should not be accepted // 2.2.284 //
If these <s>sūtras</s> are said to be for the purpose of refuting <s>Pañcarātra</s>, /

children.text: sūtrāṇyativiruddhaṃ tad yata āha sa bhārate // MAnuv_2,2.285 //
children.translated_text: that is extremely contradictory, since he says in the <s>Bhārata</s>: // 2.2.285 //
'The speaker of the entire <s>Pañcarātra</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself; /
among all these systems of knowledge, O king of kings, this one excels' // 2.2.286 //
'Those who know the <s>Pañcarātra</s>, who follow the proper order, O king, /
who have attained one-pointed devotion — they enter into <s>Vāsudeva</s>' // 2.2.287 //

children.text: iti gītā ca tacchāstrasaṅkṣepa iti hīritam /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Gītā</s> is said to be the summary of that scripture; /

children.text: vedena pañcarātreṇa bhaktayā yajñena caiva hi // MAnuv_2,2.288 //
children.translated_text: 'Through the <s>Veda</s>, through the <s>Pañcarātra</s>, through devotion, and through sacrifice indeed // 2.2.288 //
I am to be seen; I am not to be seen otherwise, even in hundreds of crores of years' — /

children.text: iti vārāhavacanaṃ ślokā iti vacaḥ śrutau // MAnuv_2,2.289 //
children.translated_text: this is the statement of the <s>Vārāha</s>; and in the <s>Śruti</s> there is the statement 'these are verses' // 2.2.289 //
'Through the <s>Vedas</s> and through the <s>Pañcarātra</s>, the supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is to be meditated upon; /

children.text: pañcarātraṃ ca vedāśca vidyaikaiva dvidheyate // MAnuv_2,2.290 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Pañcarātra</s> and the <s>Vedas</s> — [they are] one knowledge spoken of in two ways' // 2.2.290 //
By such Vedic statements, the <s>Pañcarātra</s> is vindicated; /

children.text: kathamevātra doṣaḥ ka utpattirjño 'ta ityapi // MAnuv_2,2.291 //
children.translated_text: how indeed is there any fault here? And what [about the objection] 'origination of the knower'? // 2.2.291 //
That [origination] has been stated here itself; nor is the arising from non-existence stated there either; /
the <s>jīva</s>, bound by beginningless <s>karma</s> in the circle of <s>saṃsāra</s> // 2.2.292 //
wanders eternally by the will of <s>Vāsudeva</s> — thus is the statement of that [scripture]; /

children.text: na hi saṃsārasāditvaṃ pañcarātroditaṃ kvacit // MAnuv_2,2.293 //
children.translated_text: for the beginning of <s>saṃsāra</s> is never stated anywhere in the <s>Pañcarātra</s> // 2.2.293 //
The birth of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, by name, who is <s>Śeṣa</s> the presiding deity of the <s>jīva</s>, /
from <s>Vāsudeva</s> is stated; and likewise of <s>Pradyumna</s> from him // 2.2.294 //
— the presiding deity of mind, who is <s>Kāma</s> (desire) — thus, directly from <s>Hari</s> somewhere; /
the <s>vyūha</s> (emanation) is stated by the very names <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and so forth, through eternal and inconceivable great power; /
having restated [it] otherwise, how can it be called faulty? // 2.2.295 //
'If he knew the four <s>Vedas</s>' — likewise, the completion of the <s>Vedas</s>; /
'from the <s>Pañcarātra</s>' — whence the hatred in the school of <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>? // 2.2.296 //
Therefore, the criticism of the <s>Pañcarātra</s>, which has arisen from the hatred /

children.text: dūṣaṇaṃ pañcarātrasya vīkṣāyāmapi na kṣamam // MAnuv_2,2.297 //
children.translated_text: of <s>asuras</s> (demons) toward the supreme scripture, cannot withstand even examination // 2.2.297 //
Therefore, the creator of the entire world, faultless, the ocean of great qualities — /
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is ascertained from the purport of the assemblage of <s>Śrutis</s> // 2.2.298 //
'Into blind darkness enter those who worship <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); /

children.text: tato bhūya ivāpsyanti ye tasyā naiva nindakāḥ // MAnuv_2,2.299 //
children.translated_text: into [darkness] even greater will go those who do not even criticize it' // 2.2.299 //

children.text: tato vidyāmavidyāṃ ca yo jānātyubhayaṃ saha /
children.translated_text: 'But one who knows both <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> together — /
having crossed over these by the knowledge of faults, through <s>vidyā</s> one attains immortality' // 2.2.300 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: Now, the Lord, who will remove the contradiction with the entirety of the scriptural tradition, /
regarding the <s>adhidaiva</s> (cosmic), <s>adhibhūta</s> (elemental), <s>jīva</s>, and <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self) // 2.3.1 //
for the very purpose of determining the own-nature of statements with respect to each other — /
the one of immeasurable splendor demonstrates their non-contradiction by this <s>pāda</s> // 2.3.2 //
Experience, reasoning, the reversal of many statements — and beyond that, /

children.text: etat sarvaṃ sataḥ sāmyaṃ dvāravaiyarthyameva ca // MAnuv_2,3.3 //
children.translated_text: all this: the equality of the existent, the purposelessness of doors [of knowledge] // 2.3.3 //
conformity with what is seen and with reasoning, and non-contradiction of stated meanings; /
upon accepting well-known names, conformity with many statements // 2.3.4 //
conformity with worldly observation, the equality of the <s>jīva</s>, beginninglessness, /

children.text: tatra tatra parijñānaṃ guṇasāmyaśrutī tathā // MAnuv_2,3.5 //
children.translated_text: full knowledge in each [respective context], and the <s>Śrutis</s> regarding equality of qualities — likewise // 2.3.5 //
having-originatedness, with few assumptions about experiencing one's own qualities, /
diverse <s>Śrutis</s>, and variety — these are the reasonings of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opponent's position) // 2.3.6 //
the impossibility of [proper] arrangement, conformity with independence, /

children.text: mukhyatā śaktimattvaṃ ca vairūpyaṃ sarvasaṅgrahaḥ // MAnuv_2,3.7 //
children.translated_text: primacy, being endowed with power, and diversity, comprehensive inclusion — // 2.3.7 //
motion and the like, the power of the Lord, non-contradiction with all valid authorities, /
the attainment of the desired [conclusion], clear manifestation, scripture-established reversal, /
and the specific cause — these are the establishing [arguments] for the established conclusion alone // 2.3.8 //
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>puruṣa</s> (conscious being), time, the <s>devas</s> who are the presiding deities thereof, /
<s>Mahat</s> (the great) and so forth — all originate with particularizations dependent on another; /
'He created all this' — thus, having-origination is stated here // 2.3.9 //
Space is merely room — how could it originate otherwise? /

children.text: yadyanākāśatā pūrvaṃ kiṃ mūrtanibiḍaṃ jagat // MAnuv_2,3.10 //
children.translated_text: If there were no space previously, would the world be solidly compact? // 2.3.10 //
And if there were no space, there would be complete fullness of solid matter; /

children.text: mūrtadravyāṇi cākāśe sthitānyeva hi sarvadā // MAnuv_2,3.11 //
children.translated_text: but solid substances always exist within space // 2.3.11 //
Therefore, the <s>deva</s> called <s>Vināyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) is denoted by the word 'space'; /
it is said by <s>Śruti</s> that he originated through the origination of his body // 2.3.12 //
Even the element [of space], though it exists, being dark, is within the range of divine vision alone; /
the unmanifest sky, which is within the range of the Witness, originates; /

children.text: pradeśa iti vijñeyaṃ nityaṃ notpadyate hi tat // MAnuv_2,3.13 //
children.translated_text: 'location' — thus it should be understood; that is eternal and does not originate // 2.3.13 //
Nevertheless, space, possessing particularizations dependent on prior connections, /
is called 'having origination' — this is what the words of <s>Śruti</s> intend // 2.3.14 //

children.text: prakṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ kāla ityete ca samastaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, and time — all these together /
are declared as 'originated' through particularizations dependent on the Lord // 2.3.15 //
The flow of time alone is one and eternal, but not as possessing particularizations; /
<s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) alone is the sole presiding deity of <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), and time // 2.3.16 //
Having attained the particularization of the desire to create, directly by the will of the Lord, /
she is said to be created — <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) too, [originating] from modification // 2.3.17 //
The <s>puruṣas</s> (individual souls) are said to be 'originated' because of [their] connection with bodies; /
thus, even at the time of dissolution, the gradation of higher and lower is perceived // 2.3.18 //
The chief <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), eternally equal [to himself], because of being the cause of the origination of bodies, /
is called 'having origination' through particularizations dependent on another // 2.3.19 //
Nothing whatsoever, except the Supreme, is free from origination; /
in the dependence of particularization upon origination, [there is] the absence of grossness // 2.3.20 //
And the loss of the former word — if this is called 'origination,' /

children.text: ramāyā naiva janmāsti caitanyasyāpi kevalam // MAnuv_2,3.21 //
children.translated_text: there is no origination of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), nor of consciousness (the <s>jīva</s>) merely // 2.3.21 //
And of <s>Pradhāna</s> and of the <s>Veda</s> — even of the <s>Veda</s>, by the will of the Lord, /

children.text: vyaktirnāma viśeṣo 'sti tasmāt tadvaśataiva hi // MAnuv_2,3.22 //
children.translated_text: there is a manifestation, a particularization — therefore, [everything is] under His control alone // 2.3.22 //
Here, origination is spoken of due to the independence of the Supreme Self.

children.text: naivotpattiḥ kathamapi na svatantraṃ tato 'param // MAnuv_2,3.23 //
children.translated_text: There is no origination in any way whatsoever; nothing other [than Him] is independent. // MAnuv_2,3.23 //
Even though the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is indivisible, <s>Hari</s>, having divided it in manifold ways,

children.text: kṛtvā bhogān pradāyaiva caikyamāpādayet punaḥ // MAnuv_2,3.24 //
children.translated_text: and having bestowed [various] experiences, would again bring it to unity. // MAnuv_2,3.24 //
Therefore, the entire world — sentient and insentient — is under the control of the Lord.
When <s>Keśava</s> leads the undivided toward division,
what is impossible for the Supreme Lord? — thus it is declared. // MAnuv_2,3.25 //
Even when the matter stands thus, some assert the identity of the <s>jīva</s> with the Supreme Self,
based on scriptures beginning with "tat tvam asi" ("That thou art") and by the force of inference. // MAnuv_2,3.26 //

children.text: na tad yuktaṃ yato viṣṇuḥ pṛthagevābhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: That is not correct, because <s>Viṣṇu</s> is spoken of as distinctly separate.
"The one whose eye is wisdom, in the [state] without light" — difference in <s>mukti</s> (liberation) is declared.
"This bliss" — and another [scripture says] "supreme equality" as well. // MAnuv_2,3.27 //
"Having resorted to this knowledge, they have attained similarity to My nature."

children.text: sarge 'pi nopajāyante praḷaye na vyathanti ca // MAnuv_2,3.28 //
children.translated_text: "Even in creation they are not born, and in dissolution they do not suffer." // MAnuv_2,3.28 //
"Having attained that light, [the liberated soul] manifests in its own form."

children.text: tatra paryeti jakṣaṃśca krīḍannapi sadā sukhī // MAnuv_2,3.29 //
children.translated_text: "There it moves about, eating, playing — always blissful." // MAnuv_2,3.29 //

children.text: ācakṣva me mokṣaṃ dhīrā yaṃ pravadanti tam /
children.translated_text: "Declare to me that liberation which the wise proclaim" —

children.text: ityakta āha vāgdevī paraṃ mokṣaṃ prajāpateḥ // MAnuv_2,3.30 //
children.translated_text: when thus asked, the goddess of speech spoke of the supreme liberation of <s>Prajāpati</s>. // MAnuv_2,3.30 //
"Great rivers flow, branch by branch, streaming in all directions."
"[There are] grain-cakes and those desiring meat, and always pools of milk-pudding." // MAnuv_2,3.31 //
"Wherein the gods whose mouths are fire, together with <s>Indra</s> and the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,
worshipped with the foremost sacrifices — they worship that Imperishable." // MAnuv_2,3.32 //
"The liberated enter the Supreme God; there they are enjoyers."
"They go forth as they wish, impelled by the Supreme Lord Himself." // MAnuv_2,3.33 //
With the vision of difference, through pride, and even through action devoid of attachment,

children.text: kartṛtvāt saguṇaṃ brahma puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabham // MAnuv_2,3.34 //
children.translated_text: [one worships] <s>Brahman</s> with qualities, the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person), the best among persons. // MAnuv_2,3.34 //
He, having united [them] again in time, through time itself, in the form of the Lord,
when the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) arises, creates as before. // MAnuv_2,3.35 //

children.text: ṛcāṃ tvaḥ poṣamāste ca pareṇa preritāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: "He who fosters the <s>Ṛcs</s> (Vedic hymns) and abides [therein]" — always impelled by the Supreme.
"Whatever He desires, that He creates indeed; He creates that by His own Self as well." // MAnuv_2,3.36 //
Together with <s>Brahman</s>, he enjoys desires, having transcended its qualities,
and having abandoned suffering and the like, free from the activities of the world. // MAnuv_2,3.37 //
He enjoys experiences together with the exalted ones — thus from the authority of scripture and the like.
Since the liberated soul has the cognition of difference, how can there be non-difference at all? // MAnuv_2,3.38 //
Nor can inference establish the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord.
"The difference under dispute is false, because it is a difference — like the difference of the [two] moons" —

children.text: iti cet sādhyadharmo 'yaṃ sannasan vā navobhayam // MAnuv_2,3.39 //
children.translated_text: if [one argues] thus, [we reply:] this property to be proved — does it exist, or not exist, or neither? // MAnuv_2,3.39 //
If it exists, [your] thesis is contradicted; if it is said to be non-existent,

children.text: nobhayaṃ cenna siddhaṃ taditi mānasya dūṣaṇam // MAnuv_2,3.40 //
children.translated_text: then neither [option] is established — this is a refutation of [your] means of knowledge. // MAnuv_2,3.40 //
Nor can this be established anywhere by any other means of knowledge.

children.text: anumānena cet saiva hyanavasthā bhaviṣyati // MAnuv_2,3.41 //
children.translated_text: If [you resort to] inference, that very infinite regress will follow. // MAnuv_2,3.41 //
Nor is there a scriptural text whose purpose is that. "There was not non-existence" — it would not say that.
If, by the method of elimination, [you try to] establish the inexpressibility of the Supreme Self — // MAnuv_2,3.42 //
then inexpressibility itself would be [all that] remains for it.
And there is no other scripture regarding that which is the counterpositive of both existence and non-existence. // MAnuv_2,3.43 //
Nor is there mere perception, nor is <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) accepted [as a proof here].

children.text: bādhāyogāt sata iti bādhābhāvata eva hi // MAnuv_2,3.44 //
children.translated_text: "[It is] existent because of the impossibility of sublation" — indeed, precisely because of the absence of sublation. // MAnuv_2,3.44 //

children.text: viṣayasya kuto bādho vidyamānaṃ hi bādhyate /
children.translated_text: How can there be sublation of a [real] object? For what exists is [what can be] sublated.

children.text: na hi vandhyāsuto vadhyo yajñadatto hi vadhyate // MAnuv_2,3.45 //
children.translated_text: A barren woman's son cannot be killed — [it is] <s>Yajñadatta</s> [who] is indeed killed. // MAnuv_2,3.45 //

children.text: bādhāyogaḥ sata iti vyāptireṣā kva dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: "The impossibility of sublation [proves it] existent" — where is this pervasion seen?

children.text: kaścāyaṃ bādha uddiṣṭo na hi nāśo 'sato bhavet /
children.translated_text: And what is this sublation that is pointed out? For destruction of the non-existent cannot occur,
and how can the cessation of what has never arisen be established? // MAnuv_2,3.46 //
"It was not, it is, and it will be" — that cognition alone is its measure.
If that is sublation, then its non-existence is thereby itself accepted. // MAnuv_2,3.47 //
One who says "the cognition is not of the non-existent" thereby accepts that [cognition].
For the negation of what is not cognized is in no way established. // MAnuv_2,3.48 //

children.text: na copamā bhavedatra pratyakṣāt sattvameva ca /
children.translated_text: Nor would analogy be [valid] here; and from perception, existence alone [follows].
From the Supreme Lord who is known through scripture, difference from one's own self is understood. // MAnuv_2,3.49 //
How can identity be asserted in contradiction to experience?
"I am a limited agent and a sufferer" — this is experienced by all. // MAnuv_2,3.50 //
"The <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> is omniscient and omnipotent" — thus it is heard in scripture.
On the basis of experienced difference, this scripture speaks of Him [as different]. // MAnuv_2,3.51 //
How could scripture, contradicting what it depends upon, assert identity?
When the invalidity of [the texts] that speak of difference will result, // MAnuv_2,3.52 //

children.text: sa eva dharmiṇo grāhī tadabhedaḥ kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: that very [means of knowledge] is the apprehender of the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) — how can its non-difference be?

children.text: yat svarūpagrahe mānaṃ taddharme na kathaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_2,3.53 //
children.translated_text: That which is the means of knowledge for grasping the essential nature — how can it not be [valid] for its properties? // MAnuv_2,3.53 //
By the cognition of a single cognition, both [aspects] would be means of knowledge.

children.text: na cedekamamānaṃ tad dvayamapyatra no bhavet // MAnuv_2,3.54 //
children.translated_text: If one is not a means of knowledge, then neither would be [valid] here. // MAnuv_2,3.54 //
The contradiction with the apprehension of the subject — therefore, this is a refutation of the means of knowledge.
Non-difference is not to be relied upon here anywhere, due to the force of the scriptures [declaring] difference. // MAnuv_2,3.55 //

children.text: na ca mānāntaropeyaṃ brahma tad bhavati kvacit /
children.translated_text: Nor is <s>Brahman</s> to be approached by any other means of knowledge anywhere,
and by whichever means of knowledge it is to be approached, difference is cognized by that very [means]. // MAnuv_2,3.56 //
If the Lord, who is of the nature of all knowledge, is to be approached in any way,
it is by the very quality of omniscience that difference from Him is cognized. // MAnuv_2,3.57 //
The experience of suffering never goes toward being a false experience.

children.text: na hi bādhaḥ kvacid dṛṣṭo duḥkhādyanubhavasya tu // MAnuv_2,3.58 //
children.translated_text: For sublation of the experience of suffering and the like is never seen anywhere. // MAnuv_2,3.58 //
If the experience of suffering is determined to be an error,

children.text: aduḥkhitāśrutiḥ kena na bhrāntiriti gamyate // MAnuv_2,3.59 //
children.translated_text: by what [reasoning] is the scripture [saying one is] "free from suffering" not understood as error? // MAnuv_2,3.59 //
The form of scripture and its meaning are ascertained by means of knowledge alone.

children.text: taccenmānaṃ gṛhītaṃ te kiṃ duḥkhānubhave bhramaḥ // MAnuv_2,3.60 //
children.translated_text: If that means of knowledge has been accepted by you, why [call it] error in the experience of suffering? // MAnuv_2,3.60 //
And there is no special sublation; that [experience] is indeed unsublated.

children.text: bādho yadyanubhūte 'rthe kathaṃ nirṇaya īyate // MAnuv_2,3.61 //
children.translated_text: If there is sublation of an experienced object, how can any determination be reached? // MAnuv_2,3.61 //

children.text: ko 'pi hy artho na niścetuṃ śakyate bhramavādinā /
children.translated_text: Indeed, no object whatsoever can be ascertained by one who asserts error.
Error-ness and non-error-ness — when both fall within the scope of experience,

children.text: ekasya bhramatā tatra parasyābhramatā kutaḥ // MAnuv_2,3.62 //
children.translated_text: if one [experience] is erroneous there, how could the other be non-erroneous? // MAnuv_2,3.62 //

children.text: bhramatvamabhramatvaṃ ca sarvaṃ vedyaṃ hi sākṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: Both error-ness and non-error-ness — everything is known by the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>).

children.text: sa cet sākṣī kvacid duṣyaḥ kathaṃ nirṇaya īyate // MAnuv_2,3.63 //
children.translated_text: If that witness is defective anywhere, how can any determination be reached? // MAnuv_2,3.63 //
All these distinctions are within the scope of the witness-cognition.

children.text: ūrīkṛtya ca tān sarvān vyavahāraḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: And having accepted all of them, practical activity proceeds.
The determinate cognition of the witness — that is called practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>). // MAnuv_2,3.64 //
Therefore, for the establishment of practical activity that is universally acknowledged,

children.text: sākṣī nirdoṣa evaikaḥ sadāṅgīkārya eva naḥ // MAnuv_2,3.65 //
children.translated_text: the one faultless witness must always be accepted by us. // MAnuv_2,3.65 //

children.text: śuddhaḥ sākṣī yadā siddho duḥkhitvaṃ vāryate katham /
children.translated_text: When the pure witness is established, how can suffering be denied?
That foundational means of knowledge is indeed an apprehender of difference.
Therefore, the difference between <s>jīva</s> and the Lord is firmly established by the force of scripture. // MAnuv_2,3.66 //
Nevertheless, qualities such as consciousness and bliss and the like, which resemble His,
remain as the essential nature of this [jīva] even in liberation. // MAnuv_2,3.67 //
Therefore, those scriptures speak as if of non-difference,
and the Purāṇic statements [do so] because of [their] basis in similarity and non-difference. // MAnuv_2,3.68 //
Because of similarity, because of predominance, and also because of dependence, they declare

children.text: āhurīśena jīvasya na svarūpābhidāṃ kvacit // MAnuv_2,3.69 //
children.translated_text: the designation of the <s>jīva</s> by [the name of] the Lord — never the identity of essential nature. // MAnuv_2,3.69 //
Unity of abode and unity of purpose characterize the liberated soul.

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa jaḍānāṃ dvayameva tu /
children.translated_text: And similarity is especially [notable]; for insentient beings, only two [of these] obtain.
There would be very little similarity — the third — with the Supreme Self. // MAnuv_2,3.70 //
Of the Lord's forms, actions, and qualities in every respect,
and likewise of His parts — their essential identity [with Him] is primary. // MAnuv_2,3.71 //
"Just as water poured on rugged ground runs down over the mountains,
even so, one who sees <s>dharmas</s> as separate runs after those very [separate things]." —
from this scripture, neither both — called "difference-and-non-difference" — is accepted. // MAnuv_2,3.72 //
"One alone, without a second"; "there is no diversity here whatsoever";

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati // MAnuv_2,3.73 //
children.translated_text: "He who sees as if there is diversity here goes from death to death." // MAnuv_2,3.73 //
In scripture, [the word] "iva" ("as if") — therefore, [this is] a refutation of [both] difference-and-non-difference.

children.text: ivobhaye ca sādṛśya iti vāk śabdanirṇaye // MAnuv_2,3.74 //
children.translated_text: And "iva" in both [types of texts] indicates similarity — such is the conclusion regarding the word. // MAnuv_2,3.74 //
Even from the statement of difference in liberation, there is the defeat of that [opposing] position.
If similarity in consciousness and the like is accepted as non-difference,
that has been accepted by us — but never essential identity. // MAnuv_2,3.75 //
There is no non-difference of anyone [from <s>Viṣṇu</s>], nor is there difference-cum-non-difference anywhere,

children.text: samudāyamṛte viṣṇoḥ svaguṇādīn vināpi vā // MAnuv_2,3.76 //
children.translated_text: except in the aggregate, [and] without [separating] <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s own qualities and the like. // MAnuv_2,3.76 //
Thus from scripture: there is neither difference-cum-non-difference of Him with anyone.

children.text: abhedaśrutayo' ṃśatvāt sādṛśyaṃ cāṃśatāsya tu // MAnuv_2,3.77 //
children.translated_text: The non-difference scriptures [refer to] part-hood; and the similarity is [also] due to his being a part. // MAnuv_2,3.77 //

children.text: aṃśastu dvividho jñeyaḥ svarūpāṃśo 'nya eva ca /
children.translated_text: But part-hood should be understood as twofold: the essential part (<s>svarūpāṃśa</s>) and the other [type].
The separated part has limited power and possesses only a little similarity. // MAnuv_2,3.78 //

children.text: aṃśino yattu sāmarthyaṃ yat svarūpaṃ yathā sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever power belongs to the possessor of parts, whatever is its essential nature, whatever its mode of being —

children.text: sa eva cet svarūpāṃśaḥ prādurbhāvā hareryathā // MAnuv_2,3.79 //
children.translated_text: if that itself is the essential part — like the manifestations (<s>prādurbhāvas</s>) of <s>Hari</s>. // MAnuv_2,3.79 //
There is one who pervades the orb of the sun, who has the self-identification with that radiance —

children.text: sūryo 'tha saptamābdheśca bāhyodasya ca vāripaḥ // MAnuv_2,3.80 //
children.translated_text: He is <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun); and of the seventh ocean, He is the external lord of waters. // MAnuv_2,3.80 //
Through hardness, of <s>Meru</s> and the rest, and of the earth too, the deity —
the goddess <s>Dharā</s> (Earth) — even so, the one <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s>, imperishable,
abides in the form of manifold <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations), always full in all qualities. // MAnuv_2,3.81 //
Just as the deities presiding over excrement, urine, eyes, and the like are fallen deities,
similarly this transmigrating soul is separate from the Supreme, [as they are] from <s>Sūrya</s> and others. // MAnuv_2,3.82 //
Being defiled by the defects of the body, they are called "fallen deities,"

children.text: anyāḥ sūryādidevebhyo hyanugrāhyāśca taiḥ sadā // MAnuv_2,3.83 //
children.translated_text: different from the gods such as <s>Sūrya</s> and the rest, and always to be favored by them. // MAnuv_2,3.83 //

children.text: evameva parād viṣṇoḥ pṛthak saṃsāriṇo matāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the same way, transmigrating souls are considered separate from the Supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and are to be favored by Him alone; and through His grace, they become liberated. // MAnuv_2,3.84 //
But the forms such as <s>Matsya</s> (Fish incarnation) and the rest are not considered objects of favor [by others],
because of being complete in all qualities — there is primary non-difference; but not with others. // MAnuv_2,3.85 //
All parts and reflections are parts of the Supreme — but not primarily.
"Just as the shadow of a person — in this [body], that [Supreme] is not extended." // MAnuv_2,3.86 //

children.text: na tu pumpādavat pādā jīvā ete parātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>jīvas</s> are not feet [of the Supreme] like the feet of a man.
His qualities are complete; they abide in the mode of manifestation.
Thus the supreme <s>śruti</s> (scripture) has declared <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> to be the Supreme. // MAnuv_2,3.87 //
The imperishable <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, abides in dissolution,
always meditated upon by the liberated — <s>Brahmā</s> and others — in [their] hierarchical grades (<s>tāratamya</s>). // MAnuv_2,3.88 //
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Person), <s>Kāla</s> (Time), and the <s>Vedas</s> — this fourfold [group]
is eternal in essential nature from <s>Viṣṇu</s>; merely through the attainment of special [qualities],
it is said to have origination. <s>Lakṣmī</s> is the presiding deity of that [Prakṛti]. // MAnuv_2,3.89 //

children.text: tato jātaḥ pumān nāma brahmāsyāṃ vāsudevataḥ /
children.translated_text: From her was born the one named <s>Puruṣa</s> — <s>Brahmā</s>, in her, from <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: sūtrātmā prāṇanāmā ca devyau prakṛtimāninī // MAnuv_2,3.90 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Sūtrātman</s> (thread-soul), also called <s>Prāṇa</s>; and the two goddesses presiding over <s>Prakṛti</s>. // MAnuv_2,3.90 //

children.text: tato rūpaṃ mahān nāma brahmaṇo 'haṅkṛtiḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: From that, the form called <s>Mahat</s> (the Great), the ego-sense of <s>Brahmā</s> — <s>Śiva</s>,
From <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Buddhi</s> (Intelligence) by name; from that, <s>Indra</s>, called Mind;

children.text: skandaśca tata evānye sarve devāḥ prajajñire // MAnuv_2,3.91 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Skanda</s>; and from that, all other <s>devas</s> were born. // MAnuv_2,3.91 //

children.text: tatra pūrvatanaḥ śreyān guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samastaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, each prior one is superior in all qualities, in every way.

children.text: tebhyaśca bhagavān viṣṇustadadhīnā ime sadā // MAnuv_2,3.92 //
children.translated_text: And than them all, the <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s> [is supreme] — they are always dependent on Him. // MAnuv_2,3.92 //
Birth, sustenance, dissolution, ignorance, regulation, knowledge, transmigration,
and liberation — their dependence on Him is never diminished. // MAnuv_2,3.93 //
Even in liberation, He alone is the one independent [being], full of true qualities.
Thus, by both <s>śruti</s> and reasoning, the Lord has declared in this <s>pāda</s>. // MAnuv_2,3.94 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: Where the meaning of <s>śruti</s> appears as if contradicted by <s>śruti</s> and reasoning,
the Lord settles that, through especially distinguished proofs,
in this <s>pāda</s> — [treating] <s>śruti</s> as [having] clear meaning. // MAnuv_2,4.1 //
The distinctive <s>śruti</s>, dissimilarity, greatness, manifest good qualities,
perceived reasoning, equality, the power of the agent, intermixture — // MAnuv_2,4.2 //
such reasonings in the <s>pūrvapakṣas</s> (prima facie views), well-determined;
and such reasonings of the conclusion (<s>nirṇaya</s>) itself — declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself. // MAnuv_2,4.3 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: Natural otherness, mutual non-coexistence, statements of otherness,

children.text: aviśeṣo viśeṣau ca sahabhāvo vimiśratā // MAnuv_3,1.1 //
children.translated_text: non-distinction, distinctions, coexistence, intermixture, // MAnuv_3,1.1 //
contradictory statement, being in the same place, purposelessness, and going to another [interpretation] —
these are the reasonings of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>; and the existence of both for the purpose of the superiority of qualities. // MAnuv_3,1.2 //
Proof, twofold nature, superiority, conformity,
fitness, preponderance, division, absence of cause,
arrangement, and no other resort — these are the proofs of the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion). // MAnuv_3,1.3 //
Of the seeds, non-persons, and wombs — the conjunction, regulation, and dissolution —
the <s>Bhagavān</s> states through the word 'now' (<s>atha</s>), and that too as [having] a cause. // MAnuv_3,1.4 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: Subsequently: <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), differentiations of knowledge, time, suffering, and individual existences,
difference of station, contrariety, equality of reasoning, self-origination, // MAnuv_3,2.1 //
equality of qualities, non-connection, obstruction by reasoning, contrariety,
diversity of nature, and temptation — [these] belong to the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. // MAnuv_3,2.2 //
The power of an incapable agent, ignorance from itself, and that very [ignorance],
non-evidence, arrangement, true evidence, determination, extreme paucity, and non-existences — // MAnuv_3,2.3 //
distinction, perception, statement, the power of the person, clear demonstration,
supra-mundane nature, superiority, independence — [these are] the proofs of the conclusion. // MAnuv_3,2.4 //
The impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of all things, coming from beginningless experience,
exist indeed — established in the beginningless minds of all <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls). // MAnuv_3,2.5 //
The mind, which is of the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s>, exists indeed — eternal until liberation.
And in that [mind], all impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are always accumulated. // MAnuv_3,2.6 //
In dissolution, it exists in subtle form and is augmented by [elements] arising from <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.text: sṛṣṭikāle yadā tanna kutaḥ saṃsārasaṃsthitiḥ // MAnuv_3,2.7 //
children.translated_text: At the time of creation, if that [mind] did not [persist], whence would the establishment of <s>saṃsāra</s> [come]? // MAnuv_3,2.7 //
Through the impressions, the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself, having created the manifold world,
shows [it] at the time of dream — [waking] delusion is indeed the waking state. // MAnuv_3,2.8 //

children.text: adṛṣṭe cāśrute bhāve na bhāva upajāyate /
children.translated_text: Of a thing unseen and unheard, no existence arises.
From an unseen and unheard thing, no existence arises. // MAnuv_3,2.9 //
Thus the statement of <s>śruti</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> — because of beginninglessness, it is proper.

children.text: kadācid darśanāyogyaṃ yat tatrāpi vibhāgataḥ // MAnuv_3,2.10 //
children.translated_text: Even for what is at some time unfit for perception, there [is the explanation] through division. // MAnuv_3,2.10 //

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ samānādhikaraṇaṃ dṛśyate ca sa ca bhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is seen as co-referential (<s>samānādhikaraṇa</s>) — and it is seen — that is delusion.
