Because the root is impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) alone, there is no clarity as in the waking state. // MAnuv_3,2.11 //
'Is it difference, non-difference, or both?' — this question is not proper,
because difference alone is seen by all people between the dreamer and the dream. // MAnuv_3,2.12 //
For the four faults of a question are: self-contradiction, irrelevance,

children.text: siddhārthatā ca vaiphalyaṃ na taiḥ syāt tattvanirṇayaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.13 //
children.translated_text: being already established, and futility — the determination of truth would not be [achieved] by these. // MAnuv_3,2.13 //
Contrariety to the determination of truth — even in debate, [this would be] grounds for defeat.
What should be brought out — the termination of the discussion would not occur. // MAnuv_3,2.14 //
In a debate seeking victory, the cause for the termination of discussion [is this]:
even in refutation, the establishment — [this is] the criticism of the opponent.

children.text: pratijñāyāṃ tadanyasya siddhataiva hi sādhakā // MAnuv_3,2.15 //
children.translated_text: In the thesis of the other, the very establishment [of the opposite] is the proof. // MAnuv_3,2.15 //
The non-establishment of the basis and the counter-basis, and the establishment of what is to be proved — these are criticisms.

children.text: keṣāñcin na ca te doṣā vyāptau satyāṃ kathañcana // MAnuv_3,2.16 //
children.translated_text: For some, these are not faults at all, when the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is correct. // MAnuv_3,2.16 //
The fault of self-contradiction exists in proving the existence of a man's horn.

children.text: yatra vyāhatatā nāsti ko 'tisaṅgo 'sya sādhane // MAnuv_3,2.17 //
children.translated_text: Where there is no self-contradiction, what excessive attachment [is there] to proving it? // MAnuv_3,2.17 //
All valid reasonings (<s>nyāyas</s>) are indeed rooted in perception and scripture.

children.text: nyāyābhāsā amūlāḥ syurnyāyasyānyasya tau punaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.18 //
children.translated_text: Semblances of reasoning would be rootless; for another reasoning, those two again [are the roots]. // MAnuv_3,2.18 //

children.text: adṛṣṭe vyabhicāre tu sādhakaṃ taditi sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: When deviation has not been seen, that [reasoning] clearly is the proof.

children.text: jñāyate sākṣiṇaivādvā mānabādhe na tad bhavet // MAnuv_3,2.19 //
children.translated_text: It is known by the witness alone; or, when there is invalidation by a [valid] means of knowledge, that would not be [a proof]. // MAnuv_3,2.19 //
That the validity of the means of knowledge is ascertained by the witness alone —

children.text: amānasya tu mānatvaṃ mānasatvāccalaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_3,2.20 //
children.translated_text: [and] the validity of what is not a means of knowledge, because of being [merely] mental, would be unstable. // MAnuv_3,2.20 //
Even what is obtained by default (<s>utsarga</s>), when free from exception,
[and] with an exception for deviation — will indeed be a means of valid knowledge. // MAnuv_3,2.21 //
Therefore, the inference that food and the like are means to the desired [end]

children.text: mānaṃ vyavahṛtau nityaṃ vyabhicāro hi tatra ca // MAnuv_3,2.22 //
children.translated_text: is always a means of valid knowledge in practice — even though there is deviation therein. // MAnuv_3,2.22 //

children.text: vyāptatve vyāśrayatvaṃ tu kathameva hi dūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: When pervasion is [established], how indeed is counter-basis a fault?
'The rising of <s>Rohiṇī</s> is near, because <s>Kṛttikā</s> has risen' —

children.text: ityukte sādhanaṃ no kiṃ na hyājñaivātra sādhakā // MAnuv_3,2.23 //
children.translated_text: when this is said, is it not a proof? For mere [common] knowledge is not the proof here. // MAnuv_3,2.23 //
'The universe is other than existent and non-existent' — this too is a self-contradictory statement.

children.text: asiddhasādhane doṣaḥ ko vyāptiryadi vidyate // MAnuv_3,2.24 //
children.translated_text: What fault is there in proving what is unproved, if the pervasion is present? // MAnuv_3,2.24 //
And the pervasion is known by those very [people] through negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) there.
That an unknown <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved) is said to have probative force —

children.text: liṅgasyoktau viśeṣo 'yaṃ kena mānena gamyate // MAnuv_3,2.25 //
children.translated_text: this distinction, in the statement of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), by what means of knowledge is it known? // MAnuv_3,2.25 //
When the proof of an unestablished [entity] like the atom and the like is desired,
it should be [accepted] only as experienced — it should not be accepted otherwise. // MAnuv_3,2.26 //

children.text: yatra nātiprasaṅgo 'sti mānaṃ na ca viparyate /
children.translated_text: Where there is no over-extension, and the means of knowledge is not violated,
[to say] 'this is to be proved only through tortured imagination' — this is very difficult to say. // MAnuv_3,2.27 //
Elimination (<s>pariśeṣa</s>), mutual establishment, circularity, self-dependence, and the like —
through their ability to establish the unproved, without the five-membered [syllogism],
these should be accepted by all — what is the basis for restriction [to five members]? // MAnuv_3,2.28 //
And in the case of establishing what is [already] established, the termination of discussion would not occur.
Deviation and non-establishment of the reason — even in one position, [it is] a fault. // MAnuv_3,2.29 //
The deficiency of the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> in the qualifier of the example,
futility, and in the case of non-establishment of one — [there is] non-establishment of the qualified [thesis]. // MAnuv_3,2.30 //
Irrelevance — that is the fault of the first question.
The already-established question and the like — that would fall into the pit of superfluity. // MAnuv_3,2.31 //
Presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), analogy (<s>upamā</s>), and non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) are sometimes included within inference.
Non-existence is included within perception — for pleasure and the like, necessarily [so]. // MAnuv_3,2.32 //
Elsewhere, [non-existence] is arrived at as 'sudden' (<s>khaḍiti</s>); and the reasonings of [the <s>sūtra</s>] beginning with 'commencement' —
all having invariable pervasion — [serve] the purpose of determining the meaning of scripture. // MAnuv_3,2.33 //

children.text: vākyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sthānaṃ samākhyā ca tathāvidhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Sentence, context, place, and designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) — and such [interpretive principles] —
like the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, for these, because of [their] proof, there is separate statement. // MAnuv_3,2.34 //
Proof should be done by one's own principles (<s>nyāyas</s>), and refutation by the opponent's principles.

children.text: svanyāyairdūṣaṇaṃ ca syāt sādhitaiḥ prativādinaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.35 //
children.translated_text: And refutation by one's own principles too would apply — against the opponent's established [views]. // MAnuv_3,2.35 //
Those stated for the purpose of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) are not refuters of the <s>siddhānta</s>.
'Quibble' (<s>chala</s>) and 'futile objection' (<s>jāti</s>) — two-fold; a [third] type of self-contradiction is accepted.
Futile objection (<s>jāti</s>) is to be known as self-contradiction; quibble (<s>chala</s>) is a subsequent different meaning. // MAnuv_3,2.36 //
Thus, because of contradiction with the well-examined reasoning and true scripture,
the 'indescribable' (<s>anirvācya</s>) is not stated here — [it is rejected] by the word '<s>māyā</s>-alone.' // MAnuv_3,2.37 //
'Different from both existent and non-existent' — this is self-contradictory on its face.
And its being a counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> would have to be accepted. // MAnuv_3,2.38 //

children.text: mithyā cet pratiyogitvaṃ vailakṣaṇyaṃ tato na hi /
children.translated_text: If the counter-correlate-hood is false, then there is no distinctiveness [of the world from <s>Brahman</s>].
Non-distinctiveness would be true — then the falsity of <s>Brahman</s> [would follow]. // MAnuv_3,2.39 //

children.text: anirvācyasya sattvaṃ vā yadi dharmā na kecana /
children.translated_text: If the existence of the indescribable — then no properties whatsoever

children.text: brahmaṇo naiva jijñāsyaṃ jijñāsā dharmanirṇayaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.40 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Brahman</s> are to be inquired into — [for] inquiry is the determination of properties. // MAnuv_3,2.40 //
Knowledge of 'this is such' — that is the purpose of inquiry.

children.text: itthambhāvo hi dharmo 'sya na cenna pratiyogitā // MAnuv_3,2.41 //
children.translated_text: 'Such-ness' is indeed a property of this [<s>Brahman</s>]; and if not, there is no counter-correlate-hood. // MAnuv_3,2.41 //
And all <s>śrutis</s> declare properties of the nature of 'such-ness.'
Invisibility and the like too are qualities of this [<s>Brahman</s>] — declared by the Lord. // MAnuv_3,2.42 //

children.text: yadi syustādṛśā dharmāḥ sarvajñatvādayo na kim /
children.translated_text: If such properties [exist], why not omniscience and the like too?

children.text: anyāpekṣā yadi syuṣṭe sattaivaṃ deśakālagā // MAnuv_3,2.43 //
children.translated_text: If there is dependence on other [conditions], then even existence would be [dependent on] space and time. // MAnuv_3,2.43 //

children.text: deśakālānapekṣā hi na sattā kvāpi dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: For existence independent of space and time is never seen anywhere.
Of this [<s>Brahman</s>] devoid of all properties, what is comprehended by scripture? // MAnuv_3,2.44 //
And of the <s>Veda</s> that prescribes false properties, the very invalidity [of the <s>Veda</s> follows].

children.text: aprāptāṃ bhrāntimāpādya kiṃ vedo mānatāṃ vrajet // MAnuv_3,2.45 //
children.translated_text: Having imposed a delusion that was never attained [by anyone], how would the <s>Veda</s> attain validity? // MAnuv_3,2.45 //

children.text: na hi vedaṃ vinā brahma vedyaṃ dharmāśca tadgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s> is not knowable without the <s>Veda</s>, and the properties pertaining to it [are not either].

children.text: vedavedyasya mithyātvaṃ yadi naikyasya tat katham // MAnuv_3,2.46 //
children.translated_text: If the falsity of what is to be known by the <s>Veda</s> [is maintained] — then how [would the falsity] of unity [not follow]? // MAnuv_3,2.46 //
The superimposition of properties too — of generic properties and the like, in the Daśārṇa [analogy].
If 'this-ness' and 'that-ness' are properties, then another property is imagined here. // MAnuv_3,2.47 //
Where is superimposition of properties seen for that which is devoid of all properties?
If the superimposition of properties is for the purpose of that — [then there is] infinite regress. // MAnuv_3,2.48 //
[By what means] — the Lord, knowledge of Him, the <s>Veda</s>, perception, inference, evidence —

children.text: bhrāntirviśvasya yenaiva mānābhāsena kalpyate 'tra hi // MAnuv_3,2.49 //
children.translated_text: the delusion of the world is imagined by whatever semblance of a means of knowledge here — // MAnuv_3,2.49 //

children.text: tanmātrasyānyathā bhāvāt kiṃ na syād viśvasatyatā /
children.translated_text: from the otherwise-ness of that alone, why would there not be the reality of the world?

children.text: yenedaṃ kalpyate bhrāntaṃ bhrāntistasyaiva kiṃ na sā // MAnuv_3,2.50 //
children.translated_text: By whatever [means] this [world] is imagined as delusory — is not that delusion itself [applicable to] that very [means]? // MAnuv_3,2.50 //
If that [means] is delusory, then the world and so forth — from the Lord and so forth — would be non-delusory indeed.
The delusions would be [only] of humans, never of the Lord and so forth in any way. // MAnuv_3,2.51 //
If the reality obtained through perception is considered delusory,
whence [comes] the validity even of scripture, from anything other than perception? // MAnuv_3,2.52 //
For the validity of the means of knowledge is [established] by the witness's (<s>sākṣin</s>'s) direct perception alone.

children.text: sākṣiṇaḥ svaprakāśatvamanavasthā tato na hi // MAnuv_3,2.53 //
children.translated_text: The self-luminosity of the witness — therefore there is no infinite regress. // MAnuv_3,2.53 //
When the temporal validity of perception obtains,

children.text: aikyāgamasya kiṃ na syāt tasyāpyetādṛśaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: why would it not [obtain] for the scripture of unity? If that too [has merely temporal validity],
then the falsity of the validity of unity [scripture] — the reality of the world. // MAnuv_3,2.54 //
If the validity of the scripture of unity is desired as unsublateable,
why is the validity of perception not desired as unsublateable? // MAnuv_3,2.55 //
Because of the commonality of loss of non-duality, there is no particular [reason for preference].

children.text: yadi svatastvaṃ prāmāṇye viśvasattā kathaṃ na te // MAnuv_3,2.56 //
children.translated_text: If self-validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) [is maintained], how is the reality of the world not [established] for you? // MAnuv_3,2.56 //

children.text: prāmāṇyasya ca maryādā kālato vyāhatā bhavet /
children.translated_text: And the limit of validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) would be contradicted by time.
If [something] is not a valid means of knowledge at another time, then whence comes its validity now? // MAnuv_3,2.57 //

children.text: mithyātvamānaṃ mokṣe 'pi mānaṃ kiṃ neti bhaṇyatām /
children.translated_text: Let it be stated: is not the cognition of falsity also a valid means of knowledge regarding liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>)?
If it is valid, [then] non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) is undermined; if it is not valid, then there is no liberation either. // MAnuv_3,2.58 //
When the cognition of falsity does not obstruct, there would be the re-occurrence of the universe.
If there is a state of liberation [regardless], then duality would re-occur; otherwise, // MAnuv_3,2.59 //

children.text: amuktatvaṃ tathā kāle kālādhīnā hi muktatā /
children.translated_text: there would be non-liberation at that time, for liberation is dependent on time.
Scripture too says liberation is at the cessation of time;

children.text: mukterapi nivṛttiḥ syāt saṃsāritvamato bhavet // MAnuv_3,2.60 //
children.translated_text: there would also be the cessation of liberation, and hence one would [again] be a transmigrant. // MAnuv_3,2.60 //
Where is it that [the notion of] body-selfhood, established by perception, is contradicted by inference and scripture?

children.text: dehātmatvaṃ yadi na tat prāptaṃ pratyakṣataḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: If that [body-selfhood] is not established by perception anywhere,

children.text: mama deha iti hyeva na deho 'hamiti pramā // MAnuv_3,2.61 //
children.translated_text: for indeed 'my body' — this [is the cognition], not 'I am the body' — that is the valid cognition. // MAnuv_3,2.61 //
And the figurative usage, like 'I am dark' when [one's] body is smeared with mud —
just as with a garment, it would be so if [the property] were caused by an adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>); then,

children.text: svataḥ śuklatvavat kārṣṇyaṃ na mameti pratīyate // MAnuv_3,2.62 //
children.translated_text: like whiteness being intrinsic, 'the darkness is not mine' — thus it is cognized. // MAnuv_3,2.62 //

children.text: kathaṃ ca bhedo dehāderātmano na pramīyate /
children.translated_text: And how is the difference of the self from the body and the like not ascertained?

children.text: jātamātrā mṛgā gāvo hastinaḥ pakṣiṇo khaṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Deer, cows, elephants, birds, and aquatic creatures, just born,
discern the causes of fear, safety, and their own enjoyment. // MAnuv_3,2.63 //

children.text: asmṛtau pūrvadehasya vijñānaṃ tat kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: In the absence of memory of a previous body, how could that knowledge arise?
[It arises] from positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), even when the recollection of the investigation is forgotten. // MAnuv_3,2.64 //
When there is knowledge of another body [from a past life], whence the determination of identity with [the present] body?
Because the self pervades the body, and because of ineptitude in practical dealings, // MAnuv_3,2.65 //
even when the knowledge of difference [is present], like the ember and the fire, like what is not distinct from oneself,

children.text: bhavanti vyavahārāśca na hi pratyakṣagānapi // MAnuv_3,2.66 //
children.translated_text: practical dealings proceed; for even those established by perception // MAnuv_3,2.66 //
are not able to convey objects exactly as experienced.

children.text: lokāstato hi pratyakṣasiddhaṃ nānyena kenacit // MAnuv_3,2.67 //
children.translated_text: People [communicate imperfectly]; therefore, what is established by perception cannot by anything else // MAnuv_3,2.67 //
be obstructed anywhere. If that is so, then [the self being distinct from the body] is not within the scope of a counter-argument.
How then is a future time and the liberation pertaining to it cognized? // MAnuv_3,2.68 //

children.text: āgamo 'pi hi sāmānye siddhe pratyakṣataḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Scripture too, when a general [truth] has been established by perception,
conveys [further] particulars only; how else would the apprehension of [word-]power [occur]? // MAnuv_3,2.69 //
When the apprehension of [word-]power has arisen with respect to past and future objects,

children.text: viśeṣaṃ jñāpayed vākyaṃ na tadajñātaśaktike // MAnuv_3,2.70 //
children.translated_text: a sentence can make known all the particulars — not [a sentence] whose power is unknown. // MAnuv_3,2.70 //
If [word-]power exists [only] in the present, it would not speak of the past or the future.

children.text: yadi śaktigraho 'nyatra kathaṃ sa syāt tadagrahe // MAnuv_3,2.71 //
children.translated_text: If the apprehension of [word-]power is elsewhere [i.e., regarding other times], how could that be when that [time] is not apprehended? // MAnuv_3,2.71 //
If that which is seen [as] a universal conveys [meaning] elsewhere [too],
how would it convey the intrinsic nature of a thing devoid of the universal? // MAnuv_3,2.72 //
A universal of 'intrinsic-nature-ness' has not been accepted by anyone anywhere.

children.text: svarūpaṃ cedanugataṃ vyāvṛttaṃ tatra kiṃ bhavet // MAnuv_3,2.73 //
children.translated_text: If intrinsic nature were something pervading [all], what would be the distinguishing [factor] therein? // MAnuv_3,2.73 //
The selfhood of [things] is accepted ultimately as that which pervades all properties.
When asked 'what is the distinguishing [feature]?', the answer is merely 'the intrinsic nature';

children.text: syāduttaraṃ tato 'nyaccet tadeva svayameva naḥ // MAnuv_3,2.74 //
children.translated_text: if [the answer] were something other than that, that very [other thing] itself [would serve as] ours. // MAnuv_3,2.74 //
Thus, even when there is the apprehension of [word-]power regarding the distinguishing form,

children.text: tasya sāmānyato jñānaṃ vinā sa ca bhavet kutaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.75 //
children.translated_text: the knowledge of that [arises] from the universal — and without that, whence could it arise? // MAnuv_3,2.75 //
Therefore, everything is accepted as having the form of both particular and universal.

children.text: vyāvṛttaṃ yacca sāmānyaṃ tadeva syād viśeṣataḥ // MAnuv_3,2.76 //
children.translated_text: That which is distinguished is [itself] the universal — that very [thing] would be [seen] as particular. // MAnuv_3,2.76 //
There is no identity of properties among entities thereby, mutually,
because the perception of similarity among properties [arises] only from the perception of difference. // MAnuv_3,2.77 //
Therefore, all entities, through [their] universal [aspect], are within the range of the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>).
'Everything' — this cognition of all [things] — how [could it arise] otherwise? // MAnuv_3,2.78 //
From the cognition of some similarity, the apprehension of word-power regarding the entire object
[arises]; and it would be through the validity of that-that similarity. // MAnuv_3,2.79 //
And mental perception (<s>mānasa pratyakṣa</s>), which has past objects as its domain —
the validity of memory is then particularized by pastness. // MAnuv_3,2.80 //
When pastness is accepted as additional to what was experienced,

children.text: mānatā ca kathaṃ na syāt smṛterbādhaśca nātrahi // MAnuv_3,2.81 //
children.translated_text: how could the validity of memory not obtain? And there is no sublation of it here. // MAnuv_3,2.81 //
The validity of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) too — it pervades all experience;
and it is seen to have both pastness and presentness as [its] property-bearers. // MAnuv_3,2.82 //
And it is not merely a portion of memory, since it is unified by the apprehension of 'that' [past] and 'this' [present].

children.text: ato na vatarmānaikaniyamaḥ syād grahe 'kṣaje // MAnuv_3,2.83 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there should be no restriction to the present alone in sense-born cognition. // MAnuv_3,2.83 //

children.text: na ca pramāṇato 'nyā syāt pramitirnāma kutracit /
children.translated_text: And there is nowhere a [thing called] 'resultant cognition' (<s>pramiti</s>) other than the valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).
Because of the absence of a [separate] means of knowledge and the cumbersomeness of the postulation — what use is it? // MAnuv_3,2.84 //
'I have known this' — that is within the range of the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>), having knowledge as its object.

children.text: jñānameva tato 'nyā na pramitirnāma dṛśyate // MAnuv_3,2.85 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge itself [is all there is]; therefore, no other [thing called] 'resultant cognition' is seen. // MAnuv_3,2.85 //
There is never the complete cessation of the valid means of knowledge, the knower, and the knowable.

children.text: svapnānāmapi caiteṣāṃ na bādho dṛśyate kvacit // MAnuv_3,2.86 //
children.translated_text: Even in dreams, no sublation of these is seen anywhere. // MAnuv_3,2.86 //
Waking-ness alone is the one [difference] here; otherwise, [in dreams] it is clearly seen [to be] the same.

children.text: ato mithyā na ca svapno jāgradvajjāgradeva ca // MAnuv_3,2.87 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, dream is not false; like waking, it is indeed waking [in its own domain]. // MAnuv_3,2.87 //
Like the self, the self too could somewhere be the object of error.

children.text: etāvatā na mithyāsau svapne jāgarite tathā // MAnuv_3,2.88 //
children.translated_text: By that much alone, it is not false — in dream, just as in waking. // MAnuv_3,2.88 //
If what is seen otherwise regarding the self is erroneous, even here [in waking] that would be [erroneous].
When there is unsublated continuity, whence the erroneousness of dreams and the like? // MAnuv_3,2.89 //

children.text: na ca kācit pramā viśvabhrāntatve sarvameva ca /
children.translated_text: And no cognition would be valid if the entire [world] were erroneous; and [if]

children.text: abhrāntatve pramāṇaṃ tu kathaṃ tadbhrāntitā bhavet // MAnuv_3,2.90 //
children.translated_text: everything is non-erroneous, then it is a valid means of knowledge — how could its erroneousness obtain? // MAnuv_3,2.90 //

children.text: kiñca bhrāntatvavādī sa bhrāntatvaṃ svamatasya ca /
children.translated_text: Moreover, he who advocates erroneousness necessarily accepts the erroneousness of his own doctrine too.
Therein, when agreement is reached [on this point],
the entire universe will be non-erroneous for the disputant. // MAnuv_3,2.91 //
If there is the erroneousness of [the thesis of] erroneousness, how is there not the truth of non-erroneousness?
That doctrine, vitiated by all defects, should be rejected by those who seek to know. // MAnuv_3,2.92 //
That [doctrine] by which the rejectability of one's own doctrine is always self-accepted —
because of its erroneousness, because of its self-contradictory nature, and merely because [it is] an ornament [of absurdity] — // MAnuv_3,2.93 //
even a madman — how would he wish to accept that doctrine?
Because of the inconceivability of the Lord's power, it is propagated by the greatly deluded. // MAnuv_3,2.94 //
Therefore, <s>māyā</s> here is stated to be [of the nature of] intelligence (<s>prajñā</s>). It is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) belonging to the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: nimittamaiśvarī mukhyaṃ nirmitaṃ trātameva ca // MAnuv_3,2.95 //
children.translated_text: The efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) is the divine [power]; the primary [creation] is that which is fashioned and also protected. // MAnuv_3,2.95 //
Together with and separately from both [causes], it is said to be 'mere <s>māyā</s>.'

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ mātamaiśvaryā trātaṃ saha pṛthak tataḥ // MAnuv_3,2.96 //
children.translated_text: By both, [it is] the measure of sovereignty; what is protected is together with and separately from that. // MAnuv_3,2.96 //
The mind, which is of the nature of intelligence (<s>prajñā</s>) — by that, the mental impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) having the form of mind —
'Intelligence (<s>dhī</s>), awe (<s>bhī</s>) — these are indeed mind' — thus the <s>Śruti</s> states directly. // MAnuv_3,2.97 //
This mind is a mixture of consciousness and unconsciousness, as long as <s>saṃsāra</s> [continues].

children.text: tenāvasthā imāḥ sarvā jīvaḥ paśyati sarvadā // MAnuv_3,2.98 //
children.translated_text: Through that, the <s>jīva</s> always perceives all these states. // MAnuv_3,2.98 //

children.text: manovikārā viṣayāḥ svāpnā yad bahyavanna te /
children.translated_text: Dream objects are modifications of the mind; since they are not external [and] gross like [waking objects],

children.text: sthūlā bhavantyatasteṣāṃ spaṣṭatā na tathā kvacit // MAnuv_3,2.99 //
children.translated_text: therefore their vividness is not the same anywhere. // MAnuv_3,2.99 //

children.text: kvacit spaṣṭā api syuṣye vāsanā mānasī ca sā /
children.translated_text: Somewhere they are vivid too — the mental impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) that is mental,
by the will of the Lord, is concealed within and manifested again by that [will]. // MAnuv_3,2.100 //
Having created the dream-world through the <s>vāsanās</s>, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>),
reducing it to the mere state of <s>vāsanā</s>, conceals it — He, the unborn. // MAnuv_3,2.101 //
Deep sleep, delusion, and waking — being under His own control, [He] always

children.text: jīvaṃ nayati deveśo nānyaḥ kartāsya kaścana // MAnuv_3,2.102 //
children.translated_text: leads the <s>jīva</s>, who is under His control. The Lord of gods (<s>Deveśa</s>) — no other is his agent. // MAnuv_3,2.102 //
Not even from difference of location is there any difference in the Supreme Lord.
Everywhere, He is free from all defects, full, [endowed with] auspicious qualities of consciousness. // MAnuv_3,2.103 //

children.text: tadviruddhaṃ tu yat tatra mānaṃ naiva bhavet kvacit /
children.translated_text: But as for what is contrary to that — there could never be a valid means of knowledge [for it] anywhere.
How could that be a valid means of knowledge here, given the obstruction of the great purport [of scripture]? // MAnuv_3,2.104 //
The Vedic word would be a valid means of knowledge as the cause of the cessation of suffering and the attainment of bliss;
that [comes] from the grace of the Lord alone, not otherwise. // MAnuv_3,2.105 //
Grace arises solely from the knowledge of the excellence of [His] qualities,
and from the full knowledge of [His] freedom from defects — not from anything else. // MAnuv_3,2.106 //
'He who knows Me as free from all defects,

children.text: jānātyasmai prasanno 'haṃ dadyāṃ muktiṃ nacānyathā // MAnuv_3,2.107 //
children.translated_text: endowed with the fullness of all qualities — upon him, being pleased, I would bestow liberation; not otherwise. // MAnuv_3,2.107 //

children.text: yo māmaśeṣābhyadhikaṃ vijānāti sa eva mām /
children.translated_text: He who knows Me as surpassing all — he alone

children.text: vijānātyakhilāṃstasya dadyāṃ kāmān paraṃ padam // MAnuv_3,2.108 //
children.translated_text: knows Me. To him I would grant all desires, [and] the supreme abode. // MAnuv_3,2.108 //

children.text: yo māmevamasammūḍhaḥ kiṃ mā nindanti śatravaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who [knows] Me thus, without delusion — why do enemies revile Me?'
Thus it is ascertained by statements of the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Smṛtis</s>, and the like. // MAnuv_3,2.109 //
From the worldly [perspective] too, liberation [comes] through grace, [which arises] from knowledge of [His] qualities.
Because of the contradiction with the primary [meaning of] the great purport — therefore indeed, // MAnuv_3,2.110 //
defectiveness, attributelessness (<s>nirguṇatva</s>), having few qualities, and the like — in no way
is [any of] that the meaning of <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the rest. The meaning of the entirety [of scripture],

children.text: arthaḥ svayaṃ vinirṇīto vāsudevena sādaram // MAnuv_3,2.111 //
children.translated_text: contrary to that, has been determined by <s>Vāsudeva</s> Himself, with care. // MAnuv_3,2.111 //
'This most secret teaching has been declared by Me, O sinless one.'

children.text: etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata // MAnuv_3,2.112 //
children.translated_text: 'Having understood this, one would become wise and fulfilled, O <s>Bhārata</s>.' // MAnuv_3,2.112 //
Therefore, because of contradiction with all valid scriptures, inference
does not operate there; by that, the Lord is ascertained [as possessing] all auspicious qualities. // MAnuv_3,2.113 //
And the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> from [the Lord], like the Lord, is not obtained through [the fact of both being] conscious.
For scripture declares its <s>ābhāsa</s>-nature (reflection-nature) emphatically. // MAnuv_3,2.114 //
'Just as there is a shadow of a person' — 'in this [Brahman], that [jīva] is not spread out [as identical].'

children.text: chāyā yathā puṃsadṛśā pumādhīnā ca dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Just as a shadow resembles a person [and] is seen as dependent on that person,
even so, all [beings] from <s>Brahmā</s> onwards are of the nature of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>). // MAnuv_3,2.115 //
In existence, cognition, and effects, [each] is understood as dependent on the Person;

children.text: ābhāsa eva puruṣā muktāśca paramātmanaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.116 //
children.translated_text: reflections (<s>ābhāsas</s>) indeed are [all] persons, even the liberated, of the Supreme Self. // MAnuv_3,2.116 //

children.text: chāyā viṣṇo ramā tasyāśchāyā dhātā viśeṣakau /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu's</s> shadow is <s>Ramā</s>; her shadow is <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Dhātā</s>) — these two are distinguished.
Of him, [the shadows are] <s>Indra</s> and <s>Kāma</s>; and of those two, all others. // MAnuv_3,2.117 //
Of <s>Hari</s>, [the reflection is] <s>Brahmā</s>; of him, <s>Vāc</s> (Speech); of her, the two distinguished ones are <s>Indra</s>; of these two,
<s>Māra</s> — all are reflections; of these two, [all others arise] through dependence on them. // MAnuv_3,2.118 //
All are of limited power, [while] the Supreme <s>Hari</s> is of full power.
Even in consciousness, they are different from Him; therefore, by Him always —

children.text: ityādiśrutivākyebhyo jñāyate bheda eva hi // MAnuv_3,2.119 //
children.translated_text: from such Śruti statements and the like, difference alone is known. // MAnuv_3,2.119 //
The reflection-nature (<s>ābhāsatva</s>) of the <s>jīva</s> with respect to the Supreme Self has been ascertained.

children.text: tanna yuktaṃ yadābhāsa upādhyāyatta īyate // MAnuv_3,2.120 //
children.translated_text: It is not proper [to say] that the reflection is dependent on an adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>). // MAnuv_3,2.120 //
Because of the absence of dependence on an <s>upādhi</s>, because of the contradiction with reflection-nature [if upādhi-dependent],
and because [the jīva] is a part through [its] consciousness, [the doctrine of] aggregate-identity would follow. // MAnuv_3,2.121 //
Therefore, the separateness stated [in scripture] would apply to the aggregate and the part.
The name 'Lord' (<s>Īśa</s>) belongs to the aggregate; it is declared with reference to the Lord's forms. // MAnuv_3,2.122 //
Therefore, upon the removal of adventitious conditions (<s>upādhis</s>) such as the body and the like, there would be equality [with God].
But [if] the reflections [derive] primarily from the Lord's forms, like a crystal and the like — // MAnuv_3,2.123 //
then the forms dependent on the <s>upādhi</s> would be destroyed [in liberation].
For the purpose of removing this doubt, the Lord of the <s>Vedas</s>, the Master, says:
'For this very reason [scripture uses] the simile' — [indicating] another, distinguished from [mere] reflection. // MAnuv_3,2.124 //
What has been stated [is] that dependence [of the jīva on God] in all states without exception,

children.text: jīvasya sadṛśatvaṃ ca cittvamātraṃ nacāparam // MAnuv_3,2.125 //
children.translated_text: [and] the <s>jīva's</s> similarity [to God] is consciousness alone and nothing more. // MAnuv_3,2.125 //
By that much alone, the reflection-form of these beings of conscious nature —
And there is no excessive similarity in the illustration due to dependence on conditions and so forth. // MAnuv_3,2.126 //
Even a certain similarity in bliss and so forth belongs to the Lord, [though also found] in gods and humans. /

children.text: tata ābhāsate nityaṃ tadvadābhāsate 'pi ca // MAnuv_3,2.127 //
children.translated_text: From that [source], it always shines forth; and it also shines forth in a manner similar to that. // MAnuv_3,2.127 //
Since shining and existence are not complete [in the <s>jīva</s>], therefore /

children.text: jīva ābhāsa uddiṣṭaḥ sadaiva paramātmanaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.128 //
children.translated_text: the <s>jīva</s> is designated as a reflection (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), always. // MAnuv_3,2.128 //
Not [that] dependence on him [follows] from the analogy with a reflection of the sun and so forth in water — /
rather, there is dependence on him, and there is merely a certain similarity. /
This is shown by the <s>sūtra</s> with all [relevant] means of knowledge. // MAnuv_3,2.129 //
From the perspective of the difference between <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> alone — whence the collective unity? /
Because of <s>Hari</s>'s complete freedom from all defects and [his] possession of all powers — // MAnuv_3,2.130 //
'endowed with all' — so it has been stated. How, then, can there be unity with one who has defects? /
If endowed with all powers — how, from independence, could he have defects? // MAnuv_3,2.131 //
If unity without [self-]awareness — that is not [true] oneness. /
And when there is unity of conscious beings, there is [self-]awareness — and there is no other means of proof. // MAnuv_3,2.132 //
If it is merely the collective unity devoid of [self-]awareness — /
then, in the case of conscious beings, that would be merely nominal, since [there is no true unity]. // MAnuv_3,2.133 //
If [self-]awareness [of unity] would exist in liberation — then there would be the state of false knowledge. /

children.text: sarvajña ekatāṃ nānusandhatte naiva sā yataḥ // MAnuv_3,2.134 //
children.translated_text: The omniscient one does not [self-]apprehend oneness — since that [oneness] does not exist. // MAnuv_3,2.134 //
If [self-]awareness [of unity] would exist afterward — then there would be the state of false knowledge. /
If [one says] the existing [self-]awareness does not [exist] — then ignorance would follow. // MAnuv_3,2.135 //

children.text: asadaikyaṃ bhavet paścād yadi syāt saptamo rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: If non-existent unity were to occur afterward — then a seventh <s>rasa</s> (taste) [would also be possible]. /
Therefore, collective unity is rejected from afar, always. // MAnuv_3,2.136 //
Therefore, that which is exalted with all qualities without remainder and is free from defects — /

children.text: tāvadeveśvaro nāma tatra bhedo 'pi na kvacit // MAnuv_3,2.137 //
children.translated_text: only to that extent is it called the Lord; therein, there is no difference whatsoever. // MAnuv_3,2.137 //

children.text: neha nānāsti kimapi harayo 'yamayaṃ hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Here there is no diversity whatsoever' — '<s>Haris</s> — this one is verily he' — /

children.text: ityādiśrutimānena jīvāṃśāḥ sarva eva ca // MAnuv_3,2.138 //
children.translated_text: by such <s>śruti</s> texts as these, the <s>jīvas</s> are all parts [of the Lord]. // MAnuv_3,2.138 //
If those who invariably possess [self-]awareness have oneness inherently — /
even a minimal part has complete [self-]awareness of the possessor of parts. // MAnuv_3,2.139 //
And through the part born on earth, pleasure, suffering, and so forth pertaining to it /
are experienced; but a certain distinction would be brought about by the Lord. // MAnuv_3,2.140 //
Because of the inconceivable power of the Lord, nothing whatsoever is impossible anywhere. /
Lordship itself is indeed untenable if this one has oneness with the <s>jīvas</s>. /
That a non-lord should have lordship — this is contradicted by all means of knowledge. // MAnuv_3,2.141 //
If what is known as the Lord is [then known as] a non-lord — then <s>śruti</s> /
would teach what is known as a non-lord as having lordship — or vice versa. // MAnuv_3,2.142 //
By contradiction with the relied-upon [<s>śruti</s>], it would not acquire the status of a valid means of knowledge. /
Therefore, from the very establishment of lordship — nothing whatsoever is possible for him [otherwise]. // MAnuv_3,2.143 //
When lordship and the difference from the non-lord are properly illuminated by <s>śruti</s>, /

children.text: ayuktamapi cānyatra yuktaṃ bhavati tadbalāt // MAnuv_3,2.144 //
children.translated_text: even what is inappropriate elsewhere becomes appropriate by the force of that [<s>śruti</s>]. // MAnuv_3,2.144 //
Therefore, whatever is seen elsewhere too — that is to be attributed to the Lord alone. /
For even what is obtained from an apparent <s>śruti</s> — [provided] it does not obstruct lordship. // MAnuv_3,2.145 //

children.text: īśo 'nīśo jaganmithyā duḥkhī mukto bhidā na hi /
children.translated_text: 'The Lord is a non-lord'; 'the world is false'; 'he is suffering'; 'liberated'; 'there is no difference' — /
this is a self-contradiction of the thesis — a fault exceeding all other faults. // MAnuv_3,2.146 //
Thus says the <s>Brahmatarka</s> — this is supremely to be rejected by /
all those who wish to exist — this doctrine of the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord. // MAnuv_3,2.147 //
Nothing is inappropriate for the Ruler — that which does not contradict his lordship. /
Whatever contradicts lordship — that alone is straightforwardly inappropriate. // MAnuv_3,2.148 //
Having harmonized all valid means of knowledge with the non-contradiction of lordship, /

children.text: siddheśitvena cāyuktamapi hīśe na yojayet // MAnuv_3,2.149 //
children.translated_text: and with lordship established — one should not attribute even what is inappropriate to the Lord. // MAnuv_3,2.149 //
Whatever is obtained from valid means of knowledge in its entirety — one should not attribute non-validity anywhere. /
Thus says the <s>Brahmatarka</s> — therefore, what is stated here is appropriate. // MAnuv_3,2.150 //
And he, because of having a form that is non-material, is formless [in the ordinary sense]; [yet] his form, consisting of his own qualities, /
having the nature of head, hands, feet, and so forth — this is accepted. // MAnuv_3,2.151 //
Therefore there is no impermanence, nor contradiction with the two [groups of] <s>śrutis</s>. /
For just as, even when the [ordinary material] light has been abandoned, /
'the self alone is the light' — <s>śruti</s> says this regarding the Lord as the light of the <s>jīva</s>. // MAnuv_3,2.152 //
In accordance with the gradation of devotion to him, there is a gradation in what pertains to liberation, /
and of <s>Brahmā</s> and all others — in bliss and so forth, according to sequence. // MAnuv_3,2.153 //
Even as [if] like reflections, the bliss of these [<s>jīvas</s>] and other qualities — /
are dependent on the qualities of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and are extremely small in comparison. // MAnuv_3,2.154 //
Therefore, [the <s>jīva</s>] is always different. The knowledge of the Supreme is other; /

children.text: anyajjñānaṃ tu jīvānāmanya ānanda īśatā // MAnuv_3,2.155 //
children.translated_text: the knowledge of the <s>jīvas</s> is other; the bliss is other; the lordship [is other]. // MAnuv_3,2.155 //

children.text: mukhyeśatā pareśasya gauṇī jīvasya sā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: The primary lordship belongs to the Supreme Lord; secondary [lordship] belongs to the <s>jīva</s> — because /
of <s>śruti</s>. Since creation and destruction are stated to be dependent on him, /
[the argument that] persistence does not require [a cause] because of being natural — is not appropriate. // MAnuv_3,2.156 //
Because the entire nature of everything is dependent on the Lord. /

children.text: avyakto 'pi svaktayaiva bhaktānāṃ dṛśyate hariḥ // MAnuv_3,2.157 //
children.translated_text: Even though unmanifest, <s>Hari</s> is seen by devotees through their own devotion. // MAnuv_3,2.157 //
His qualities, though non-different [from him], are eternally [existing]; yet all are distinguished — /
established as quality and qualified, and as enjoyed and enjoyer. // MAnuv_3,2.158 //
By having the nature of <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) in them, and having the nature of eternal power, /
because of eternal persistence — the non-eternality of properties, actions, and so forth [does not follow]. // MAnuv_3,2.159 //
And this having-the-nature-of-<s>viśeṣa</s> is not non-eternal, [nor is] the having-the-nature-of-power [non-eternal]. /

children.text: saiva yat saviśeṣā syād viśeṣo 'nyo nacāpyayam // MAnuv_3,2.160 //
children.translated_text: If that very thing is with-<s>viśeṣa</s> — [then] <s>viśeṣa</s> is not something other [from it] either. // MAnuv_3,2.160 //
Nevertheless, from the cause of self-sustenance, it would be through <s>viśeṣa</s>; /
because of being known as <s>viśeṣa</s> by all means of knowledge as well. // MAnuv_3,2.161 //
'He created, he withdrew' — <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) is indeed understood [therein]. /

children.text: śrutyaiva sa sa eveti tadabhedaśca gamyate // MAnuv_3,2.162 //
children.translated_text: And by <s>śruti</s> — 'he is that very one' — non-difference also is understood. // MAnuv_3,2.162 //

children.text: bhedo yadi viśeṣasya sa bhedo bhedinā katham /
children.translated_text: If there is a difference of the <s>viśeṣa</s> [from the entity] — how is that difference [related] to the possessor of difference? /

children.text: bhinnaścedanavasthā syādabhinnaścet purā na kim // MAnuv_3,2.163 //
children.translated_text: If different [from it] — there would be a regress; if non-different — why not [accept it] in the first place? // MAnuv_3,2.163 //
'<s>Viśeṣa</s> is indeed non-different' — by that, it is not accepted [by the opponent]. /
If the non-different is without <s>viśeṣa</s> — then whence the difference between that [and the entity]? // MAnuv_3,2.164 //
'This is different from that by this and by that' — that which [distinguishes] is through <s>viśeṣa</s>. /

children.text: bheda evaiṣa bahudhā dṛśyate tat kimuttaram // MAnuv_3,2.165 //
children.translated_text: This very [thing] is difference — it is seen in many forms; what further [objection]? // MAnuv_3,2.165 //
Both non-difference and difference have the nature of the possessor-of-difference as their own nature. /
If those two are without distinction — then the two words [bheda and abheda] would be synonyms. // MAnuv_3,2.166 //
And who would say that the words 'difference' and 'non-difference' are synonyms? /
Difference from each other, and non-difference from the possessor-of-difference — if [you claim] <s>viśeṣa</s> [is needed] — // MAnuv_3,2.167 //
how [is there] difference in the without-<s>viśeṣa</s>? One difference from the possessor-of-difference — likewise the distinction. /
And the further differentiation of those two — would arise from the mere nature of difference. // MAnuv_3,2.168 //
If the <s>viśeṣa</s> of the possessor-of-difference and difference is understood — /
[then] is there also a difference of non-difference and the possessor-of-non-difference? What of the difference of non-difference and difference? // MAnuv_3,2.169 //
If dealings everywhere would be through <s>viśeṣa</s> alone — /

children.text: kalpanāgauravāyaiva kiṃ bhedaḥ kalpyate tadā // MAnuv_3,2.170 //
children.translated_text: for the very sake of avoiding cumbersomeness of postulation — why is difference [separately] postulated then? // MAnuv_3,2.170 //
Because of the absence of a cognition of unity — difference alone [exists] between a cow and a horse. /

children.text: sa eveti pratītau hi viśeṣo nāma bhaṇyate // MAnuv_3,2.171 //
children.translated_text: In the cognition 'he is that very one' — that is called <s>viśeṣa</s>. // MAnuv_3,2.171 //
For the purpose of establishing the non-synonymity of existence (<s>sat</s>), consciousness (<s>cit</s>), and so forth — even by the <s>Māyāvādin</s> /
this <s>viśeṣa</s> must be accepted. If [it is qualified by] 'unreal <s>viśeṣa</s>' — /
a separate word to refute each one individually — is [then] desired. // MAnuv_3,2.172 //
The distinctness of the real would also arise through the <s>viśeṣa</s> characterized by the absence of unreal <s>viśeṣa</s>; /

children.text: satyasyāpi bhavet sā ca tathā cedanavasthitiḥ // MAnuv_3,2.173 //
children.translated_text: and if so, there would be a regress. // MAnuv_3,2.173 //

children.text: yadi satye viśeṣo na na taduktirbhavet tadā /
children.translated_text: If <s>viśeṣa</s> does not [exist] in the real — then the statement of that [reality] would not be possible. /

children.text: lakṣyate cet tena lakṣyamityapi syād viśeṣitā // MAnuv_3,2.174 //
children.translated_text: If [the real] is indicated [by a mark] — then the distinctness 'it is indicated by that mark' would also arise. // MAnuv_3,2.174 //
In the case of repeated indication too, there would be a regress. /
If being-distinguished-by-absence is accepted by you — // MAnuv_3,2.175 //
freedom from non-omniscience and so forth will also be [established] for you in this way. /
Then there would be omniscience itself — since both [negative particles] '<s>a</s>' and '<s>na</s>' have the meaning of [affirming] existence. // MAnuv_3,2.176 //
If [you say] this is not acceptable — because non-pleasure cannot be removed [by double negation]; /
then non-existence, non-consciousness, and so forth would follow — then non-existence and so forth [would apply]. // MAnuv_3,2.177 //
If it is accepted that [<s>Brahman</s>] is contradictory to untruth and the like — /
then why is being-contradictory-to-non-lordship not similarly prevented? // MAnuv_3,2.178 //
Through the very refutation of [the doctrine of] the 'partless' — thus <s>viśeṣa</s>, by the proponent of the partless — /
even when [his own position is] refuted — must be accepted with an unchanged mind, there being no alternative. // MAnuv_3,2.179 //
By both the proponent of the partless and [the proponent of] the refutation [of the partless], with the part and the whole — /

children.text: mahādareṇa śirasi viśeṣo dhārya eva hi // MAnuv_3,2.180 //
children.translated_text: <s>viśeṣa</s> must indeed be borne on the head with great reverence. // MAnuv_3,2.180 //
Therefore, with three illustrations, the <s>Bhagavān</s> declared the extreme non-difference /
of qualities, with reverence — and that [follows] the <s>abhihitānvaya</s> (expressed-connection) [theory]. // MAnuv_3,2.181 //
When the statement of all <s>viśeṣas</s> is made in general terms, /
by even a single subsequent word, the understanding of the specific [<s>viśeṣa</s>] would arise. // MAnuv_3,2.182 //
Since there is indeed oneness of the entity with all its <s>viśeṣas</s>, /
therefore, having been known in general — by the force of another word, again, /
there would be specific knowledge — hence the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (connected-denotation) [theory follows]. // MAnuv_3,2.183 //
Since a word's own meaning is always connected with some specific [other meaning] — /
'by this [it is connected]' — that very connected-denotation is known through experience. // MAnuv_3,2.184 //
If this word were to denote its own meaning as unconnected — /

children.text: tathānyānyapi sarvāṇi kaḥ kuryādanvayaṃ punaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.185 //
children.translated_text: then all other [words] too [would denote unconnected meanings]; who then would make the connection? // MAnuv_3,2.185 //

children.text: vyāpāro na hi śabdasya paraḥ svārthaprakāśanāt /
children.translated_text: For the word has no operation beyond the illumination of its own meaning. /
Even a person, when by a single utterance his purpose is fulfilled — // MAnuv_3,2.186 //

children.text: anvayasya kathaṃ jñānaṃ śabdārthatvaṃ yadāsya na /
children.translated_text: how would there be knowledge of the connection, when it is not the meaning of the word? /
When the utterance is made with those words of unconnected meaning — // MAnuv_3,2.187 //

children.text: ananvitaḥ syācchabdārtho na tadartho hi so 'nvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: the word-meaning would be unconnected; for that connection is not its meaning. /
The wise say that a sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is merely words free from expectancy. // MAnuv_3,2.188 //

body.translated_text: And that freedom-from-expectancy would be achieved by the denotation of each respective meaning. // MAnuv_3,2.189 //

children.translated_text: First, incompleteness of meanings is desired as expectancy. /

children.text: karmakartṛkriyāṇāṃ tu pūrtau ko 'nyo 'nvayo bhavet // MAnuv_3,2.190 //
children.translated_text: But when object, agent, and action are complete — what other connection could there be? // MAnuv_3,2.190 //
If incompleteness [exists even] with the words spoken — is it filled by a hare's horn? /

children.text: vyāpāraścet punasteṣāmanuktāvapi kiṃ na saḥ // MAnuv_3,2.191 //
children.translated_text: If there is [still] an operation of those [words] even when unstated — why is that [operation] not [already present]? // MAnuv_3,2.191 //
If, when spoken, the operation is desired as [making the meaning] established in the intellect — /

children.text: buddhisthatvāya yatnaṃ na kathaṃ kuryuḥ puraiva ca /
children.translated_text: then why would they not first make an effort for [the meaning] to be established in the intellect? /

children.text: puruṣādhīnatā teṣāṃ yadi paścācca sā samā // MAnuv_3,2.192 //
children.translated_text: If their [operation] is dependent on a person — afterward, that [dependence] is the same. // MAnuv_3,2.192 //
If a person is required for their connection afterward — /
then for those whose denotation is unconnected, when he exerts [himself] in stating other meanings — /

children.text: yatatāṃ śabdaśaktiścet tatra naivānvaye katham // MAnuv_3,2.193 //
children.translated_text: if it is the power of the word [that connects] — then how not in the [original] connection? // MAnuv_3,2.193 //
Because of faults such as cumbersomeness of postulation — the <s>abhihitānvaya</s> (expressed-connection) [theory] /
is also contradicted by experience — [and] should be rejected by the wise. // MAnuv_3,2.194 //
For when the word 'agent' is stated, since the general property is known, /
desiring [to know] the specific property — one asks 'what [exactly]?' // MAnuv_3,2.195 //
When the specific properties of quality, action, and so forth are subsequently stated, /
one becomes free from expectancy — because words are denotative of connected [meanings]. // MAnuv_3,2.196 //
Therefore, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, one, having the nature of infinite qualities, alone /
is spoken of by all the <s>Vedas</s> — and those [qualities] are entirely unique. // MAnuv_3,2.197 //
All [qualities] have the nature of all qualities; all are indeed the makers of all. /
Nevertheless, they are also possessed of distinctions, and from the understanding of the learned // 3.2.198 //
they are denoted by various words, and this is proper from the perspective of teaching; /
the similarity with other forms of bliss and the like is through favorableness and so forth; the supreme // 3.2.199 //

children.text: pūrṇatvādi mahat teṣāṃ vailakṣaṇyaṃ śrutau śrutam /
children.translated_text: fullness and the like — their great distinctiveness is heard in the <s>Śruti</s>; /
in the fullness, He is the controller of all; from bliss — the supreme unique one // 3.2.200 //
this great aggregate of qualities is <s>Vāsudeva</s>; He is without parts; /

children.text: vāsudevaśrutiḥ saiṣā guṇān vakti hareḥ parān // MAnuv_3,2.201 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Vāsudeva Śruti</s> declares the supreme qualities of <s>Hari</s> // 3.2.201 //
He alone, always seeing the innumerable and beginningless <s>dharmas</s> and <s>adharmas</s> /

children.text: dharmādharmān sadā paśyan svecchayā bodhayatyajaḥ // MAnuv_3,2.202 //
children.translated_text: abiding in all <s>jīvas</s>, awakens [them] by His own will, the unborn one // 3.2.202 //

children.text: kāṃścit teṣāṃ phalaṃ caiva dadāti svayamacyutaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s> (the infallible one) Himself gives to some of them the fruit [of their <s>karmas</s>]; /
they [the <s>karmas</s>] do not effect any particular impulsion and the like — /
this is said; never could they do so at any time; therefore He is independent, without metaphor // 3.2.203 //

children.text: karmāṇi tāni ca pṛthak cetanānyeva sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: And those <s>karmas</s> are each separately conscious entities entirely, /
with non-conscious bodies, and bearing the fruits of their own <s>karma</s> // 3.2.204 //
And in each one of them, there are infinite <s>karmas</s> of this very kind; /
and those too [are] likewise — thus the Lord's limitless supreme power // 3.2.205 //
Even a single <s>brahmahatyā</s> (Brahmin-slaying) — as declared by <s>Hari</s> in the <s>Varāha</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] — /
was expelled from the king's body by the hymn praising <s>Brahman</s> alone // 3.2.206 //

children.text: stotrasya tasya māhātmyād vyādhatvaṃ gamitā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the greatness of that hymn, it was then transformed into a disease; /

children.text: prāpya jñānaṃ paraṃ cāpa tathānyānyapi sarvadā // MAnuv_3,2.207 //
children.translated_text: having attained supreme knowledge, [it was liberated]; and thus other [<s>karmas</s>] too, always // 3.2.207 //
infinite [in number] — thus stated by the Lord <s>Kapila</s> — /

children.text: saṃsāre pacyamānāni karmāṇyapi pṛthak pṛthak // MAnuv_3,2.208 //
children.translated_text: are ripening in <s>saṃsāra</s>, each <s>karma</s> separately // 3.2.208 //
Therefore, <s>Janārdana</s>, the aggregate of infinite greatness and qualities, /

children.text: bhaktyā paramayā'rādhya iti pādārtha īryate // MAnuv_3,2.209 //
children.translated_text: should be worshipped with supreme devotion — thus the meaning of this <s>pāda</s> is declared // 3.2.209 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: From detachment, firmness of devotion; when from that <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation) arises, /

children.text: āparokṣyaṃ bhaved viṣṇoriti pādakramo bhavet // MAnuv_3,3.1 //
children.translated_text: direct perception (<s>aparokṣa</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s> would come about — thus is the order of this <s>pāda</s> // 3.3.1 //
Having understood the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> through reasoning, having rejected rival doctrines, /
and having removed the mutual contradiction of all statements // 3.3.2 //
having become an <s>adhyātma-praṇava</s> (one who has internalized <s>Om</s>), because of His proximity, /
because of the cognition of the contradictions in many reasonings, because of the <s>Śruti</s> associated with that // 3.3.3 //
and having removed the contradictions of <s>Śrutis</s>, having removed the contradictions /
in the statements about <s>prāṇa</s> and skin, being delighted by His grace // 3.3.4 //
knowing the Lord's creatorship of the body, from the remembrance of His fatherhood, /
generating special affection, beyond [what comes from] His creatorship of all // 3.3.5 //
and producing great reverence, and because of extreme suffering elsewhere [i.e., in <s>saṃsāra</s>], /
generating intense detachment, from the knowledge of the abundance of His qualities // 3.3.6 //
and because everything is under His control, having attained firmness of devotion, /
one should strive for <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation) alone, through the attainment of a distinguished teacher // 3.3.7 //
When it is said '<s>Brahman</s> is to be inquired into' — what is the doubt? /
Even when 'therefore' is stated, because of the non-statement of the specific [reason], again // 3.3.8 //
because of having heard of His creatorship of creation, bondage, liberation, and the rest — /
'since He is the bestower of liberation and the rest, therefore He is to be inquired into by you' — /

children.text: ityāha tat paraṃ brahma vyāsākhyaṃ jñānaraśmimat // MAnuv_3,3.9 //
children.translated_text: thus speaks that supreme <s>Brahman</s>, named <s>Vyāsa</s>, radiant with rays of knowledge // 3.3.9 //

children.text: yenaiva bandhamokṣaḥ syāt sa ca jijñāsayā gataḥ /
children.translated_text: He by whom alone bondage and liberation would come about — He is reached through inquiry; /
the Lord, being well-pleased, would become the bestower of liberation through inquiry into Him // 3.3.10 //
How indeed is the Lord's bestowal of liberation and the rest known? /
If so — because He is the source of scripture; for the bestower of liberation is known through scripture // 3.3.11 //
If liberation could somehow come from things ascertained by perception, /
then why are all these beings drowned in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>? // 3.3.12 //
Since the removal of suffering invariably occurs through perception, /
all beings, from kings and others, run toward that [perceptible remedy] alone // 3.3.13 //
If liberation were knowable through inference, the very inference of that /
would preclude the bestower-of-liberation-hood, as in the case of an observed person // 3.3.14 //
Therefore, the sole bestower of liberation is certainly knowable through scripture alone; /
and there is no other knowable through scripture as bestower of liberation besides <s>Keśava</s> // 3.3.15 //

children.text: mokṣado hi svatantraḥ syāt paratantraḥ svayaṃ sṛtau /
children.translated_text: For the bestower of liberation must be independent; one who is dependent and himself /

children.text: vartamānaḥ kathaṃ śaktaḥ paramokṣāya kevalam // MAnuv_3,3.16 //
children.translated_text: situated in <s>saṃsāra</s> — how would he be capable of giving liberation to another alone? // 3.3.16 //

children.text: anyāśrayeṇa yadyeṣa dadyānmokṣaṃ sa eva hi /
children.translated_text: If he would give liberation by depending on another, then that very one [on whom he depends] /
if not followed by him, would not give liberation — from the statement of another [<s>Śruti</s>]; /
therefore, for that purpose too, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be known by those who seek liberation // 3.3.17 //

children.text: yamevaiṣa iti śrutyā tameveti ca sādaram /
children.translated_text: 'Whom this [self] chooses' — by this <s>Śruti</s>; and 'him alone' — with respect; /
the source-of-scripture-hood belongs to Him alone — this is known by those who follow the <s>Vedas</s> // 3.3.18 //
'Those who know Him become immortal' — and the one who is ocean-going [<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>]; /
'That alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — thus ascertained by <s>Śruti</s> // 3.3.19 //

children.text: yataḥ prasūteti tataḥ sṛṣṭimāha tato hariḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From whom these [are] born' — from that He declares creation; from that, <s>Hari</s> /
is the source of scripture — and that no other is, primarily — this is understood // 3.3.20 //
The source-of-scripture-hood of this [<s>Hari</s>] is known indeed from harmonization; /
with the prefix 'sam-,' the primary and supreme meaning is expressed // 3.3.21 //
Thus, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the supremely primary meaning — from <s>Śruti</s>; /
for ascertainment, the word 'na' (not) — thus sang the Lord of the <s>Vedas</s> // 3.3.22 //
How is harmonization to be known by people who know only a few <s>Śākhās</s> (branches)? /

children.text: vedā hyanantā iti hi śrutirāhāpyanantatām // MAnuv_3,3.23 //
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Vedas</s> are infinite' — thus the <s>Śruti</s> declares their infinitude // 3.3.23 //
The determination of infinite <s>Vedas</s> would be like crossing /
the ocean of the great dissolution — therefore harmonization cannot be known here // 3.3.24 //
To dispel this doubt, He, the ocean of compassion, says: /
even though the ocean of scripture is impossible to cross, /
'this is determined by Me alone — [Me] in whom [universes are] dissolved in [My] body-pores' // 3.3.25 //
Even though the meaning of all the <s>Vedas</s> is inaccessible by all means of knowledge, /
'in My knowledge, in the unmanifest space, it attains the size of an atom' // 3.3.26 //
Thus illuminating, the Lord of the universe declares the knowability /
of the entire <s>Veda</s> — the general purport — directly // 3.3.27 //
Who indeed could state the general purport of the wealth of infinite scripture /
other than that one sun of knowledge — <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>)? // 3.3.28 //
Another, even of small intellect, knowing the substance of four or five branches, /
could state [it] inferentially, by his [<s>Vyāsa</s>'s] grace // 3.3.29 //
Thus, the Lord who primarily knows the general purport of all [<s>Vedas</s>] entirely, /

children.text: pratijajñe dṛḍhaṃ yasmād devānāmapi pūryate // MAnuv_3,3.30 //
children.translated_text: firmly promised — since he fulfills [the understanding] even of the <s>devas</s> // 3.3.30 //
Therefore, the harmonization of all the <s>Vedas</s> is thus established; /

children.text: iti sujñāpitārtho 'pi pṛthak cāha samanvayam // MAnuv_3,3.31 //
children.translated_text: even though the meaning has been well explained, he also states the harmonization separately // 3.3.31 //
Therein, first, the harmonization of words well-known elsewhere /
is in the one to be denoted here — like the overthrow of a great wrestler // 3.3.32 //
Even though [there is] great superiority beyond this, of what is stated in the fourth <s>pāda</s>, /
in that great harmonization, not everyone has the qualification // 3.3.33 //
<s>Brahman</s> alone is the primary qualified [person] there; others in due order; /
and because of difficulty, it is not stated here directly in the first place // 3.3.34 //
Therefore, for the determination of words well-known elsewhere, /
the Lord first undertook [this]; therein, bliss and other qualities /
are determined as belonging to the Lord alone, by recourse to <s>Śruti</s> and reasoning // 3.3.35 //
All [words] that pertain to other deities, because of the etymological reason for their usage, /
actually denote <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; and by association, figuratively // 3.3.36 //
they speak here of other deities; because of declaring their specific qualities, /
they would speak of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone as the supreme — thus others too, entirely // 3.3.37 //
Thus, the great mass of words well-known elsewhere, in its entirety — /

children.text: jñāte samanvaye viṣṇau liṅgairhyeṣa samanvayaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.38 //
children.translated_text: when the harmonization with <s>Viṣṇu</s> is known through indicatory marks, this is the harmonization // 3.3.38 //

children.text: teṣāmanyagatatve tu na syāt samyak samanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If they pertained to another, there would not be a proper harmonization; /
thus, the harmonization of all indicatory marks is with <s>Brahman</s> alone // 3.3.39 //
Or, there might be pertinence to both — of the indicatory marks and words — /
to remove this doubt, [the harmonization is shown] from the cognition in both [contexts] // 3.3.40 //
The harmonization of words that are current, together with indicatory marks, particularly, /
is with <s>Hari</s> alone — which is never primarily elsewhere // 3.3.41 //

children.text: śabdā liṅgāni ca yato naivānyatra svatantratā /
children.translated_text: Since neither the words nor the indicatory marks have independence elsewhere — /
in what lacks independence, the etymological reason for a word's usage is not primary // 3.3.42 //
Therefore, those who, being dependent on Him, have attained the status of word-meanings, /
[do so] through a very minor quality that serves as the reason for the word's usage // 3.3.43 //

children.text: ayo yathā dāhakatvaṃ sa eveśaḥ svatantrataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as iron [has] the property of burning [only through fire] — He, the Lord, alone, by independence, /

children.text: mukhyaśabdārtha iti hi svīkartavyo manīṣibhiḥ // MAnuv_3,3.44 //
children.translated_text: should be accepted by the wise as the primary word-meaning // 3.3.44 //
Thus he says; and even when the harmonization of all words with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> /
is established, for all words, it is not in any way proper // 3.3.45 //
that there be the attainment of contradiction, inferiority, and the like; since that attainment would occur — /
if so, inferiority and the like are perceived to be twofold // 3.3.46 //
that which is the cause of the inferiority of the supreme — [the supreme] itself being supreme — /

children.text: so 'pi hyavaraśabdārtho yathā rājā jayī bhavet // MAnuv_3,3.47 //
children.translated_text: that too is the meaning of the word 'inferior'; just as a king might be 'conquered' // 3.3.47 //
Another [sense of] inferiority is the experience of it; the former exists in <s>Keśava</s>; /

children.text: dvitīyo jīva evāsti svātantrānnaca dūṣaṇam // MAnuv_3,3.48 //
children.translated_text: the second exists in the <s>jīva</s> alone — from independence, there is no fault // 3.3.48 //
Thus, when the harmonization of all words in their entirety with <s>Hari</s> /
is stated, since what is free from contradiction would have harmonization, /
therefore all contradictions have been removed by the Lord // 3.3.49 //
When the determination of reality has been achieved through harmonization and non-contradiction, /

children.text: kiṃ mayā kāryamityeva syād buddhiradhikāriṇaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.50 //
children.translated_text: the thought of the qualified person would be: 'What is to be done by me?' // 3.3.50 //
Therein, for the purpose of prescribing devotion, in the continuous series of evils of non-devotion, /
having stated [the evils], for the firmness of devotion, when the accumulation of all qualities is declared, /
<s>upāsanā</s> (meditation) is to be stated — 'always to be practiced' — with respect indeed // 3.3.51 //
And that <s>upāsanā</s> is twofold: having the form of study of scripture, /

children.text: dhyānarūpā parā caiva tadaṅgaṃ dhāraṇādikam // MAnuv_3,3.52 //
children.translated_text: and the higher one having the form of meditation; its auxiliaries are <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and the rest // 3.3.52 //
And [meditation that is] of both natures — in this <s>pāda</s>, <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) /
teaches <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation) at length, preceded by <s>Śruti</s> // 3.3.53 //
Separate vision, impossibility, non-determination, combination, /
seeing of distinctions, loss of result, diverse statement, quickness // 3.3.54 //
confusion, refutation, indicatory mark, infinite-regress-particularized, /
purposelessness, excessive extension, near-proximity // 3.3.55 //
specific cause, desired [conclusion], observed diversity, elevation, /
non-statement, effortlessness, firm bondage and defeat // 3.3.56 //
equality of persons, abandonment of what is attained, non-determination of cause, confusion, /
showing of distinction, discourse, equality of qualities, separate vision // 3.3.57 //
inaccessible path, connection, desired fruit, non-construction, /
pure diversity, limb-hood, non-distinction-vision, action // 3.3.58 //
— these are the reasonings of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opponent); easy-knowability, prescribed action, /
greatness, limited power, appropriate fruit, existence // 3.3.59 //
equality of fruit, distinction, superiority of qualities, primacy /
Action according to one's capacity, connection [with the Lord], the strength of valid evidence, humility, // MAnuv_3,3.60 //
causation, the distinction of effects, own-nature, refutation of [opposing] entities,
counter-action, non-contradiction, counter-connection, non-deficiency, // MAnuv_3,3.61 //
proficiency of impressions, regulation by one's own will, the greatness of the entity,
specific statement, non-evidence [of the opponent], primacy, delight, scripture, // MAnuv_3,3.62 //
firm stability, attainment of what is accomplished, the extent of beginningless qualities,
supreme excellence of the means, diverse perspectives, instruction, non-deficiency, // MAnuv_3,3.63 //
absence of obstacles and non-contradiction, the distinction of qualities, scripture —
these reasonings in the determination of the <s>siddhānta</s> are always uncontradicted. // MAnuv_3,3.64 //
According to one's capacity, having understood all the <s>Vedas</s>, meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) should occur.

children.text: tatrākhilasya vijñaptiḥ samyag brahmaṇa eva hi // MAnuv_3,3.65 //
children.translated_text: Therein, the complete understanding [of the <s>Vedas</s>] pertains to <s>Brahman</s> alone, indeed. // MAnuv_3,3.65 //
For others, as befitting, complete understanding is desired.
To that extent, every person would be fit for meditation. // MAnuv_3,3.66 //
'Having known the supreme extent of [His] greatness, <s>Janārdana</s>
will be praised [by them]' — that there is [complete] satisfaction [in such praise] does not exist, O <s>Nārada</s>. // MAnuv_3,3.67 //
Rather, with unwavering devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), in proportion to self-knowledge,

children.text: yaḥ stoṣyati sadā bhaktastuṣyastasya sadā hariḥ // MAnuv_3,3.68 //
children.translated_text: he who will always praise [the Lord] with devotion — <s>Hari</s> is always pleased with him. // MAnuv_3,3.68 //
From such an arrangement of statements: knowledge of all [qualities], as befitting,
[and] proportionality to self-knowledge — [these are attained] from investigating according to one's capacity. // MAnuv_3,3.69 //
'The entire <s>Veda</s> should be comprehended' — [otherwise,] the self-study and learning
[prescribed by] such statements would become purposeless — this cannot be prevented otherwise. // MAnuv_3,3.70 //

children.text: adyāpi tena devādyāḥ śṛṇvate manvate sadā /
children.translated_text: Even now, by that [Lord], the <s>devas</s> and others always hear, reflect,
and meditate, as is proper. Nevertheless, until the determination of the reality [of <s>Brahman</s>],

children.text: śravaṇaṃ mananaṃ caiva kartavyaṃ sarvathaiva hi // MAnuv_3,3.71 //
children.translated_text: hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and reflection (<s>manana</s>) must certainly be performed in every way. // MAnuv_3,3.71 //
The supreme teacher knows the specific [times for] reflection, hearing, and meditation.

children.text: vetti tasyoktimārgeṇa kurvataḥ syāddhi darśanam // MAnuv_3,3.72 //
children.translated_text: For one who follows the path indicated by him, direct vision (<s>darśana</s>) would [arise]. // MAnuv_3,3.72 //
For one who has seen the reality: hearing, reflection, and meditation [continue]
for the attainment of special bliss; for another, these [serve] for [attaining] vision. // MAnuv_3,3.73 //
If such a teacher does not exist, [one should perform] hearing and the rest as determined
in accordance with the <s>siddhānta</s>, under the guidance of one who knows the conclusion. // MAnuv_3,3.74 //

children.text: śravaṇādi vinā naiva kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭhedapi kvacit /
children.translated_text: Without hearing and the rest, one should not stand still even for a moment, anywhere.

children.text: atyaśakye tu nidrādau punareva samārabhet // MAnuv_3,3.75 //
children.translated_text: When it is utterly impossible [to continue] — as during sleep — one should begin again. // MAnuv_3,3.75 //
In the absence of one who knows the conclusion, one should always [study]
the true scriptures (<s>sacchāstras</s>) — if an abundance of true knowledge is obtained [thereby]. // MAnuv_3,3.76 //
From great devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, according to one's capacity, one should resolve doubts.
In the absence of one superior to oneself, one should practice by oneself. // MAnuv_3,3.77 //
The completeness of all qualities without exception and the removal of all faults,
belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the dependence of everything else on Him — this is the correct determination. // MAnuv_3,3.78 //

children.text: svatantratvaṃ sadā tasya tasya bhedaśca sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: His independence forever, and the difference of that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] from everything —
for the purpose of establishing His faultlessness; where there is non-difference, its connection [is explained]. // MAnuv_3,3.79 //
The dependence of the liberated ones too on Him — for the completion of His qualities.
And the difference of the liberated ones too — for that which is different does not go to non-difference,
as is seen anywhere; its absence too is established by experience. // MAnuv_3,3.80 //
If there were non-difference formerly, the Lord would be faulty — hence the utter difference.
That the liberated ones too are [different] from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, correctly — this is the established [doctrine]. // MAnuv_3,3.81 //
In [accepting] both difference and non-difference, through non-difference, the faults too would arise [in God].
The faultlessness of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), and her being next [to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in rank] — // MAnuv_3,3.82 //
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, then <s>Indra</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and their consorts,

children.text: śakrakāmau tadanye ca kramānmuktāvapīti ca // MAnuv_3,3.83 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, and then others — in order, even in liberation — and thus [is the hierarchy]. // MAnuv_3,3.83 //

children.text: satsiddhānta iti jñeyo nirṇīto hariṇā svayam /
children.translated_text: This is to be known as the true <s>siddhānta</s>, determined by <s>Hari</s> Himself.

children.text: etadvirodhi yat sarvaṃ tamase 'ndhāya kevalam // MAnuv_3,3.84 //
children.translated_text: Whatever is opposed to this — [leads] to blind darkness alone. // MAnuv_3,3.84 //
'They enter into blind darkness' — <s>śruti</s> declares most clearly.
Thus all <s>śrutis</s> without exception, and all the <s>Pañcarātra</s>, // MAnuv_3,3.85 //
and the original <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, and the <s>Bhārata</s>, and all <s>Smṛtis</s>,
and the <s>Vaiṣṇava Purāṇas</s>, and the higher <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, // MAnuv_3,3.86 //
and the <s>Brahmatarka</s> and <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> — [these constitute] an infinite ocean of scripture;
and infinite reasonings too, rooted in perception and scripture. // MAnuv_3,3.87 //
And the perception of the Lord Himself, and of <s>Ramā</s> and the rest without exception,
and of the liberated ones too, and of the unliberated — this very supreme meaning, // MAnuv_3,3.88 //
leaving no room for any other [interpretation], is revealed with reverence.

children.text: etadeva ca sacchāstraṃ duḥśāstraṃ tu tataḥ param // MAnuv_3,3.89 //
children.translated_text: This alone is the true scripture (<s>sacchāstra</s>); a bad scripture is beyond that. // MAnuv_3,3.89 //
One should always study the true scripture and abandon the bad scripture.
When reality is determined without doubt — [that is] the vision of <s>Brahman</s>. // MAnuv_3,3.90 //
In accordance with the gradation of correct and incorrect knowledge,

children.text: phalaṃ bhavet tāratamyāt sukhaduḥkhātmakaṃ nṛṇām // MAnuv_3,3.91 //
children.translated_text: the fruit would be, through gradation, of the nature of happiness or suffering for people. // MAnuv_3,3.91 //
And from superior correct knowledge, greater happiness would [accrue] to people.

children.text: ato yathātmaśaktayaiva śravaṇaṃ mananaṃ tathā // MAnuv_3,3.92 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, according to one's own capacity: hearing, and likewise reflection — // MAnuv_3,3.92 //
because of association with sense-objects, and because of doubt about the eternal,

children.text: manasā cānyadākāṅkṣāt paraṃ na pratipādyate // MAnuv_3,3.93 //
children.translated_text: and because the mind desires something else — the supreme [truth] is not realized. // MAnuv_3,3.93 //
Thus the statement of the <s>Bhārata</s>; therefore, one who is free from these faults,
endowed with constant meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>), sees <s>Vāsudeva</s>. // MAnuv_3,3.94 //
Faults connected since beginningless [time] — they are obstacles to liberation.

children.text: santyeva prāyaśaḥ puṃsu tena mokṣo na jāyate // MAnuv_3,3.95 //
children.translated_text: They exist generally in people; therefore liberation does not arise [easily]. // MAnuv_3,3.95 //

children.text: sarve ta ete jīveṣu dṛśyante tāratamyataḥ /
children.translated_text: All these are seen in <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) in gradation.
For the righteous ones (<s>ṛjus</s>), there is one [fault] alone: the absence of supreme enthusiasm.
That [fault], being merely a smallness of quality, is contradicted by [their] righteous nature. // MAnuv_3,3.96 //
Therefore, supreme devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and to His devotees such as <s>Ramā</s> and the rest,
should be practiced in gradation, by one who desires the highest human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). // MAnuv_3,3.97 //
Self-regard for all beings is naturally established.
Greater than that [should be practiced] toward one's superiors, in proportion to their superiority, // MAnuv_3,3.98 //
up to <s>Vāsudeva</s> — by one who desires the auspicious in every way.

children.text: na kadācit tyajet taṃ ca krameṇainaṃ vivardhayet // MAnuv_3,3.99 //
children.translated_text: One should never abandon that, and should gradually increase it. // MAnuv_3,3.99 //

children.text: sameṣu svātmavat snehaḥ satsvanyatra tato dayā /
children.translated_text: Toward equals, affection as toward oneself; toward the virtuous elsewhere, compassion.
Through such [practice], with direct perception, the Lord is seen swiftly. // MAnuv_3,3.100 //
He enters that blind darkness who perceives equality with <s>Viṣṇu</s>
of <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and the rest — even in liberation, in any way. // MAnuv_3,3.101 //
How much more so for one who sees [them as] superior to [<s>Viṣṇu</s>]; and for one who thinks He is devoid of qualities;
and for one who perceives faults [in Him]; and for one who sees non-difference [with the world]; and for one who sees both [faults and non-difference]. // MAnuv_3,3.102 //
Thus says the true <s>śruti</s>; therefore, endowed with the qualities properly taught,

children.text: upāsīta hariṃ dṛṣṭvā muktistenaiva jāyate // MAnuv_3,3.103 //
children.translated_text: one should worship <s>Hari</s> — having seen [Him thus], liberation is born through that alone. // MAnuv_3,3.103 //
Whatever declaration of liberation [is made] out of hatred, that is contradictory to Vedic statements.
Those who are enemies of <s>Rāma</s>, because of aversion, are without nourishment.

children.text: abhidrohapade nityamandhe tamasi te sthitāḥ // MAnuv_3,3.104 //
children.translated_text: Abiding forever in the domain of injury, in blind darkness — they are established. // MAnuv_3,3.104 //
Those who hate <s>Hari</s> go to darkness, and those who are non-different from them,
