and those who know Him as quality-less, and those who perceive faults in Him. // MAnuv_3,3.105 //
From such a collection of scriptural statements, the haters go to darkness.
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> too, through reviling the <s>Bhagavān</s>, [went to] darkness —
the razor of ordinance he transgressed, through the influence of his son <s>Prahlāda</s>. // MAnuv_3,3.106 //

children.text: yadanindat pitā mahyaṃ tvadbhakte mayi cāghavān /
children.translated_text: 'That my father reviled You, [my Lord], and [reviled] me, Your devotee — the sinful one —

children.text: tasmāt pitā me pūyeta durantād dustarādaghāt // MAnuv_3,3.107 //
children.translated_text: therefore may my father be purified from that terrible, insurmountable sin.' // MAnuv_3,3.107 //
One who hears reviling of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, or of a person devoted to Him,

children.text: tato nāpaiti yaḥ so 'pi yātyaghaḥ sukṛtāccyutaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.108 //
children.translated_text: and does not depart from there — even he goes to sin, fallen from merit. // MAnuv_3,3.108 //
'The deluded disregard Me, [who have] assumed a human body,
not knowing My supreme nature — [that I am] the great Lord of beings.' // MAnuv_3,3.109 //
'Of vain hopes, vain actions, vain knowledge, and devoid of understanding,

children.text: rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohanīṃ śritāḥ // MAnuv_3,3.110 //
children.translated_text: they resort to the <s>rākṣasī</s> (demonic), <s>āsurī</s> (titanic), and deluding nature.' // MAnuv_3,3.110 //
'Hating Me in their own and others' bodies, the envious ones —
those cruel, lowest of men, inauspicious — I hurl them constantly
in <s>saṃsāra</s> into demonic wombs alone.' // MAnuv_3,3.111 //
'Fallen into a demonic womb, deluded in birth after birth,

children.text: māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim // MAnuv_3,3.112 //
children.translated_text: not attaining Me, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, they go to the lowest destination.' // MAnuv_3,3.112 //

children.text: yo dviṣṭād vibudhaśreṣṭhaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum /
children.translated_text: 'One who hates the best of the wise, Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Master —

children.text: kathaṃ sa na bhaved dveṣya ālokāntasya kasyacit // MAnuv_3,3.113 //
children.translated_text: how could he not be hateful to everyone until the end of the world?' // MAnuv_3,3.113 //

children.text: yo dviṣṭād vibudhaśreṣṭhaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum /
children.translated_text: 'One who hates the best of the wise, Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Master —
his ancestors sink in hell for eternal years.'
From such a collection of statements, the haters [go] to darkness indeed. // MAnuv_3,3.114 //
'Liberation does not exist at all' — those established in the <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialist) view [say].
'Enjoyment [extends only] until the body [perishes]; then there is reduction to ashes.' // MAnuv_3,3.115 //

children.text: iti tat kena mānena dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣavādinā /
children.translated_text: By what means of valid knowledge was this seen by one who [claims to] hold perception [as sole authority]?
For the non-existence of liberation is not ascertained by the means of perception. // MAnuv_3,3.116 //
The vision of liberation is possible for a great person.

children.text: neti vakturmahattvaṃ tu kathañcana na vidyate // MAnuv_3,3.117 //
children.translated_text: But for one who says 'No' — greatness does not exist in any way. // MAnuv_3,3.117 //
How could one who establishes what is common to all be distinguished?
And people are seen in the world who know the higher and the lower. // MAnuv_3,3.118 //
Those of direct vision, established in <s>yoga</s>, of pure sight,
having directly perceived the deity and obtained prosperity through that [deity's] grace — // MAnuv_3,3.119 //
knowers of the far shore of knowledge and realization (<s>vijñāna</s>) — how are they refuted by [ordinary] people?
And their supremely great power is seen — of those of supremely great energy. // MAnuv_3,3.120 //

children.text: yadi te 'pi niṣiddhayante kiṃ noktiste niṣiddhayate /
children.translated_text: If even they are refuted, why is not what you say [also] refuted?
When the validity of their statements is perceived through perception. // MAnuv_3,3.121 //

children.text: varādayo 'pi taddattāḥ sadā satyā bhavanti hi /
children.translated_text: And boons and the like given by them are always true indeed.
And the invalidity of their statements is ascertained [only] through idle speech. // MAnuv_3,3.122 //
For there is no purpose whatsoever in denying the other world.

children.text: vṛthāvācaṃ vṛthā hanyād yadi tasya kimuttaram /
children.translated_text: If one would senselessly kill a speaker of empty words — what answer [could there be]?

children.text: svajīvanavirodhāya vadan kiṃ nāma buddhimān // MAnuv_3,3.123 //
children.translated_text: What intelligent person would speak in opposition to his own life? // MAnuv_3,3.123 //

children.text: prāmāṇye saṃśayaḥ kiṃ syāt tayoḥ puruṣayorapi /
children.translated_text: Would there be doubt about the validity of even those two persons?
One who speaks in opposition to his own life — [he is] an ignorant one, even [if] perceived. // MAnuv_3,3.124 //
And one who hears the words of a deity beyond the senses, who has seen the higher and the lower,
who makes all past and future [events] arrive at worldly experience —

children.text: ataḥ pratyakṣagamyatvād vedamātvasya ca sphuṭam // MAnuv_3,3.125 //
children.translated_text: therefore, because of being accessible to perception, the Vedic nature is clear. // MAnuv_3,3.125 //
If scripture has no validity, the same would apply to perception.

children.text: yadyakṣajasya mātvaṃ syādāgamasya kathaṃ na tat /
children.translated_text: If perception has validity, how could scripture not?
And the distinction from ordinary speech is established through non-deviation. // MAnuv_3,3.126 //
Liberation also exists — through <s>dharma</s> and also through correct knowledge.
And the validity of inference in establishing the trustworthiness of the <s>Jina</s> — // MAnuv_3,3.127 //
from his words, the ascertainment of true <s>dharma</s> and knowledge occurs — and [that is the claim].
'<s>Dharma</s> is non-violence above all, [there is] no other; knowledge is the perception of <s>pudgala</s> (soul-substance).' // MAnuv_3,3.128 //

children.text: iti jaināḥ kathaṃ tat syāt pramāṇamanumānataḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus [say] the <s>Jainas</s> — how could that be? The means of valid knowledge [they claim] is inference.

children.text: viṣayān prati sthitaṃ hyakṣaṃ pratyakṣamiti gīyate /
children.translated_text: The sense-organ established with respect to [its] objects — that is declared to be perception. /
following perception and scripture, inference is [thus] well-known. // MAnuv_3,3.129 //

children.text: ā samantād gamayati dharmādharmau paraṃ padam /
children.translated_text: It conveys fully — from all sides — <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, the supreme abode,
and whatever else is beyond the senses; therefore it is remembered as <s>āgama</s> (scripture). // MAnuv_3,3.130 //
For this very reason, the validity of each [means of knowledge] is accepted.
For that is the intrinsic nature of these [means]; otherwise, validity [would come] from [something] unestablished. // MAnuv_3,3.131 //

children.text: ato 'numā kathaṃ dharmaṃ pudgalaṃ cāpi darśayet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, how could inference demonstrate <s>dharma</s> and the <s>pudgala</s> (person/soul) as well?
Regarding the intrinsic nature of the <s>pudgala</s>, the stated defects [apply], and [its nature is] bliss alone.

children.text: na manyate pudgalaṃ sa duḥkhābhāvaḥ sukhaṃ tviti // MAnuv_3,3.132 //
children.translated_text: He [the Jain] does not consider the <s>pudgala</s> [to have the nature]: 'the absence of suffering is pleasure.' // MAnuv_3,3.132 //
Because the increase of pleasure is seen to exceed the [mere] extent of enjoyment,

children.text: sukhasyābhāvatā kena na ca syāt kiṃ viparyayaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.133 //
children.translated_text: by what [argument] could there be the non-existence of pleasure? And would there not be the opposite? // MAnuv_3,3.133 //

children.text: yadi bhāvo 'pi kaścit syāt tasyaivābhāvatā kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: If there were some positive entity, whence would there be the non-existence of that very [entity]?
If all were non-existences, then through mutual [negation] there would be positive existence. // MAnuv_3,3.134 //

children.text: abhāvābhāvatā yat syāt kiṃ naśchinnaṃ tadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: If there were the non-existence of non-existence — what then would be definitely cut off?
Positive existence is the form of affirmation; non-existence is the form of negation. // MAnuv_3,3.135 //

children.text: niṣedhasya niṣedho 'pi bhāva eva balād bhavet /
children.translated_text: The negation of negation would forcibly become positive existence itself.
The primary apprehension, however, is that which determines [the distinction between] existence and non-existence. // MAnuv_3,3.136 //

children.text: na ca pudgalavijñānaṃ mokṣadaṃ bhavati kvacit /
children.translated_text: And the knowledge of the <s>pudgala</s> (person) never bestows liberation anywhere,

children.text: asvātantryāt pudgalasya jñāto 'pi sukhado na hi // MAnuv_3,3.137 //
children.translated_text: because of the non-independence of the <s>pudgala</s>; even when known, it does not give happiness. // MAnuv_3,3.137 //
For suffering is not removed by the knowledge of a suffering being.
If through knowledge of the <s>pudgala</s>, one somehow becomes free from suffering —

children.text: dehavānapi nāduḥkhī kiṃ jñānāduttaraṃ sadā // MAnuv_3,3.138 //
children.translated_text: even one with a body would not be suffering; why is there always [suffering] after knowledge? // MAnuv_3,3.138 //
According to the arrangement of the Lord — [this answers] the proponents of time and God [as causes].
But the causality of <s>karma</s> [according to Jains] — because of [karma's] non-sentience, [it] is never [viable] anywhere. // MAnuv_3,3.139 //
Just as there is no cause for the dissolution of all suffering now,

children.text: tathottaraṃ ca naiva syād dṛṣṭipūrvānumā yataḥ // MAnuv_3,3.140 //
children.translated_text: so too there would be none afterward — since inference follows what has been seen. // MAnuv_3,3.140 //
If the knowledge of another who is capable generates pleasure in him,

children.text: tayaiva bandhahāniḥ syāditi kiṃ nāma dūṣaṇam // MAnuv_3,3.141 //
children.translated_text: then through that very [pleasure] the bondage would be removed — so what objection is there? // MAnuv_3,3.141 //
But the removal of bondage through knowledge of oneself — of whom is that seen, anywhere?
And by what valid means of knowledge is the <s>dharma</s>-nature of <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) known?

children.text: hiṃsāyā eva dharmatvamityukte syāt kimuttaram // MAnuv_3,3.142 //
children.translated_text: If it were stated that <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) itself is <s>dharma</s> — what answer would there be? // MAnuv_3,3.142 //
By what [valid means] is it known that <s>dharma</s> is a cause of happiness?
By what valid means of knowledge is the claim that killing is a cause of liberation precluded? // MAnuv_3,3.143 //
And through the knowledge of <s>śūnya</s> (emptiness), or through the meditation on emptiness,

children.text: mokṣaḥ kathañcana bhaved yadīdānīṃ kathaṃ na saḥ // MAnuv_3,3.144 //
children.translated_text: liberation could never occur; if [it occurs] now, why not [always]? // MAnuv_3,3.144 //
For one who wishes to please another [i.e. God], a delay is indeed fitting.

children.text: pumicchādhīnatā no ced viḷambaḥ kiṅkṛto bhavet // MAnuv_3,3.145 //
children.translated_text: If [liberation is] not dependent on the person's wish — by what [cause] would there be delay? // MAnuv_3,3.145 //
In other [systems] too, there would be delays, caused by the will of the Lord.

children.text: anyathā kāraṇaṃ cet syāt kiṃ kāryaṃ nopajāyate /
children.translated_text: If otherwise — when the cause exists, why does the effect not arise?

children.text: kāraṇe sati kāryasya bhāvaḥ suniyato 'sya hi // MAnuv_3,3.146 //
children.translated_text: When the cause is present, the existence of the effect is strictly determined. // MAnuv_3,3.146 //
And for the <s>Vijñānavādins</s> (Yogācāra Buddhists) too, from the knowledge of consciousness-only non-duality,

children.text: vijñānabhāvanāccaiva mokṣo na ghaṭate kvacit // MAnuv_3,3.147 //
children.translated_text: and from the meditation on consciousness — liberation is never possible anywhere. // MAnuv_3,3.147 //
From the knowledge that inner consciousness is [also found] externally, and from the knowledge of momentariness,
and from meditation by the stated method — because of the absence of a valid means [of knowledge], one is not liberated. // MAnuv_3,3.148 //
The discrimination of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) from <s>Puruṣa</s> (self) as a means of liberation —

children.text: iti śaṅkayā na caitasmin mānamīśāprasādataḥ // MAnuv_3,3.149 //
children.translated_text: with this doubt — there is no valid means of knowledge for this, apart from the grace of the Lord. // MAnuv_3,3.149 //
If the <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Smṛtis</s> declare, from the grace of the Lord,

children.text: vadanti niyamānmuktiṃ tamṛte 'taḥ kuto bhavet // MAnuv_3,3.150 //
children.translated_text: liberation with certainty — without Him, whence could it come? // MAnuv_3,3.150 //
<s>Kaṇāda</s>, the Yoga [school], and the <s>Ākṣapāda</s> [Naiyāyikas] too — [they] also speak of liberation from the grace of the Lord;
they also speak of the exhaustion of <s>karmas</s> through experience alone.

children.text: kṣayaṃ prāhuḥ kutaścaitat prasanne jagadīśvare // MAnuv_3,3.151 //
children.translated_text: Whence [could there be liberation in those systems]? [It is] when the Lord of the universe is gracious. // MAnuv_3,3.151 //
'The knot of the heart is pierced; all doubts are cut asunder;

children.text: kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare // MAnuv_3,3.152 //
children.translated_text: and his <s>karmas</s> are destroyed — when that [<s>Brahman</s>], the higher and the lower, is seen.' // MAnuv_3,3.152 //
'The knot of the heart is pierced; all doubts are cut asunder;
and his <s>karmas</s> are destroyed — when the Lord is seen in the self.'
Thus, from the statements of <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like — because otherwise it does not follow. // MAnuv_3,3.153 //
And [liberation is] not from the grace of <s>Śiva</s> and the like as taught by the <s>Pāśupatas</s> and others.

children.text: nānyaḥ panthā iti hyuktaṃ puruṣajñānataḥ śrutau // MAnuv_3,3.154 //
children.translated_text: 'There is no other path' — thus it is stated in the <s>Śruti</s>, [referring to] the knowledge of the [Supreme] Person. // MAnuv_3,3.154 //
'All twinklings were born from the lightning, from the Person' —
thus the word 'Person' (<s>Puruṣa</s>) is used with reference to <s>Hari</s>, who reclines on the ocean. // MAnuv_3,3.155 //

children.text: na tasyeśe kaścana tasya nāma mahad yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no one who is His lord; there is no name for Him; great is His glory' —

children.text: iti cādhipatistasya pratiṣiddhaḥ svayaṃ śrutau // MAnuv_3,3.156 //
children.translated_text: thus a ruler over Him is denied in the <s>Śruti</s> itself. // MAnuv_3,3.156 //

children.text: viśvataḥ paramāṃ nityaṃ viśvaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim /
children.translated_text: 'The supreme [being], eternal in all respects, the universe, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>' —
by the statement of supreme superiority, even an equal is precluded.
Because of the absence of an equal or a superior, He is not a figurative 'Person.' // MAnuv_3,3.157 //

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yacca bhavyam /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this — whatever has been and whatever shall be.'
'And [He is] the Lord of immortality, which grows beyond [mortal] food.' // MAnuv_3,3.158 //
That <s>Śruti</s> declares His lordship over the liberated, the unliberated, and the supreme.
From the statement 'Lord of the immortal,' His lordship over all is declared. // MAnuv_3,3.159 //
If 'all-ness' [were already] stated [in the first half], then 'uta' ('and also') '[He is] Lord' would be redundant.
The word 'uta' expresses the cumulative [addition] of lordship. // MAnuv_3,3.160 //

children.text: puruṣeṇedaṃ vyāptamiti brāhmaṇaṃ cāha taṃ prati /
children.translated_text: 'This [universe] is pervaded by the <s>Puruṣa</s>' — and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> also speaks about Him.

children.text: etāvānasya mahimeti mahimno vaco hi tat // MAnuv_3,3.161 //
children.translated_text: 'This much is His greatness' — for that is a statement about [His] greatness. // MAnuv_3,3.161 //
'He is the Lord of the immortal, of the fearless; [He is] mortal food, which He surpassed' —
thus, having reiterated the lordship over the unliberated stated in the first half, // MAnuv_3,3.162 //
[the verse] 'and also Lord of the immortal' ordains lordship over the liberated.
Therefore, from the knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone [comes] liberation, not from anything else.

children.text: tad yatheti śruteścaiva tataḥ karmakṣayo bhavet // MAnuv_3,3.163 //
children.translated_text: 'In this manner' — from this <s>Śruti</s> also — then the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> occurs. // MAnuv_3,3.163 //
'Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā // MAnuv_3,3.164 //
children.translated_text: so the fire of knowledge reduces all <s>karmas</s> to ashes.' // MAnuv_3,3.164 //
'Abandoning all <s>dharmas</s>, take refuge in Me alone.

children.text: ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ /
children.translated_text: I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.'
By such statements of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the stated meaning is established. // MAnuv_3,3.165 //
'Performing the regular and occasional duties (<s>nityanaimittikakarma</s>), while renouncing other [actions],
one is liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>' — this too is refuted by that [principle].
'By knowledge alone' — this very meaning the Lord of the <s>Vedas</s> Himself states. // MAnuv_3,3.166 //

children.text: vinā karma na mokṣaḥ syājjñānenetyapi sā śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without <s>karma</s> there is no liberation through knowledge' — that too the <s>Śruti</s>

children.text: nānyaḥ panthā iti hyeva nivārayati sādaram // MAnuv_3,3.167 //
children.translated_text: 'There is no other path' — thus restrains, with reverence. // MAnuv_3,3.167 //
Even alternative worship (<s>anyathopāsana</s>), [the Śruti,] saying 'Him alone, in this manner,'

children.text: nivārayatyādareṇa na pratīka iti prabhuḥ // MAnuv_3,3.168 //
children.translated_text: restrains with reverence. 'Not a symbol' — [says] the Master. // MAnuv_3,3.168 //
'Into blind darkness enter those who worship ignorance' —
and because of the contradiction with [this] <s>Śruti</s>, there should be no alternative worship. // MAnuv_3,3.169 //
And one is not liberated through the knowledge of oneness, by the reasoning stated.
Therefore, having discerned all this through all reasoning and true scriptures,

children.text: upāsīta hariṃ nityaṃ guṇaireva svayogataḥ // MAnuv_3,3.170 //
children.translated_text: one should worship <s>Hari</s> eternally, through [His] qualities alone, according to one's capacity. // MAnuv_3,3.170 //
<s>Brahmā</s> [worships <s>Hari</s>] with all qualities; <s>Vāc</s> (Speech/Sarasvatī) with the commonality of all actions;
<s>Rudra</s> with the commonality of qualities; the rest with the commonality of substances. // MAnuv_3,3.171 //
Through the distinction of authority, through <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), knowledge, bliss, and the like,

children.text: viśeṣo devatādīnāṃ mokṣe caiva viśeṣataḥ // MAnuv_3,3.172 //
children.translated_text: there is distinction among the deities and others, and especially in liberation. // MAnuv_3,3.172 //
There is no contradiction in that, because of [their] complete freedom from defects,

children.text: ābhāsatvāt pareṣāṃ tadavarāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.173 //
children.translated_text: because of the reflection-nature (<s>ābhāsatva</s>) of the others, and [because] they are inferior in every respect. // MAnuv_3,3.173 //

children.text: yato 'varāṇāṃ sarve 'pi guṇāḥ sarvāḥ kriyā api /
children.translated_text: Since, for the inferior [beings], all qualities and all actions
are invariably dependent on the grace of [their] superiors,

children.text: ataḥ sacchiṣyavat teṣāṃ naiverṣyādiḥ kathañcana // MAnuv_3,3.174 //
children.translated_text: therefore, like good disciples, there is never envy or the like among them. // MAnuv_3,3.174 //
And the <s>saṃsārin</s> deities are not time-dependent like the others [claim].

children.text: sūtre hyārabdhamātrasya bhogenaiva kṣayo dhruvaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.175 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sūtra</s>, [it is stated that] the <s>karma</s> that has begun to bear fruit is certainly exhausted through experience alone. // MAnuv_3,3.175 //
'But the others [are exhausted] through experience of the <s>karma</s> that has not begun to bear fruit' — thus it is taught.

children.text: paunaruktayena tenaite uktārthe iti niścayaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.176 //
children.translated_text: By that redundancy, the conclusion is that these [verses] refer to the stated meaning. // MAnuv_3,3.176 //

children.text: uṣāḥ svāhā ca parjanyo mitro 'gnirvaruṇo vidhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Uṣas</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vidhu</s> (Moon),

children.text: pravaho 'niruddha indrome rudro vāṇī ca mārutaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Pravaha</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Ūma</s> (?), <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s> (Speech), and <s>Māruta</s> (Wind) —
each successively higher than the next in all qualities — and [all are] attainers of liberation. // MAnuv_3,3.177 //
Like <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Dharma</s>; like <s>Soma</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
<s>Śacī</s>, <s>Rati</s> — equal to <s>Aniruddha</s>; and <s>Tārā</s> equal to <s>Mitra</s>. // MAnuv_3,3.178 //
Like <s>Soma</s>, <s>Śatarūpā</s>; <s>Prasūti</s> like <s>Agni</s>; <s>Virāṭ</s>

children.text: parjanyavad vāruṇī ca tathā sañjñā ca rohiṇī // MAnuv_3,3.179 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Parjanya</s>; and <s>Vāruṇī</s>, likewise <s>Sañjñā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s>. // MAnuv_3,3.179 //
<s>Dharmī</s> is declared as equal to <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Prāvahī</s> [likewise].
Between <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Parjanya</s> stand the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Vighna</s> (Gaṇeśa), and <s>Vittapa</s> (Kubera). // MAnuv_3,3.180 //
<s>Bhṛgu</s> is equal to <s>Agni</s>; between <s>Mitra</s> and that [level] are the sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: varuṇāgnyantarā tatra nāradaḥ prāya indravat // MAnuv_3,3.181 //
children.translated_text: Between <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Agni</s>, there <s>Nārada</s> is approximately like <s>Indra</s>. // MAnuv_3,3.181 //
<s>Kāma</s> and <s>Suparṇī</s> are like <s>Umā</s>; <s>Vīndra</s> is said to be like <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Nirṛti</s> is like <s>Mitra</s>; <s>Viśvāmitra</s> is like <s>Kaśyapa's</s> son. // MAnuv_3,3.182 //
<s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> is after the <s>Aśvins</s>; others are inferior to him.
<s>Cyavana</s>, <s>Ucathya</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s> (Vainya), <s>Śaśabindu</s>, and <s>Haihaya</s> —
and like that, there is also a certain distinction among <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>kṣatriyas</s> herein. // MAnuv_3,3.183 //
Likewise <s>Priyavrata</s>; and the other hundred deities
are in the interval between <s>Parjanya</s> and <s>Mitra</s>; and the rest are inferior to them. // MAnuv_3,3.184 //
<s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) is ever superior to all these — being eternally liberated, especially.

children.text: tatsamo nāsti paramo harireva nacāparaḥ // MAnuv_3,3.185 //
children.translated_text: There is none equal to Her; the Supreme is <s>Hari</s> alone, and no other. // MAnuv_3,3.185 //
In the great <s>Saṃhitā</s>, it is declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself.
All this is <s>Prāṇa</s> (Vāyu/the vital breath) and indeed [related to] <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (the ego-principle).
The vision [of Brahman comes] immediately after <s>Indra</s>, according to one's fitness. // MAnuv_3,3.186 //
The grace of a proper guru is primarily the cause of [divine] vision.

children.text: śravaṇādi ca kartavyaṃ nānyathā darśanaṃ kvacit // MAnuv_3,3.187 //
children.translated_text: Hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the like must be performed; there is no vision otherwise. // MAnuv_3,3.187 //

children.text: guṇādhikaṃ guruṃ prāpya taddhīnaṃ nāpnuyāt kvacit /
children.translated_text: Having obtained a guru superior in qualities, one should never approach an inferior one.
The reverse, however, must be done by one who desires liberation in every way. // MAnuv_3,3.188 //

children.text: same vikalpa eva syāt pūrvānujñā ca sarvathā /
children.translated_text: When [two gurus are] equal, there is indeed an option; and in all cases, the permission of the former [guru is required].
But for obtaining a superior guru, the former's permission need not be sought. // MAnuv_3,3.189 //
The guru of all gurus is <s>Brahmā</s>; and knowledge itself is <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
The deity [of all] is the <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s> — for all, without distinction. // MAnuv_3,3.190 //
By His grace alone liberation would occur — never otherwise, in any way.
Those successively superior to oneself are heard to be the gurus of all.
But the instruction of <s>Brahmā</s> is for the liberation of all. // MAnuv_3,3.191 //
<s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) is superior to [all other] means of attainment; there is nothing else comparable anywhere.
And <s>bhakti</s> is primarily directed toward <s>Hari</s>; toward others, in due order. // MAnuv_3,3.192 //

children.text: svādhikā tveva sarvatra svottameṣu krameṇa ca /
children.translated_text: Toward those successively superior to oneself, everywhere, and toward those above them, in order —
<s>bhakti</s> continues, and in liberation it takes the form of bliss.
Worship preceded by that [bhakti] should thus be performed for liberation, through [knowledge of His] qualities. // MAnuv_3,3.193 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the blessed <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the venerable <s>Ānandatīrtha</s> (Madhva), the master. ||

children.translated_text: Thus, from the ever-arisen, faultless vision of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
the attainment of the desired fruit [comes], because of not transgressing the [karma] that has begun to bear fruit. // MAnuv_3,4.1 //
Of gods, sages, humans, and so forth — according to their respective classes; /
what <s>Jaimini</s> stated [applies to] humans — and there are certain specifics thereof. // MAnuv_3,4.2 //
The general [rule] is spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>; for gods and so forth, specifically. /
In the presence of a strong contradicting [authority], the statement of <s>Jaimini</s> and others is accepted. // MAnuv_3,4.3 //
There is no staining by wrong action whatsoever for those of right vision. /
And there is no diminishment of qualities for <s>Brahman</s>, because of the absence of wrong action. // MAnuv_3,4.4 //

children.text: devānāmapi na prāyaḥ kḷptasya tu kathañcana /
children.translated_text: For gods too, generally — of what is established [by destiny], somehow, /

children.text: prāptahrāso bhavet kvāpi mahatā tu vikarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: there may be a diminishment obtained somewhere through great wrong action; /

children.text: tathāpi tat kḷptameva tasmānna niyamojkhitiḥ // MAnuv_3,4.5 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, even that is destined; therefore, there is no loss of the ordained [position]. // MAnuv_3,4.5 //
Even for <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) and <s>Sugrīva</s>, from the seizure of the wives of their superiors, /
the diminishment obtained [was in the realm of experience] — never a diminishment of the destined [position], in any way. // MAnuv_3,4.6 //
Diminishment of bliss even for humans and so forth, through wrong action, /
would occur in liberation, especially — from the offenses of one's superiors. // MAnuv_3,4.7 //
For sin [committed] after [attaining] knowledge — in the fourth [category], non-staining is stated. /
The result of that [knowledge] is that impurity and the like do not arise for him. /
Herein, the certainty of liberation as the fruit of knowledge alone is stated. // MAnuv_3,4.8 //
Of that which has already begun to bear fruit (<s>prārabdha karma</s>) alone — like death from eating poison — /
even of what has been obtained [and] is irreversible — a partial consumption through awareness /

children.text: upamarda iha prokto devādīnāṃ yathākramam // MAnuv_3,4.9 //
children.translated_text: is declared here — for gods and so forth, according to sequence. // MAnuv_3,4.9 //
But the total non-enjoyment of <s>prārabdha</s> <s>karma</s> /

children.text: na brahmadarśino 'pi syāt phalahrāsastu vidyate // MAnuv_3,4.10 //
children.translated_text: would not occur even for a seer of <s>Brahman</s>; but there is indeed a diminishment of the fruit. // MAnuv_3,4.10 //
If there were total diminishment of the fruit of non-commenced <s>karma</s>, /
the optional injunctions would become purposeless — thus the stated rule would hold. /
This has been clearly stated even today in the <s>Tantra</s> and the <s>Bhāgavata</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.11 //

children.text: tāratamyaṃ phale no ced brahmādīnāṃ kathaṃ śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: If there is no gradation in the fruit for <s>Brahmā</s> and others — how [does] <s>śruti</s>, /
having declared liberation as 'free from crookedness, unafflicted by desire,' /

children.text: ānandatāratamyaṃ ca teṣāṃ brūyāt pṛthak pṛthak // MAnuv_3,4.12 //
children.translated_text: then speak of a gradation of bliss among them, separately? // MAnuv_3,4.12 //

children.text: saṃsāra eva cedetat tāratamyaṃ na mukhyataḥ /
children.translated_text: If this gradation is in <s>saṃsāra</s> itself and not primarily [in liberation], /
then the meaning of 'unafflicted by desire' and 'freedom from crookedness' would not hold. // MAnuv_3,4.13 //
'Where desires are fulfilled — there, make me immortal!' /

children.text: iti yallakṣaṇaṃ mukteḥ śrutirāha balīyasī // MAnuv_3,4.14 //
children.translated_text: — this characteristic of liberation is declared by the mighty <s>śruti</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.14 //
Whence the affliction by desire elsewhere? For one whose desires are fulfilled, that would be [impossible]. /
When the obtaining of desires comes about without effort — /
only then is there the state of being unafflicted by desire; whence indeed would it be otherwise? // MAnuv_3,4.15 //
But for a conscious being who is not asleep — where is desirelessness observed? /

children.text: avyaktireva kāmānāṃ na nāśo mohasuptayoḥ // MAnuv_3,4.16 //
children.translated_text: It is merely the non-manifestation of desires, not their destruction — in delusion and sleep. // MAnuv_3,4.16 //
'With whatever desire one falls asleep — that very [desire], when awakened, whence [does it return]?' /
'Even involuntarily, one speaks' — whence desirelessness in sleep? // MAnuv_3,4.17 //
'One who has attained liberation obtains all desires together with <s>Brahman</s>.' /

children.text: paryeti tatra jakṣaṃśca krīḍan ratimavāpnuvan // MAnuv_3,4.18 //
children.translated_text: 'He moves about there, eating, playing, finding delight.' // MAnuv_3,4.18 //
'With desire for food, with desire for form, being — traversing these worlds; /

children.text: āste gāyan sāma mukta ityādiśrutisadbalāt // MAnuv_3,4.19 //
children.translated_text: the liberated one sits singing <s>Sāma</s>' — and so forth: by the force of such <s>śruti</s> texts. // MAnuv_3,4.19 //

children.text: akāmaḥ syāt kathaṃ muktaḥ kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'How can the liberated one be desireless?' — 'The desires that are lodged in his heart' — /
this indeed speaks of the liberation of desires that are in the inner organ. /

children.text: āha śrutirhṛdītyeva na ced vyarthaṃ viśeṣaṇam // MAnuv_3,4.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śruti</s> says 'in the heart' — otherwise the qualifier would be purposeless. // MAnuv_3,4.20 //

children.text: hṛdyeṣa teṣāṃ śrayaṇamiti pakṣo na bhāsate /
children.translated_text: The position that 'in the heart' means 'their resort' — is not apparent. /
For <s>śruti</s> speaks of the state of desiring for the liberated in separate branches [of the <s>Veda</s>]. // MAnuv_3,4.21 //
Therefore, being unafflicted by desire belongs primarily to the liberated alone. /

children.text: mukhyārthasya vṛthā tyāgo māyināmeva bhūṣaṇam // MAnuv_3,4.22 //
children.translated_text: The purposeless abandonment of the primary meaning is the ornament of the <s>Māyāvādins</s> alone. // MAnuv_3,4.22 //
Freedom from sin, freedom from suffering, and freedom from crookedness are stated here. /

children.text: apriyaṃ vṛjinaṃ duḥkhamakaṃ toda itīyarte // MAnuv_3,4.23 //
children.translated_text: 'What is unpleasant is crookedness, suffering, and harm' — this is [etymologically] derived thus. // MAnuv_3,4.23 //

children.text: tatkāraṇatvāt pāpaṃ vā vṛjinaṃ nāma kathyate /
children.translated_text: Because of being its cause, sin too is called crookedness — /
thus the meaning of the name was stated by the Lord himself in the <s>Śabdanirṇaya</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.24 //
And freedom from sin does not exist as long as <s>saṃsāra</s> [continues]. /

children.text: ārabdhapāpamastyeva duḥkhaṃ ca jñānino 'pi hi // MAnuv_3,4.25 //
children.translated_text: For <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced) sin exists, and suffering too, even for the knower. // MAnuv_3,4.25 //
'Therefore, from that, desirelessness' — this is an unfounded imagination. /
From the statement 'unafflicted by desire,' the abandonment of what is heard [in <s>śruti</s>] is also evident. // MAnuv_3,4.26 //

children.text: kutracit kāminaḥ puṃsaḥ kāmābhāvāt kvacit kvacit /
children.translated_text: For a desiring person somewhere — because of the absence of desire somewhere else — /
the experience of the bliss of <s>Indra</s> and others exists [in some degree] — this [objection from] experience is refuted. // MAnuv_3,4.27 //
Therefore, having stated separately the gradation pertaining to the bliss of the unliberated, /

children.text: uktvā yaśceti muktānāṃ tāratamyaṃ sukhe śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'and he who...' — <s>śruti</s> states the gradation in bliss of the liberated. /

children.text: āheti peśalaṃ tacca caśabdādeva gamyate // MAnuv_3,4.28 //
children.translated_text: And the elegance of this is understood from the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) itself. // MAnuv_3,4.28 //
'<s>Rāddha</s>' (successful), '<s>saṃsiddha</s>' (accomplished) — is understood as the liberated one alone. /

children.text: sādhunā viṣṇunā yukto muktaḥ sādhuyuvā mataḥ // MAnuv_3,4.29 //
children.translated_text: United with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the good — the liberated one is considered a 'good youth.' // MAnuv_3,4.29 //

children.text: yauvanaṃ nityametasya muktasyeti yuvā sa ca /
children.translated_text: The youth of this liberated one is eternal — hence he is a 'youth.' /
The fruit of study has been obtained by him — hence he is called a 'student' (<s>adhyāyaka</s>). // MAnuv_3,4.30 //
Because of the obtainment of bliss without diminishment — he is sung as '<s>āśiṣṭha</s>' (most blessed). /
Because of the unalterable obtainment of one who is established — he is called '<s>dṛḍhiṣṭha</s>' (most firm). // MAnuv_3,4.31 //
And '<s>baliṣṭha</s>' (strongest) by nature — the liberated one becomes exclusively [thus]. /
'His is this earth' and so forth — in reference to prior existence. // MAnuv_3,4.32 //

children.text: sa eka iti saṃsāragatamuktavā sukhaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is one' — whether the bliss [referred to] is of the saṃsāra-bound or the liberated — again, /
'of the learned one' — [<s>śruti</s>] speaks of a hundredfold nature in comparison to the liberated. // MAnuv_3,4.33 //
And of the saṃsāra-bound — the hundredfold [superiority] of the saṃsāra-bound itself. /
A hundredfold [superiority] of the liberated over the liberated — this would be proper — as stated and observed in <s>śruti</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.34 //
And it is proper that from superiority in means (<s>sādhana</s>), there is superiority in the end (<s>sādhya</s>) — for gods and so forth. /

children.text: nādhikyaṃ yadi sādhye syāt prayatnaḥ sādhane kutaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.35 //
children.translated_text: If there were no superiority in the end — whence the effort in the means? // MAnuv_3,4.35 //
And the effort of those great-souled ones is seen to be very great indeed. /
Where there is abundance of means — there is abundance of the goal [to be achieved]; /

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ niyamato no cenna yatnaṃ kuryarañjasā // MAnuv_3,4.36 //
children.translated_text: this is invariably observed — otherwise one would not make effort readily. // MAnuv_3,4.36 //
Through means [obtained] with great difficulty alone — it is not declared to be like ordinary liberation. /
<s>Rudra</s> performed austerities for ten <s>kalpas</s> in the salt ocean, /

children.text: tyaktavā sukhāni sarvāṇi kliṣṭena lavaṇāmbhasā // MAnuv_3,4.37 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all pleasures, afflicted by the salt water. // MAnuv_3,4.37 //
And <s>Śakra</s> [drank] smoke for ten million years with great suffering. /

children.text: varṣāyutaṃ ca sūryeṇa tapo 'vākchirasā kṛtam // MAnuv_3,4.38 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Sūrya</s> performed austerities for ten thousand years standing head-downward. // MAnuv_3,4.38 //
With great difficulty, having abandoned pleasure, <s>Dharma</s>, sleeping on the ground, /
drank mirage-waters for a thousand years with extreme reverence. // MAnuv_3,4.39 //
With extreme difficulty, even knowers of <s>Brahman</s> make their effort. /
How would all this [make sense] if there were no distinction in liberation? // MAnuv_3,4.40 //
'Divine wealth leads to liberation; demoniac [wealth] is considered [to lead] to bondage.' /
And the distinction in liberation was declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself. // MAnuv_3,4.41 //
'Worship him alone, with the functions of your self — with the qualities of mind, speech, and body, through your own actions, /
without deceit — his lotus feet, which are wish-fulfilling — according to your respective eligibility, for the accomplishment of the desired goal.' // MAnuv_3,4.42 //
'Those who have eyes, those who have ears, friends — unequal in the speed of thought, they became. /

children.text: ādaghnāsa upakakṣāsa u tve hradā iva snātvā u tve dadṛśre // MAnuv_3,4.43 //
children.translated_text: Some [reached] up to the knees, some up to the armpits — like [bathers] having bathed in pools, they appeared.' // MAnuv_3,4.43 //
These and other statements clearly declare a gradation in liberation. /

children.text: vyaktaṃ vadanti tat kena sāmyaṃ mukteṣu gamyate // MAnuv_3,4.44 //
children.translated_text: By what [means], then, is equality among the liberated understood? // MAnuv_3,4.44 //
Equality in the absence of suffering and the like — this is understood as the meaning of equality-statements. /
And in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, inequality is stated in the presence of qualities such as devotion. /
Distinction of means is also spoken of everywhere. // MAnuv_3,4.45 //
Difficult to know is the Lord, of terrible form, the destroyer of the three worlds — /
[difficult to know] by gods, sages, accomplished ones, and great yogins, // MAnuv_3,4.46 //
eternally devoted, greatly blessed, freed from the affliction of <s>kleśas</s>, /
of great enthusiasm, great firmness, established in <s>sattva</s>, resolute, // MAnuv_3,4.47 //
knowers of the arising and dissolution of past and future [events], /
endowed with purity, self-study, contentment, austerity, truth, and compassion — // MAnuv_3,4.48 //
how much less by mortals, beset with fear, bewilderment, destruction, delusion, and disease, /
of short life, meager valor, intelligence, goodness, resolution, learning, and vows! // MAnuv_3,4.49 //
'Who is worthy to know that God — intoxicating and non-intoxicating — other than me?' /

children.text: brahmaiva kiñcijjānāti na tadanyo hi kaścana // MAnuv_3,4.50 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahmā</s> alone knows somewhat; no one else whatsoever.' // MAnuv_3,4.50 //
'Even among the liberated and the accomplished, one who is devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, /
of peaceful soul, is supremely rare — among millions, O great-minded one.' // MAnuv_3,4.51 //

children.text: iyaṃ visṛṣṭiryata ā babhūva yadi vā dadhe yadi vā na /
children.translated_text: 'This creation, whence it came about — whether he upheld it, or whether not — /

children.text: yo asyādhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman tso aṅga veda yadi vā na veda // MAnuv_3,4.52 //
children.translated_text: he who is its overseer in the highest heaven — he indeed knows, or perhaps he knows not.' // MAnuv_3,4.52 //

children.text: yaḥ svātmamāyāvibhavaṃ svayaṃ gato nāhaṃ nabhasvāṃstamathāpare kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who has himself reached the glory of his own <s>māyā</s>-power — neither I, nor <s>Vāyu</s> — whence then the others? /

children.text: brahmāpi yaṃ vetti naiveha samyaganye kuto devamunīndramartyāḥ // MAnuv_3,4.53 //
children.translated_text: Even <s>Brahmā</s> does not know him truly here — whence then the other foremost gods, sages, and mortals?' // MAnuv_3,4.53 //
'Salutation to you, of infinite reality, and to the creator of <s>dharma</s> and the rest, /

children.text: nirguṇāya ca satkāṣṭhāṃ nāhaṃ vedāpare kutaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.54 //
children.translated_text: to one without [material] qualities, the ultimate limit of existence — I do not know [you]; whence then the others?' // MAnuv_3,4.54 //

children.text: nāhaṃ parāyur ṛṣayo na marīcimukhyā jānanti yadviracitaṃ khalu sattvasaṅgāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Neither I, who am of the longest life, nor the sages, nor those headed by <s>Marīci</s>, know what was created by him — those attached to <s>sattva</s>. /

children.text: yanmāyayā muṣitacetasa īśadaityamartyādayaḥ kimuta śaśvadabhadravṛttāḥ // MAnuv_3,4.55 //
children.translated_text: Those whose minds are deluded by whose <s>māyā</s> — gods, demons, mortals, and so forth — how much less those of ever-wicked conduct?' // MAnuv_3,4.55 //

children.text: ahaṃ mahendro nirṛtiḥ pracetāḥ somo 'gnirīśaḥ pavano 'rko viriñcaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>Pracetas</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Pavana</s> (Wind), <s>Arka</s> (Sun), <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), /

children.text: ādityaviśve vasavo 'tha sādhyā marudgaṇā rudragaṇāḥ sasiddhāḥ // MAnuv_3,4.56 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, the hosts of <s>Rudras</s>, and the <s>Siddhas</s>; // MAnuv_3,4.56 //
and other world-creators and lords of the immortals, <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others, untouched by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> — /

children.text: yasyehitaṃ na viduḥ spṛṣṭṛmāyāḥ sattvapradhānā api kiṃ tato 'nye // MAnuv_3,4.57 //
children.translated_text: do not know his purpose, though touched by <s>māyā</s>, even those predominating in <s>sattva</s> — how much less the others?' // MAnuv_3,4.57 //
At the beginning of creation, <s>Brahmā</s> was remembered; after him, [the next] god. /
He knows the foremost of gods, and more than that, O king. // MAnuv_3,4.58 //
'They will not surpass you, even in liberation, in any way. /
Through devotion to me and through knowledge, you will surpass all.' // MAnuv_3,4.59 //
Just as a distinction in devotion is seen here toward the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), /
so too a distinction in liberation [exists] for knowers, in the differentiation of the mark [of attainment]. // MAnuv_3,4.60 //
Even gods and all others, having attained <s>sāyujya</s> (union with the Lord), /

children.text: tāratamyāddhi tiṣṭhanti tāratamyaṃ hi sādhane // MAnuv_3,4.61 //
children.translated_text: remain in gradation — for there is indeed gradation in the means. // MAnuv_3,4.61 //
'Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection. /

children.text: yatatāmapi siddhānāṃ kaścinmāṃ vetti tattvataḥ // MAnuv_3,4.62 //
children.translated_text: Among those who strive and those who are accomplished, scarcely one knows me in truth.' // MAnuv_3,4.62 //
'He who will impart this supreme secret to my devotees — /

children.text: bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.63 //
children.translated_text: having offered supreme devotion to me, will come to me alone — there is no doubt.' // MAnuv_3,4.63 //
'And no one among men is dearer to me in action than he. /

children.text: bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi // MAnuv_3,4.64 //
children.translated_text: Nor will there be another dearer to me on earth than he.' // MAnuv_3,4.64 //

children.text: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And he who will study this righteous dialogue of ours — /

children.text: jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ // MAnuv_3,4.65 //
children.translated_text: by him I would be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge — such is my view.' // MAnuv_3,4.65 //
'And the man who, full of faith and free from envy, would even hear [this] — /

children.text: so 'pi muktaḥ śubhān lokān prāpnuyāt puṇyakarmaṇām // MAnuv_3,4.66 //
children.translated_text: he too, liberated, would attain the auspicious worlds of those of meritorious deeds.' // MAnuv_3,4.66 //
'Some, through meditation, see the Self in the self by the self; /

children.text: anye sāṅkhayena yogena karmayogena cāpare // MAnuv_3,4.67 //
children.translated_text: others through <s>Sāṅkhya</s> <s>yoga</s>; and others through <s>karma yoga</s>.' // MAnuv_3,4.67 //
'Others, however, not knowing thus, having heard from others, worship. /
They too cross beyond death — devoted to what they have heard.' // MAnuv_3,4.68 //
together with all <s>viśeṣas</s> (distinctions), however subtle, He sees

children.text: svātmānaṃ bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sarvarūpo 'pi sarvadā // MAnuv_3,4.69 //
children.translated_text: His own Self — the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s>, though having all forms, always. // MAnuv_3,4.69 //

children.text: savartra cānyadapyevaṃ tenādṛṣṭaṃ na hi kvacit /
children.translated_text: And everywhere, everything else likewise — nothing is unseen by Him anywhere.

children.text: sarvatra sarvadaiveśaṃ paśyatyeva ramāpi tu // MAnuv_3,4.70 //
children.translated_text: Everywhere and at all times, <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) too sees the Lord indeed. // MAnuv_3,4.70 //
But they do not see Him with all [His] distinctions, though [seeing] more than others.
[She] always sees her own self and all else as well. // MAnuv_3,4.71 //
<s>Brahmā</s>, however, would see [Him as] all-pervading and His qualities even more [than others],

children.text: natu sarveṣu kāleṣu tathā paśyatyamuktigaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.72 //
children.translated_text: but not at all times does he see thus when not [yet] liberated. // MAnuv_3,4.72 //

children.text: muktastu sarvadā paśyet sarvagatvena cāpi tu /
children.translated_text: But when liberated, he would see at all times and also as all-pervading;

children.text: na ramāvad viśeṣāṇāṃ darśanaṃ śaknuyāt kvacit // MAnuv_3,4.73 //
children.translated_text: yet he could never [attain] the vision of distinctions as <s>Ramā</s> does. // MAnuv_3,4.73 //
His own self and everything else, always, with all distinctions —
<s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) sees clearly likewise, but not [as many] distinctions as [Brahmā sees].

children.text: traiguṇyāt parataḥ paśyed vyāptaṃ śataguṇaṃ harim // MAnuv_3,4.74 //
children.translated_text: Beyond the three <s>guṇas</s>, she would see <s>Hari</s> as pervading a hundredfold [more]. // MAnuv_3,4.74 //
<s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and <s>Garuḍa</s> see <s>Hari</s> as extending only through <s>tamas</s> (darkness);

children.text: paśyed viśeṣānapi hi vāṇīdṛṣṭān na paśyati // MAnuv_3,4.75 //
children.translated_text: they see distinctions too, but do not see those seen by <s>Vāṇī</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.75 //

children.text: umā suparṇī ca mahattattvaṃ yāvat prapaśyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s> and <s>Suparṇī</s> (Garuḍa's wife) see up to the <s>Mahat-tattva</s> (Great Principle);

children.text: rudradṛṣṭān viśeṣāṃśca naiva paśyet kadācana // MAnuv_3,4.76 //
children.translated_text: but they never see the distinctions seen by <s>Rudra</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.76 //
Their own forms and the forms of others — the liberated gods know entirely:
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Kāma</s> [know] up to <s>Brahman</s>, down to <s>Ahaṅkṛti</s> (ego-principle). // MAnuv_3,4.77 //
Seeing — <s>Manu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and others — <s>Hari</s> as situated in the <s>Buddhi-tattva</s> (intellect-principle);

children.text: paśyanti somasūryau tu manasthaṃ parameśvaram // MAnuv_3,4.78 //
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> (Moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) see the Supreme Lord as situated in <s>Manas</s> (mind). // MAnuv_3,4.78 //

children.text: anye bhūtasthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ devāḥ paśyanti sarvadā /
children.translated_text: Other gods always see <s>Viṣṇu</s> as situated in the elements;
in the <s>Mahat-tattva</s>, only occasionally, after many thousands of years. // MAnuv_3,4.79 //
And yet others [see] <s>Hari</s> as dwelling within the cosmic egg, each according to their fitness;
and the Lord of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> — and some others, only in the heart;

children.text: kadācideva tatrāpi kecit paśyanti keśavam // MAnuv_3,4.80 //
children.translated_text: and even there, some see <s>Keśava</s> only occasionally. // MAnuv_3,4.80 //
Up to <s>Umā</s>, infinite portions — from those previously seen,
the distinctions of <s>Vāsudeva</s> they perceive afterward, having been instructed. // MAnuv_3,4.81 //
<s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), <s>Kāma</s>, and the rest perceive the distinctions situated in <s>Brahman</s> —
only a hundredth part of those [perceived] by <s>Umā</s> and others who have been awakened. // MAnuv_3,4.82 //
Thus, from the statements of the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Smṛtis</s>, and other texts, as they truly mean,

children.text: tāratamyaṃ vimuktānāṃ sādhanānāṃ ca dṛśyate // MAnuv_3,4.83 //
children.translated_text: the hierarchy (<s>tāratamya</s>) of the liberated and of the means [of liberation] is seen. // MAnuv_3,4.83 //
The dissimilarity of the goal and the means — if not seen, by whom is it imagined?

children.text: vaiṣamyaṃ nirghṛṇatvaṃ ca tena syātāṃ parasya ca /
children.translated_text: Partiality and cruelty would then belong to the Supreme,

children.text: sāpekṣatvāditi ca tau vidyādhīśena vāritau // MAnuv_3,4.84 //
children.translated_text: but both of these have been refuted by the Lord of Knowledge through [the argument of] dependence [on prior merit]. // MAnuv_3,4.84 //
Because of the hierarchy of the means, the corresponding hierarchy of the goal from the Lord —
the absence of partiality and the like would always hold in the Supreme Lord. // MAnuv_3,4.85 //
Although independence exists in the Supreme Lord regarding the means and the like,
by taking into account the beginningless diversity [of souls] — there is no fault: thus is His word.
"Because of its beginninglessness" — thus it has been said; "it is fitting" — so too. // MAnuv_3,4.86 //
Taking into account the diversity of means, the corresponding status of the goal —

children.text: mayā kayā viruddhā syād rājādāvapi dṛśyate // MAnuv_3,4.87 //
children.translated_text: by what [reasoning] would this be contradicted? It is seen even in [the case of] a king and others. // MAnuv_3,4.87 //
The abandonment of what is seen and the imagining of what is unseen — both are extremely difficult;

children.text: māyibhyo 'nyena kenāpi tat kimanyaiśca vādibhiḥ // MAnuv_3,4.88 //
children.translated_text: by whom other than the <s>Māyāvādins</s> [could this be done]? And what [use are] other disputants [compared to them]? // MAnuv_3,4.88 //
The <s>Māyāvādins</s> are followed in this [regard] — [they practice] the abandonment of what is heard and the acceptance of what is not heard.

children.text: apyatra māyināṃ liṅge tat ke doṣāstato 'dhikāḥ // MAnuv_3,4.89 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the mark of the <s>Māyāvādins</s> — what faults [could be] greater than those? // MAnuv_3,4.89 //
For those whose faults have entirely departed, through many births,
there would be the direct realization of <s>Hari</s> — whence then hatred, jealousy, and the like? // MAnuv_3,4.90 //

children.text: bhaveyuryadi cerṣyādyāḥ sameṣvapi kuto na te /
children.translated_text: If jealousy and the like were to arise, why not among equals too?
Being tormented upon seeing equals, endowed with hatred, jealousy, and the like —

children.text: dṛśyante bahavo loke doṣā evātra kāraṇam // MAnuv_3,4.91 //
children.translated_text: many are seen in the world [to be like this]; faults alone are the cause here. // MAnuv_3,4.91 //
If there is faultlessness there, how is it vitiated by [another's] superiority?
If jealousy and the like are prevented by not seeing [anyone superior],
how are not-seeing, displeasure, and the like prevented by that? // MAnuv_3,4.92 //
Even of <s>Brahmā</s>, displeasure was seen when he was formerly alone — in scripture:

children.text: naiva reme sa caikākī tasamānna ramate kvacit /
children.translated_text: "He did not rejoice; alone, he rejoiced nowhere."
"He desired a second" — thus the scriptures have declared. // MAnuv_3,4.93 //

children.text: yadīcchā tatra naivāstītyeva tat kalpyate mṛṣā /
children.translated_text: If it is simply imagined falsely that there is no desire there,
why is not the very faultlessness stated by scripture itself accepted? // MAnuv_3,4.94 //

children.text: tāratamyaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca śrutamevātihāya tu /
children.translated_text: Setting aside the hierarchy and desire that are heard in scripture,

children.text: aśrutā samatā kena kalpyate yuktimāninā // MAnuv_3,4.95 //
children.translated_text: by what self-styled logician is the unheard equality imagined? // MAnuv_3,4.95 //
What means of knowledge for the equality of the liberated is found by you?
This insistence is pointless — why abandon what is heard and grasp what is not heard? // MAnuv_3,4.96 //
Even in liberation there is hierarchy, because of sentience, just as before —

children.text: ityukta uttaraṃ kiṃ te kalpanāmātravādinaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.97 //
children.translated_text: thus it is said; what is your reply, O proponents of mere imagination? // MAnuv_3,4.97 //
And suffering and the like should not be imagined [in liberation], due to the force of the scripture [declaring] freedom from suffering.
"The knower of the Self crosses over sorrow" — "having crossed, free from all suffering." // MAnuv_3,4.98 //
"By which one becomes blissful indeed, one never grieves."
"Free from sin, the desire of the Father, delighting here — the Lord." // MAnuv_3,4.99 //
"Whatever end he desires to attain, that he becomes here by [mere] resolve" —
such scriptures are the authority for the possession of freedom from suffering and the like. // MAnuv_3,4.100 //
Therefore, there is no scope here for the inference of suffering and the like.
The inference of hierarchy would thus not be overly extensive. // MAnuv_3,4.101 //
By the force of scripture and reasoning, the hierarchy is thus established

children.text: muktāvapi tataḥ ke 'tra virodhaṃ kartumīśate // MAnuv_3,4.102 //
children.translated_text: even in liberation; who then here is able to raise an objection? // MAnuv_3,4.102 //
And the beginningless fitness [of souls], extending up to the lord of <s>Kali</s> and <s>Vāṇī</s> —
who is able to obstruct [this], empowered as it is by the strength of reasoning and scripture? // MAnuv_3,4.103 //
Except for <s>Brahmā</s>, the disputed time regarding the superiority-qualification [of others] —

children.text: kālo hyayaṃ yathetyādi mānumāmānino bhavet // MAnuv_3,4.104 //
children.translated_text: "for this time is such-and-such" — thus the inference would be for those who accept [such reasoning]. // MAnuv_3,4.104 //
The word "other" is used with the intention of referring to those other than <s>Hari</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, and their equals;

children.text: prayukto naiva doṣāya rudrādiṣu ca yuktitaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.105 //
children.translated_text: it is not a fault [when applied] to <s>Rudra</s> and others, and [this is] reasonable. // MAnuv_3,4.105 //

children.text: uttamatvaṃ tu muktānāmapi na brahmaṇo bhavet /
children.translated_text: But the supremacy [stated for <s>Brahmā</s>] among the liberated would not belong to [anyone other than] <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: vyaktiḥ sukhasya tu bhavennatvādhikyaṃ sukhasya ca // MAnuv_3,4.106 //
children.translated_text: There would be manifestation of bliss, but not superiority of bliss [for others]. // MAnuv_3,4.106 //

children.text: balajñānādhikatvaṃ ca tebhyo hi brahmaṇaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: And the superiority in power and knowledge is always of <s>Brahmā</s> over them.
But for the impermanence of that superiority, no means of knowledge is found. // MAnuv_3,4.107 //
"One hears of the hero, fierce upon fierce, subduing one after another, led by that [power];

children.text: edhamānadviḷubhayasya rājā coṣkūyate viśa indro manuṣyān // MAnuv_3,4.108 //
children.translated_text: the king swelling with the might of both sides — <s>Indra</s> urges the people." // MAnuv_3,4.108 //

children.text: parā pūrveṣāṃ sakhyā vṛṇakti vitarturāṇo aparebhireti /
children.translated_text: "He selects the friendship of the ancients; the generous one goes among the later ones.
Shaking off experiences not [yet] had — <s>Indra</s> transcends the earlier and later autumns." // MAnuv_3,4.109 //

children.text: divedive sadṛśīranyamardhaṃ kṛṣṇā asedhadapa sadmano jāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Day by day, [driving away] the equal ones, half the other — the dark [clouds] he drove away, the water-born from their abodes.

children.text: ahan dāsā vṛṣabho vasnayantodavraje varcinaṃ śambaraṃ ca // MAnuv_3,4.110 //
children.translated_text: I [Indra] slew the <s>dāsas</s> (demons), the bull bartering, and [I slew] the radiant <s>Śambara</s>." // MAnuv_3,4.110 //

body.text: taṃ bhūtiriti devā upāsāñcakrire te babhūvustasmāddhāpyetarhi supto bhūbhrūrityeva praśvasityabhūtirityasurāste ha parābabhūvuḥ // MAnuv_3,4.111 //
body.translated_text: "The gods worshipped Him as Prosperity (<s>Bhūti</s>); they became [prosperous]. Therefore, even now, one who sleeps [says] 'Prosperity!' — thus he breathes out. The <s>Asuras</s> [worshipped Him as] Non-prosperity (<s>Abhūti</s>); they were defeated." // MAnuv_3,4.111 //

body.text: tad yathā peśaskarī peśaso mātrāmapādāyānyannavataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ tanuta evamevāyamātmedaṃ śarīraṃ nihatyāvidyāṃ gamayitavānyannavataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ kurute pitṛyaṃ pitṛyaṃ vā gāndharvaṃ vā daivaṃ vā prājāpatyaṃ vā brāhmaṃ vānyeṣāṃ vā bhūtānām // MAnuv_3,4.112 //
body.translated_text: "Just as a weaver, taking a portion of material from the loom, fashions a newer, more beautiful form — even so does this Self, having cast aside this body and dispelled ignorance, fashion a newer, more beautiful form: either ancestral, or <s>Gāndharva</s>, or divine, or of <s>Prajāpati</s>, or of <s>Brahman</s>, or of other beings." // MAnuv_3,4.112 //

children.translated_text: "They quickly attain the supreme perfection, both in this world and the next,
which is not attainable by any <s>Asuras</s>, imperishable and free from affliction.

children.text: na tāṃ gatiṃ prapadyante vinā bhāgavatān narān // MAnuv_3,4.113 //
children.translated_text: That state is not reached without [being] devotees of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." // MAnuv_3,4.113 //
"Fools disregard Me when I am clothed in a human body,
not knowing My supreme nature as the great Lord of beings." // MAnuv_3,4.114 //
"Of futile hopes, futile actions, futile knowledge, devoid of discrimination,

children.text: rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohanīṃ śritāḥ // MAnuv_3,4.115 //
children.translated_text: they resort to the deluding nature of <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Asuras</s>." // MAnuv_3,4.115 //
"But the great souls, O <s>Pārtha</s>, resorting to the divine nature,
worship Me with undivided mind, knowing [Me to be] the imperishable origin of beings." // MAnuv_3,4.116 //
"Fearlessness, purity of being, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge,

children.text: dānaṃ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam // MAnuv_3,4.117 //
children.translated_text: charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, and uprightness; // MAnuv_3,4.117 //
non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, absence of slander,
compassion to beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness; // MAnuv_3,4.118 //
vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice, absence of excessive pride —
these belong to one born to the divine nature, O <s>Bhārata</s>." // MAnuv_3,4.119 //
"Hypocrisy, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, harshness,
and ignorance belong to one born to the demonic nature, O <s>Pārtha</s>." // MAnuv_3,4.120 //
"Those who hate Me in their own and others' bodies, who are envious —
those hateful, cruel, lowest of men in <s>saṃsāra</s>,
I hurl incessantly into inauspicious, demonic wombs alone." // MAnuv_3,4.121 //
"Attaining a demonic womb, deluded birth after birth,

children.text: māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim // MAnuv_3,4.122 //
children.translated_text: not reaching Me, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, they then go to the lowest state." // MAnuv_3,4.122 //

children.text: dvividho bhūtasargo 'tra daiva āsura eva ca /
children.translated_text: "The creation of beings here is twofold: divine and demonic.
The divine is devoted to the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the opposite is the demonic." // MAnuv_3,4.123 //

children.text: devānāṃ paramo dharmaḥ sadā yajñādikāḥ kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The supreme <s>dharma</s> of the gods is always sacrifices and other rites,
study of scripture, knowledge of reality, worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and delight therein" — thus it is remembered. // MAnuv_3,4.124 //
"Of the <s>Daityas</s>: prowess of arms, rivalry, reverence for battle,
expertise in the science of statecraft, worship of <s>Śiva</s>, and delight therein" — thus it is remembered. // MAnuv_3,4.125 //
"Observance of <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste and life-stage) conduct, study of scripture, devotion to <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),

children.text: śive sūrye tathā devyāṃ svabhāvo mānuṣaḥ smṛtaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.126 //
children.translated_text: and to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and the Goddess" — [this] is remembered as the human nature. // MAnuv_3,4.126 //
"The gods are devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> by nature from beginningless time.
The <s>Daityas</s> are the opposite, always, from beginningless time." // MAnuv_3,4.127 //
"Humans are of mixed disposition, and also of mixed destinies."
From such collections of statements, the beginningless fitness [of souls] is known. // MAnuv_3,4.128 //
If the distinction is beginningless, how [does it exist] at present?
[We reply:] the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) is accepted from the unseen itself by <s>Sarvavādins</s> (the proponents of all [schools]). // MAnuv_3,4.129 //
If the distinction is [said to be] accidental — and yet <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (the unseen) is accepted in some [cases],
then there would be accidentality everywhere — there would be no dependence on <s>adṛṣṭa</s>.

children.text: adṛṣṭāśced viśeṣo 'yamanāditvaṃ kuto na tat // MAnuv_3,4.130 //
children.translated_text: If this distinction is from <s>adṛṣṭa</s> — why is its beginninglessness not [accepted]? // MAnuv_3,4.130 //
And the difference in <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not like difference in other [beings]; even for those who see [such difference],
recognition itself is seen in [His] many forms. // MAnuv_3,4.131 //

children.text: bahutvaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa na bhedena kathañcana /
children.translated_text: And the multiplicity [of His forms] is through distinction, not through difference in any way.

children.text: pratyabhijñā ca yeṣāṃ na te 'pi tanmuṣyadṛṣṭayaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.132 //
children.translated_text: And those who lack recognition — they too are of a vision stolen by that [Lord]. // MAnuv_3,4.132 //

children.text: bhedaṃ naiva prapaśyanti bhedamanyebhya eva ca /
children.translated_text: They do not perceive difference [in Him] at all; and difference from others,
they do perceive — thus <s>Hari</s> reveals Himself to them, not otherwise. // MAnuv_3,4.133 //
Thus the statement in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s> — not [the statement] from the Purāṇas —
worldly perception and the like alone could obstruct the <s>Vedas</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.134 //
And unexamined perception — examined perception
alone would be able to obstruct the <s>Vedas</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.135 //
And for one whose difference [from Viṣṇu] is ascertained, there is no Purāṇic [statement] regarding the vision [of identity] —

children.text: vākyaṃ kvaciddhi sammugdhadarśanaṃ tatra gamyate // MAnuv_3,4.136 //
children.translated_text: a statement is somewhere understood as a confused vision — that is understood there // 3.4.136 //
The unexamined alone [seems faulty] here — the piercing and so forth of the Lord; /

children.text: parīkṣādarśane naiva dṛśyate kenacit kvacit // MAnuv_3,4.137 //
children.translated_text: in the examined vision, no [fault] is ever seen by anyone anywhere // 3.4.137 //
<s>Brahmā</s> saw Him as entirely faultless, possessing all forms; /

children.text: nirdoṣameva rudro 'drāṅ nirdoṣaṃ taṃ purandaraḥ // MAnuv_3,4.138 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> too saw Him as faultless; <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) [saw] Him as faultless // 3.4.138 //
His forms were thus seen as faultless by the best of the <s>devas</s>; /
all others are with faults; <s>Hari</s> alone is faultless — /

children.text: iti barkuśruteścaiva sadoṣaṃ nāsya darśanam // MAnuv_3,4.139 //
children.translated_text: from the <s>Barku Śruti</s> too, there is no fault in seeing Him // 3.4.139 //
'Unpierced, <s>Viṣṇu</s> appears as if pierced; unborn, He falsely appears as if born; /
unbound, He appears as if bound — the one of immeasurable splendor' — /

children.text: iti paiṅgiśrutiścaiva prāha nirdoṣatāṃ hareḥ // MAnuv_3,4.140 //
children.translated_text: thus the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s> too declares the faultlessness of <s>Hari</s> // 3.4.140 //
'Only by an unexamined vision is <s>Hari</s> seen as having faults; /

children.text: parīkṣādarśane naiva dṛśyo doṣo hareḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: in the examined vision, no fault of <s>Hari</s> is ever seen anywhere' — /

children.text: iti paiṅgiśrutiścāha pramāṇaṃ hi parīkṣitam // MAnuv_3,4.141 //
children.translated_text: thus the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s> also says — for the examined is the valid authority // 3.4.141 //
There is no infinite regress in examination, because of the absence of doubt in what is established by the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>); /
faults may exist in mental vision, but not in the vision of the witness; /

children.text: sudṛḍho nirṇayo yatra jñeyaṃ tat sākṣidarśanam // MAnuv_3,4.142 //
children.translated_text: where there is a firmly established determination — that should be known as the vision of the witness // 3.4.142 //
Desire, knowledge, pleasure, pain, fear, fearlessness, compassion, and the like — /

children.text: sākṣisiddhā na kaściddhi tatra saṃśayavān kvacit /
children.translated_text: are established by the witness; no one whatsoever has any doubt regarding them; /

children.text: yat kvacid vyabhicārī syād darśanaṃ mānasaṃ hi tat // MAnuv_3,4.143 //
children.translated_text: wherever there may be deviation — that is a mental vision // 3.4.143 //
Even for the vision of mind, eye, and the rest, where the validity /

children.text: prāmāṇyaṃ sugṛhītaṃ syāt tat parīkṣitadarśanam // MAnuv_3,4.144 //
children.translated_text: is well-grasped by the witness — that is the examined vision // 3.4.144 //
The validity of that [knowledge] is not seen merely through the vision of knowledge; /
invariably, the validity regarding pleasure and the rest is within the range of the witness // 3.4.145 //
The witness always sees its own validity, because of firm certainty; /
since the validity of knowledge is measured by the witness, the grasper // 3.4.146 //
Validity obtains in the absence of faults; the absence of faults is ascertained /
by the witness in some cases — [this is what is] accepted as self-validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) // 3.4.147 //

children.text: ato na sarvamānānāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ niścitaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the validity of all means of knowledge is not invariably ascertained; /

children.text: sākṣiṇā niścitaṃ yatra tat prāmāṇyasvalakṣaṇam // MAnuv_3,4.148 //
children.translated_text: where it is ascertained by the witness — that is the intrinsic characteristic of validity // 3.4.148 //

children.text: na hi kaścit sukhādyeṣu saṃśayaṃ kurute janaḥ /
children.translated_text: For no person whatsoever has doubt regarding pleasure and the like; /
nor does every person ascertain all means of knowledge // 3.4.149 //
Therefore, what is directly established in experience — for what purpose is it apprehended [again]? /

children.text: doṣābhāvādikaṃ caiva sākṣī samyak prapaśyati // MAnuv_3,4.150 //
children.translated_text: The absence of faults and the like — the witness properly perceives // 3.4.150 //

children.text: tat parīkṣitamānena na doṣo viṣṇavi kvacit /
children.translated_text: By that examined means of knowledge, there is no fault in <s>Viṣṇu</s> anywhere; /
but the unexamined vision — in what matter is it not found? // 3.4.151 //
Therefore, even scripture has no validity in a matter contradicted by perception; /
where perception is relied upon, elsewhere [scripture prevails] — this is the reversal // 3.4.152 //
In worldly transactions, perception has priority; /
in the seeing of <s>avatāras</s> and the like, scripture has priority // 3.4.153 //

children.text: āgamena hi viṣṇutvaṃ jñātvā doṣo 'tra kalpyate /
children.translated_text: By scripture, having known the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood [of the <s>avatāra</s>], a fault is construed here; /

children.text: na cet syāt doṣavānanyaḥ śāstrasiddhaṃ hi lakṣaṇam // MAnuv_3,4.154 //
children.translated_text: if not, another would be the faulty one — for the characteristic is established by scripture // 3.4.154 //
That someone has faults — to this extent alone, perception applies; /

children.text: na viṣṇordeṣavattve hi pratyakṣaṃ vartate svataḥ // MAnuv_3,4.155 //
children.translated_text: perception does not by itself operate regarding the faultfulness of <s>Viṣṇu</s> // 3.4.155 //
'Some see faults' — even here, perception would not [be the authority]; /
the <s>Purāṇic</s> statement alone is here — and that is contradicted by <s>Śruti</s> itself // 3.4.156 //
And the <s>Purāṇa</s> depends upon the <s>Veda</s> alone, not upon anything else; /

children.text: tadvirodhe kathaṃ mānaṃ tat tatra ca bhaviṣyati // MAnuv_3,4.157 //
children.translated_text: when it contradicts that [<s>Veda</s>], how will it have validity there? // 3.4.157 //
And how can an unexamined vision be [treated as] perception? /

children.text: yadyevaṃ devadattādibhramaḥ kiṃ nākṣajaṃ bhavet // MAnuv_3,4.158 //
children.translated_text: If so, then would not the error regarding <s>Devadatta</s> and others also be perception? // 3.4.158 //
As long as there is examination of what is relied upon, and as long as the defeasor [is absent] — /
the fault lies in the unexamined fault; the status of being relied upon is not weak // 3.4.159 //
Even in error, there is a non-erroneous portion; relying on that much alone, /
the operation of the defeating cognition would occur; but not in what is well-examined — /

children.text: sarvaṃ tadupajīvyaiva pramāṇaṃ vartate yataḥ // MAnuv_3,4.160 //
children.translated_text: since all of that, being relied upon, operates as a valid authority // 3.4.160 //
'How is <s>Brahman</s> [to be known]?' — that should be known as having the characteristic of omniscience and the like; /

children.text: vihāya yasmātkasmāccit svarūpasyaiva ced yadi // MAnuv_3,4.161 //
children.translated_text: if, setting aside that, from some [other basis], the own-form itself [is proposed] // 3.4.161 //
the status of being relied upon is excluded from this by just as much /
as is excluded — and the status of being relied upon belongs to the own-form alone, nowhere else // 3.4.162 //
But if the own-form is declared as possessing all characteristics, /

children.text: astu no naiva hāniḥ syāt svapakṣaścāyamañjasā // MAnuv_3,4.163 //
children.translated_text: let it be so — there is no loss for us; and this is directly our position // 3.4.163 //
Since indeed the connected meaning of words in every way /
becomes the entire own-form through the relation of specific and general // 3.4.164 //
In the error regarding <s>Devadatta</s> and others, being-in-front and other [features] /

children.text: vyāvartayanti tadrūpaṃ caitramātrad vinaiva hi // MAnuv_3,4.165 //
children.translated_text: exclude that form [of another person] from <s>Caitra</s> and the rest, without [those features] alone // 3.4.165 //
Since <s>Brahman</s> is without distinction — what then excludes? /
From some thing or other — if so, then there is the proof of what is already proved // 3.4.166 //
Mere consciousness is not even accepted by the proponent of non-distinction; /

children.text: tāvanmātraṃ yadīṣyaṃ syāt sarvajñatvaṃ kuto na tat // MAnuv_3,4.167 //
children.translated_text: if only that much is accepted, then why not omniscience? // 3.4.167 //
Even in proving the non-difference of mere consciousness, it is [already] established for the opponent; /
for consciousness-hood is his own view too, from his own acceptance of non-difference // 3.4.168 //
'Omniscience is from relatedness to everything' — if this is [argued], then /

children.text: iti ceccetanatvaṃ ca jñatvaṃ na jñeyavarjitam // MAnuv_3,4.169 //
children.translated_text: consciousness-hood and knower-hood do not exist without the knowable // 3.4.169 //
And he does not consider the self to be its own knowable, with distinction; /
even the word 'sva' (self/own) depends on another; therefore, exclusion alone /

children.text: svaśabdārtha iti proktaḥ svarūpaṃ nāma kiṃ na cet // MAnuv_3,4.170 //
children.translated_text: is declared as the meaning of the word 'sva'; what then is 'own-form'? // 3.4.170 //
By the word 'rūpa' (form), because of fullness — and that is a statement of generality; /

children.text: na svarūpābhidhāyi syād vaiyarthyaṃ svaravasya yat // MAnuv_3,4.171 //
children.translated_text: it would not denote the own-form; what purpose would the [additional] syllable 'sva' serve? // 3.4.171 //
For the nature of a conscious being is sung as consciousness; /
therefore, the abundance of distinctions — through the distinction of consciousness // 3.4.172 //

children.text: na jñeyajñātṛhīnaṃ hi jñānaṃ nāma kvacid bhavet /
children.translated_text: For knowledge devoid of the knowable and the knower is nowhere possible; /

children.text: jñeyajñānavihīnaśca jña ityatra ca na pramā // MAnuv_3,4.173 //
children.translated_text: and a knower devoid of the knowable and knowledge — there is no valid authority for this // 3.4.173 //
And if knowledge is devoid of knower and knowable, then eating too, devoid of eater and what is eaten, /

children.text: hīnaṃ bhojanameva syāt tāḍanaṃ kartṛtāḍyataḥ // MAnuv_3,4.174 //
children.translated_text: would exist; and striking, devoid of striker and what is struck // 3.4.174 //
If [it is said that] because of being eternal, it would be of that sort — then even eternal speech /

children.text: vācyavaktṛvihīnā syānnahi sā caiva tādṛśī // MAnuv_3,4.175 //
children.translated_text: would be devoid of what is expressed and the speaker; but that is not the case // 3.4.175 //

children.text: draṣṭāro vedavāco hi santi vācyāni cāñjasā /
children.translated_text: For the seers of the Vedic words do exist, and the expressed [meanings] do exist directly; /

children.text: nityo draṣṭā ca vācyaśca bhagavāneva ca svayam // MAnuv_3,4.176 //
children.translated_text: the eternal seer and the [eternally] expressed is the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself // 3.4.176 //

children.text: na hi vaktṛvihīnā ca vācyahīnāpi vāk kvacit /
children.translated_text: For there is never any speech devoid of speaker and devoid of what is expressed; /

children.text: jñātṛjñeyavihīnaṃ ca jñānamevaṃ na tad bhavet // MAnuv_3,4.177 //
children.translated_text: knowledge devoid of knower and knowable likewise cannot exist // 3.4.177 //
For even an eternal speaker does not exist devoid of statements and what is expressed; /
a knower devoid of knowledge and knowable likewise does not exist // 3.4.178 //
Moreover, by what valid authority is the negation of everything understood? /

children.text: sarveṇa saha tad vākyāmarthaśca yadi gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: If the meaning of that statement is grasped together with everything, /

children.text: tadabhāvena sarvasya nāpalāpo bhavet tadā // MAnuv_3,4.179 //
children.translated_text: then, because of its [own] absence, the negation of everything would not hold // 3.4.179 //

children.text: na gṛhyate ced tannyāyādapalāpo na hi kvacit /
children.translated_text: If it is not grasped — then by that very reasoning, the negation is nowhere [valid]; /
the meaning of a statement devoid of logical support is not understood // 3.4.180 //
Among the interpretive signs beginning with introduction (<s>upakrama</s>), each subsequent one is stronger; /
while in <s>Śruti</s> and the rest, each prior one [is stronger] — from the determination of <s>Brahmatarka</s> // 3.4.181 //
When perception, logical reasoning, and many scriptures /
contradict — and there is no meaning where there is contradiction of interpretive signs // 3.4.182 //
how can that very meaning be accepted? When [the reasoning] is sound, it is non-contradictory; /

children.text: mukhyārthe vidyamāne tu kva sāvarjñyaṃ niṣiddhayate // MAnuv_3,4.183 //
children.translated_text: when the primary meaning is available, where is omniscience refuted? // 3.4.183 //
Therefore, <s>Brahman</s> as possessing all qualities must be accepted; /

children.text: apalāpo 'pi sarvasya na kathañcana yujyate // MAnuv_3,4.184 //
children.translated_text: the negation of everything is not in any way proper // 3.4.184 //
Beginningless fitness is also stated — therefore it should be accepted in every way; /

children.text: muktānāṃ tāratamyaṃ ca mānairuktairna cālyate // MAnuv_3,4.185 //
children.translated_text: and the gradation among the liberated is not shaken by the stated valid authorities // 3.4.185 //

children.text: jñānino 'pi yato nityaṃ kurvanti śubhameva hi /
children.translated_text: Since even the knowers always perform only auspicious [deeds], /

children.text: tāratamyaṃ tu muktau ca tenaivādhyavasīyate // MAnuv_3,4.186 //
children.translated_text: the gradation in liberation too is thereby ascertained // 3.4.186 //

children.text: tāratamyaṃ na cenmuktau kutaḥ kuryuḥ śubhaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: If there is no gradation in liberation, why then would they again perform auspicious deeds? /

children.text: kṛcchreṇāpi tapo jñānaṃ karmāpyete caranti hi // MAnuv_3,4.187 //
children.translated_text: Even with difficulty, they practice austerity, knowledge, and <s>karma</s> // 3.4.187 //
They are always afraid of inauspicious [deeds] and always desirous regarding the auspicious; /
and this is not merely own-nature, because of the activity preceded by fear, /
and because of the repeated and difficult performance of the auspicious alone // 3.4.188 //
If such were [merely their] own-nature, even the ignorant would be the same; /

children.text: phalavattve pramāṇaṃ cet tatra jñasya samaṃ hi tat // MAnuv_3,4.189 //
children.translated_text: if [the argument is] that it is because it bears fruit — then for the knower, that [fruit] is equal // 3.4.189 //
