Desireless, preceded by knowledge — this is declared here as '<s>nivṛtta</s>' (renounced action); /
'one who practices renounced [action] attains the eternal <s>Brahman</s>' // 3.4.190 //
Through auspicious [deeds], there is increase of bliss; and through inauspicious, diminishment; /

children.text: jñānino 'pi yatastena kartavyaṃ śubhameva taiḥ // MAnuv_3,4.191 //
children.translated_text: since even the knowers [experience this], therefore auspicious deeds alone must be performed by them // 3.4.191 //

children.text: upāste sa ya ātmānaṃ kṣīyate nāsya karma ha /
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on the Self — his <s>karma</s> is not destroyed; /

children.text: asmāddhayevātmano yadyat kāmayet sṛjate ca tat // MAnuv_3,4.192 //
children.translated_text: whatever he would desire from this very Self, he creates that' // 3.4.192 //
'Even one who is ignorant and performs many <s>karmas</s> obtains only finite fruit; /
but whatever one does with knowledge — that indeed is supremely powerful' — /
from the force of such statements, the gradation extends to liberation // 3.4.193 //
And it is not said here that the fruit of the meditator alone is imperishable; /

children.text: na hi jñānaṃ vinā kvāpi phalasyākṣayatā bhavet /
children.translated_text: for the imperishability of fruit does not occur anywhere without knowledge; /
if [one says it occurs] through the medium of knowledge — then there is no opposition to our position // 3.4.194 //
Only what follows knowledge has imperishability, and not otherwise; /
for the fulfillment of auspicious [deeds] performed prior [to knowledge occurs] through knowledge alone // 3.4.195 //
But for <s>prārabdha karmas</s> (commenced karmas), through experience; and for <s>karmas</s> [performed] after knowledge, /
there would be entry into liberation; otherwise there would be no performance of them // 3.4.196 //
All auspicious [deeds] prior to knowledge are for the attainment of knowledge; /
the undesired and prohibited ones are for the obstruction of knowledge, for [one's own] experience [of suffering] // 3.4.197 //
And whatever abundance of auspicious [deeds exists] from the beginning, by the force of fitness, /
that produces abundance of knowledge — it is not the cause of anything else // 3.4.198 //
Since knowledge has devotion as its part, devotion is called knowledge; /
that which is the distinction of knowledge itself is called devotion // 3.4.199 //
Just as indirect-ness (<s>parokṣatva</s>) and directness (<s>aparokṣatva</s>) are distinctions pertaining to knowledge, /

children.text: snehayogo 'pi tadvat syād viśeṣo jñānagocaraḥ // MAnuv_3,4.200 //
children.translated_text: the connection with affection too would be a distinction pertaining to knowledge // 3.4.200 //
With this intent, the <s>Śrutis</s> generally say that knowledge alone leads to liberation; /

children.text: vadanti śrutayaḥ so 'yaṃ viśeṣo 'pi hyudīryate // MAnuv_3,4.201 //
children.translated_text: but this distinction [of devotion] too is declared // 3.4.201 //

children.text: bhaktirjñānamiti kvāpi na hi dveṣayutā dṛśiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Devotion is knowledge' — somewhere [this is stated]; for vision conjoined with hatred /
does not lead to the goal of man — because of contradiction with all <s>Śrutis</s> // 3.4.202 //

children.text: cetanasya dvayaṃ bhogyaṃ saṃsāro muktireva ca /
children.translated_text: For the conscious being, there are two [objects of] experience: <s>saṃsāra</s> and liberation; /
<s>Saṃsāra</s> is threefold therein: heaven, middle, and lower // 3.4.203 //

children.text: muktiśca dvividhā tatra sukhaṃ nityaṃ tathāparam /
children.translated_text: And liberation too is twofold therein: [one of] eternal bliss, and another /
It should be known that the means [leading to] eternal suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> also [exist] —

children.text: kāmyaṃ karma niṣiddhaṃ ca sājñānamiti niścayaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.204 //
children.translated_text: desire-prompted action and prohibited action, together with [false] knowledge — such is the settled view. // MAnuv_3,4.204 //
Hatred and devotion — in liberation, [these are] the cause of two [kinds of] liberation.
Thus, from the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s>, hatred is not the cause of true liberation. // MAnuv_3,4.205 //
It is the cause of false liberation. 'In liberation' — here <s>Keśava</s>

children.text: muktiśabdodito mokṣaṃ svabhaktānāṃ karoti yat // MAnuv_3,4.206 //
children.translated_text: is indicated by the word '<s>mukti</s>' (liberation), since He grants liberation to His own devotees. // MAnuv_3,4.206 //
If liberation [were attained] even through hatred, [that would constitute] an obstruction of the great purport [of scripture].
That the Lord, pleased through devotion, grants liberation — [proclaiming] His qualities thus,

children.text: vadanti śrutayaḥ sarvāḥ purāṇānyāgamā api // MAnuv_3,4.207 //
children.translated_text: all the <s>śrutis</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and <s>Āgamas</s> declare. // MAnuv_3,4.207 //

children.text: yadi dveṣeṇa muktiḥ syād vaktavyo doṣasañcayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If liberation were [attainable] through hatred, [then] the collection of faults [in hatred] should be stated.
The <s>Bhagavān</s> is to be remembered constantly — with this very meaning, in some places
qualities are spoken of as if through hatred, as in the speech of an angry [father] in the <s>Purāṇa</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.208 //
Just as an angry father tells his son 'Die!' with reproof,
[yet] speaks for the purpose of another intended action — thus the <s>Purāṇa</s> passage too. // MAnuv_3,4.209 //
Because of contradiction with <s>śruti</s>, self-contradiction,
and contradiction with many scriptures, [the passage] does not declare liberation through hatred. // MAnuv_3,4.210 //

children.text: tamo dveṣeṇa saṃyānti bhaktayā muktiṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Through hatred they go to darkness; through devotion, to liberation likewise —
regarding <s>Viṣṇu</s>, through <s>Viṣṇu's</s> grace, and through the reverse [respectively].
This statement of six [attributes] also determines the [above] stated meaning. // MAnuv_3,4.211 //
And when the great purport is obstructed, how can the statement attain authority?
For the great purport is considered to be the form of all meanings. // MAnuv_3,4.212 //

children.text: vācakatvaṃ hi tātparyaṃ yadarthā akhilā ravāḥ /
children.translated_text: For <s>tātparya</s> (purport) is the denotative capacity — that meaning for which all utterances [exist] —
how could that meaning be abandoned when doubt [arises] about a single word?

children.text: ato vijñānabhaktibhyāṃ puruṣārthaḥ paro bhavet // MAnuv_3,4.213 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, through knowledge and devotion, the supreme human goal is attained. // MAnuv_3,4.213 //

children.text: yasya deve parā bhaktiryathā deve tathā gurau /
children.translated_text: He who has supreme devotion to the deity, and [treats] the <s>guru</s> as he [treats] the deity —

children.text: tasyaite kathitā hyarthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.214 //
children.translated_text: to that great soul, these declared meanings become illuminated. // MAnuv_3,4.214 //

children.text: bhaktyā jñānaṃ tato bhaktistato dṛṣṭistataśca sā /
children.translated_text: From devotion [arises] knowledge, from that [arises] devotion, from that [arises] vision, and from that

children.text: tato muktistato bhaktiḥ saiva syāt sukharūpiṇī // MAnuv_3,4.215//
children.translated_text: liberation, and from that devotion itself — that very [devotion] becomes the form of bliss. // MAnuv_3,4.215 //
The <s>Bhagavān</s>, pleased through devotion, would grant undisturbed knowledge.
Through that very [devotion], having attained [His] vision, He would grant liberation through it. // MAnuv_3,4.216 //

children.text: nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena nacejyayā /
children.translated_text: 'Not through the <s>Vedas</s>, not through austerity, not through gifts, nor through sacrifice
am I able to be seen in this form' — He would grant liberation through that [devotion]. // MAnuv_3,4.217 //
'But through exclusive devotion, I can be [known] in this form, O <s>Arjuna</s> —

children.text: jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣyuṃ ca parantapa // MAnuv_3,4.218 //
children.translated_text: known, seen in truth, and entered into, O scorcher of foes.' // MAnuv_3,4.218 //
From such statements too, that very stated meaning is understood.

children.text: na ca prasādamāpnoti dveṣād bhaktyā tamāpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: One does not obtain [His] grace through hatred; through devotion one may obtain it.
Thus, conformity with what is seen is also understood in this meaning. // MAnuv_3,4.219 //

children.text: ye pṛthag vihitā viṣṇorguṇā vedena sādaram /
children.translated_text: Those qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s> which are separately established by the <s>Veda</s> with respect —
those very [qualities] are to be accepted through observed converse analogy, and nothing else. // MAnuv_3,4.220 //
Other [qualities] are also understood regarding <s>Vāsudeva</s> through conformity with what is seen.

children.text: doṣābhāvāśca ye vedairuditā avihāya tān // MAnuv_3,4.221 //
children.translated_text: And those absences of faults declared by the <s>Vedas</s> — without abandoning them, // MAnuv_3,4.221 //
even those unstated [qualities] should be accepted through the power of the great purport.

children.text: evaṃ bṛhatsaṃhitāvāk siddhānto hi tadīritaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.222 //
children.translated_text: Thus the doctrine stated by the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s> passage is established. // MAnuv_3,4.222 //
In a hierarchical manner, devotion to His devotees also is to be firmly determined,
and this devotion to His [devotees] must be practiced according to worldly convention and <s>Veda</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.223 //

children.text: yo hi bhaktaḥ pradhāne syāt tadīyeṣvapi bhaktimān /
children.translated_text: For one who is devoted to the chief [deity] is invariably seen
to be devoted also to those belonging to Him; the opposite in the contrary case. // MAnuv_3,4.224 //
If there is deviation anywhere, a decrease in devotion is to be inferred there.

children.text: bhaktidoṣo hyasau yanna tadbhakteṣvapi bhaktimān // MAnuv_3,4.225 //
children.translated_text: For that is a fault in devotion — that one is not devoted even to the devotees of Him. // MAnuv_3,4.225 //
Devotion to them in a hierarchical manner, truly, according to what is observed,
should be practiced in accord with <s>Viṣṇu's</s> grace; otherwise it is a fault. // MAnuv_3,4.226 //
In the world too, love in accordance with one's own affection is indeed seen.
Knowledge of the hierarchy is also the means through this very [principle]. // MAnuv_3,4.227 //
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Viriñca</s> (Brahmā), <s>Vāṇī</s> (Sarasvatī), <s>Īśa</s> (Rudra), <s>Girijā</s> (Pārvatī), <s>Indra</s>, <s>Aṅgiras's</s> sons,
<s>Sūrya</s> and others — in order, [these are] objects of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> affection. // MAnuv_3,4.228 //

children.text: teṣu bhaktiḥ krameṇaiva kāryā nityaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Devotion to them in order must be practiced constantly by seekers of liberation.

children.text: sarve 'pi guravaścaite puruṣasya sadaiva hi // MAnuv_3,4.229 //
children.translated_text: All of these are indeed always the <s>gurus</s> of a person. // MAnuv_3,4.229 //

children.text: tasmāt pūjyāśca namyāśca dhyeyāśca parito harim /
children.translated_text: Therefore they are to be worshipped, saluted, and meditated upon, around <s>Hari</s>.
From the statement of six [attributes] also, this meaning is ascertained. // MAnuv_3,4.230 //
Devotion to <s>Hari</s> in order, remembrance of <s>Hari</s> in those [devoted to Him],
praise of <s>Hari</s>, and remembrance of Him, and praise of Him, worship of <s>Hari</s>,
renunciation enjoined by His worship — these, in liberation, are in order
invariably the means, and [are] to be always practiced by all. // MAnuv_3,4.232 //
Thus the statement of practice, in the determination of the means,
when the <s>Pañcarātra</s> has been set forth — therein is the firm ascertainment of the means. // MAnuv_3,4.233 //
Hatred of <s>Hari</s> is not auspicious, because of being hatred of the good, just as [hatred] of the <s>guru</s>.
Devotion in a hierarchical manner is the cause of <s>Hari's</s> pleasure; devotion reaching His dear ones —

children.text: bhaktiryato yathā svasminnityādyā yuktiratra ca // MAnuv_3,4.234 //
children.translated_text: because devotion [is efficacious] as in one's own [case] — this is the reasoning here also. // MAnuv_3,4.234 //
The highest devotion, following the hierarchy of primacy,

children.text: prītidaiva hareryasmād bhaktiḥ sā svopagā yathā // MAnuv_3,4.235 //
children.translated_text: is that which gives pleasure to <s>Hari</s>, since such devotion extends to one's own [sphere]. // MAnuv_3,4.235 //
Or thus — the fruit of knowledge, action, etc. accrues to these [beings] in a hierarchical manner.

children.text: svātantryatāratamyena phalaṃ hi phalināṃ bhavet // MAnuv_3,4.236 //
children.translated_text: Through the hierarchy of independence, the fruit of the fruitful [actions] comes about. // MAnuv_3,4.236 //
But inauspicious [fruit] in inauspicious [action] of these [beings] also — through [their] independence, through <s>Hari's</s> pleasure,

children.text: ājñayā cānyagaṃ naiva bhogāya bhavati kvacit // MAnuv_3,4.237 //
children.translated_text: and by [His] command — does not reach others, nor ever serves for [their] enjoyment. // MAnuv_3,4.237 //
'Merit alone brings this one to [the devas]; sin does not reach the <s>devas</s>.'
Such <s>śruti</s> passages are the authority; in the established meaning, [there are] other reasonings [too]. // MAnuv_3,4.238 //
Since the fruit of the <s>dharma</s> of meditation is continued existence in another body,
and by the command of <s>Vāsudeva</s> alone, in accordance with prior <s>karma</s>, // MAnuv_3,4.239 //

children.text: prerayanti hi te jīvān puṇyapāpeṣu nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: they impel the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) toward merit and sin constantly,
and [being] free from attachment and hatred, how could they incur faults? // MAnuv_3,4.240 //
By carrying out <s>Hari's</s> command alone, merit is obtained by them.

children.text: haripūjeti coddeśāt kathaṃ na śubhamāpnuyuḥ // MAnuv_3,4.241 //
children.translated_text: Since it is directed as worship of <s>Hari</s>, how could they not obtain what is auspicious? // MAnuv_3,4.241 //
Therefore, in order, the fruit of <s>dharma</s> and knowledge directly
pertaining to all living beings — the <s>devas</s> obtain [it], up to <s>Viriñca</s> (Brahmā). // MAnuv_3,4.242 //

children.text: devā eva hi devānāṃ viśiṣṭā viniyāmakāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>devas</s> themselves are the distinguished controllers of [other] <s>devas</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> is the controller of all <s>devas</s> and of humans.
Therefore he obtains all qualities in greater [measure] than others. // MAnuv_3,4.243 //
Through excellence in substance, independence, knowledge, and effort, greater fruit [accrues].

children.text: devānāmanyagaṃ cāpi teṣu yad brahmaṇo hi tat // MAnuv_3,4.244 //
children.translated_text: And what pertains to others among the <s>devas</s> — that [also belongs] to <s>Brahmā</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.244 //
The statement spoken by <s>Hari</s> in the text called <s>Bṛhattantra</s>, in the determination of fruits —
in the world too, through such qualities, superiority of fruit is indeed seen. // MAnuv_3,4.245 //
And thus, the great fruit of the <s>asuras</s> prior to <s>Kali</s> [age]
in inauspicious [actions] would always be [great], in false knowledge and the like. // MAnuv_3,4.246 //
The <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s> would obtain the fruits of auspicious and inauspicious [actions]

children.text: krameṇaiva yathāśakti yathā ye ye prayojakāḥ // MAnuv_3,4.247 //
children.translated_text: in order, according to capacity, according to whoever are the instigators. // MAnuv_3,4.247 //

children.text: prerakā api pāpānāṃ na devāḥ pāpamāpnuyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Though impellers of sins, the <s>devas</s> would not incur sin —

children.text: iti prakāśikāyāṃ hi provāca harirañjasā // MAnuv_3,4.248 //
children.translated_text: thus <s>Hari</s> directly declared in the text called <s>Prakāśikā</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.248 //

children.text: yadyapyevaṃ surāṇāṃ ca daityānāṃ ca mahat phalam /
children.translated_text: Even though thus for the <s>suras</s> and <s>daityas</s> the fruit is great

children.text: śubhāśubhebhya evañca kartuśca syād yathoditam // MAnuv_3,4.249 //
children.translated_text: from auspicious and inauspicious [actions] respectively, and for the doer also as stated — // MAnuv_3,4.249 //
therefore, those who experience hell, human state, heaven, and liberation —
starting from the best of humans, the <s>devas</s> [experience all] except hell. // MAnuv_3,4.250 //
But the <s>asuras</s>, without liberation, attain even blinding darkness —

children.text: iti tattvavivekoktaṃ svayaṃ bhagavatā vacaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.251 //
children.translated_text: thus the statement made by the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself in the <s>Tattvaviveka</s>. // MAnuv_3,4.251 //
Teachers who give knowledge obtain a distinguished fruit.
In liberation, the <s>guru</s> obtains from his student eightfold auspiciousness. // MAnuv_3,4.252 //
The guru's guru [obtains] twofold from that, and one-and-a-half times that for the others thereafter.

children.text: devāḥ sahasraguṇitaṃ kramāt tasmād yathottaram // MAnuv_3,4.253 //
children.translated_text: The <s>devas</s> [obtain] a thousand-fold in order from that, successively higher. // MAnuv_3,4.253 //
<s>Brahmā</s> [obtains] multiplied by a great flood — thus is the determination of fruits.
So said the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself in the <s>śāstra</s> called <s>Guruvṛtta</s>.

children.text: yuktaṃ ca tanna godātā gomātraphalamāpnuyāt // MAnuv_3,4.254 //
children.translated_text: And this is fitting — a cow-giver would not obtain merely the fruit of the cow's mother. // MAnuv_3,4.254 //
'He who will declare this supreme secret to My devotees,

children.text: bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ // MAnuv_3,4.255 //
children.translated_text: having offered supreme devotion to Me, will come to Me alone — without doubt.' // MAnuv_3,4.255 //
'And there is no one among humans who is dearer to Me in action than he,

children.text: bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi /
children.translated_text: nor will there be another dearer to Me on earth than he.'
Thus said the <s>Bhagavān</s> — even so, the [worthy] recipient is required. // MAnuv_3,4.256 //
In just this way, without contradiction, of <s>prārabdha karma</s> (commenced karma) alone,

children.text: jñānaṃ dṛṣṭaphalaṃ proktaṃ muktiścehaiva labhyate // MAnuv_3,4.257 //
children.translated_text: knowledge is said to have visible fruit, and liberation is obtained in this very [life]. // MAnuv_3,4.257 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Śrīmad Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the revered <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya</s> (Madhvācārya). ||

children.translated_text: When the subject matter — [namely] the object [of knowledge] and the means [of attaining it] — has been established through concordance and non-contradiction,
and all the means have been examined in detail, // MAnuv_4,1.1 //
that which is to be constantly and absolutely and inevitably practiced as a means —
first among those, the question arises: is <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing) and the like to be done once, // MAnuv_4,1.2 //
or with repetition? When doubt [arises], repetition indeed is to be performed.
The instruction 'You are That' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>) etc. — since it is [given] not just once, // MAnuv_4,1.3 //
from the indicator — <s>Lāṭavya</s>, formerly belonging to the <s>Ṛc</s> [Veda], being of Brahman-nature, [who heard] a hundred [times];

children.text: śuśrāvogratapā nāma yogyo rudrapadasya yaḥ // MAnuv_4,1.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ugratapas</s> by name, one worthy of the rank of <s>Rudra</s>, heard — // MAnuv_4,1.4 //

children.text: sārddhaṃ parārddhaṃ viṣṇostu guṇān bhaktayā sadodyataḥ /
children.translated_text: for one-and-a-half <s>parārddha</s> [periods], the qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, constantly devoted with devotion.
He performed meditation for one-third of that, with a collected mind. // MAnuv_4,1.5 //
For ten <s>manvantaras</s>, <s>Sunanda</s> by name, worthy of the rank of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra),
worthy of the rank of <s>Garutmat</s> (Garuḍa), from <s>Sumanas</s>,
heard and practiced meditation diligently for four <s>manvantaras</s>. // MAnuv_4,1.6 //
And those worthy of the ranks of <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Candra</s>, of great radiance —
<s>Surūpa</s> and <s>Śāntarūpa</s> — for four <s>manvantaras</s>
heard from <s>Sumanas</s> and meditated for one <s>manvantara</s>. // MAnuv_4,1.7 //
Then all those devotees — <s>Ugratapas</s> and others — were told [by Viṣṇu],
and they saw the supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>, always nourished by His grace.

children.text: ityuktaṃ viṣṇunā sākṣād granthe sattatvasañjñite // MAnuv_4,1.8 //
children.translated_text: Thus was spoken by <s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself directly in the text named <s>Sattattva</s>. // MAnuv_4,1.8 //
The name '<s>Ātmā</s>' (Self) is declared to be directly of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> —

children.text: ātmā brahma mahāṃstāraḥ parameśaḥ śuciśravāḥ // MAnuv_4,1.9 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ātmā</s>, <s>Brahma</s>, the great Deliverer, the supreme Lord, of pure fame, // MAnuv_4,1.9 //
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Infinite' — thus <s>Śrīpati</s> (Lord of <s>Śrī</s>) is celebrated.
Thus the <s>Piṅga Śruti</s>, and likewise the <s>Parama Śruti</s>. // MAnuv_4,1.10 //
'<s>Om</s> — the Self is the <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s>, the Self-blissful, the Imperishable, the Self-sovereign,
the Protector of all, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the Unborn, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Urukrama</s> (of wide strides).' // MAnuv_4,1.11 //
<s>Anasūyā</s> likewise bore from <s>Atri</s> sinless sons —
<s>Datta</s> (Dattātreya), <s>Durvāsas</s>, and <s>Soma</s>, born as the Self (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the Lord (<s>Śiva</s>), and <s>Brahmā</s> [respectively]. // MAnuv_4,1.12 //
Thus in the <s>Bhāgavata</s> as well — therefore the Self is <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: tasmādupāsyo viṣṇuriti jñātavyaḥ sajjanaiḥ sadā // MAnuv_4,1.13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be meditated upon — this should be known by the good always. // MAnuv_4,1.13 //
Thus the saintly ones meditate, and thus they instruct.
And because the word '<s>Ātmā</s>' has the meaning of taking [all unto Himself], it denotes the Lord.
"<s>Viṣṇu</s> is my Lord" — thus one should always worship directly. // MAnuv_4,1.14 //
"My Lord is <s>Viṣṇu</s>" — this meditation, in terms of qualifier and qualified,
must be performed in every way; one should never forget this. // MAnuv_4,1.15 //
Thus [states] the <s>Sattattva</s> (True Reality) text, and the supreme statement of the six-fold [divine] attributes:

children.text: mama svāmī harirnityaṃ sarvasya patireva ca /
children.translated_text: "<s>Hari</s> is my Lord always, and He is the master of all" —

children.text: iti dhyeyaḥ sarvadaiva bhagavān viṣṇuravyayaḥ // MAnuv_4,1.16 //
children.translated_text: thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the imperishable, is always to be meditated upon. // MAnuv_4,1.16 //
The meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s> should not be done with a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) as [its] object;
a symbol is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> — false worship indeed yields no benefit. // MAnuv_4,1.17 //
He who apprehends the Lord of the self, who exists in one way, as being otherwise —

children.text: kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ coreṇātmāpahāriṇā // MAnuv_4,1.18 //
children.translated_text: what sin has not been committed by that thief who steals the Self? // MAnuv_4,1.18 //
He who apprehends the self, which exists in one way, as being otherwise —

children.text: kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ coreṇeśāpahāriṇā // MAnuv_4,1.19 //
children.translated_text: what sin has not been committed by that thief who robs the Lord? // MAnuv_4,1.19 //
He who apprehends <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is established in one way, as being otherwise —

children.text: kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ coreṇa brahmacāriṇā // MAnuv_4,1.20 //
children.translated_text: what sin has not been committed by that thief, though a celibate? // MAnuv_4,1.20 //
Whoever meditates on his own self, or an image, or another deity,
or anything sentient or insentient as being <s>Keśava</s> —

children.text: kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ cāreṇeśāpahāriṇā // MAnuv_4,1.21 //
children.translated_text: what sin has not been committed by that spy who robs the Lord? // MAnuv_4,1.21 //

children.text: yo 'nyad viṣṇuriti dhyāyejjānīyād vā hariṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Whoever meditates on something else as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or knows <s>Hari</s> thus [incorrectly] —

children.text: andhe tamasi majjet sa yatra naivotthitiḥ kvacit // MAnuv_4,1.22 //
children.translated_text: he sinks into blind darkness, from which there is never any rising. // MAnuv_4,1.22 //

children.text: yo 'nyad viṣṇuriti dhyāyed viṣṇuranyaditi sma vā /
children.translated_text: Whoever meditates on something else as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or on <s>Viṣṇu</s> as something else —
by the fault of wrong meditation, he sinks into great darkness. // MAnuv_4,1.23 //

children.text: yo 'nyad viṣṇuriti dhyāyed viṣṇuranyaditi sma vā /
children.translated_text: Whoever meditates on something else as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or on <s>Viṣṇu</s> as something else —

children.text: mahātamasi magnasya tasya naivotthitiḥ kvacit // MAnuv_4,1.24 //
children.translated_text: for one sunk in great darkness, there is never any rising. // MAnuv_4,1.24 //
Whatever thing, existing in one way, is meditated upon directly as being otherwise —
that produces great fault for the meditator; how much more so [when it concerns] <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of all! // MAnuv_4,1.25 //
Whatever thing, existing in one way, is known directly as being otherwise —
[that] produces great fault; how much more so [when it concerns] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of all lords! // MAnuv_4,1.26 //
Whatever thing, existing in one way, is known directly as being otherwise —
[that] is a cause of ruin in the world; how much more so [when it concerns] the Lord of all lords! // MAnuv_4,1.27 //

children.text: na kiñcidanyathā jñeyaṃ dhyeyaṃ vā tena kutracit /
children.translated_text: Nothing should be known or meditated upon as otherwise anywhere;

children.text: kimu sarvottamo viṣṇurjñeyo nīcatayā kvacit // MAnuv_4,1.28 //
children.translated_text: how much less should <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the highest of all, ever be known as inferior! // MAnuv_4,1.28 //

children.text: tasmād vastu yathārūpaṃ jñeyaṃ dhyeyaṃ ca sarvadā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, every reality should always be known and meditated upon according to its true form;

children.text: kāraṇaṃ puruṣārthasya nānyathā bhavati kvacit // MAnuv_4,1.29 //
children.translated_text: [this] is the cause of the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human goal) — it never happens otherwise. // MAnuv_4,1.29 //
Thus, by the force of the statements of scripture and the Purāṇas, a symbol-status
should never be ascribed to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in meditation anywhere, since false knowledge produces ruin. // MAnuv_4,1.30 //

children.text: ityabhipretya na hi sa ityāha bhagavān prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Having intended this, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Lord, said "that is not so" —
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is not to be meditated upon as residing in a symbol, nor otherwise. // MAnuv_4,1.31 //

children.text: brahmeti ca sadā dhyeyo bhagavān viṣṇurañjasā /
children.translated_text: And as <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> should always be meditated upon directly,

children.text: utkṛṣṭo brahmaśabdārthaḥ pūrṇatvaṃ brahmatā yataḥ // MAnuv_4,1.32 //
children.translated_text: since the exalted meaning of the word "<s>Brahman</s>" is fullness — for <s>Brahman</s>-hood is completeness. // MAnuv_4,1.32 //
Even for one whose mind is agitated by physical and mental afflictions,
the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of <s>Viṣṇu</s> should always be meditated upon, with devotion, without interruption —

children.text: iti prakāśikāyāṃ ca vacanaṃ viṣṇuneritam // MAnuv_4,1.33 //
children.translated_text: thus the statement proclaimed by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the <s>Prakāśikā</s>. // MAnuv_4,1.33 //
The <s>sūtra</s> "not the self" is a statement establishing the Lord's [distinction from the] <s>jīva</s>-hood.

children.text: ātmaśabdaṃ yato hetuṃ kṛtvā jīvaṃ nyavārayat /
children.translated_text: Because, having taken the word "self" as the reason, He excluded the <s>jīva</s>;

children.text: svaśabdāt prāṇabhṛccaiva nokta ityeva vedarāṭ // MAnuv_4,1.34 //
children.translated_text: and the breath-bearer is not referred to by its own [individual] word — thus the King of the <s>Vedas</s> [declared]. // MAnuv_4,1.34 //
If the word "self" [applies] to the <s>jīva</s> as well, how could He exclude [the jīva by it]?
Therefore, the word "self" (<s>ātman</s>) denotes <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone and none other. // MAnuv_4,1.35 //
Words such as "<s>ātman</s>" (Self), "<s>Brahman</s>," and the like, without the imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: na vadanti yato nāptā kvāpi tairguṇapūrṇatā /
children.translated_text: do not designate [anything]; for authoritative [speakers] never [attribute] fullness of qualities by those [words] elsewhere.
"Pertaining to the Supreme Self, pertaining to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>" — this is the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> statement. // MAnuv_4,1.36 //
If the lord of the <s>Vedas</s> considers there to be identity of the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord,
how does he logically exclude the word "self" from that [identity]? // MAnuv_4,1.37 //

children.text: bhedasya vyapadeśaṃ ca sthitiṃ cādanameva ca /
children.translated_text: The designation of difference, its persistence, and even its being consumed [by experience] —
the Lord of the world stated [these] as reasons for the firmness of difference, with purposeful intent. // MAnuv_4,1.38 //
If difference is merely empirical (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) — where is there that which is non-empirical?
The very statement "it is empirical" is itself empirical. // MAnuv_4,1.39 //

children.text: uta neti vikalpe tu yadi syād vyāvahārikam /
children.translated_text: Or [is it] not? — in the dilemma: if it were empirical,

children.text: tasyāpi bādhyatā cet syād bhedaḥ syāt pāramārthikaḥ // MAnuv_4,1.40 //
children.translated_text: and if that too were sublatable, then difference would be absolutely real (<s>pāramārthika</s>). // MAnuv_4,1.40 //
If [the statement "it is empirical"] is non-empirical, then this difference has attained the status of truth.
For of two mutually contradictory [things], when one is false,

children.text: anyasya satyataiva syāditi kena nivāryate // MAnuv_4,1.41 //
children.translated_text: the truth of the other necessarily follows — by what can this be prevented? // MAnuv_4,1.41 //
When it is said "the false is not stated," people know [it means] "the true is stated."
And when it is said "the true is not stated," [they know its] falsity as well. // MAnuv_4,1.42 //

children.text: na svapne 'pi dvayaṃ mithyā tatraikaṃ satyameva hi /
children.translated_text: Not even in a dream are both false — for there one is true indeed.

children.text: bhāvābhāvāvubhau tatra kathaṃ mithyā bhaviṣyataḥ // MAnuv_4,1.43 //
children.translated_text: Existence and non-existence — both being there, how could both be false? // MAnuv_4,1.43 //

children.text: bhāvasya hi niṣedhe tu nābhāvasya niṣedhanam /
children.translated_text: For in the negation of existence, there is no negation of non-existence;

children.text: svavāco 'satyatā cet syāt tasmād bhedasya satyatā // MAnuv_4,1.44 //
children.translated_text: and if the falsity of one's own statement [would follow] — therefore, the truth of difference [is established]. // MAnuv_4,1.44 //
Therefore, the difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord is understood by the reasoning stated [above].
From this, the word "self" (<s>ātman</s>) would be a designation of the Supreme Self. // MAnuv_4,1.45 //
The vision of <s>Viṣṇu</s> should not be [applied] with a symbol as its object;

children.text: pratīke viṣṇurityeva tasmāt kāryā hyupāsanā // MAnuv_4,1.46 //
children.translated_text: in the symbol, "this is <s>Viṣṇu</s>" — therefore, worship should be performed thus. // MAnuv_4,1.46 //

children.text: na ca viṣṇuḥ pratīkaṃ yat tasmānnātmetyupāsanā /
children.translated_text: And what is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> is a symbol; therefore, the meditation "not the Self" [applies].
When the position that "the <s>Brahman</s>-vision is opposed here" [is taken],
"that is not so" — the reasoning [applies] there too, and the stated contradiction is resolved. // MAnuv_4,1.47 //
Even if, by mere superiority [of the symbol over other objects], worship [is done] even when it is not that [Brahman],
the self too would have superiority — because of being sentient, [as opposed to] the insentient.
Therefore, what is not real should not be worshipped — this is the view of the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>. // MAnuv_4,1.48 //
If, from meditating on <s>Brahman</s>-hood [of something] through [its] superiority, fruit arises directly,

children.text: brahmaṇo nīcatādhyānādanarthaḥ kiṃ na jāyate // MAnuv_4,1.49 //
children.translated_text: would not ruin arise from meditating on the inferiority of <s>Brahman</s>? // MAnuv_4,1.49 //
In the meditation of an insentient [object] as <s>Brahman</s>, there is never any satisfaction [for Brahman];

children.text: nīcasya svātmatādhyāne kupyati brahma lokavat // MAnuv_4,1.50 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> becomes angry, as a person in the world would, when an inferior [being] is meditated upon as one's own self. // MAnuv_4,1.50 //
If an outcaste is called "king" and the king is called "outcaste" —

children.text: ko viśeṣaḥ parijñāte nṛpeṇa syāt kathañcana // MAnuv_4,1.51 //
children.translated_text: what difference would there be, once recognized by the king, in any way? // MAnuv_4,1.51 //
If in the presence of the king, an outcaste is honored

children.text: rājavat kiṃ na kopaḥ syād rājño loke hi paśyati // MAnuv_4,1.52 //
children.translated_text: as if he were the king — would there not be anger? For the king sees in the world. // MAnuv_4,1.52 //

children.text: rājñastu purataḥ prokte caṇḍālaṃ nṛpa ityapi /
children.translated_text: And if before the king, the outcaste is called "king" —

children.text: ātmānaṃ sa iti proktamitivaddhayeva kupyati // MAnuv_4,1.53 //
children.translated_text: [the king,] as if told "he is yourself," becomes angry in just the same way. // MAnuv_4,1.53 //
In the meditation of non-difference between these two, what distinction is there even in the words?

children.text: ayaṃ rājā tvamityukte caṇḍāle 'tha nṛpe 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: When "this one is the king" is said to an outcaste and also to the king,

children.text: caṇḍāla iti tu prokte samameva hi dūṣaṇam // MAnuv_4,1.54 //
children.translated_text: and when "outcaste" is said — the fault is equal in both cases. // MAnuv_4,1.54 //

children.text: dhyāte tvekasya tadbhāve tadbhāvo 'nyasya kiṃ na tat /
children.translated_text: When the nature of one is meditated upon as being in the other, why not the nature of the other [in the one]?
And this is never unknown to the omniscient <s>Brahman</s> anywhere. // MAnuv_4,1.55 //
Therefore, all speech attributing <s>Brahman</s>-hood to another is improper.
Therefore, <s>Brahman</s> should be worshipped by seekers of liberation through the path as stated [in scripture]. // MAnuv_4,1.56 //

children.text: tathopāsyāñjasā dṛṣṭaṃ brahma pāpaṃ ca bhasmasāt /
children.translated_text: When thus worshipped, <s>Brahman</s>, directly seen, reduces all prior sin to ashes,
and produces non-attachment even to subsequent [sin];
and for one who hates Him, even merit is destroyed and non-attachment [to worldly things lost]. // MAnuv_4,1.57 //
"That which is [performed] with knowledge" — here it is distinguished from what was said earlier.
Earlier, action was enjoined as possessing vigor for the attainment of heaven and the like;

children.text: karma vidyāyutaṃ paścānmokṣe vīryapradaṃ tviti // MAnuv_4,1.58 //
children.translated_text: afterward, action united with knowledge is said to be vigor-giving for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). // MAnuv_4,1.58 //

children.text: tato bhogena puṇyaṃ ca kṣapayitvetarat tathā /
children.translated_text: Then, having exhausted merit through enjoyment and [having exhausted] the other [demerit] likewise,
the hater of <s>Brahman</s> and the seer of <s>Brahman</s> attain darkness and liberation respectively. // MAnuv_4,1.59 //
A hundred periods of <s>Brahmā</s> before [liberation], the exhaustion of <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma) [begins].
The duration of <s>Brahmā</s>'s [karma-exhaustion] is exactly that; for fifty [periods] of <s>Brahmā</s>, and likewise
for <s>Rudra</s>, only twenty; for <s>Indra</s>, the Sun, and others, ten. // MAnuv_4,1.60 //
For others, the exhaustion of commenced karma [begins] at the end of one <s>Brahmā</s>-period only.
Together with <s>Brahmā</s> himself, the exhausted one would go to the Supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> —
thus [states] the <s>Sattattva</s> text, spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself. // MAnuv_4,1.61 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha</s> (<s>Madhva</s>). ||

children.translated_text: For gods and humans, this much is common indeed.

children.text: utkrāntimārgau devānāṃ na prāyeṇa bhaviṣyataḥ // MAnuv_4,2.1 //
children.translated_text: The paths of departure — for the gods, they will generally not apply. // MAnuv_4,2.1 //
The exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, the departure, the path, and the enjoyment — this fourfold [scheme]

children.text: phalaṃ mokṣa iti proktaḥ kramāt pādeṣu coditaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.2 //
children.translated_text: is said to be the fruit, <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — taught sequentially in the [four] <s>pādas</s>. // MAnuv_4,2.2 //

children.text: sraṣṭṛṣveva tu sṛjyānāṃ praveśo brahmaṇo laye /
children.translated_text: The created beings enter their creators, and <s>Brahmā</s> [enters <s>Viṣṇu</s>] at dissolution.
The path of the gods is stated [to be such]; not the path of light (<s>arcirādi</s>), nor departure (<s>utkrama</s>). // MAnuv_4,2.3 //
And for the creator who is absorbed, the body undergoes dissolution there;

children.text: yataḥ sṛjyasya devasya naivotkrāntistato bhavet // MAnuv_4,2.4 //
children.translated_text: since the created god has no departure [from a body]. // MAnuv_4,2.4 //
And since the worlds of light (<s>arcirādi</s>) and all others undergo dissolution,

children.text: kathaṃ mārgo bhavet teṣāṃ viśatāmuttamaṃ svataḥ // MAnuv_4,2.5 //
children.translated_text: how would there be a path for those who enter the Supreme by their own nature? // MAnuv_4,2.5 //

children.text: jātānāṃ mānuṣe loke devānāṃ ca kadācana /
children.translated_text: For the gods who are sometimes born in the human world,

children.text: utkrāntimārgau bhavato na tadā muktiriṣyate // MAnuv_4,2.6 //
children.translated_text: the departure and the path do exist — but liberation is not considered [to occur] then. // MAnuv_4,2.6 //

children.text: anyeṣāmapi sākṣāttu muktiḥ prāpyāpi taṃ harim /
children.translated_text: For others too, liberation, even though they have directly attained <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: sahaiva brahmaṇā bhūyāditi śāstrasya nirṇayaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.7 //
children.translated_text: would be together with <s>Brahmā</s> alone — this is the determination of the scripture. // MAnuv_4,2.7 //
"Enveloped by earth, water, fire, wind, space, mind, senses, sense-objects, elements, and the like,

children.text: avyākṛtaṃ viśati yarhi guṇatrayātmā kālaṃ paraṃ svamanubhūya paraḥ svayambhūḥ // MAnuv_4,2.8 //
children.translated_text: when the self-born one (<s>Brahmā</s>), who is of the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s>, desiring to re-absorb, enters the unmanifest, having experienced the supreme time" — // MAnuv_4,2.8 //

children.text: evaṃ paretya bhagavantamanupraviṣṭā ye yogino jitamarunmanaso virāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Thus, having departed, the <s>yogins</s> who have entered the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who have conquered breath and mind, who are dispassionate,

children.text: tenaiva sākamamṛtaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ brahma pradhānamupayāntyagatābhimānāḥ // MAnuv_4,2.9 //
children.translated_text: together with Him, approach the immortal, ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, the primordial — free from ego." // MAnuv_4,2.9 //
Having attained the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>yogins</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s>,
go to supreme liberation through the breaking of the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>). // MAnuv_4,2.10 //

children.text: prāptā api paraṃ devaṃ sahaiva brahmaṇā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having attained the Supreme God, together with <s>Brahmā</s> once again,
they go to the full manifestation of bliss through the destruction of the subtle body. // MAnuv_4,2.11 //
Thus, from the force of the statements of scripture and Purāṇas, this is understood.

children.text: bhogastu sarvadevānāṃ narādīnāṃ ca vidyate // MAnuv_4,2.12 //
children.translated_text: But enjoyment [of the fruits of action] exists for all gods and for humans and others. // MAnuv_4,2.12 //
Therein, the entry of the gods [into their creators] is stated progressively, from higher to higher;

children.text: ucyate dehagānāṃ ca vṛttīnāmevameva tu // MAnuv_4,2.13 //
children.translated_text: and of the embodied ones and their faculties — likewise indeed. // MAnuv_4,2.13 //
Regarding the nature of liberation there, the disputants, relying on [mere] fancy,

children.text: nānā vadanti puṃsāṃ hi matayo guṇabhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: speak variously; for the views of people arise separately
according to the differences in [their] <s>guṇas</s> (qualities); wrong understanding is from <s>tamas</s> (darkness) alone. // MAnuv_4,2.14 //
Mixed understanding is from <s>rajas</s> (passion); through <s>sattva</s> (goodness) alone, understanding is right.
The understanding of the liberated, being beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, is pure consciousness, since // MAnuv_4,2.15 //
in equilibrium and also eternal, and through the yoga of the respective greatness [of each liberated soul],

children.text: bahaḷā cātiviśadā spaṣṭā caiva śriyo matiḥ // MAnuv_4,2.16 //
children.translated_text: the understanding of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is abundant, exceedingly clear, and distinct. // MAnuv_4,2.16 //
By being of the nature of great pure consciousness, [the understanding of <s>Brahmā</s>] is even greater pure consciousness than that;
by the extreme clarity of all the vast distinctions,
the understanding of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is supreme — always of one mode, the highest. // MAnuv_4,2.17 //
Like the radiance of the sun, illuminating everything, uninterruptedly —
unattached, free from defects, and eternally unchanging. // MAnuv_4,2.18 //
Having abandoned the portions and the distinctions (<s>viśeṣas</s>) that belong to Her, for the most part, the characteristics of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) [are described].
Just so, because of the absence of explicitness and because [She is] entirely dependent on that [Brahman],

children.text: na tādṛśī brahmaṇastu prāya eva śriyo yathā // MAnuv_4,2.19 //
children.translated_text: [Her nature] is not exactly like <s>Brahman's</s>, but for the most part like <s>Śrī's</s> [own description]. // MAnuv_4,2.19 //
But for the other liberated [souls], other than Her, [their vision] is like the waves of the ocean;

children.text: agnijvālāvadeva syāt smṛtigānāṃ dṛśo bhavaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.20 //
children.translated_text: [or] it would be like the flames of a fire. The arising of the vision of those spoken of in <s>Smṛti</s> [is such]. // MAnuv_4,2.20 //
In such [gradations of] knowledge, those whose sight is robbed by <s>tamas</s> (darkness),
having extremely little knowledge like a firefly, seeing otherwise,
disputants declare [various views on] liberation, taking shelter in various doctrines. // MAnuv_4,2.21 //
Taking recourse to an exceedingly <s>tāmasic</s> (dark) intuition, the <s>Jina</s> says:
'Liberation occurs from the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> through knowledge, from the cage called the body. // MAnuv_4,2.22 //
Like a bird released from a cage, [the soul] goes to the realm of space,
always moving upward — the <s>pudgala</s> (person), possessing hands and feet.' // MAnuv_4,2.23 //

children.text: iti tat kena mānena mokṣarūpaṃ pradṛśyate /
children.translated_text: By what valid means of knowledge is such a form of liberation demonstrated?
And upward movement would be suffering, because of being movement — like worldly [movement].
When this is stated, what answer has one whose sole refuge is inference? // MAnuv_4,2.24 //
If the non-upward-movement there [in ordinary cases] is the distinguishing condition (<s>upādhi</s>) for the bird too,

children.text: dūrordhvagamane duḥkhamiti sādhyānugo na saḥ // MAnuv_4,2.25 //
children.translated_text: 'in far upward movement there is suffering' — that [reason] follows the thesis (<s>sādhya</s>), not the [opposing] reason. // MAnuv_4,2.25 //
There is no refutation of a counter-inference that has the form of a counter-proof.

children.text: upādhiḥ pratirūpaṃ hi sādhanaṃ tannacāparam // MAnuv_4,2.26 //
children.translated_text: For a counter-proof is indeed a counter-form of proof — and not [anything] else. // MAnuv_4,2.26 //
Moreover, 'having a body' — that too would not be the distinguishing condition (<s>upādhi</s>) here.

children.text: gatitvaṃ yatra dehitvamiti yat sādhanānugam // MAnuv_4,2.27 //
children.translated_text: 'Where there is movement, there is embodiment' — that [reason] follows the thesis. // MAnuv_4,2.27 //
Because of not following scripture, this objection [applies]; therefore,

children.text: nāpasiddhāntatā doṣaḥ prasaṅge yadi sā bhavet /
children.translated_text: the fault of the opponent's own thesis being unestablished is not a defect in a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio). If that [fault] did apply [in reductio],

children.text: tadaivātiprasaṅgaḥ syānna pasaṅgaḥ kvacid bhavet // MAnuv_4,2.28 //
children.translated_text: then it would itself be an excessive extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>); no reductio would be possible anywhere. // MAnuv_4,2.28 //
If 'movement in worldly space' is the distinguishing condition — [that too] follows the thesis.

children.text: so 'pītyukte vadet kiṃ sa tasmād vedodito bhavet // MAnuv_4,2.29 //
children.translated_text: When even that [is said], what would he reply? Therefore, [liberation] should be as declared by the <s>Vedas</s>. // MAnuv_4,2.29 //
Liberation is thus [as established]. <s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself, although the omniscient Lord,

children.text: cakāra saugatamataṃ mohāyaiva cakāra yat // MAnuv_4,2.30 //
children.translated_text: composed the Buddhist doctrine — [and] He composed it precisely for the delusion [of the unworthy]. // MAnuv_4,2.30 //
Of the <s>Asuras</s> who are unfit, [lest they] engage in the Vedic path.
Therefore, because it is intended for <s>Asuras</s>, that doctrine should never be accepted. // MAnuv_4,2.31 //
And that [Buddhist doctrine] is declared to be fourfold: emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>), consciousness-only (<s>vijñāna</s>) alone,
external reality inferable [from consciousness], and external reality directly perceived. // MAnuv_4,2.32 //

children.text: iti tatra tu ye śūnyaṃ vadantyajñānamohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, those who, deluded by ignorance, declare emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>) —

children.text: te mokṣaṃ tādṛśaṃ brūyurniśśaṅkaṃ māyino yathā // MAnuv_4,2.33 //
children.translated_text: they would declare such a liberation without hesitation, like the <s>Māyāvādins</s> (illusionists). // MAnuv_4,2.33 //
In the state of liberation, there is nothing — neither the self nor what belongs to the self.
When a single [being] is liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>, nothing whatsoever remains. // MAnuv_4,2.34 //
This difference, consisting of the conscious and the unconscious, is through <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional reality) alone.
Upon the destruction of <s>saṃvṛti</s>, there is only undifferentiated emptiness. // MAnuv_4,2.35 //

children.text: na sattvaṃ naiva cāsattvaṃ śūnyatattvasya vidyate /
children.translated_text: Emptiness-as-reality has neither existence nor non-existence,

children.text: na sukhatvaṃ na duḥkhatvaṃ na viśeṣo 'pi kaścana // MAnuv_4,2.36 //
children.translated_text: neither pleasure nor suffering, nor any distinction whatsoever. // MAnuv_4,2.36 //
Undifferentiated, self-arisen, unattached, ageless, immortal,
empty, reality without obstruction, free from manifold <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional overlay), // MAnuv_4,2.37 //
free from all defects, beyond the reach of mind and speech —
this is called 'liberation' by the [so-called] 'wise,' [though it is] tainted by manifold <s>saṃvṛti</s>. // MAnuv_4,2.38 //
The state of <s>saṃsāra</s> is to be understood as being characterized by <s>saṃvṛti</s> alone.

children.text: sthitayā dhvastayā caiva saṃsṛtirmokṣa ityapi // MAnuv_4,2.39 //
children.translated_text: When [<s>saṃvṛti</s>] persists, [that is] <s>saṃsāra</s>; when destroyed, [that is] 'liberation' — thus [they say]. // MAnuv_4,2.39 //
Some among them state otherwise: through <s>saṃvṛti</s> alone, in many ways,
the great emptiness is delimited, spoken of as manifold '<s>pudgalas</s>' (persons). // MAnuv_4,2.40 //
He whose single-flavored emptiness — through knowledge, that [perception of manifoldness] departs —
he, freed from person-hood, will attain the great emptiness. // MAnuv_4,2.41 //
Another, delimited by <s>saṃvṛti</s>, fully experiences sufferings.
Thus the illusionists (<s>Māyāvādins</s>) speak — the proponents of a single <s>jīva</s>. // MAnuv_4,2.42 //
Those holding the doctrine of many <s>jīvas</s> also [say so]; and for them, <s>māyā</s> is <s>saṃvṛti</s>.

children.text: nirviśeṣatvavācaiva śūnyaṃ brahmaiva no bhidā // MAnuv_4,2.43 //
children.translated_text: Through the expression of 'absence of distinction' alone, emptiness is <s>Brahman</s> itself; [they say] there is no difference. // MAnuv_4,2.43 //
Existence, consciousness, bliss, and the like — what, and from where? — [ask] the proponents of the 'partless' (<s>akhaṇḍa</s>).
There is merely a difference in what is excluded — that exists [between them and] the emptiness-proponent. // MAnuv_4,2.44 //
The exclusion of untruth and the like — he himself indeed accepts [that].
Because of the absence of distinctions, there is simply no distinction between <s>Brahman</s> and emptiness. // MAnuv_4,2.45 //

children.text: prāmāṇyādi ca vedasya phalataḥ samameva hi /
children.translated_text: And the validity and the like of the <s>Vedas</s> — in terms of result, it is exactly the same.
Since it does not reveal the [ultimate] reality, the means of knowledge is called [valid only] in that [conventional sense].
Non-revelation of reality — that is what the good consider to be invalidity. // MAnuv_4,2.46 //
If a cognition producing long delusion were a valid means [simply because it] does not reveal reality,
then even compared to the rope-snake cognition, because of its excess [of delusion], there would be invalidity;
it would be [so] because of scripture's being a producer of great, irremovable delusion. // MAnuv_4,2.47 //
The cognition of blueness and the like in the sky would attain validity,
the cognition of the umbrella-shape [of the sky] and the cognition that the moon is a span wide [too]. // MAnuv_4,2.48 //
But the non-differentiated nature of emptiness is always accepted even by that [Advaitin].
The absence of properties such as existence, non-existence, and the like is the view of both [Śūnyavādin and Māyāvādin]. // MAnuv_4,2.49 //

children.text: na hi satpratiyogitvaṃ śūnyatvaṃ tena ceṣyate /
children.translated_text: For he does not accept that emptiness is [merely] the counter-positive of existence.
Nor is any bliss other than [mere] opposition to suffering accepted [by him]. // MAnuv_4,2.50 //
For the <s>Māyāvādin</s> too, in the emptiness position, knowledge is contradictory to inertness.

children.text: dharmaste 'pi na santyeva ko viśeṣastatastayoḥ // MAnuv_4,2.51 //
children.translated_text: Those properties too do not really exist [for him] — so what distinction is there between the two? // MAnuv_4,2.51 //
The refutation of such positions has been accomplished by the Master [<s>Vyāsa</s>]
through the establishment of his own position alone. And [it is said] that absence [of self] is not [the case]. // MAnuv_4,2.52 //
If the self is absent, what human goal [could there be]? — since the desired [goal] has the self as its limit.
If liberation is not limited by the self, then liberation would be 'the emptiness of a pot' [i.e., mere absence].

children.text: kalpitatvād viśeṣāṇāṃ māyino 'pi samaṃ hi tat // MAnuv_4,2.53 //
children.translated_text: Because of the fictitious nature of distinctions — for the <s>Māyāvādin</s> too, that is equally [problematic]. // MAnuv_4,2.53 //
If, even when distinctions are seen, there is non-distinction —
then the absence of a pot would be non-distinction. If [you say] it is future and not yet come — // MAnuv_4,2.54 //
'liberation is not the disputed [point], since the absence of a pot is bodiless' — just as [absurd].

children.text: yathetyukte vadet kiṃ sa yo 'numāmātramānakaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.55 //
children.translated_text: When this is stated, what would he say — he whose sole valid means is inference? // MAnuv_4,2.55 //

children.text: na ca māyī vadet tatra pūrvoktenaiva vartmanā /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Māyāvādin</s> would not speak there [in defense], by the very path stated earlier.
Because of the invalidity of scripture for him; and scripture does not teach bodilessness. // MAnuv_4,2.56 //
Whatever scripture [speaks of] bodilessness — [it refers to] the non-material body (<s>aprākṛtaśarīra</s>).

children.text: mokṣe bhogaṃ yato brūte jakṣan krīḍanniti śrutiḥ // MAnuv_4,2.57 //
children.translated_text: Since [scripture] declares enjoyment in liberation: 'eating, playing' — thus the <s>Śruti</s>. // MAnuv_4,2.57 //
'That is not [the nature of] liberation because of freedom from suffering' — [this,] as agreed upon — and

children.text: anumādūṣaṇaṃ kiṃ syād vādinoḥ śūnyamāyinoḥ // MAnuv_4,2.58 //
children.translated_text: what refutation of the inference could there be by the two disputants, the Śūnyavādin and the Māyāvādin? // MAnuv_4,2.58 //
Because suffering is non-different from suffering, liberation too would be [suffering] — without doubt.
If [there is] difference, there would be duality itself. Because of such and limitless defects,

children.text: heyaṃ māyāmatenaiva saha śūnyamataṃ budhaiḥ // MAnuv_4,2.59 //
children.translated_text: the emptiness doctrine should be rejected by the wise, along with the <s>Māyā</s>-doctrine itself. // MAnuv_4,2.59 //
Thus the <s>Vijñānavāda</s> (consciousness-only doctrine) too, [being distinguished] merely by the particular of knowledge —
if one removes its particular of momentariness and the like,
it directly becomes the non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) doctrine; therefore, the stated defects [apply to it too]. // MAnuv_4,2.60 //
Time is not a bare knower — because of being time, like the [time] agreed upon.
By this inference, because of the obstruction — that form of liberation is not [valid]. // MAnuv_4,2.61 //

children.text: yadi kālo 'pi netyāha kadeti praśna uttaram /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'time also is not [real]' — to the question 'when?', what answer

children.text: kiṃ vakṣyati yadāvasthāṃ vadet sā pakṣatāṃ vrajet // MAnuv_4,2.62 //
children.translated_text: will he give? If he states a state [of affairs], that would [itself] become a position [implying time]. // MAnuv_4,2.62 //

children.text: avasthātvāditi hyeva hetuḥ sāpi kadeti ca /
children.translated_text: 'Because of being a state' — this very [thing] is the reason. And to [the question] 'when?' for that too,

children.text: pṛṣṭe kālaśca vaktavyo nākālatvaṃ tato bhavet // MAnuv_4,2.63 //
children.translated_text: time must be stated; non-temporality does not follow from that. // MAnuv_4,2.63 //
In the general negation 'not time,' the valid cognition of time-ness

children.text: niruṇaddhi vaktavyo nākālatvaṃ tato bhavet // MAnuv_4,2.64 //
children.translated_text: obstructs. Time must be stated; non-temporality does not follow from that. // MAnuv_4,2.64 //
In the position of a single <s>jīva</s>, this valid cognition, [arising] from the absence of time,
being provoked, would, taking time [as evidence], establish duality itself. // MAnuv_4,2.65 //
'Time, which is the disputed [point], involves manifoldness — because of being time, like the time agreed upon' —
thus another inference would also preclude the oneness of the <s>jīva</s>. // MAnuv_4,2.66 //
The doctrines of the identity of time, word, and God [with Brahman] are likewise

children.text: nirākṛtāni teṣāṃ ca samatvāt pakṣadoṣayoḥ // MAnuv_4,2.67 //
children.translated_text: refuted, because of the equality of their positions and defects. // MAnuv_4,2.67 //
Knowledge, being inherently momentary, is accepted as an eternal continuum [by the Buddhists].
But against the other two Buddhists [Sautrāntika and Vaibhāṣika] too, the stated inference is an adversary. // MAnuv_4,2.68 //
Liberation is not a continuum of pure consciousness — because of being temporal.
Like the agreed-upon [example] — this inference is the reply to that [position]. // MAnuv_4,2.69 //
All inferences [of opponents] are refuted through the method of counter-proof,
by the stated [mode of] refutation alone; and the <s>Śrutis</s> support our statement. // MAnuv_4,2.70 //
The <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, and others declare liberation to be devoid of pleasure,
[involving] the complete dissolution of desire, aversion, effort, and the like. // MAnuv_4,2.71 //
Therein [we] say: this too is not proper here, since the <s>Śrutis</s>

children.text: mahānandaṃ ca bhogaṃ ca niyamena vadanti hi // MAnuv_4,2.72 //
children.translated_text: invariably declare great bliss and enjoyment [in liberation]. // MAnuv_4,2.72 //
The loss of material (<s>prākṛta</s>) pleasure, however, is termed 'non-contact with pleasure.'
That which is unpleasant and adverse — that is referred to without distinction [by the term 'suffering']. // MAnuv_4,2.73 //

children.text: nāsti hyaprākṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ sato jīvasya kutracit /
children.translated_text: For there is no non-material suffering anywhere for the existing <s>jīva</s>.
Pleasure is its very nature — from statements such as 'power, bliss' and the like. // MAnuv_4,2.74 //
Because only the unpleasant is to be rejected, and because the loss of pleasure is undesirable,

children.text: na samastapriyābhāvo mokṣe prokte tu yujyate // MAnuv_4,2.75 //
children.translated_text: the complete absence of all pleasure in the declared liberation is not fitting. // MAnuv_4,2.75 //
The natural state of unpleasantness is heard [to apply] to the <s>Asuras</s> alone.
'The <s>Asuras</s> are not thus, and not thus' — and 'all humans are not thus either.'

children.text: ityātmapriyahānāya ko yateta ca buddhimān // MAnuv_4,2.76 //
children.translated_text: So what wise person would strive for the destruction of his own pleasure? // MAnuv_4,2.76 //
'There is no cognition' — and yet, 'it is not that the liberated one is not to be known.'
For the subsequent <s>Śruti</s> is about to declare the non-destruction of his properties. // MAnuv_4,2.77 //
Apprehending the destruction of his knowledge, when <s>Maitreyī</s> said to Him,

children.text: bhavānityuktavatyā hi nāhaṃ mohaṃ vadāmi te /
children.translated_text: 'You are bringing me delusion, O lord' —
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> indeed, having said 'I am not declaring delusion to you,' declared the non-destruction of [the soul's] essential nature. // MAnuv_4,2.78 //
That the destruction of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) would be the destruction of one whose nature is knowledge —
for the purpose of destroying the emptiness doctrine, again, [beginning] with bliss,
He declared the properties as non-destroyed — refuting [the views] held by the logicians.
The <s>Mādhyandina Śruti</s> also declares [the soul's] contact with [transcendent] measures. // MAnuv_4,2.79 //

children.text: ācikṣepa mataṃ tacca yasmin na viṣayādanam /
children.translated_text: And it criticized that doctrine according to which there is no enjoyment of objects.
The <s>Śruti</s>, with the intention of showing the undesirability of the absence of enjoyment through smell and the like — // MAnuv_4,2.80 //
'By which one knows all this — [and] the knower himself —

children.text: kena taṃ ca vijānīyādityaniṣṭaṃ hi sarvathā // MAnuv_4,2.81 //
children.translated_text: by what could one know Him?' — thus [the absence of all cognition] is thoroughly undesirable. // MAnuv_4,2.81 //
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the revealer of all, is certainly not unknowable.
For the purpose of knowing Him is the operation of all the <s>Vedas</s>. // MAnuv_4,2.82 //
Because of the non-contradiction with perception, scripture, self-knowledge, and experience,

children.text: na svavijñānitāyāṃ ca virodhaḥ kaścaneyate // MAnuv_4,2.83 //
children.translated_text: and no contradiction whatsoever is understood regarding [God's] being known by Himself. // MAnuv_4,2.83 //
The contradiction of agent and object [being the same] — because of the contradiction with eternal experience,

children.text: kathameva padaṃ gacched virodho dṛṣṭabādhanam // MAnuv_4,2.84 //
children.translated_text: how could [that contradiction] even gain a foothold? The [supposed] contradiction is sublated by what is seen. // MAnuv_4,2.84 //
'He enjoys all desires' and 'having desires as food, having desires as form' —
such <s>Śrutis</s> declare the stated meaning indeed. // MAnuv_4,2.85 //
'Because of non-independence' and the like — [this] has been stated; not because of the absence of duality anywhere.
'He became the self alone' — because of the absurd consequence of non-distinction from this [statement]. // MAnuv_4,2.86 //
'Non-independence, comparison, non-difference' — [these] are stated in [the context of] differences as well.

children.text: śabdatattva iti proktaṃ maitreyyuktottaraṃ ca kim // MAnuv_4,2.87 //
children.translated_text: What is stated as the reality of sound — and what is the reply to <s>Maitreyī's</s> [question]? // MAnuv_4,2.87 //
If qualities such as bliss and the rest are lost, what then is the purpose of liberation? /
If the goal is the removal of suffering, the destruction of bliss would be a non-goal // 4.2.88 //
And of the two, the destruction of bliss from the removal of suffering would be greater; /
a person strives to attain even a small measure of bliss even by incurring great suffering; /

children.text: yatate sukhahānau hi ko mokṣāya yatet pumān // MAnuv_4,2.89 //
children.translated_text: but in the destruction of bliss, what person would strive for liberation? // 4.2.89 //
A person fears exceedingly even the small destruction of bliss; /
and incurs even great suffering for the prevention of the destruction of bliss // 4.2.90 //

children.text: na ca rāganimittaṃ tad vītarāgā api sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: And this is not caused by attachment, for even those who are clearly free from attachment — /
<s>Nārada</s> and the others — bear suffering directly for the sake of bliss; /
since they undertake even with great suffering the viewing of battles and the like // 4.2.91 //
When <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s> were greatly tormented by the <s>brahmāstras</s>, /
even then <s>Nārada</s> and the others did not abandon [the scene] out of delight in battle — /

children.text: iti skāndavacastasmāt sukhābhāvasya ko yatet // MAnuv_4,2.92 //
children.translated_text: thus is the statement of the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>; therefore, who would strive for the absence of bliss? // 4.2.92 //
The conscious being, when devoid of bliss, is conjoined with suffering because of the dispute; /

children.text: pratipanno yathetyeva cānumā kena vāryate // MAnuv_4,2.93 //
children.translated_text: as it is thus understood — by what [authority] is this inference prevented? // 4.2.93 //
Since in all <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> there is the statement of the existence of bliss /

children.text: muktau na grāhyamevaitat sukhābhāvamataṃ budhaiḥ // MAnuv_4,2.94 //
children.translated_text: in liberation — the doctrine of the absence of bliss in liberation should not be accepted by the wise // 4.2.94 //
'He, being liberated from non-bliss, clearly becomes blissful'; /

children.text: nirguṇe brahmaṇi mayi dhārayan viśadaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Fixing the mind clearly on Me, the attributeless <s>Brahman</s>, /
he attains supreme bliss, where desire is fulfilled' // 4.2.95 //

children.text: na viṣṇusadṛśaṃ daivaṃ na mokṣasadṛśaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: 'There is no deity equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, no bliss equal to liberation, /

children.text: na vedasadṛśaṃ vākyaṃ na varṇo 'kārasammitaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.96 //
children.translated_text: no statement equal to the <s>Veda</s>, no syllable equal to the letter A' // 4.2.96 //
'Where joys, delights, pleasures, and great pleasures abide — /

children.text: kāmasya yatrāptāḥ kāmāstatra māmamṛtaṃ kṛdhi // MAnuv_4,2.97 //
children.translated_text: where the desires of desire are fulfilled — make me immortal there' // 4.2.97 //
— thus <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> declare in various places; /

children.text: ato mokṣe sukhābhāva iti yatkiñcideva hi // MAnuv_4,2.98 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the [claim of] absence of bliss in liberation is of no consequence // 4.2.98 //
And the absence of head, hands, and the rest does not pertain to the liberated one anywhere; /

children.text: śrutayaśca purāṇāni mānamatra bahūni ca // MAnuv_4,2.99 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> are many valid authorities here // 4.2.99 //

children.text: na vartate yatra rajastamastayoḥ sattvaṃ ca miśraṃ na ca kālavikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where neither <s>rajas</s> nor <s>tamas</s> exist, nor <s>sattva</s> in admixture, nor the vicissitude of time; /

children.text: na yatra māyā kimutāpare hareranuvratā yatra surāsurārcitāḥ // MAnuv_4,2.100 //
children.translated_text: where there is no <s>māyā</s> — what to speak of anything else of <s>Hari</s>'s? — where those devoted to Him, worshipped by <s>suras</s> and <s>asuras</s> // 4.2.100 //
dark-complexioned and fair, lotus-eyed, wearing tawny garments, of beautiful radiance, of beautiful form, /
all four-armed, adorned with shining jewels, <s>niṣka</s> ornaments, and gems, of splendid appearance // 4.2.101 //
amid those great souls whose luster is like coral, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and lotus-stalks, /
with earrings, crowns, and garlands flashing — He shines all around, surrounded by rows of brilliant aerial chariots // 4.2.102 //
with the most excellent women shining radiantly, like the sky with rows of lightning-bearing clouds — /

children.text: śrīryatra rūpiṇyurugāyapādayoḥ karoti mānaṃ bahudhā vibhūtibhiḥ // MAnuv_4,2.103 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) there, in embodied form, at the feet of the widely-praised [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], performs worship in many ways with [her] powers' // 4.2.103 //

children.text: ṛcāṃ tvaḥ poṣamāste pupuṣvān gāyatraṃ tvo gāyati śakvarīṣu /
children.translated_text: 'He who abides nourishing the <s>Ṛks</s>, who has nourished [them]; who sings the <s>Gāyatra</s> among the <s>Śakvarī</s> meters; /

children.text: brahmā tvo vadati jātavidyāṃ yajñasya mātraṃ vimibhīta u tvaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.104 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> who speaks the born-knowledge for you; who has measured out the measure of the sacrifice for you' // 4.2.104 //
'Desiring, he moves about in a form consisting of food' — by such prior <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Purāṇic</s> statements too, there is no fault; /

children.text: dehaḥ svarūpātmaka eva teṣāṃ muktiṃ gatānāmapi ceyate hi // MAnuv_4,2.105 //
children.translated_text: the body is of the nature of their own-form — this is accepted even for those who have attained liberation // 4.2.105 //

children.text: śiraḥkarādyairapi muktibhājo yuktā yataste puruṣā idānīm /
children.translated_text: The persons who enjoy liberation are indeed endowed with head, hands, and the rest now; /
the inferences beginning with 'as it is' prove that the own-form of the <s>jīva</s> is endowed with limbs and the rest // 4.2.106 //

children.text: na brahmarūpatvamamuṣya dehino muktāvapi syāt pramayā kathañcit /
children.translated_text: This embodied one does not attain <s>Brahman</s>-form even in liberation, by any valid authority; /

children.text: sa brahmaṇā sahito 'śeṣabhogān bhuṅkte tathopetya sukhārṇavaṃ tam // MAnuv_4,2.107 //
children.translated_text: 'He, united with <s>Brahman</s>, enjoys all enjoyments'; and thus, 'having approached that ocean of bliss' // 4.2.107 //

children.text: yattat paraṃ jyotirupetya jīvo nijasvarapūtvamavāpya kāmān /
children.translated_text: 'Having approached that supreme light, the <s>jīva</s>, attaining its own form, [fulfills its] desires; /

children.text: bhuṅkte sa daivaṃ puruṣottamo 'ja ātmeti cokto guṇapūrtihetoḥ // MAnuv_4,2.108 //
children.translated_text: he experiences that divine [bliss]' — <s>Puruṣottama</s>, the unborn; and He is called '<s>Ātman</s>' because of being the cause of the fullness of qualities // 4.2.108 //
'He is the bridge, the <s>deva</s>, of all who share in liberation'; 'the Lord of immortality here' — /

children.text: ityādivākyairbhagavadvaśaḥ san bhuṅkte'khilān muktigato 'pi bhogān // MAnuv_4,2.109 //
children.translated_text: by such statements, being under the Lord's control, one who has attained liberation also enjoys all enjoyments // 4.2.109 //

children.text: kālo 'pyasau naikyayutaḥ pareṇa jīvasya kālo yata eṣa yadvat /
children.translated_text: Time too is not in unity with the Supreme; since this [time] is the time of the <s>jīva</s>, just as — /

children.text: ityādikā apyanumāḥ pramāṇaṃ muktau ca jīvasya paratvarodhe // MAnuv_4,2.110 //
children.translated_text: such inferences too are valid authorities, [establishing] the prevention of the supreme-hood of the <s>jīva</s> even in liberation // 4.2.110 //

children.text: kathaṃ ca yaḥ pūrvamasau na paścād bhavet sa evetyapi yuktimeti /
children.translated_text: And how can one who did not exist before come to exist afterwards — this too stands to reason; /

children.text: yato na dṛṣṭaṃ yadabhūnna pūrvaṃ paścāt tadāseti kutaśca kiñcit // MAnuv_4,2.111 //
children.translated_text: since nowhere is it seen that what did not exist before comes to exist afterwards // 4.2.111 //

children.text: nacaiva muktau tu hareḥ pṛthaktavamaikyaṃ tathā syāditi yuktimeti /
children.translated_text: And separateness from <s>Hari</s> in liberation, as well as unity, is not possible — this stands to reason; /

children.text: yato na kutrāpi bhidābhidā ca dṛṣṭā citaścetanayā kutaścit // MAnuv_4,2.112 //
children.translated_text: since nowhere is difference and non-difference of consciousness with consciousness seen from any [source] // 4.2.112 //

children.text: itthaṃ matāni bhramajāni yasmānmokṣaṃ samuddeśyamapi bhrameṇa /
children.translated_text: Thus, since these doctrines are born of error, even liberation, the [supposed] goal, /

children.text: vidurna samyag yadapīha laukikāḥ sukhaṃ mama syācca sadeti jānate // MAnuv_4,2.113 //
children.translated_text: they do not know properly through error — although even worldly people know 'may there be bliss for me, always' // 4.2.113 //
Generosity, varied powers, firmness of own-form, one's own nature, /
independence, fitness for complete distinction, and removal of contradiction — in the fourth <s>pāda</s> // 4.2.114 //
establishment, non-distinction, stability, and prohibition of general prescribed actions, /
distinctness, and achievement through haste alone — these are the arguments against the opponent's position, with contrary reasons // 4.2.115 //
easy capability, perpetual well-known-ness, discrimination, arrangement, deliberation, designation — /

children.text: nānāpravṛttiḥ kṛtakṛtyatā ca vipakṣatarkāḥ samatītapāde // MAnuv_4,2.116 //
children.translated_text: diverse activity, state of having accomplished one's purpose — these are the opponent's arguments in the past <s>pāda</s> // 4.2.116 //
great-fruitfulness, discrimination, connection-grasping, means, accomplished action, /

children.text: viśeṣakāryaṃ kṛtisaṃsthitiśca suyuktayo nirṇayagāḥ svapakṣe // MAnuv_4,2.117 //
children.translated_text: specific effect, establishment of action — these are the well-fitting arguments for one's own position // 4.2.117 //
intermixture, being the cause of effect, construction of meaning, firm establishment, dependence, /

children.text: samānadharmaḥ kṛtaśeṣatā ca lokopamā pūrvamatānusārāḥ // MAnuv_4,2.118 //
children.translated_text: common property, having a remaining [task], worldly analogy — these follow the prior doctrines // 4.2.118 //
specific equality, <s>Śruti</s>, affluence, common loss, greatness, distinction, /
having accomplished one's purpose, perpetual activity — these are the distinguished arguments determining the <s>siddhānta</s> // 4.2.119 //
The chief <s>Vāyu</s> here — by the name <s>Vāyu</s> — even though stated among the elements, by reasoning, /

children.text: yasmācchrutau pavate ceti bhūri prokto yato bhūtamānī ca so 'pi /
children.translated_text: since in <s>Śruti</s> he is abundantly stated as 'he purifies' (<s>pavate</s>), and since he is the presiding deity of elements, he too; /

children.text: mahāmānī tvalpamānī ca yasmāt tacchabdenāpyucyate tena so 'pi // MAnuv_4,2.120 //
children.translated_text: since [he is] a great presiding deity, but a lesser presiding deity [relative to <s>Viṣṇu</s>] — by that very word he too is spoken of // 4.2.120 //

children.text: tasmin layaṃ yānti bhūtānyaśeṣakramāvirodhena sa eva viṣṇau /
children.translated_text: In him all elements dissolve in sequence without contradiction; he in turn [dissolves] in <s>Viṣṇu</s>; /

children.text: indrādīnāṃ tatra layaḥ kramaṃ tu proktaṃ viśeṣādanusṛtya nānyat // MAnuv_4,2.121 //
children.translated_text: the dissolution of <s>Indra</s> and others there follows a stated sequence from their distinctions — not otherwise // 4.2.121 //

children.text: tasmādaśeṣā girijāṃ praviśya tayaiva rudraṃ saha tena vāṇīm /
children.translated_text: Therefore, all [beings], having entered <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), and through her <s>Rudra</s>, and with him <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>), /

children.text: tayā patiṃ prāpya sahaiva tena layaṃ harau yānti samastajīvāḥ // MAnuv_4,2.122 //
children.translated_text: and through her the Lord [<s>Brahmā</s>], and together with him — all <s>jīvas</s> dissolve in <s>Hari</s> // 4.2.122 //

children.text: somastu vārīśayuto 'niruddhaṃ viśatyasau kāmamasau ca vāruṇīm /
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s>, joined with the lord of waters, enters <s>Aniruddha</s>; he [enters] <s>Kāma</s> (<s>Pradyumna</s>); and he [enters] <s>Vāruṇī</s>; /

children.text: sā śeṣadevaṃ sa giraṃ ca saiva vāyuṃ viśatyañja itīha nirṇayaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.123 //
children.translated_text: she [enters] the <s>Śeṣa</s>-lord (<s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>); he [enters] <s>Girā</s> (Speech); and she in turn enters <s>Vāyu</s> directly — such is the determination here // 4.2.123 //

children.text: umāgirīśāvapi bhāratīrāviti sma vāg vedagatā bravīti /
children.translated_text: '<s>Umā</s> and <s>Girīśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and <s>Bhāratī</s> and <s>Rā</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)' — thus the Vedic speech declares; /

children.text: ahīndrapatnīmahipaṃ viriñcapatnīṃ viriñcaṃ ca vimuktikāle // MAnuv_4,2.124 //
children.translated_text: the wife of <s>Ahīndra</s> (<s>Śeṣa</s>), the lord, the wife of <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), and <s>Viriñca</s> — at the time of liberation // 4.2.124 //

children.text: ta eva yat tatpadamāpnuvanti tatkāla etān samupāsya jīvāḥ /
children.translated_text: those very ones attain that state; at that time, <s>jīvas</s>, having worshipped them, enter them; /

children.text: brahmatvakāle praviśanti caitānīti sma vāk tādṛśatāmupaiti // MAnuv_4,2.125 //
children.translated_text: at the time of attaining <s>Brahman</s>-hood, they enter these — thus the speech attains this meaning // 4.2.125 //

children.text: sūryo 'gniyukto gurumāpya tena śakraṃ sahainena suparṇapatnīm /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūrya</s>, joined with <s>Agni</s>, reaches the teacher [<s>Bṛhaspati</s>]; with him [he reaches] <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>); together with him, the wife of <s>Suparṇa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>); /

children.text: tayā suparṇaṃ saha tena vāṇīṃ brahmāṇametadgata eva yāti // MAnuv_4,2.126 //
children.translated_text: with her, <s>Suparṇa</s>; with him, <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>); with her, <s>Brahmā</s> — having entered all these, he goes [to <s>Viṣṇu</s>] // 4.2.126 //
But when the entry into <s>Indra</s> is stated here, then it is said '<s>Umā</s>' for the wife of <s>Suparṇa</s>; /

children.text: uktā suparṇaśca girīśanāmnā tato virodhaśca na kaścanātra // MAnuv_4,2.127 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Suparṇa</s> is called by the name <s>Girīśa</s> — therefore there is no contradiction here at all // 4.2.127 //
<s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others, having reached <s>Dakṣa</s>, and through him having reached <s>Indra</s>, [and then] the wife of <s>Suparṇa</s>, /

children.text: viśanti ye manavo rājamukhyā manuṃ praviśyātra gatā mahendram // MAnuv_4,2.128 //
children.translated_text: enter; and those <s>Manus</s> who are chief among kings, having entered <s>Manu</s>, go to <s>Mahendra</s> // 4.2.128 //

children.text: ākāśa urvī ca guruṃ praviśya tenaiva yātaḥ puruhūtadevam /
children.translated_text: Space and earth, having entered the teacher [<s>Bṛhaspati</s>], through him alone go to the <s>deva</s> <s>Puruhūta</s> (<s>Indra</s>); /

children.text: sanādayo yatayaḥ kāmameva viśanti śiṣṭā api havyavāham // MAnuv_4,2.129 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sanaka</s> and the other ascetics enter <s>Kāma</s> himself; and the remaining [beings] enter <s>Havyavāha</s> (<s>Agni</s>) // 4.2.129 //

children.text: varṇāśramācāraratā manuṣyā dharmaṃ manuṃ so 'pi sameti kāle /
children.translated_text: People devoted to the conduct of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> [enter] <s>Dharma</s>; [he enters] <s>Manu</s>; and he too in time merges; /

children.text: tameva sarve pitaraḥ surānugāḥ sarve kuberaṃ sa ca somameva // MAnuv_4,2.130 //
children.translated_text: all the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors), followers of the <s>suras</s>, all [enter] <s>Kubera</s>; and he [enters] <s>Soma</s> himself // 4.2.130 //
At the time of liberation, they enter repeatedly and enjoy pleasures, dwelling in that body [of the Lord]; /
the clear manifestation of bliss occurs for them there; therefore they are understood to have gone forth; /

children.text: krīḍanti bhūyaśca samāviśanti tāneva sāyujyamidaṃ vadanti // MAnuv_4,2.131 //
children.translated_text: they play and again enter — this they call <s>sāyujya</s> (union) // 4.2.131 //

children.text: sāyujyahīnāśca laye tu sarve proktena mārgeṇa viśanti sṛṣṭau /
children.translated_text: And all those who are without <s>sāyujya</s>, at dissolution, enter by the stated path during creation; /

children.text: bahiśca niryānti tato 'nyadāpi sāyujyabhājāṃ bhavati praveśaḥ // MAnuv_4,2.132 //
children.translated_text: and they go forth externally from there at another time too; but for those who share in <s>sāyujya</s>, there is [permanent] entry // 4.2.132 //

children.text: uktaṃ samastaṃ paramaśrutau hi proktaṃ tu sargakramato viparyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: All this has been stated in the supreme <s>Śruti</s>; and the stated order of creation is reversed — /
