children.text: muktau laye yadvadatho layaśca viparyayeṇetyavadad girāṃ patiḥ // MAnuv_4,2.133 //
children.translated_text: in liberation and dissolution, as [in creation], and dissolution too [follows] the reverse — thus spoke the Lord of speech // 4.2.133 //

children.text: layo yato muktiriyaṃ surāṇāṃ bhogo viśeṣeṇa ca yaṃ vadiṣyati /
children.translated_text: Since this dissolution is the liberation of the <s>suras</s>, and the enjoyment which he will describe in particular — /
and the relation of original and reflection has been stated, following the dissolution stated in the <s>Piṅga Śruti</s> // 4.2.134 //

children.text: bimbe layo yanniyataśca muktau cidātmanāṃ tadvaśatā ca sarvadā /
children.translated_text: the dissolution in the original that is fixed in liberation — and the dependence of conscious beings at all times; /

children.text: tejo 'bhidhāṃ tu śriyamāpya viṣṇumagre tataḥ putratayaiva vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: having reached <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), called '<s>Tejas</s>' (radiance), [and then] <s>Viṣṇu</s> — first, then <s>Vāyu</s> as a son, /

children.text: āptaḥ prasūtaḥ punareva viṣṇuṃ praviśya muktaḥ praḷaye 'tra tiṣṭhati // MAnuv_4,2.135 //
children.translated_text: having been born, and having again entered <s>Viṣṇu</s>, stands liberated in dissolution // 4.2.135 //
All those hosts of the liberated, abundantly [enjoying] their own bliss in its entirety, /

children.text: bhuñjanta evāsata īśadehe laye 'tha sarge bahireva yānti // MAnuv_4,2.136 //
children.translated_text: existed enjoying [it] in the body of the Lord during dissolution; and at creation, they go forth // 4.2.136 //

children.text: prayāti dharmaṃ nirṛtistu śakraṃ marudgaṇāḥ pārṣadāstathaiva /
children.translated_text: [Some] go to <s>Dharma</s>; <s>Nirṛti</s> [goes] to <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>); the <s>Marudgaṇas</s> (hosts of <s>Maruts</s>) and the attendants likewise; /
all the army-leaders and the rest [go] to <s>Aniruddha</s> — the <s>Tura Śruti</s> indeed [declares] — this is liberation // 4.2.137 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: The path of departure and the destination of the liberated — stated in this <s>pāda</s>; <s>Śukra</s> (brightness) and non-transgression; /

children.text: sāntānikaṃ prāptirabhīṣyatā ca saukayarmityanyamatasya tarkāḥ // MAnuv_4,3.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Sāntānika</s> [fire], attainment, desirability, and ease — these are the arguments of the other doctrine // 4.3.1 //
Attainment of the particular, greatness, reaching, sequential devotion, stated conformity — /

children.text: siddhāntanirṇītikarāḥ pratīkaṃ dehādikaṃ tadgatameva ye narāḥ // MAnuv_4,3.2 //
children.translated_text: these are the determiners of the <s>siddhānta</s>; the symbol (<s>pratīka</s>), the body and the like — those men who being devoted to that // 4.3.2 //
worship — they first attain <s>Brahmā</s>; from us, having obtained the right understanding, they will attain <s>Viṣṇu</s>; /

children.text: prāpsyantyato 'nye 'pi tamāpya tasmāddhariṃ gatā muktibhājaḥ parānte // MAnuv_4,3.3 //
children.translated_text: and therefore others too, having reached him, thence — those who have gone to <s>Hari</s> become sharers in liberation at the final end // 4.3.3 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda</s> [<s>Madhvācārya</s>].

children.translated_text: Statement of transcendence, accomplishment, attainment of the goal, the supreme destination, reaching the far shore, that abode, /

children.text: samastakāryaṃ vaśitā ca viśvasambhāvanā yuktayastvanyapakṣe // MAnuv_4,4.1 //
children.translated_text: total effect, mastery, and universal possibility — these are the arguments of the other side // 4.4.1 //
General form, intuition, liberation, wonderfulness, naturalness, and its fault, /
particular construction, accomplished effortlessness, and greatness — these are for the purpose of firm determination // 4.4.2 //
The servitude to none other is stated here by those [scriptures], to prevent servitude to any other; /

children.text: patiṃ yadeṣāmapi viṣṇumāha hyutāmṛtatvasya patitvavāgdhareḥ // MAnuv_4,4.3 //
children.translated_text: since it declares <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the lord of even these [gods], and the statement of lordship over immortality belongs to <s>Hari</s> // 4.4.3 //
And even these [gods], though endowed with sovereignty over others, are like [ordinary] men in being governed by one other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>; /

children.text: prasiddhibhājastviti cānumaiva hyabhīṣyasiddhayai bhavatīha niścayāt // MAnuv_4,4.4 //
children.translated_text: the inference that they are well-known [as lords] serves certainly to establish the desired conclusion here // 4.4.4 //
Even in liberation, there exists the capacity of the liberated to restrain their own [subordinates], for those headed by <s>Brahmā</s>; /

children.text: anena devena tathāmunā ca hīṣye parārvāktanalokināmiti // MAnuv_4,4.5 //
children.translated_text: 'By this god and by that one, I am ruled' — [so think] those whose worlds are above and below // 4.4.5 //
<s>Śruti</s> declares the fruit from knowledge for the liberated; and this is indicated by the destruction of all inauspicious [karma]; /
sovereignty over worlds belongs to <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator) alone, as the <s>Tura Śruti</s> states 'for all selves'; /

children.text: sarve baliṃ devagaṇā vahantītyetacca nānyasya hi yuktimeti // MAnuv_4,4.6 //
children.translated_text: 'all the hosts of gods bring tribute' — and this is not logical for any other // 4.4.6 //

children.text: lokā itīhāpi tu lokināṃ vaco lokā iti hyeva ravaḥ prajāsu /
children.translated_text: 'Worlds' — even here, the word of those who have worlds; 'worlds' — for this word is used /

children.text: prayujyate sarvajanaiḥ sadaiva tanmānino lokapadena coktāḥ /
children.translated_text: among people always by everyone; those who are proud of that are called by the word '<s>loka</s>'; /

children.text: tadgāstu muktā iha lokaśabdā anyonyanāthā iti paiṅgināṃ śrutiḥ // MAnuv_4,4.7 //
children.translated_text: and the liberated whose movement is toward that are [denoted by] the word '<s>loka</s>' — 'mutually lords' — thus the <s>Śruti</s> of the <s>Paiṅgins</s> // 4.4.7 //

children.text: alokaśabdena vimuktibhājo vācyāḥ padaṃ tādṛgapīha yuktam /
children.translated_text: By the word 'non-world' (<s>aloka</s>), those who partake of liberation are to be denoted — such a meaning is also fitting here; /

children.text: lokābhidhāścāpi yato hi muktāḥ prakāśarūpāḥ satataṃ ca sarve /
children.translated_text: and since the liberated are also called by the name 'worlds' (<s>loka</s>), for they are all always of the nature of luminosity, /

children.text: brahmaiva lokādhipatirvimukto bhavediti prāha turaśrutiśca // MAnuv_4,4.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> alone, being liberated, would be the lord of worlds — so the <s>Tura Śruti</s> also declares // 4.4.8 //

children.text: naceha vijñānaphalaṃ samuktaṃ lokādhipatyaṃ ravibimbato harau /
children.translated_text: And it is not said here that the sovereignty over worlds is the fruit of knowledge; regarding <s>Hari</s>, from the orb of the sun, /

children.text: uktaṃ pṛthak tacca puraiva yasmād bhedo 'munetyādi ca samyaguktaḥ // MAnuv_4,4.9 //
children.translated_text: that [sovereignty] was stated separately and previously, since the difference of that one was properly stated as 'of this one' etc. // 4.4.9 //

children.text: tvapratyayaṃ cāpyatihāya naiva rūpeṇa teneti bhavedihārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And without abandoning the pronoun 'tva' (you), the meaning here would be 'in that very form'; /

children.text: bhavatyasāvityaṇuśabdamatra vihāya vākyāni bahūni doṣaḥ // MAnuv_4,4.10 //
children.translated_text: 'he becomes that' — setting aside the word '<s>aṇu</s>' (atomic/subtle) here, [from] many statements, [otherwise] there would be a fault // 4.4.10 //

children.text: ato jagadvayāpṛtimanta eva brahmādayaḥ pūrṇaguṇāḥ krameṇa /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, endowed with activity regarding the world, with full qualities in gradation, /
enjoying ever-abundant bliss perpetually, abide in the Unborn One through their own [nature] // 4.4.11 //
Salutation, salutation to <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person), the sole abode of qualities complete with every distinction, /
the bestower of exceedingly pure consciousness through compassion for devotees, whose nature is beloved good qualities without limiting adjuncts // 4.4.12 //

children.text: yasya trīṇyuditāni vedavacane rūpāṇi divyānalaṃ baṭ tad darśatamitthameva nihitaṃ devasya bhargo mahat /
children.translated_text: Whose three forms are proclaimed in the Vedic word — the divine fire: 'Baṭ! That is to be seen!' — thus indeed is established the great splendor of the God; /

children.text: vāyo rāmavaconayaṃ prathamakaṃ pṛkṣo dvitīyaṃ vapurmadhvo yattu tṛtīyametadanumā granthaḥ kṛtaḥ keśave // MAnuv_4,4.13 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāyu</s>, by the word of <s>Rāma</s>, this first; <s>Pṛkṣa</s> (Hanumān) is the second body; and the third is <s>Madhva</s>'s — this treatise is composed in [devotion to] <s>Keśava</s> // 4.4.13 //
Free from all defects without remainder, [possessing] all auspicious good qualities, /

children.text: bhūtisvayambhuśarvādivandyaṃ tvāṃ naumi me priyam // MAnuv_4,4.14 //
children.translated_text: worshipped by <s>Bhūti</s>, <s>Svayambhu</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and others — I praise You, my beloved // 4.4.14 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the Fourth <s>Adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtrānuvyākhyāna</s> composed by the revered <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya</s> ||
